a community is a social unit ( a group of living things ) with commonality such as norms , religion , values , customs , or identity . communities may share a sense of place situated in a given geographical area ( e.g . a country , village , town , or neighbourhood ) or in virtual space through communication platforms . durable relations that extend beyond immediate genealogical ties also define a community , important to their identity , practice , and roles in social institutions such as family , home , work , government , society , or humanity at large . although communities are usually small relative to personal social ties , `` community '' may also refer to large group affiliations such as national communities , international communities , and virtual communities.the english-language word `` community'' derives from the old french `` comuneté '' ( currently `` communauté '' ) , which comes from the latin `` communitas '' `` community,'' , `` communis '' , `` common '' , and `` common _ community '' ( from latin ` communis’ , ``common '' ) .human communities may have intent , belief , resources , preferences , needs , and risks in common , affecting the identity of the participants and their degree of cohesiveness .

chondrostei is a group of primarily cartilaginous fish showing some degree of ossification . the cartilagous condition is thought to be derived , and the ancestors of this group were bony fish with fully ossified skeletons . members of this small group share with the elasmobranchii certain features such as the possession of spiracles , a heterocercal tail , and an absence of scales . nevertheless , the fossil record suggests they have more in common with the teleosts . chondro stei is probably a paraphyletic grouping ; the 52 living species are divided among two orders , the acipenseriformes ( sturgeons and paddlefishes ) , the polypteriforme ( reedfishes and bichirs ) .

the glass frogs are frogs of the amphibian family centrolenidae ( order anura ) . while the general background coloration of most glass frogs is primarily lime green , the abdominal skin of some members of this family is transparent and translucent . the internal viscera , including the heart , liver , and gastrointestinal tract , are visible through the skin , hence the common name is given as glass frog . glass frog are arboreal , meaning they mainly live in trees , and only come out for mating season .

benthos is the community of organisms that live on , in , or near the seabed , river , lake , or stream bottom , also known as the benthic zone . this community lives in or near marine or freshwater sedimentary environments , from tidal pools along the foreshore , out to the continental shelf , and then down to the abyssal depths.many organisms adapted to deep-water pressure can not survive in the upperparts of the water column . the pressure difference can be very significant ( approximately one atmosphere for each 10 metres of water depth ) .because light is absorbed before it can reach deep ocean-water , the energy source for deep benthine ecosystems is often organic matter from higher up in the water below the surface of the ocean . this dead and decaying matter sustains the food chain ; most organisms are scavengers or detritivores.the term `` benthos '' , coined by haeckel in 1891 , comes from the greek noun `` depth of the sea '' . the term is used in freshwater biology to refer to organisms at the bottom of freshwater bodies of water , such as lakes , rivers , and streams . there is also a redundant synonym , `` bothon '' .

monday is the day of the week between sunday and tuesday . according to the international standard ISO 8601 , in countries that adopt the convention of the `` sunday-first '' convention , it is the first day of thursday . in countries where adopt the `` saturday-tuesday'' convention ,it is the second day of a week.the name of monday is derived from old english `` mōnandæg '' and middle english `` monenday '' , originally a translation of latin `` dies lunae '' `` day of moon '' .

gliese 667 cc ( also known as gj 667cc , hr 6426cc , or hd 156384cc ) is an exoplanet orbiting within the habitable zone of the red dwarf star gliese six67 c , which is a member of the gliesa 667 triple star system , approximately 23.62 light-years ( 6.8 parsecs , or about 217,000,000,-000,0000 km ) away in the constellation of scorpius . the exoplanets was found by using the radial velocity method , from radial-velocity measurements via observation of doppler shifts in the spectrum of the planet 's parent star .

caryophyllaceae , commonly called the pink family or carnation family , is a family of flowering plants . it is included in the dicotyledon order caryophylales in the apg iii system , alongside 33 other families , including amaranthaceae , cactaceae , and polygonaceae . it has a large family , with 81 genera and about 2,625 known species.this cosmopolitan family of mostly herbaceous plants is best represented in temperate climates , with a few species growing on tropical mountains . some of the more commonly known members include pinks and carnations ( `` dianthus '' ) , and firepink and campions ( `` lychnis '' and `` silene '' ) . many species are grown as ornamental plants , and some species are widespread weeds . most species grow in the mediterranean and bordering regions of europe and asia . the number of genera can be found in the southern hemisphere is rather small , although the family does contain antarctic pearlwort ( `` colobanthus quitensis '' , the world 's southernmost dicota , which is one of only two flowering plants found in antarctica.the name comes from `` caryophora '' , an obsolete synonym of `` dorianthus '' .

a leaf blower , commonly known as blower, is a gardening tool that propels air out of a nozzle to move debris such as leaves and grass cuttings . leaf blowers are powered by electric or gasoline motors . gasoline models have traditionally been two-stroke engines , but four-stroke generators were recently introduced to partially address air pollution concerns . leafblowers are typically self-contained handheld units , or backpack mounted units with a handheld wand . the latter is more ergonomic for prolonged use . larger units may rest on wheels and even use a motor for propulsion . these are sometimes called `` walk behind leaf blows '' because they must be pushed by hand to be operated.some units can also suck in leaves and small twigs via a vacuum , and shred them into a bag . in that role it is called a blower vac .

interstate 69 ( i-69 ) is an interstate highway in the united states currently consisting of ten disjointed parts with an original continuous segment from indianapolis , indiana , northeast to the canada–us border in port huron , michigan , and at . the remaining separated segments are variously completed and posted or unposted sections of an extension southwest to the mexican border in texas . of this extension—nicknamed the nafta superhighway because it would help trade with canada and mexico spurred by the north american free trade agreement—five pieces near corpus christi , houston , northwestern mississippi , memphis , and evansville have been built or upgraded and signposted as i-68 . a sixth segment of i-7 through kentucky utilizing that state 's existing parkway system and a section of i–24 was established by federal legislation in 2008 , but only a portion is signposted . this brings the total length to about .the proposed extension evolved from the combination of corridors 18 and 20 of the national highway system as designated in the intermodal surface transportation efficiency act of 1991 , but the federally recognized corridor also includes connecting and existing infrastructure , including i-94 between chicago and port duron and several spurs from I-69 . among these proposed spurs are an extension to i-530 from pine bluff , arkansas , and an upgrade of u.s. route 59 ( us 59 ) from texarkana , texas , and a split in southern texas to serve three border crossings at laredo , pharr , and brownsville.in august 2007 , we-69 was selected by the United States department of transportation as one of six corridors of the future , making it eligible for additional federal funding and streamlined planning and review . this funding has since been withheld , causing some states to suspend construction indefinitely .

kathleen rachel makinson ( née white ) ( 15 february 1917 – 18 october 2014 ) was an australian physicist and the first woman to become a chief research scientist at the country 's research organization , csiro .

heian-kyō was one of several former names for the city now known as kyoto . it was the official capital of japan for over one thousand years , from 794 to 1868 with an interruption in 1180.emperor kanmu established it as the capital in 794 , moving the imperial court there from nearby nagaoka-kyo at the recommendation of his advisor wake no kiyomaro and marking the beginning of the heian period, marking the end of the shogunate . the city was modelled after the tang dynasty chinese capital of chang'an ( modern-day xi'an ) . it remained the chief political center until 1185 , when the samurai minamoto clan defeated the taira clan in the genpei war , moving administration of national affairs to kamakura and establishing the kamaki shogunates.though political power would be wielded by the samurai class over the course of three different shogunations , heian remained the site of the imperial courts and seat of imperial power , and thus remained the official Capital . in fact , even after the seat of Imperial power was moved to tokyo in 1868 , since there is no law which makes tokyō the capital , there is a view that kyota legally or officially remains the capital even today.in 1994 , kyOTO city held various events commemorating its 1200th anniversary .

the globe artichoke ( `` cynara cardunculus '' var . `` scolymus '' ) , also known by the names french artichokes in the u.s. , is a variety of a species of thistle cultivated as a food.the edible portion of the plant consists of the flower buds before the flowers come into bloom . the budding artichok flower-head is a cluster of many budding small flowers ( an inflorescence ) , together with many bracts , on an edible base . once the buds bloom , the structure changes to a coarse , barely edible form . another variety of the same species is the cardoon , a perennial plant native to the mediterranean region . both wild forms and cultivated varieties ( cultivars ) exist .

sportverein grödig is an austrian association football club from Grödig . the team currently competes in the austrian regional league west , the third tier of austrian football.grödig were relegated from the austria bundesliga at the end of the 2015–16 season ; however , they dropped down two levels to the austrians regional league east due to financial problems .

singapore has sent athletes to most summer olympics held since 1948 , when it was established as a separate british crown colony from the straits settlements just over three months before the commencement of the 1948 summer o Olympics . it continued to send a team to the games until 1964 when singapore was part of Malaysia , which sent a combined team . upon singapore 's full independence from malaysia in 1965 , the country continued to participate in all subsequent editions of the summer oolsics except in 1980 when the country participated in a large olympic boycott . singapore made their winter olympus debut at the 2018 winter oOlympics , with speed skater , cheyenne goh , competing in the short track speed skating event.the country has won five Olympic medals , the inaugural was at the 1960 summer oleics , the second at the 2008 summer oletics and the third and fourth at the 2012 summer ossics . at the 2016 summer ompics singapore won their first ever gold medal and the fifth overall. < ref >

donn alan pennebaker ( ; july 15 , 1925 – august 1 , 2019 ) ( often credited as d.a . penne baker ) was an american documentary filmmaker and one of the pioneers of direct cinema . performing arts and politics were his primary subjects . in 2013 , the academy of motion picture arts and sciences recognized his body of work with an academy honorary award.pennebacher has been described as `` arguably the pre-eminent chronicler of sixties counterculture '' .

pullman ( ) is the largest city in whitman county , located in southeastern washington state within the palouse region of the pacific northwest . the population was 29,799 at the 2010 census , and estimated to be 34,506 in 2019 . originally founded as three forks , the city was renamed after industrialist george pullman in 1884.pullman is noted as a vastly fertile agricultural area known for its many miles of rolling hills and the production of wheat and legumes . it is home to washington State university , a public research land-grant university , and the international headquarters of schweitzer engineering laboratories . pullman is from moscow , idaho , home to the university of idaho . and is served by the pullman-moscow regional airport .

international left handers day is an international day observed annually on august 13 to celebrate the uniqueness and differences of the right handers . the day was first observed in 1976 by dean r. campbell , founder of the lefthanders international , inc. international left hander 's day was created to celebrate sinistrality and raise awareness of the advantages and disadvantages of being left-handed in a predominantly right-handed world . it celebrates left-hand people’s uniqueness and similarities , a subset of humanity comprising seven to ten percent of the world 's population .the day also spread awareness on issues faced by left-haters e.g . the importance of the special needs for left- handed children , and the likelihood forleft-handers to develop schizophrenia . there are approximately 708 million left-footed people in the world . men are more likely to be left handed than women.in the past , left-wingers were forced to become right-handed . former american president harry s. truman wrote left-off as a child but was forced by his parents to write right-sided . on international lefths day , we can help raise awareness about the difficulties of being Left-handed .

voltage , electric potential difference , electric pressure or electric tension is the difference in electric potential between two points , which ( in a static electric field ) is defined as the work needed per unit of charge to move a test charge between the two points . in the international system of units , the derived unit for voltage ( potential difference ) is named `` volt '' . in si units , work per unit charge is expressed as joules per coulomb , where 1 volt = 1 joule ( of work ) per 1 coulom ( of charge ) . the old si definition for `` volt'' used power and current , since 1990 quantum hall and josephson effect were used and recently ( 2019 ) fundamental physical constants were introduced for the definition of all si units and derived units . voltage or electric potential differences is denoted symbolically by , simplified `` v '' , or `` u '' , for instance in the context of ohm 's or kirchhoff 's circuit laws.electric potential differences between points can be caused by electric charge , by electric current through a magnetic field , by time-varying magnetic fields , by some combination of these three . a voltmeter can be used to measure the voltage ( or potential difference ), electric pressure , electric tension , or electric pressure . a voltage meter may be used as a reference potential for a point in a system ; often a common reference potential such as the ground of the system is used as one of the points .a voltage may represent either a source of energy ( electromotive force ) or lost , used , or stored energy ( potential drop ) .

wisconsin 's 8th congressional district is a congressional district of the united states house of representatives in northeastern wisconsin . it is currently represented by mike gallagher , a republican . gallagher won the open seat vacated by reid ribble in 2016 .it is also one of two congressional districts to ever elect a catholic priest , robert john cornell.the 8th leaned republican for many years ; only four democrats represented it in the 20th century . however , it became more of a swing seat in the 1990s . in 2004 , republican george w. bush won 55 % of the vote in the district , while in 2008 , democrat barack obama received 53.6 % of votes . the last democrat to represent the district was steve kagen from 2007 to 2011 . since kagen lost in the 2010 election , the seat has been held by republicans , who have consistently won it by double digit percent margins in each election to the seat since 2012.since the 1970s , the district has encompassed the northeastern part of wisconsin , including cities such as green bay and appleton , the peninsula of door county , and ( until redistricting following the 2010 census ) most of the state’s counties bordering michigan .

merced county ( ) , is a county located in the northern san joaquin valley section of the central valley , in the u.s. state of california.as of the 2010 census , the population was 255,793 . the county seat is merced .the county is named after the merced river.merced city comprises the merces , ca metropolitan statistical area , which is included in the modesto-merced , ca combined statistical area . it is located north of fresno county and fresno , and southeast of santa clara county and san jose .

the term fish processing refers to the processes associated with fish and fish products between the time fish are caught or harvested , and the time the final product is delivered to the customer . although the term refers specifically to fish , in practice it is extended to cover any aquatic organisms harvested for commercial purposes , whether caught in wild fisheries or harvested from aquaculture or fish farming.larger fish processing companies often operate their own fishing fleets or farming operations . the products of the fish industry are usually sold to grocery chains or to intermediaries . fish are highly perishable . a central concern of fish processing is to prevent fish from deteriorating , and this remains an underlying concern during other processing operations.fish processing can be subdivided into fish handling , which is the preliminary processing of raw fish , and its manufacture of fish products . another natural subdivision is into primary processing involved in the filleting and freezing of fresh fish for onward distribution to fresh fish retail and catering outlets . the secondary processing that produces chilled , frozen and canned products for the retailing trades.there is evidence humans have been processing fish since the early holocene . these days , fish processing (or fish processing ) is undertaken by artisan fishermen , on board fishing or fish processing vessels , and at fish processing plants .

atlantis ( , `` island of atlas '' ) is a fictional island mentioned in an allegory on the hubris of nations in plato 's works `` timaeus '' and `` critias '' , where it represents the antagonist naval power that besieges `` ancient athens '' , the pseudo-historic embodiment of plato ’s ideal state in `` the republic '' . in the story , athens repels the atlantean attack unlike any other nation of the known world , supposedly bearing witness to the superiority of platon 's concept of a state . the story concludes with atlantis falling out of favor with the deities and submerging into the atleantic ocean.despite its minor importance in plat 's work , the atllantis story has had a considerable impact on literature . the allegorical aspect of atlanta was taken up in utopian works of several renaissance writers , such as francis bacon 's `` new atlatantis '' and thomas more 's`` utopia '' . on the other hand , nineteenth-century amateur scholars misinterpreted plato's narrative as historical tradition , most famously ignatius l. donnelly in his `` '' . plato "s vague indications of the time of the events—more than 9,000 years before his time—and the alleged location of Atlantis— '' beyond the pillars of hercules '' —has led to much pseudoscientific speculation . as a consequence , plato's narrative has become a byword for any and all supposed advanced prehistoric lost civilizations and continues to inspire contemporary fiction , from comic books to films.while present-day philologists and classicists agree on the story 's fictional character , there is still debate on what served as its inspiration . as for instance with the story of gyges, plato is known to have freely borrowed some of his allegories and metaphors from older traditions . this led a number of scholars to investigate if plato created an entirely fictional account , drawing loose inspiration from contemporary events such as the failed athenian invasion of sicily in 415–413 bc or the destruction of helike in 373 bc .

the british rail class 304 electric multiple units were built for suburban use on the first phases of the west coast main line electrification between crewe and manchester/liverpool/rugby . originally classed as am4 units , they later became class 304 under the tops numbering system , and could be found in operation over most of the east coast main branch . the units conformed to the 1959-design for alternating current ( ac ) electrical multiple units , and were externally very similar to the class 305 , class 308 and the 1,200 v direct current ( dc ) class 504 units . no units survived into preservation , and all units were eventually scrapped .

in mathematics , a continuous function is a function that does not have any abrupt changes in value , known as discontinuities . more precisely , sufficiently small changes in the input of a continuous functions result in arbitrarily small changes or changes in its output . if not continuous , a function is said to be `` discontinuous '' . up until the 19th century , mathematicians largely relied on intuitive notions of continuity , during which attempts such as the epsilon–delta definition were made to formalize it.continuity of functions is one of the core concepts of topology , which is treated in full generality below . the introductory portion of this article focuses on the special case where the inputs and outputs of functions are real numbers . a stronger form of continuity is uniform continuity . in addition , this article discusses the definition for the more general case of functions between two metric spaces . in order theory , especially in domain theory , one considers a notion of continuity known as scott continuity . other forms of continuity do exist but they are not discussed in this article.as an example , the function denoting the height of a growing flower at time would be considered continuous . in contrast, the function Denoting the amount of money in a bank account at time is considered discontinuous , since it `` jumps '' at each point in time when money is deposited or withdrawn .

manchukuo , officially the state of manchuria prior to 1934 and the empire of japan after 1934 , was a puppet state of the imperial japan in northeast china and inner mongolia from 1932 until 1945 . it was founded in 1932 after the japanese invasion of mancuria , and in 1934 it became a constitutional monarchy . under the `` de facto '' control of japantas , it had limited international recognition.the area was the homeland of the manchus , including the emperors of the qing dynasty . in 1931 , the region was seized by japan following the mukden incident . a pro-japanese government was installed one year later with puyi , the last qing emperor , as the nominal regent and later emperor . manchukuo 's government was dissolved in 1945 after the surrender of imperial rapan at the end of world war ii . the territories claimed by manchu were first seized in the soviet invasion of the area in august 1945 , and then formally transferred to chinese administration in the following year.manchus formed a minority in manchuo , whose largest ethnic group was han chinese . the population of koreans increased during the period of the second world war , and there were also a number of other ethnic groups in the area . the korean population increased during this period . the mongol regions of western manchia were ruled under a slightly different system in acknowledgement of the mONGolian traditions there . the southern tip of the liaodong peninsula ( present-day dalian ) continued to be directly ruled by japon as the kwantung leased territory . the largest ethnic groups were han ileans and the population grew during the manchuko period , and many were also Japanese , mongols , white russians and other minorities . the northern tip of western hechus were ruled by a slightly changed system in recognition of the importance of the traditional mongoling traditions there ; the southern part of the Liaodong Peninsula ( present day dalian , continued to been directly ruled over japan as the Kwantung lease territory .

'' he encouraged missionary activity abroad and condemned the slave trade . however , his harsh repression , financial extravagance and neglectfulness left him deeply unpopular domestically.he is the most recent pope to take the pontifical name `` gregories '' , and the most-recent non-bishop to become pope . he was , until the accession of pope francis in 2013 , the first pope to have been a priest of a religious order .

world music ( also called global music or international music ) is a western musical category encompassing many different styles of music from other parts of the globe . it includes many forms of music that westerners consider ethnic , indigenous music , folk music , neotraditional music , and music where more than one cultural tradition , such as non-western music and western popular music , intermingle.world music 's inclusive nature and elasticity as a musical category may pose some obstacles to a universal definition , but its ethic of interest in the culturally exotic is encapsulated in `` froots '' magazine 's description of the 'genre ' as `` local music from out there '' .the term was popularized in the 1980s as a marketing category for non-Western traditional music . it has grown to include subgenres such as ethnic fusion ( clannad , ry cooder , enya , etc . ) and worldbeat .

Square roots are found using numerical analysis algorithms to determine the non-negative square root of a real number. This means finding a number that, when multiplied by itself, equals the given number. Algebraically, it's solving the equation \(x^2 - s = 0\). Geometrically, it involves finding the side length of a square given its area. Every real number has two square roots, but the principal square root is the non-negative one. Most square roots are irrational numbers with infinite decimal expansions, so their decimal values can only be approximated. Even for perfect square integers, the result might need to be approximated. The continued fraction representation of a real number can help, as it shows periodic expansions for square roots of rational numbers. Common methods, like Newton's method, are iterative. They involve starting with a guess and refining it until the desired accuracy is reached. Fewer iterations are needed if the initial guess is closer to the actual root. Other methods, like synthetic division and series expansion, don't require a starting guess. Sometimes, an integer square root is needed, which is the square root rounded or truncated to the nearest whole number. The choice of method depends on the required accuracy, the effort and tools available. Methods can be classified as suitable for mental calculation, those needing paper and pencil, or those implemented in computer programs. Finding square roots has been known since ancient Babylon around 1700 BCE. Heron's method from first-century Egypt was the first known algorithm. Modern methods started in the Renaissance period. Today, most computing devices have a fast and accurate square root function.

In telecommunications networks, a node is either a place where information is redistributed or the endpoint for communication. The exact definition of a node depends on the network and the layer being considered. A physical network node is an electronic device connected to a network, capable of sending or receiving information. A passive distribution point, like a distribution frame or patch panel, is not considered a node.

hypothyroidism, also called underactive thyroid or low thyroid, is when the thyroid gland makes too little thyroid hormone. It can cause feeling cold, being tired, constipation, a slow heart rate, feeling sad, and gaining weight. Sometimes, there's swelling in the neck because of a goiter. If not treated during pregnancy, it can affect a baby's growth and intelligence. Not having enough iodine in food is the most common cause of hypothyroidism worldwide. In places with enough iodine, Hashimoto's thyroiditis is the most common cause. Other causes include past radiation treatment, injuries to the brain or pituitary gland, certain medicines, no working thyroid at birth, or surgery on the thyroid. Doctors can confirm hypothyroidism using blood tests that measure thyroid hormone and thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) levels. In many places, adding iodine to salt has helped prevent hypothyroidism. Treating it involves taking thyroid hormone medicine called levothyroxine. Doctors adjust the dose based on symptoms and test results. This medicine is safe during pregnancy. While iodine in the diet is important, too much can worsen certain types of hypothyroidism. About one billion people are iodine-deficient globally, but it's unclear how often this leads to hypothyroidism. In the U.S., about 0.3% to 0.4% of people have hypothyroidism. A milder form, subclinical hypothyroidism, is found in 4.3% to 8.5% of Americans. Women and older people are more likely to have it. Dogs, cats, and horses can also develop hypothyroidism, but less often. The word "hypothyroidism" comes from Greek, where "hypo-" means less, "thyreos" means shield, and "eidos" means form.

Jens Spahn, born on May 16, 1980, is a German politician. He works as the federal minister of health in the fourth Merkel cabinet. Spahn is part of the lower house of the federal parliament, the Bundestag, representing Steinfurt I – Borken I. He belongs to the Christian Democratic Union of Germany (CDU), a center-right party that governs together with the Social Democratic Party of Germany (SPD). Spahn became a member of the CDU when he was 22, elected to the Bundestag in 2002. He has served in the 15th, 16th, and 17th Bundestags. He is one of the main people working on pension reform in Germany. Spahn is part of the health committee in the 17th Bundestag and leads the health working group. He also speaks for the CDU/CSU health group in the Bundestag. In 2018, when Angela Merkel said she would not run for the CDU party leadership again, Spahn said he would try to become the new leader. However, he did not win in the first voting round. The position went to Annegret Kramp-Karrenbauer instead. In February 2020, Kramp-Karrenbauer decided to step down. Spahn then said he would not run for the CDU leadership but would support Armin Laschet as the candidate.
Barnas is a commune in the Ardèche department, which is in the Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes region of southern France. The people who live there are called Barnassiens or Barnassiennes.

Jesse and Joy are a Mexican pop duo. They were formed in 2005 by brothers and sisters Jesse, born on December 31, 1982, and Joy, born on June 20, 1986. Both are from Mexico City. They have made four studio albums, one live album, and one EP for Warner Music Latin. They have also toured internationally. Jesse and Joy have won a Best Latin Album Grammy and six Latin Grammy Awards in different categories. "Latin Times" said they are probably some of the purest and most talented artists of their generation.

Ghost Whisperer was an American TV show about ghosts. It was on CBS from September 23, 2005, to May 21, 2010. The main character, Melinda Gordon, played by Jennifer Love Hewitt, can see and talk to ghosts. She is married and owns an antique store but helps ghosts. Her job is hard because some people don't believe in her. At first, ghosts can be mysterious and scary. Melinda uses clues to help them. The show was made by John Gray and produced by Sander/Moses Productions with Jennifer Love Hewitt. It was also made with ABC Studios and CBS Television Studios. CBS stopped the show after five seasons.

Soli Dias Abeywickrema Jayatilleke Senewiratna Rajakumaruna Kadukeralu Bandaranaike (Sinhala: සොලමන් ඩයස් අබේවික්‍රම ජයතිලක සෙනෙවිරත්න රාජකුමාරුණ කඩුකෙරළු බණ්ඩාරනායක) was born on May 22, 1862, and died on July 31, 1946. He was a headman in Ceylon during the colonial era. He was appointed as a head mudaliyar and aide-de-camp to the British governor of Ceylon. This made him one of the most powerful people in British colonial Ceylon.

Carthage is a village in the town of Wilna, which is in Jefferson County, New York, United States. The village had 3,747 people in 2010. Carthage is named after the ancient city of Carthage in Tunisia. The village is located near the southern edge of the town of Wilna and is east of Watertown.

Leendert "Leen" Verbeek, born on March 5, 1954, is a Dutch politician. He has been the king's commissioner of Flevoland since 2008. Verbeek is a member of the Labour Party (PVDa). From 2003 to 2008, he was the mayor of Purmerend. Verbeek grew up in Eindhoven. He studied at MULO and had a year of high school in the United States. After that, he went to the Academy for Educational Labour in Baarn. He then worked as a youth worker in Leiden. In 1989, Verbeek began his political career as an alderman in Houten. He was mayor of Purmerend from 2003 to 2008. In between, he was the director of a company he created himself. In December 2007, Verbeek and Rob van Gijzel were candidates for mayor of Eindhoven. A referendum was held in January 2008. Verbeek got 33% of the votes, but the referendum was nullified. Van Gijzel became the mayor instead. Verbeek was replaced as mayor of Purmerend in November 2008. He was then appointed as the king's commissioner of Flevoland in 2008, a title that changed to king's commissioner in 2013.

Dawlish is a seaside town and part of Teignbridge in Devon, England. It is near the county town Exeter and the bigger resort Torquay. In 2018, it had about 16,000 people. More people are expected as new homes are being built, especially in the north and east of the town. Dawlish became a popular seaside place in the 18th century, starting as a small fishing port. Its neighbor, Teignmouth, also grew into a famous seaside resort in the 19th century.

Wilhelm Gustav Keitel was a German field marshal and war criminal during the Nazi era. He served as the chief of the armed forces high command (Oberkommando der Wehrmacht, OKW) during World War II. In this role, he signed orders that caused a very brutal war. Keitel became the head of the armed forces office at the Reich Ministry of War in 1935. In 1938, Hitler took over the Wehrmacht and replaced the ministry with the OKW, with Keitel as its chief. His colleagues in the military often criticized him for always agreeing with Hitler. After the war, Keitel was tried at Nuremberg and found guilty of crimes against humanity, crimes against peace, criminal conspiracy, and war crimes. He was sentenced to death and executed by hanging in 1946.

Mária Pozsonec was born on January 16, 1940, and passed away on April 3, 2017. She was a Slovenian politician of Hungarian background. From 1990 to 2008, she represented the Hungarian community in Slovenia's National Assembly. She was born to Hungarian parents in Dolga Vas, near Lendava, which was part of the Drava Banovina of the Kingdom of Yugoslavia (now in Slovenia). She studied at a high school in Subotica, Serbia, and later at the University of Maribor in Slovenia. She taught elementary school in Prekmurje, her home region. In the 1980s, she became active in helping the Hungarian minority in Slovenia. In the first free Slovenian elections in April 1990, she was elected to the National Assembly. She was re-elected four times, in 1992, 1996, 2000, and 2004. In 2008, she lost to László Göncz. She also served as vice-mayor of Lendava from 2006 to 2011. Pozsonec lived to be 77 years old.

Magnús Eiríksson was born on June 22, 1806, in Skinnalón (Norður-Þingeyjarsýsla), Iceland, and died on July 3, 1881, in Copenhagen, Denmark. He was an Icelandic theologian. Eiríksson criticized the ideas of Søren Aabye Kierkegaard and Hans Lassen Martensen in Copenhagen. Eiríksson was very critical of the church's teachings, especially about the Holy Trinity and Jesus being divine. Instead, he believed in the unity of God and saw Jesus as a prophet and teacher. People often called him a "pioneer" or "precursor" to the Unitarian movement in Denmark.

In baseball, an error happens when a fielder makes a mistake with the ball. This mistake allows a batter or a runner to move to a different base. It also means a player on the batter's team can keep their turn at bat. Sometimes, "error" refers to the exact play where this happened.
aigné is a town in the sarthe department, which is in the pays-de-la-loire region of western france.

The heat index is a measure that combines temperature and humidity to show how hot it feels outside in the shade. It is also known as the "felt air temperature," "apparent temperature," "real feel," or "feels like" temperature. For instance, if the temperature is 70% humidity, the heat index would adjust the temperature based on the humidity. The human body cools itself by sweating. Sweat evaporates, taking heat away from the body. But high humidity makes sweat evaporate slower, so the body loses heat more slowly. This makes people feel hotter. How hot people feel can vary. Different factors like body shape, health, hydration, pregnancy, menopause, and certain medications can affect this. Scientists estimate the heat index based on how people feel at different temperatures and humidity levels. Since the heat index measures shade temperatures, it might not reflect the actual outdoor temperature, especially in sunny areas. People who are active or exercising might feel even hotter than the heat index suggests.

Beth Grant, born on September 18, 1949, is an American actress who often plays strict or religious characters. She was a regular actress in the TV show "The Mindy Project" from 2012 to 2017, playing Beverly Janoszewski. She also appeared as Gracie Leigh in the TV drama "Jericho" and as Marianne Marie Beetle in "Wonderfalls," "Pushing Daisies," and "Mockingbird Lane." In movies, she played Mother in "Rain Man" (1988), Miss Kettlewell in "Child's Play 2" (1990), Helen in "Speed," and Pageant Official Jenkins in "Little Miss Sunshine" (2006). She starred in "Flatliners," "Sordid Lives," "Dear Lemon Lima," and "Bad Words." Recently, she acted as Claudia "Lady Bird" Johnson in "Jackie," and in the critically acclaimed films "Faults" (2014) and "Lucky" (2017). She also appeared as a character with hair but no beard in Netflix's "A Series of Unfortunate Events" and as the cat lady in Hulu's "Dollface."

Yair Aрон was born on April 30, 1945. He is an Israeli historian and expert on the Holocaust, genocide, racism, and Jewish people today. Since 2005, he has worked as the head of the sociology, political science, and communication department at the Open University of Israel. He is also an associate professor there.

Linda Hopkins, born on December 14, 1924, and died on April 10, 2017, was an American actress and singer. She performed blues and gospel music. She sang classic, traditional, and urban blues. She also sang R&B and soul, jazz, and show tunes.

David, described in the Hebrew Bible, became the third king of Israel and Judah after Ish-bosheth. In the Books of Samuel, David was a young shepherd who gained fame as a musician and later by defeating Goliath. He became Saul's favorite and a close friend to Saul's son Jonathan. Saul grew jealous and turned against David. After Saul and Jonathan died in battle, David was made king. He captured Jerusalem, brought the Ark of the Covenant there, and established a kingdom. As king, David had an affair with Bathsheba, which led to the death of her husband, Uriah. David's son Absalom tried to take over the kingdom. David fled Jerusalem during Absalom's rebellion but returned after Absalom's death to rule. God didn't allow David to build a temple because he had shed much blood. Before he died, David chose Solomon as his successor. He is seen as a perfect king in prophetic writings and is considered the ancestor of a future messiah. Many psalms are attributed to him. Historians agree that a real David likely existed around 1000 BCE, though there's little clear evidence. The Tel Dan stele mentions "house of David." David is also discussed in the New Testament and the Quran. His story has inspired art and literature for centuries.
eon or eons may refer to very long periods of time.

Thomas Terrell Sessums was born on June 11, 1930, and passed away on June 6, 2020. He served as the Speaker of the Florida House of Representatives from 1972 to 1974. After that, he continued his career in leadership and public service.
Maximilian Josef Sommer, born on June 26, 1934, is an actor from Germany and America. He performs on stages, in TV shows, and in movies.

Tyrus Raymond Cobb, nicknamed the Georgia Peach, was an American baseball player. He was born on December 18, 1886, in Narrows, Georgia. Cobb played for the Detroit Tigers for 22 seasons, becoming the team's player-manager for his last six seasons. He finished his career with the Philadelphia Athletics. In 1936, he received 98.2% of the votes on the first Baseball Hall of Fame ballot, with 222 out of 226 votes. In 1999, he was ranked third on a list of baseball's 100 greatest players by "Sporting News." Cobb set 90 Major League Baseball records during his career. He scored 4,065 runs, which is the highest combined total of runs scored and runs batted in (after adjusting for home runs). He holds the highest career batting average (.366 or.367) and most career batting titles (11 or 12). He also has the most career hits (4,189 or 4,191), runs (2,245 or 2,246), games played (3,035), and at-bats (11,429 or 11,434) in the American League. He still holds the record for most career stolen bases (892) and for stealing home (54 times) and for stealing second, third, and home in succession (4 times). Cobb was the youngest player to compile 4,000 hits and score 2,000 runs. He is also known for committing 271 errors, the most by any American League outfielder. Cobb's legacy includes a college scholarship fund for Georgia residents, financed by his early investments in Coca-Cola and General Motors. However, his reputation was damaged by allegations of racism and violence, stemming from discredited biographies released after his death. Cobb was known for sometimes violent conflicts but supported the integration of black players into the major leagues and was a philanthropist.
Vittsjö is a place in Hässleholm municipality, Skåne county, Sweden. It had 1,665 people living there in 2010.

Liu Shaoqi, born on November 24, 1898, and died on November 12, 1969, was a Chinese leader. He was important in politics and had ideas about society. From 1954 to 1959, he was the chairman of a committee. From 1956 to 1966, he was the first vice chairman of the Communist Party. He was also the president of China from 1959 to 1968. During this time, he worked on rebuilding the economy. For 15 years, he was one of the three most important people in China, behind only Mao Zedong and Zhou Enlai. Liu was chosen to take over after Mao, but he did not agree with Mao early in the Cultural Revolution. Mao then criticized and removed Liu. Liu disappeared from public life in 1968. He was called names like "leader of China's bourgeoisie" and "capitalist roader." He was also seen as a traitor. Liu died because of poor treatment during the Cultural Revolution. In 1980, Deng Xiaoping's government said Liu was rehabilitated and had a national memorial service.

The Oriental Library, located in Tokyo, is Japan's largest library for Asian studies and one of the world's five largest. It also works as a research center for studying Asian history and culture. The library has helped develop Asian studies by getting books and other materials and publishing research by Japanese scholars. Currently, it has about 950,000 books, which are organized using Asian, Western, and Japanese languages.

Elizabeth Welter Wilson lived from April 4, 1921, to May 9, 2015. She was an American actress with a career lasting almost 70 years. She acted in both films and TV shows. In 1972, she won a special award called the Tony Award for her performance in a play called "Sticks and Bones." In 2006, she was honored and became a member of the American Theater Hall of Fame.
George Shaw was a botanist and zoologist from England. He lived from December 10, 1751, to July 22, 1813.

The ruby slippers are special shoes worn by Dorothy Gale in the 1939 film "The Wizard of Oz." They were played by actress Judy Garland. These shoes are very valuable because they are famous. Several pairs were made for the movie, but exactly how many is not clear. Five pairs survived. One pair was stolen from a museum in 2005 but was found again in 2018. In the original book from 1900, Dorothy wore silver shoes. But in the movie, the shoes were changed to red. This was done to make the shoes look better with the new color technology used in Hollywood movies. The idea to change the shoe color came from a writer named Noel Langley.

The Wilmington insurrection of 1898, also known as the Wilmington massacre or coup, happened in Wilmington, North Carolina, on November 10, 1898. This event marked a turning point in post-reconstruction North Carolina politics. It led to stricter racial segregation and took away voting rights from African Americans across the South. Laura Edwards wrote in "Democracy Betrayed" (2000) that what happened in Wilmington showed that white supremacy was confirmed not just in that city but throughout the South and the nation. The white press first called it a race riot caused by black people. But as more facts came out, it was seen as a "coup d'état" - when a group of white supremacists overthrew a legally elected government. Multiple factors led to this. The event is considered the only such incident in American history. It involved 2,000 white men overthrowing the elected local government. They forced out black and white political leaders, destroyed black citizens' property and businesses, and killed an estimated 60 to more than 300 people.

chemical stability, used in chemistry, means that a chemical system is in its lowest energy state or in chemical equilibrium with its surroundings. In this state, the system remains stable, even if individual atoms or molecules change form. This stability lasts until the system is altered. Chemical systems can involve changes in matter's state or a series of chemical reactions. When we say one state is more stable than another, it means the energy change from the first state to the second is positive.

Sarah Shahi, born on January 10, 1980, is an American actress of Iranian and Spanish ancestry. She has acted in TV shows and movies. She played Carmen in "The L Word" in 2008, Kate Reed in "Fairly Legal" from 2011 to 2012, and Sameen Shaw in "Person of Interest." She also played Det. Dani Reese in "Life" and had a supporting role in "Alias." In 2018, she starred in "Reverie." In 2019, she was in a few episodes of "City on a Hill" and appeared in seven episodes of "The Rookie" as Jessica Russo.

Vikram Chatterjee is a Bengali film actor. He started with a small role in Mainak Bhowmik's 2012 movie "Bedroom" and was quickly noticed. In the same year, he acted as the main character in "Elar Char Adhyay," based on Rabindranath Tagore's novel "Char Adhyay." He then acted in "Ami Aar Amar Girlfriends," "Hoichoi," and "Britto." His career changed after he acted in the realistic movie "Mistake," directed by S.K. Bangalore, in 2013. This movie was liked by young people. He has been in many films and is now a main actor in Bengali movies. He is very popular from his TV show "Ichchenodi," where he played the main character Anurag, and has many fans. He won many prizes for his role in "Shaheb Bibi Golaam" as Zico. In 2013, he was on the reality TV show "Bigg Boss Bangali." In 2017, "Calcutta Times" said he was the hottest man on TV and one of the most desirable men. He has been a heartthrob for many people recently. His recent movies, "Khoj" and "Meghnad Badh Rahasya," have been well-received by critics and successful at the box office.

Como, founded in 1907, is an Italian football club from Como, in Lombardy. They play in Serie C. Como were in Serie A in 2002-03. They then lost three times in a row and went down to Serie C2 at the end of the 2004-05 season after losing a playoff to Novara Calcio. They even had to stop playing professionally because they went bankrupt. They then joined Serie D, the top level of non-professional football in Italy. They stayed there for three seasons before getting promoted back to Serie C2 in the 2007-08 season. In 2016, they went bankrupt again. A new company restarted the club in 2017 and joined Serie D in the 2017-18 season.

ronald johnson was an American football running back. He played college football for the University of Michigan from 1966 to 1968. In 1967, he ran for 270 yards in a game, breaking a Michigan record. In 1968, he became the first African-American to be captain of a Michigan football team. That year, he set an NCAA record by running for 347 yards in a game and also set Big Ten conference records with 92 points and 1,017 rushing yards in seven games. He also set Michigan records with 2,524 career rushing yards, 19 rushing touchdowns in a season, and 139.1 rushing yards per game in 1968. Johnson played seven seasons in the NFL from 1969 to 1975. In 1970 and 1972, he became the first New York Giants player to rush for 1,000 yards in a season. He led the NFL in rushing attempts in 1970 and 1972. He retired in 1976, was inducted into the College Football Hall of Fame in 1992, and became chairman of the National Football Foundation in 2006. Johnson was diagnosed with Alzheimer's disease in 2008 and died in 2018. He had a brother, Alex Johnson, who was the 1970 American League batting champion.

The Ron, Ronic, or Ron-fyer languages belong to group A.4 of the West Chadic branch of the Afro-Asiatic language family. These languages are spoken in Plateau State, which is in north-central Nigeria. The Ron languages have been significantly affected by the Tarok language.

Montgomery County is in the central part of Missouri, in the United States. In 2010, it had 12, 236 people. The county seat is Montgomery City. It was named after Richard Montgomery, a general in the American Revolutionary War who died in 1775. The county has a winery branch in New Florence and is part of the Missouri Rhineland. It is roughly halfway between Columbia and St. Louis.

Eric Peter Brewer, born on April 17, 1979, is a former Canadian professional ice hockey player who played defense. He played in the NHL for 16 seasons, ending his career with the Toronto Maple Leafs. Brewer was an NHL All-Star and an Olympic gold medalist. Brewer started his career as a top junior player. He was named to the WHL West Second All-Star Team and the Western Conference roster for the 1998 WHL All-Star Game, though he missed the game due to injury. He was drafted fifth overall by the New York Islanders in the 1997 NHL Entry Draft. Brewer played for several NHL teams: the Islanders, Oilers, Blues, Lightning, Ducks, and Maple Leafs. He also captained the Blues for two years. Additionally, he played for the Prince George Cougars in the WHL and the Lowell Lock Monsters in the AHL. In 1999, Brewer was selected for the Prince George Cougars' all-time team. He represented Canada in eight international events, winning three world championship gold medals and one World Cup of Hockey gold medal. He also won an Olympic gold medal at the 2002 Winter Olympics. For this achievement, he was inducted into the BC Sports Hall of Fame with his teammates in 2003.

The Creation Museum, in Petersburg, Kentucky, U.S., is run by Answers in Genesis (AIG), a Christian organization. It explains the start of the universe using a young Earth creationist view based on the Bible. The museum cost $27 million and opened on May 28, 2007, with money from private donations. Besides exhibits, it has a theater, a planetarium, a dinosaur skeleton, and an insect collection. The museum employs about 300 people, and workers must agree with AIG’s beliefs. It shows humans and dinosaurs together, says the Earth is about 6,000 years old, and questions evolution. Scientists and teachers say it presents a false view of science and might harm science education. People with other religious ideas about the Earth's history say it hurts Christianity. Many Americans still believe in young Earth creationism, making the museum popular. The museum is often talked about, with some saying its exhibits are not real museums because they lack connections to current knowledge.

Ștefan Tașnadi, also known as István Tasnádi in Hungarian, was born on March 21, 1953, and died on February 28, 2018. He was a Romanian heavyweight weightlifter. Tașnadi won a silver medal at the 1984 Olympics. He started lifting weights in 1970 at a sports school. From 1976 to 1984, he was part of the national team. He stopped competing in 1984 and became a weightlifting coach.
La ferrière is a commune in Vendée, which is in the Pays de la Loire region of western France.
This list includes dinosaurs found in North America. North America has many dinosaur fossils, with a lot of different kinds of dinosaurs.

Svenstavik is a small town in Berg municipality, Jämtland county, Sweden. It had 1,004 people living there in 2010. A road called European Route E45 goes through Svenstavik. County Road 321 (Länsväg 321) starts in Svenstavik and ends at Mattmar in Åre. A train line called Inland Line came to the area in the 1910s. Two train lines were built: Svenstavik to Brunflo in 1917, and Svenstavik to Åsarna in 1918.
