Alingsås VBK is a volleyball club in Alingsås, Sweden. It was founded on June 1, 1961. The club joined the Swedish Volleyball Federation on December 19 of the same year. Alingsås VBK won the Swedish Women's National Championship in 1971.

Koi... Mil Gayi is a 2003 Indian Hindi sci-fi movie. Rakesh Roshan directed it and it was the first in the Krrish series. The film came out on August 8, 2003, and stars HRKithik Roshan, Preity Zinta, and Rekha. It won the National Film Award for best film on other social issues. The movie was shown at film festivals in Jerusalem and Denmark. It also won awards like Best Picture and Best Director (Rakesh Roshan) and Best Actor (HRithik Roshan) at big Bollywood award ceremonies. The film led to two more movies in the Krrish series—Krrish and Krrish 3. It also had a kids' TV show called J Bole Toh Jadoo, which aired on Nickelodeon India. The movie’s story is similar to E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial and Satyajit Ray's The Alien. However, the director said Koi... Mil Gayi is not an Indian version of E.T., as the story is more like The Alien.

The Canary Islands, also called "the canaries," are a Spanish archipelago and part of Spain's southernmost autonomous community, located in the Atlantic Ocean, west of Morocco. It is one of eight regions recognized by the Spanish government for its historical nationality. The main islands, from largest to smallest, are Tenerife, Fuerteventura, Gran Canaria, Lanzarote, La Palma, La Gomera, El Hierro, and La Graciosa. The archipelago includes smaller islands and islets like Alegranza, Isla de Lobos, Monte Clara, Roque del Oeste, and Roque del Este, and some nearby rocks. The Canary Islands, the largest and most populated of Macaronesia, are often called "the fortunate isles" and are a major tourist destination with over 12 million visitors each year. They have a subtropical climate, with long hot summers and warm winters. The islands are famous for their beaches, especially in Maspalomas on Gran Canaria, and for Teide National Park and Mount Teide, a world heritage site. Mount Teide is the third tallest volcano in the world, measured from its base on the ocean floor. Historically, the Canary Islands were a bridge between Africa, North America, South America, and Europe. In 2019, the archipelago had 2,153,389 inhabitants, with the largest concentrations on Tenerife and Gran Canaria. The capital cities, Santa Cruz de Tenerife and Las Palmas de Gran Canaria, share the status of capital cities of the autonomous community. Las Palmas de Gran Canaria has been the largest city since 1768, except for a brief period in the 1910s. The city of San Cristóbal de La Laguna, also a world heritage site, is the third largest city on the islands. The Canary Islands were a key stop for Spanish galleons traveling to the Americas. Today, their high mountains are ideal for astronomy, hosting professional observatories on Tenerife and La Palma.

Yellowcake is a type of uranium powder. It is produced during the processing of uranium ores and is obtained after mining but before fuel production or enrichment. Yellowcake is made by extracting and refining uranium ore using different methods depending on the type of ore. It looks like a coarse powder, has a strong smell, does not dissolve in water, and contains about 80% uranium oxide, which melts at around 2880°C.

The Arctic National Wildlife Refuge (ANWR) is in northeastern Alaska, United States. It is the biggest national wildlife refuge in the country. ANWR is in the Alaska North Slope region and is a bit larger than the Yukon Delta National Wildlife Refuge. Offices manage it from Fairbanks. ANWR has many types of plants and animals, including polar bears, grizzly bears, black bears, moose, caribou, wolves, eagles, lynx, wolverines, martens, beavers, and migratory birds. Just across the border in Yukon, Canada, are two national parks called Ivavik and Vuntut.

The Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA) is a group that represents the music industry in the United States. It has record labels and distributors as members. These members make, produce, and distribute about 85% of the legally sold music in the United States. The RIAA's main office is in Washington, D.C. The RIAA was created in 1952. At first, it handled copyright fees, worked with trade unions, and studied the music industry and government rules. Early RIAA standards included the equalization curve, the format of stereophonic record grooves, and the sizes of 33 1/3, 45, and 78 rpm records. Now, the RIAA's main job includes spending over $6 million yearly on lobbying in the U.S. It also manages the use of music collectively and certifies gold and platinum albums and singles in the U.S.

deer island is an unincorporated community and census-designated place in columbia county, oregon, united states. The 2010 census showed 294 people lived there. It is near Columbia City, north-northwest along U.S. Route 30. Deer island has a post office with zip code 97054.

Muse, an English rock band, released their second studio album called "Origin of Symmetry" on June 18, 2001. The album's title and theme come from ideas in a book by physicist Michio Kaku. "Origin of Symmetry" was very successful in the UK. It reached number three on the UK album charts and was certified platinum by the British Phonographic Industry (BPI). Four singles were released from the album: "Plug in Baby," "New Born," "Bliss," and "Hyper Music" / "Feeling Good."
Craig is a town in Plymouth County, Iowa, United States. In 2010, it had 89 people. Craig became a town in Plymouth County on April 26, 1911.

Beam bridges, also called stringer bridges, are simple structures supported by an abutment or pier at each end. These bridges don't transfer moments at the supports, so they are called "simply supported." The simplest beam bridge might be a log, a wooden plank, or a stone laid across a stream. Modern bridges are usually made of steel or reinforced concrete, or a mix of both. Concrete parts may be reinforced, prestressed, or post-tensioned. These modern bridges include girder, plate girder, and box girder bridges, all types of beam bridges. They can be built with many beams side by side and a deck on top, or with main beams on each side supporting a deck between them. The main beams can be -beams, trusses, or box girders. They can be half-through or braced across the top to create a through bridge. Because no moments are transferred, these bridges can't handle the horizontal forces like arch bridges. This leads to innovative designs, such as lenticular trusses and bow string arches. Beam bridges can have multiple simply supported spans supported by piers, like in the Feiyunjiang Bridge in China. This is different from viaducts using continuous spans over the piers. Beam bridges are mostly used for short distances because they have no built-in supports. The only supports are provided by piers. The farther apart the supports, the weaker the bridge gets. As a result, beam bridges rarely span more than short distances. However, they can still be used to cross great distances by joining a series of beam bridges together, creating what is known as a continuous span.

Lupita Amondi Nyong'o (born March 1, 1983) is a Kenyan-Mexican actress and author. She was born in Mexico City, where her father, Kenyan politician Peter Anyang' Nyong'o, was teaching. After turning one, she moved to Kenya and grew up there. She studied film and theatre in the United States, getting a bachelor's degree from Hampshire College. Nyong'o started in Hollywood as a production assistant. In 2008, she acted in a short film called "East River." Later, she starred in the TV show "Shuga" from 2009 to 2012. That year, she also wrote, produced, and directed a documentary titled "In My Genes." In 2013, she had a big role as Patsey in the movie "12 Years a Slave." The movie was very good, and she won several awards, including an Academy Award for best supporting actress. She was the first Kenyan and Mexican actress to win an Academy Award. Nyong'o acted in the play "Eclipsed" on Broadway in 2015, where she was nominated for a Tony Award. She also voiced characters in "Star Wars" and "The Jungle Book." In 2018, she played Nakia in "Black Panther," and in 2019, she was in the movie "Us." Nyong'o cares about protecting historic places and fights against sexual harassment. She supports women's and animal rights. In 2014, she was chosen as the most beautiful woman by People magazine. She wrote a children's book called "Sulwe" in 2019, which became very popular. In the same year, she narrated a TV show called "Serengeti" for Discovery Channel and was nominated for an Emmy Award. In 2020, she was listed as one of Africa's 50 most powerful women by Forbes.

Carlo Caffarra was born on June 1, 1938, and passed away on September 6, 2017. He was an Italian priest in the Catholic Church. From 2003 to 2015, he was the Archbishop of Bologna. He retired in 2015. Before that, from 1981 to 1995, he was the president of the Pontifical John Paul II Institute for Studies on Marriage and Family. From 1995 to 2003, he was the Archbishop of Ferrara-Comacchio. Pope Benedict XVI made him a cardinal in 2006.
Rachel Marilyn Lloyd (born Laird) was an American politician and businesswoman. She served in the United States House of Representatives from 1975 to 1995.

Mallemort is a small town in the Bouches-du-Rhône department, in southern France. It is near the Durance River, south of the Luberon Mountains. Mallemort is not on a major highway to the south or to Marseille. However, it is close to Arles, Saint-Rémy, and Salon-de-Provence.

James Stephen Fossett, born on April 22, 1944, and died on September 3, 2007, was an American businessman and adventurer. He set many records in flying solo around the world in a balloon and a fixed-wing aircraft. Fossett earned a lot of money in financial services. He held records for five nonstop trips around the world: as a solo balloonist, sailor, and pilot in a fixed-wing aircraft. He was a member of the Royal Geographical Society and the Explorers Club. Fossett set over 100 records in different sports, with 60 still standing at his death. He broke three of seven absolute world records for fixed-wing aircraft. In 2002, he received the Gold Medal from the Royal Aero Club of the UK. He was inducted into the National Aviation Hall of Fame in 2007. On September 3, 2007, Fossett went missing while flying a small plane in the desert between Nevada and California. Search efforts found nothing, and he was declared dead in February 2008. In September 2008, someone found Fossett’s identification cards in the Sierra Nevada mountains in California. This led to finding the plane wreckage. Only two large bones, probably from Fossett, were found near the crash site, likely scattered by animals.

Charlie Countryman is a 2013 American-Romanian romantic drama film. Fredrik Bond directed it, which was his first time. Matt Drake wrote it. Shia LaBeouf, Evan Rachel Wood, and Mads Mikkelsen acted in it. The film first showed at the 2013 Sundance Film Festival on January 21. It was also shown at the 63rd Berlin International Film Festival. In the U.S., it came out on November 15, 2013. In the U.K., it was released on October 31, 2014.
Termen is a town in the Brig district of the Valais canton in Switzerland.

Happy Valley Shanghai is an amusement park in Shanghai, China. It is in Songjiang District and is about from the city center. The park covers an area of. It opened on August 16, 2009, and is the fourth park in the Happy Valley chain.

The 2003 Pacific hurricane season was the first since 1977 without any major hurricanes. It had many tropical storms that affected Mexico. Two of the most notable were Hurricanes Ignacio and Marty. Ignacio caused 2 deaths and Marty, 12. These storms together cost about $1 billion in damage. Three other Pacific storms, two hurricanes, and three Atlantic storms also hit Mexico directly. The only other significant storm was Hurricane Jimena, which passed near Hawaii, the first storm to threaten Hawaii in several years. The season began on May 15, 2003, in the eastern Pacific and on June 1, 2003, in the central Pacific, ending on November 30, 2003. On average, 16 tropical storms and 7 hurricanes form in this area each year. The total damage was $129 million, and 23 people died from the storms.

A trauma center, or trauma centre, is a hospital ready to treat people who have serious injuries, like falling, car accidents, or gunshot wounds. Sometimes, a trauma center just means an emergency room that can handle basic care but doesn’t have special services for serious injuries. In the United States, a hospital can become a trauma center if it meets rules set by the American College of Surgeons and passes a checkup. Whether a hospital gets this title depends on the state’s laws. Trauma centers are grouped into levels: Level I is the best, and Level III is the least advanced. Some states have more levels, with Level V being the lowest. Level I trauma centers have specialists in many areas, including surgery, critical care, and imaging. Lower levels can only handle basic care and might need to transfer patients to a better hospital. Running a trauma center costs a lot, especially in rural areas. Patient traffic can vary a lot because emergencies can happen anytime. Different ways are used to deal with this variability. Trauma centers often have special landing pads for helicopters. People in remote areas can get quicker and better care when flown to a trauma center instead of going by ambulance to a closer hospital. The level of trauma care can greatly affect how well a patient recovers.

Panphagia is a genus of dinosaur that lived about 231 million years ago during the Carnian age of the Late Triassic period. It was found in northwestern Argentina. The fossils were discovered in the La Peña member of the Ischigualasto formation. The name "Panphagia" means "all eating" in Greek, suggesting it ate different things. Panphagia is one of the earliest known dinosaurs and shows early sauropodomorphs might have eaten both plants and animals.

Harry Gulkin was born on November 14, 1927, and passed away on July 23, 2018. He was from Montreal, Quebec, and worked in film and theatre. His job titles included producer, arts director, and project manager. Mr. Gulkin produced a film called "Lies My Father Told Me," which won a Golden Globe award.

Stewart-Haas Racing is an American professional stock car racing team. It currently competes in NASCAR's Cup Series, Xfinity Series, K & N Pro Series West, and Coca-Cola iRacing Series. The team is owned by Tony Stewart, a three-time Cup Series champion, and Gene Haas, who founded Haas Automation. It was started in 2002 as Haas CNC Racing. In 2009, Stewart, who had been racing for Joe Gibbs Racing, joined Stewart-Haas Racing and got a 50% stake in the team. The team is based in Kannapolis, North Carolina, near Charlotte Motor Speedway. It has a sister team, the Haas F1 Team, but they are separate for legal reasons. In the Cup Series, Stewart-Haas Racing uses four Ford Mustang GT cars: one driven by Kevin Harvick, another by Aric Almirola, one by Clint Bowyer, and one by Cole Custer. In the Xfinity Series, they use one full-time Ford Mustang driven by Chase Briscoe. In the K & N Pro Series West, they use a part-time Ford Mustang driven by Aric Almirola. The Xfinity team works with Biagi-DenBeste Racing. From the start until 2016, the team used Chevrolet engines and chassis from Hendrick Motorsports. Starting in 2017, they began using Roush-Yates engines and Ford chassis, building them themselves. Stewart-Haas Racing has won in all three national touring divisions, joining Hendrick Motorsports, Richard Childress Racing, Joe Gibbs Racing, and Roush Fenway Racing as the only teams to do so.
Bernard Greenhouse was born on January 3, 1916, and passed away on May 13, 2011. He was an American cellist. He was also one of the people who started the Beaux Arts Trio.

sridevi (Sridevi came in) is a Tamil drama. The actors are Ananya, Nandhan Loganadhan, Lasya Nagraj, Meera Krishnan, and Devi Priya. It is a remake of a Kannada show called Lakshmi Baramma. The show replaced Enga VeeTU Mapillai and was on Colors Tamil from April 18, 2018, to June 28, 2019.

Ryan Zinke was born on November 1, 1961. He is an American politician and businessman. From 2015 to 2017, he was a U.S. representative for Montana. Before that, from 2009 to 2013, he served as a senator in Montana. Zinke played football in college at the University of Oregon and studied geology, business, and leadership. He worked as a U.S. Navy SEAL from 1986 to 2008, retiring as a commander. Zinke supported using ground troops in the Middle East and opposed some health and environmental rules. He was chosen by President Donald Trump to be the U.S. Secretary of the Interior in 2017. In this job, he made more land available for oil, gas, and mineral work. Some people thought his spending was not right. In 2018, he faced more problems. Trump said Zinke would leave his job on January 2, 2019, and his assistant would take over.
Congo confirmed the arrival of COVID-19 in March 2020.

Ingrid of Sweden, born on March 28, 1910, and died on November 7, 2000, was the queen of Denmark from 1947 to 1972. She was married to Crown Prince Frederick of Denmark and they had three daughters: Margrethe, the current queen of Denmark; Benedikte, who is now a princess of Sayn-Wittgenstein-Berleburg; and Anne-Marie, who was the Greek queen. In 1947, her husband became King Frederick IX after his father died. As queen, Ingrid changed the court life by making it less formal and more relaxed. King Frederick IX passed away in 1972, and their daughter Margrethe became the new queen. Ingrid was also the aunt of King Carl XVI Gustaf of Sweden.

Hillside Lake is a small community in Dutchess County, New York. The population was 1,084 in the 2010 census. It is in the Poughkeepsie–Newburgh–Middletown, NY metropolitan area and also part of the larger New York–Newark–Bridgeport, NY-NJ-CT-PA combined statistical area.

Also known as the great wave or simply the wave, it is a woodblock print by the Japanese artist Hokusai. Published between 1829 and 1833, it is the first print in Hokusai's series "Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji." This is Hokusai's most famous work and one of the most recognizable pieces of Japanese art. The image shows a huge wave threatening three boats off the coast in Sagami Bay, with Mount Fuji in the background. It is often thought to be a tsunami, but it is more likely a large rogue wave. Like the other prints in the series, it shows the area around Mount Fuji under different conditions. The series uses a lot of blue pigment.

Owls are birds from the order strigiformes. There are over 200 species, mostly live alone and are active at night. They have a big head, sharp claws, and special feathers for silent flying. Exceptions are the northern hawk-owl, which is active during the day, and the burrowing owl, which lives in groups. Owls mainly eat small animals like mammals, insects, and other birds. Some species hunt fish. You can find them almost everywhere except in very cold areas and some remote islands. Owls are grouped into two families: the true owl family (Strigidae) and the barn-owl family (Tytonidae). A group of owls is called a "parliament."

Kenneth Gary Albert, born on February 2, 1968, is an American sportscaster. He is the son of sportscaster Marv Albert and the nephew of sportscasters Al Albert and Steve Albert. Kenneth is special because he does the play-by-play for all four major professional sports leagues in the U.S. and Canada: the NFL, NBA, MLB, and NHL.

Chattanooga was a pop group made up of three sisters named Mia, Ackie, and Clara Kempff from Halmstad, Sweden. They had some success in the early 1980s. In 1982, they performed the song "Hallå Hela Pressen" at Melodifestivalen and placed 4th. In 2004, the sisters reunited to record the song again with Nina & Kim.

The Malagasy Wikipedia is a version in the Malagasy language of Wikipedia. It started in April 2004. Currently, it has many articles, ranking as the 63rd largest Wikipedia by the number of articles. There are 3 administrators, 13,671 registered users, and 25 active users.
The 970s decade started on January 1, 970, and ended on December 31, 979.

A record chart, also known as a music chart, ranks songs based on certain criteria over a period. Various criteria are used in global charts, often together. These include sales, radio play, downloads, and streaming. Some charts focus on specific music types, while most cover a particular area. Most charts update weekly, printed or broadcast at the end of the week. Yearly and decade-long charts are made from weekly charts. Weekly charts help measure song success. Running down a music chart is a common format in radio and TV shows.
Jan Kobuszewski is a person's name.

Blackjack Mulligan, whose real name was Robert Deroy Windham, was born on November 25, 1942, and passed away on April 7, 2016. He was a professional wrestler, author, and former American football player. People knew him by his ring name, Blackjack Mulligan. He had two wrestling sons named Barry and Kendall Windham. His daughter-in-law was Mike Rotunda. He was also the grandfather of wrestlers Bray Wyatt and Bo Dallas.
Sidney Haight was born on August 21, 1847, and died on September 17, 1918. He received the Medal of Honor during the American Civil War for his actions during the Siege of Petersburg.

Antonio T. Brown Sr., born July 10, 1988, is an American football wide receiver and free agent. He grew up in Liberty City, Miami, and played football and track at Miami Norland High School. Brown went to Central Michigan University for college, where he was an all-American as a punt returner in 2008 and 2009. Selected by the Pittsburgh Steelers in the sixth round, Brown set a record in his rookie season from 2010 to 2018 by having more receptions than any other player in the league. During his first season with the Steelers, the team reached Super Bowl XLV but lost. That year, he had 16 receptions for 167 yards in ten games. In his second NFL season, Brown became the first player to get over 1,000 yards in both receiving and punting in the same year. He was chosen for the 2012 Pro Bowl as a punt returner. In 2013, he was the only receiver to record at least 50 yards in every game. Despite his productivity, his relationship with the Steelers, especially quarterback Ben Roethlisberger, became bad, and he asked for a trade. In 2019, Brown was traded to the Oakland Raiders, becoming the highest-paid receiver in the league. However, his time there was brief. After some off-field issues, including a conflict with the general manager, he was released without playing a regular-season game. Brown then joined the New England Patriots but was cut after just one game. At the time, the NFL was looking into sexual assault claims against him.

Jan Hus, also known as John Hus or Johannes Huss, lived from around 1369 to July 6, 1415. He was a Czech theologian and philosopher who wanted to reform the church. Hus's ideas helped lead to Protestantism and were important for the Bohemian Reformation. He was seen as the second church reformer after John Wycliffe, as he lived before Martin Luther, Calvin, and Zwingli. Born poor in Husinec, Bohemia, Hus became a priest to escape poverty. He studied and worked in Prague, where he preached and criticized the Catholic Church. He opposed the Church's views on many topics, such as the Eucharist and simony. When Pope Alexander V sided with the Bohemian church authorities against Hus and his followers, he excommunicated Hus, but this was not enforced. Later, Hus criticized Pope John XXIII for selling indulgences, leading to his excommunication and two years in exile. Called to the Council of Constance, Hus was arrested and imprisoned. After being asked to change his views, he refused, saying he would not give up his beliefs even for gold. He was executed by burning on July 6, 1415, for heresy. After Hus's death, his followers, known as Hussites, refused to choose a Catholic monarch. They defeated five papal crusades between 1420 and 1431, in what became known as the Hussite Wars. The Bohemian and Moravian populations stayed mostly Hussite until the 1620s. Then, following the Battle of the White Mountain, the lands of the Bohemian Crown came under Habsburg rule, leading to forced conversion back to Catholicism.
Browning is a village in Schuyler County, Illinois, United States. In the year 2000, the number of people living there was 130.

Megaraptor, meaning "giant thief," is a type of large dinosaur from the late Cretaceous period. Its fossils were found in Argentina. At first, scientists thought it was a large dromaeosaur-like coelurosaur. Later, it was classified as a neovenatorid allosauroid. However, more recent studies and findings of related dinosaurs suggest that Megaraptor might be either a basal tyrannosauroid or a basal coelurosaur.
Los Osos is a place near the Pacific Ocean in San Luis Obispo County, California. It uses zip codes 93402 and 93412 and area code 805. In 2010, the population was 14,276 people.
Most of the 35 streams are small and don't last all year. They get water from melting snow until late April. Some streams only flow in winter and dry up during the summer.

The Arc de Triomphe de l'Etoile is a famous monument in Paris, France. It is at the end of the Champs-Elysées, in the middle of Place Charles de Gaulle, which used to be called Place de l'Etoile. The Arc stands at the center of 12 roads that spread out from it. The monument is shared by three parts of Paris: the 16th, 17th, and 8th districts. The Arc de Triomphe honors soldiers who fought and died in the French Revolutionary and Napoleonic Wars. It has the names of victories and generals on its inside and outside. There is also a tomb for an unknown World War I soldier under its arch. The Arc de Triomphe is part of the "Historic Axis," a route that starts from the Louvre and goes to Grande Arche de la Défense. Jean Chalgrin designed it in 1806. Its design shows young French men without clothes fighting against bearded German warriors wearing chain mail. The Arc de Triomphe is very tall, about 50 meters high and 45 meters wide. It has a large arch that is 25 meters high and 20 meters wide. Three weeks after the big parade in 1919, a pilot flew his plane under the main arch, and it was recorded on film. Before the Monumento a la Revolución in Mexico City was built in 1938, the Arc de Triomphe was the tallest triumphal arch. In Pyongyang, North Korea, there is a similar Arch of Triumph, which is slightly taller. Near Paris, there is a very tall structure called La Grande Arche, but it is not called an Arc de Triomphe.
founex is a town in the Nyon district of the Vaud canton in Switzerland.
A carapace is the upper part of the hard outer shell in animals like crustaceans, arachnids, and turtles. In turtles and tortoises, the bottom part is called the plastron.

Amite County is in Mississippi, near Louisiana. In 2010, it had 13, 131 people. The main town is Liberty. The county is named after the Amite River, which goes through it. Amite County is also part of the McComb, MS area.

The Whopper is Burger King's signature sandwich and a popular product. It has been sold since 1957. Over time, the sandwich has changed, with new sizes and bread types. Burger King calls itself "the home of the Whopper." The Whopper is very important for Burger King's business. Other fast food restaurants try to make similar sandwiches to compete. Burger King offers different Whopper versions for different seasons and local tastes. They sometimes create special limited-time Whoppers for promotions. The Whopper is often used in Burger King's advertising and jokes. The company has many trademarks to protect the Whopper.

IBK Sundsvall was a floorball club in Sundsvall, Sweden. It started in 1986. The men's team played in Sweden's top floorball league in the 1990s. In 2006, the club joined with IBK Nordic, becoming Sundsvall City. In 1991, the club also played soccer in Division 6 for men.

Vanzone con San Carlo is a "municipality" in the province of Verbano-Cusio-Ossola in Piedmont, Italy. It is located northeast of Turin and west of Verbania. Vanzone con San Carlo borders these municipalities: Antrona, Schieranco, Bannio Anzino, Calasca-Castiglione, Ceppo Morelli.

Giuseppina Bozzacchi was born on November 23, 1853, in Milan. She was an Italian ballerina who, at 16, created the role of Swanhilda in Léo Delibes' ballet "Coppélia" for the Paris Opera Ballet. Bozzacchi came to Paris to study with Mme Dominique. The choreographer Arthur Saint-Léon and the director Émile Perrin were looking for a suitable Swanhilda. They had chosen neither Léontine Beaugrand nor Angelina Fioretti. Saint-Léon had started to prepare the role for a favorite ballerina but she fell ill. In 1869, they asked Léo Delibes to find a Swanhilda. He returned without a suitable candidate. Saint-Léon and Perrin then found 16-year-old Bozzacchi. She performed Swanhilda for the first time on May 25, 1870, in front of Emperor Napoleon III. She danced the role several times in the following weeks. In July, France declared war on Prussia. Bozzacchi danced Swanhilda for the last time on August 31, when the Paris Opera closed during the Franco-Prussian War. She was weak from lack of food and became ill. She contracted smallpox and fever and died on her 17th birthday in the morning. She was buried in the Cimetière de Montmartre in Paris.

Dark Souls is an action role-playing game made by FromSoftware and released by Namco Bandai Games in 2011. It follows the story of FromSoftware's "Demon's Souls" and is the second game in the "Souls" series. The game is set in a fictional kingdom called Lordran, where players control a cursed undead character who starts a journey to learn about their fate. A Windows version came out in August 2012, adding extra content not in the original versions for PlayStation 3 and Xbox 360. In October 2012, this new content was made available for consoles as "Artorias of the Abyss." Critics praised Dark Souls for its challenging combat, detailed levels, and interesting descriptions. However, its difficulty was criticized by some for being too hard. The Windows version faced some technical problems. By April 2013, it had sold more than two million copies worldwide. Two sequels were released in the middle of the 2010s, and a remastered version came out in 2018.

Three 6 Mafia is an American hip hop group from Memphis, Tennessee. They formed in 1991. Initially, they were an underground rap group with a horror theme. Later, they gained mainstream success. Their first album, "Mystic Stylez," came out in 1995 and became a popular, influential album. They have released music on independent labels like Prophet Entertainment and their own label, Hypnotize Minds, as well as on Relativity, Loud, and Columbia Records. Two of their albums, "The Boomin' Hell" (2000) and "Most Known Unknown" (2005), were certified platinum by the RIAA. The latter album included their hit song "Stay Fly." In 2006, they won an Academy Award for the best original song for "It's Hard Out Here for a Pimp" from the movie "Hustle & Flow." Their latest studio album, "Last 2 Walk," was released in 2008. As of 2016, their worldwide album sales reached 5.5 million.

Lewis Michael Eisenberg, born on October 12, 1942, is an American financier and investor. He became the United States Ambassador to Italy. Eisenberg co-founded and led a private equity firm called Granite Capital International Group. He has been involved in American political fundraising for many years and held several important positions, including being the chairman of the Port Authority of New York and New Jersey when the World Trade Center was attacked on September 11, 2001. In July 2017, President Donald Trump nominated Eisenberg to be the United States Ambassador to Italy. The U.S. Senate confirmed him in August 2017.

Kublai was the fifth leader of the Mongol Empire, ruling from 1260 to 1294. He was also the first emperor of the Yuan Dynasty in China, which he founded in 1271. Kublai was the fourth son of Tolui and a grandson of Genghis Khan. He became leader after his older brother Möngke in 1260 and had to fight his younger brother Ariq Böke in a civil war from 1260 to 1264. This war showed the beginning of the empire's division. Kublai had real power mainly in China and Mongolia, but still had some influence over other parts of the empire. His rule extended from the Pacific to the Black Sea, and from Siberia to Afghanistan. In 1271, Kublai created the Yuan Dynasty, which ruled over Mongolia, China, Korea, and nearby areas. He became the first non-Han person to rule all of China after defeating the Song Dynasty in 1279. Kublai's portrait, part of a collection of Yuan emperors, is now at the National Palace Museum in Taipei. The color white, Kublai's royal color, was the imperial color of the Yuan Dynasty.
Lisa Latrelle Blunt Rochester (née Blunt; born February 10, 1962) is an American politician. She has been a U.S. representative since 2017. She belongs to the Democratic Party.

The 2003 invasion of Iraq began on March 19, 2003, with air attacks and continued on March 20 with ground troops. This lasted about one month, including 26 days of major fighting. About 177,194 soldiers from the United States, the United Kingdom, Australia, and Poland invaded Iraq. On May 1, 2003, U.S. President George W. Bush declared an end to major combat operations. The Coalition Provisional Authority then took control, leading to the first Iraqi parliamentary election in January 2005. U.S. forces stayed in Iraq until 2011. During the initial invasion, 130,000 U.S. troops and about 45,000 British soldiers, 2,000 Australian soldiers, and 194 Polish soldiers joined. Other countries provided support. About 100,000 U.S. troops gathered in Kuwait by February 18. The Peshmerga, Kurdish fighters, also supported the coalition. U.S. President Bush and UK Prime Minister Blair said the goal was to disarm Iraq of weapons of mass destruction, stop Saddam Hussein's support for terrorism, and free the Iraqi people. Some saw the September 11 attacks as a key factor. A January 2003 CBS poll showed 64% of Americans approved of military action against Iraq, but 63% preferred a diplomatic solution, and 62% believed the threat of terrorism would increase. Some long-term U.S. allies, including France, Canada, Germany, and New Zealand, opposed the invasion. They said there was no evidence of weapons of mass destruction, and invading was unjustified according to UN reports. Before the invasion, there were protests worldwide. A rally in Rome had about 3 million people. Between January and April 2003, 36 million people across the globe participated in almost 3,000 anti-war protests. The invasion started with airstrikes on Baghdad on March 20, and a land attack into Basra province. Special forces secured Basra and nearby oil fields. Main forces advanced into southern Iraq and engaged in the Battle of Nasiriyah on March 23. Air strikes and attacks on command centers caused confusion in the Iraqi army. On March 26, 173rd Airborne troops were dropped near Kirkuk. They joined Kurdish rebels and secured the north. Main forces moved into Iraq's heart and faced little resistance. By April 9, most of Iraq's military was defeated, and Baghdad was occupied. Kirkuk was captured on April 10, and Tikrit on April 15. Saddam Hussein and his leaders went into hiding. On May 1, President Bush declared an end to major combat operations, ending the invasion and starting the occupation period.

The South African Republic, also known as Transvaal, was an independent state from 1852 to 1902. It was in the area that is now South Africa. In the First Boer War, it defeated the British. The Republic stayed independent until May 31, 1902, when it surrendered to Britain. Over 27,000 civilians died because of a British scorched earth policy and concentration camps. After the war, the area became the Transvaal Colony. During World War I, there was a rebellion to revive the Republic. The land that used to be the South African Republic now includes parts of Gauteng, Limpopo, Mpumalanga, and North West provinces in northeastern South Africa.
Farid Abedi was born on August 28, 1977, in Firouzabad. He is an Iranian football player. Currently, he plays for Bargh Shiraz in the Azadegan League.
Italy has participated in all Military World Games since the first edition in 1995.

A euphemism is a mild word or phrase used instead of one that might be upsetting or suggest something unpleasant. Some are used to be funny, while others use simple, non-offensive terms to make something less important. Euphemisms can hide swear words or talk about sensitive subjects like disabilities, sex, going to the bathroom, or death in a polite way.

The flag of Saint Lucia has a blue background with a yellow triangle in front of a black triangle with white edges. It replaced the British blue ensign with the colony's arms in 1967. Saint Lucia used this flag after becoming an associated state of the United Kingdom in 1967. While the design stayed the same, some parts were changed over time.

College Station is a city in Brazos County, Texas. It is located in east-central Texas, in the Brazos Valley, near the center of the Texas Triangle. College Station is northwest of Houston and northeast of Austin. In 2010, it had about 93,857 people, and by 2019, its population grew to around 117,911. College Station and Bryan together form the Bryan-College Station area, which has about 273,101 people in 2019. College Station is where Texas A&M University is located. The city's name comes from the university being on a railroad. Texas A&M does research in many areas, and it gets money from NASA, the National Institutes of Health, and other groups. Because of the university, College Station was named the most educated city in Texas by Money magazine in 2006, and the 11th most educated city in the United States.
Giornico is a town in the Leventina district, which is in Ticino, a canton in Switzerland.

The governor of Vermont is the leader of Vermont's government. The person in this job is chosen by people voting directly every two years in even-numbered years. Vermont and New Hampshire are the only states that have gubernatorial elections every two years, unlike the other 48 states which do it every four years. There is no limit on how many terms a Vermont governor can serve. If no candidate gets more than half the votes in an election, the state legislature selects the governor. The current governor of Vermont is Phil Scott, a Republican. He started his term on January 5, 2017, becoming Vermont's 82nd governor.

Eino Tamberg was born on May 27, 1930, and passed away on December 24, 2010. He was an Estonian composer whose music is performed around the world. He wrote operas like "Cyrano de Bergerac," four symphonies, and several concertos. Tamberg taught composition at the Estonian Academy of Music for many years.
Jefferson County is the name of 26 counties and one parish in the United States.

An editorial, a leading article in the United States or a leader in the United Kingdom, is a written opinion piece by the senior editors or publisher of a newspaper, magazine, or other written material, often without a name. In Australian and major U.S. newspapers like The New York Times and The Boston Globe, editorials are usually found under the "opinion" section. Sometimes, these editorials are illustrated with cartoons. Editorials discuss important issues and are published on the editorial page. This page also includes letters from readers. The opposite page is called the op-ed page, featuring opinions by writers not connected to the publication. Occasionally, a newspaper might place an editorial on the front page, especially for very important topics. In some European countries like Denmark, Spain, Italy, and France, this happens more frequently. Newspapers sometimes publish editorials without naming the author to encourage discussion on the issue. However, the newspaper editor still holds responsibility. When New Zealand's The Press, based in Christchurch, changed from a broadsheet to a compact format in 2018, they published a list of editorials showing changes in their views over 157 years. An example was their editorial on women's suffrage in New Zealand, where they previously said women would prefer staying at home instead of voting. In fashion magazines, the term "editorial" refers to feature articles with full-page photos on a specific theme, designer, model, or other single topic, often without accompanying text.
Blingel is a commune in the Pas-de-Calais department, which is in the Hauts-de-France region of northern France.

The Citadel Center is a 580 feet tall skyscraper in Chicago. It is on 131 South Dearborn Street, Chicago, Illinois. The building was designed by Ricardo Bofill, a Spanish architect. As of fall 2018, it was the 57th tallest building in Chicago, soon to become the 60th. It was completed in 2003 and has 37 floors above ground and 3 below, making a total of 40 floors. It covers 1,536,548 square feet and was certified as LEED Gold in 2017. In the lobby, there was a special sculpture of the Winged Victory of Samothrace, a famous world sculpture, which was removed in late 2018. The original is at the Louvre Museum. The lobby used to have a curved wall made of red wood. The Citadel Center was the first building in Chicago to use a raised-floor pressurized plenum system, which allowed for better temperature control.

Balaguer is the capital of the Noguera comarca in the province of Lleida, Catalonia, Spain. It is near the Segre River, which flows into the Ebro. The town has an area called an exclave to its east. Balaguer became the capital after being taken from the Moors by Count Ermengol VI of Urgell in 1106. It remained the capital for later counts of Urgell. The town has a Gothic bridge called Pont de Sant Miquel over the Segre River. This bridge was destroyed during the Spanish Civil War in 1938, but was rebuilt after the war. There is also a Gothic Santa Maria Church on a hill above the city. The church is near a well-preserved 15th-century wall. The historic part of the town is on the right bank of the Segre River. After the Spanish Civil War, construction began on a modern bridge. This led to the development of a new part of the town on the left bank. During the Spanish Civil War, General Franco's forces entered Catalonia through Balaguer's bridgehead in 1938.

Luke Isaac Moore was born on February 13, 1986. He is an English former professional football player who played as a striker. Moore played for England's U21 team. He is the younger brother of Stefan Moore, who was also a professional footballer.

Percy Bysshe Shelley (born August 4, 1792, died July 8, 1822) was a major English Romantic poet, often considered one of the best lyric and philosophical poets in the English language. His poetry and political views were radical. He gained recognition after his death. Shelley was part of a close group of visionary poets and writers, including Lord Byron, John Keats, Leigh Hunt, Thomas Love Peacock, and his second wife, Mary Shelley (who wrote "Frankenstein"). He is famous for poems like "Ozymandias," "Ode to the West Wind," "To a Skylark," "Music, When Soft Voices Die," "The Cloud," and "The Masque of Anarchy." Other major works include the drama "The Cenci" (1819), and longer, visionary poems such as "Queen Mab" (later called "The Daemon of the World"), "Alastor," "The Revolt of Islam," "Adonais," "Prometheus Unbound" (1820), "Hellas: A Lyrical Drama" (1821), and "The Triumph of Life" (1822). Shelley's close friends included important thinkers like his father-in-law, the philosopher William Godwin, and Leigh Hunt. Most publishers refused his work for fear of legal troubles. His poetry was sometimes only read by a few people during his time, but his achievements are now widely recognized. His ideas influenced Karl Marx, Leo Tolstoy, and Martin Luther King Jr. Many poets, like Robert Browning and Dante Gabriel Rossetti, were inspired by Shelley. He was admired by famous people such as Oscar Wilde, Thomas Hardy, and George Bernard Shaw. His writings on nonviolence influenced Henry David Thoreau. Shelley's influence on poetry continues today.
Saint-Jean-sur-Erve was a village in the Mayenne department of northwest France. On January 1, 2017, it became part of a new village called Blandouet-Saint-Jean.

The Flint River is a river in Georgia, the U.S. state. It flows from the western part of Georgia, south from the upper Piedmont region near Atlanta, to the wetlands in the southwestern corner of the state. Along with the Apalachicola and Chattahoochee rivers, it makes up the ACF basin. In the upper part, through the Red Hills of the Piedmont, the river is particularly scenic, running freely for many miles. Historically, it was also known as the Thronateeska River.

Sound drowned is a UK-based music website. It is funded by Silentway, an artist management company. The site was created by editor Sean Adams. It includes reviews, news, interviews, and discussion forums.

hydrography studies the physical features of oceans, seas, coastal areas, lakes, and rivers. It also predicts how these features change over time. The main goal is to ensure safe navigation. It supports other marine activities like economic development, security, defense, scientific research, and environmental protection.
lay-lamidou is a commune in France. It is located in the Pyrénées-Atlantiques department, in southwestern France.

The Amu Darya, also known as the Amu, Amo River, or Amudaryo, is a significant river in Central Asia and Afghanistan. It starts in the Pamir Mountains, north of the Hindu Kush. The Amu Darya is formed by the joining of the Vakhsh and Panj rivers. They meet in the Tigrovaya Balka nature reserve, on the border between Afghanistan and Tajikistan. The river then flows northwest into the southern part of the Aral Sea. In its upper course, the river borders Afghanistan to the north with Tajikistan, Uzbekistan, and Turkmenistan. Historically, the Amu Darya was seen as the boundary between greater Iran and Turan, an area roughly corresponding to present-day central Asia.

Tanuja Samarth, known as Tanuja, is an Indian actress who works mainly in Hindi films. She is part of the Mukherjee-Samarth family and is the daughter of actress Shobhna Samarth and producer Kumarsen Samarth. Tanuja was married to filmmaker Shomu Mukherjee, and they have two daughters, actresses Kajol and Tanisha. Tanuja received two Filmfare Awards. She is famous for her roles in movies like "Memdidi" (1961), "Chand Aur Suraj" (1965), "Baharen Phir Bhi Aayengi" (1966), "Jewel Thief" (1967), "Nai Roshni" (1967), "Jeene Ki Raah" (1969), "Haathi Mere Saathi" (1971), "Anubhav" (1971), "Mere Jeevan Saathi" (1972), and "Do Chor" (1972). Her acting with actors Sanjeev Kumar, Rajesh Khanna, and Dharmendra was popular in the late 1960s and early 1970s.
The 20th century BC lasted from 2000 BC to 1901 BC.
Rebergues is a town in the Pas-de-Calais department, which is in the Hauts-de-France region of France.

A structure is an arrangement and organization of connected parts in an object or system. It can be a man-made object like a building or a machine, or a natural object like a living thing, a mineral, or a chemical. Structures can also be abstract ideas like computer data or musical forms. Structures can have different types. One type is a hierarchy, where parts are connected in a top-down way. Another type is a network, where parts connect to many others. The last type is a lattice, where parts connect to nearby neighbors.

Hipparchus of Nicaea was a Greek astronomer, geographer, and mathematician. He is known for creating trigonometry and discovering the precession of the equinoxes. Hipparchus was born in Nicaea, which is now in Turkey, and likely died on the island of Rhodes in Greece. He worked as an astronomer from 162 to 127 BCE. Hipparchus is considered one of the greatest ancient astronomers. He used observations and techniques from Babylonians and other ancient astronomers like Meton of Athens, Timocharis, and Eratosthenes to develop models for the sun and moon's movements. He created trigonometric tables and solved problems in spherical trigonometry. He might have been the first to predict solar eclipses accurately. Other achievements include the first comprehensive star catalog and possibly inventing the astrolabe and armillary sphere.

Visibility measures how far you can see an object or light clearly. It is shown in weather reports, both in meters and statute miles. Visibility affects traffic on roads, sailing, and aviation. Meteorological visibility means how clear the air is. At night, visibility is the same as during the day, depending on the air quality.
The Royal Museums of Fine Arts of Belgium are in Brussels, Belgium. They have over 20,000 drawings, sculptures, and paintings from the early 15th century to now.

Cara McCollum was born on February 6, 1992, and passed away on February 22, 2016. She was an American journalist. Cara was the lead news anchor for "SNJ Today," starting her role in July 2015. She was also Miss New Jersey 2013 and competed in the Miss America 2014 pageant.

On November 14, 2017, some parts of the Zimbabwe Defence Forces (ZDF) gathered in Harare, the capital of Zimbabwe. They took control of the Zimbabwe Broadcasting Corporation and some important areas of the city. The next day, the ZDF said they were not trying to take over the government and that President Mugabe was safe. They said they would return things to normal after dealing with people around Mugabe who they thought were responsible for Zimbabwe's problems. The ZDF's actions happened because there were disagreements in Mugabe's ruling party, ZANU-PF. Former First Vice President Emmerson Mnangagwa, who the ZDF supported, was fighting with First Lady Grace Mugabe, who had the support of the younger ZANU-PF group, about who would take over as president. After Mnangagwa was fired and had to leave the country, the ZDF chief, Constantino Chiwenga, said that removing high-ranking ZANU-PF officials had to stop. On November 19, ZANU-PF removed Mugabe as party leader and chose Mnangagwa to take his place. They told Mugabe to resign as president by November 20 or face being removed from office. Mugabe did not resign, so on November 21, a special meeting in parliament decided to remove him. Mugabe then wrote a letter to the parliament, saying he was resigning. Phelekezela Mphoko, the Second Vice President, became the acting president. Mnangagwa was made president on November 24, 2017.

Diomedes, or Diomede, is a hero from Greek mythology known for fighting in the Trojan War. He was born to Tydeus and Deipyle. Later, he became the king of Argos, succeeding his maternal grandfather, Adrastus. In Homer's "Iliad," Diomedes is seen as one of the best warriors, alongside Ajax the Great and Agamemnon, after Achilles. This is especially clear in Book 7, where he, Ajax the Greater, and Agamemnon are the most chosen to fight Hector out of nine volunteers. After the war, Diomedes founded several Italian cities. After his death, he was worshipped as a god under different names in Italy and Greece.

Charles Henry Scherza was born on February 15, 1923, in Brandon, Manitoba. He played ice hockey professionally for 11 seasons in the American Hockey League. In 1949, he won a Calder Cup championship with the Providence Reds. Scherza passed away on March 16, 2014, at the age of 91.

electromagnetic hypersensitivity ( ehs ) is a claimed sensitivity to electromagnetic fields , to which negative symptoms are attributed . ehs has no scientific basis and is not a recognised medical diagnosis . claims are characterized by a `` variety of non-specific symptoms , which afflicted individuals attribute to exposure to electromagnetic fields '' .those who are self-described with ehs report adverse reactions to electromagnetic fields at intensities well below the maximum levels permitted by international radiation safety standards . the majority of provocation trials to date have found that such claimants are unable to distinguish between exposure and non-exposure to electromagnetic fields . a systematic review of medical research in 2011 found no convincing scientific evidence for symptoms being caused by electromagnetic fields . since then , several double-blind experiments have shown that people who report electromagnetic hypersensitivity are unable to detect the presence of electromagnetic fields and are as likely to report ill health following a sham exposure as they are following exposure to genuine electromagnetic fields , suggesting the cause in these cases to be the nocebo effect.some people who feel they are sensitive to electromagnetic fields may seek to reduce their exposure or use alternative medicine . government agencies have enforced false advertising claims against companies selling devices to shield against em radiation .

Hannes Schäfer, born on October 2, 1965, in Göttingen, Germany, is a German bass guitarist, singer, and physician. He was a founding member of the rock band Fury in the Slaughterhouse. After his musical career in 1996, he studied medicine. Today, he is a gynecologist working in his own clinic in Hanover, Germany. In 1982, Schäfer played in a punk band called Defekt, where he was the bass guitarist and singer. From 1985 to 1987, he was in a jazz rock band named Cit, which included Mousse T. During this time, he also worked as a studio musician at Stakkato Studio Hannover. In 1987, Schäfer and some friends started the rock band Fury in the Slaughterhouse. He played bass guitar in the band until 1996, when he left. Christian Deker took his place. During his time with the band, they sold about three million albums and CDs, and Schäfer’s band won six gold records for their albums "Fury in the Slaughterhouse" (1988), "Mono" (1992), and "The Hearing and the Sense of Balance" (1995). In 1995, they won Germany’s most important music award, the "Comet," as the best rock act of the year. Schäfer played in over 1,400 concerts with more than five million people as a member of Fury in the Slaughterhouse. He played at their last three concerts in Hanover in August 2008. On May 14, 2011, he played one more concert for Fury in the Slaughterhouse in front of more than 40,000 people at the AWD-Arena, celebrating Hannover 96’s qualification for the UEFA Europa League. After leaving the band in 1996, Schäfer studied medicine and became a gynecologist. Today, he works in his own clinic in Hanover, Germany.
Erin Richards was born on May 17, 1986. She is a Welsh actress, director, and writer. She is famous for playing Molly Hughes in the TV show "Breaking In" and Barbara Kean in "Gotham."

Fabio Cudicini, born on October 20, 1935, is an Italian former professional goalkeeper who played from 1955 to 1972. He was very tall for a goalkeeper. Even though he didn't play for the Italy national team, many people think he was one of the best goalkeepers of his time and one of Italy's greatest ever. Cudicini is best known for his successful and dominant time at A.C. Milan. He helped the team win important titles, including the 1969 European Cup.

Pat Hoyt Taylor Jr., also known as Pat (April 1, 1924 – April 22, 2018), was an American politician and lawyer. He worked as the speaker of the North Carolina House of Representatives. Taylor also served as the 26th Lieutenant Governor of North Carolina.

Igor Nikolayevich Rodionov, born on December 1, 1936, and died on December 19, 2014, was a Russian general and Duma deputy. He was known for being a strict politician and his role as head of the Russian Federation's defense ministry. Rodionov had a long career as a Soviet army officer. He served in East Germany, Czechoslovakia, and the Far East, among other places. In 1970 to 1973, he was the commander of a motorized rifle regiment in the 24th motorized rifle division, often called the "Iron Division," in the Carpathian Military District. Later, he commanded the 17th motor rifle division in the same district. He also led the 5th army in the Far East Military District from 1983 to 1985, and the 40th army in Afghanistan in 1985 to 1986. In 1986, he was the first deputy chief commander of the Moscow Military District until 1988. Then, he became the commander of the Transcaucasus Military District. In April 1989, Rodionov was blamed for the violent suppression of protests in Tbilisi, where 19 people died and many were injured. He was removed from his post and sent to the General Staff Academy, a place where people often went after losing favor. However, it is believed that he was a scapegoat, as the orders likely came from Defense Minister Yazov, at the request of local Communist Party officials. Rodionov's personal and political views suggest he might have been made to take the blame. Rodionov served as a People's Deputy and head of the General Staff Academy from 1989 to 1996. In 1996, Russian President Boris Yeltsin replaced Defense Minister Pavel Grachev with Rodionov. Rodionov had written many military doctrine articles and was familiar with analysis from his role at the General Staff Academy, which Grachev lacked. During his time as defense minister, the main obstacle to reform was politics. Rodionov proposed reforms but believed that Russia should remain an adversary of the West. Over his term, he changed his mind on whether the military should be restructured or continue in the Soviet style, placing it above social and economic needs. He was dismissed because he refused to subordinate the ministry to civilian control and had a disagreement with Yuriy Baturin over military reform. Since 1999, Rodionov was a state Duma member of the Rodina faction, serving on the committee on national security and as chairman of the professional union of military personnel. He was laid to rest at the Federal Military Memorial Cemetery in Moscow Oblast.

Ravi Shankar, born as Robinindra Shankar Chowdhury and later known as Ravindra Shankar Chowdhury, was an Indian musician and composer of Hindustani classical music. He was often called Pandit (master). He is famous for playing the sitar and influenced many musicians worldwide in the second half of the 20th century. Shankar was awarded India's highest civilian honor, the Bharat Ratna, in 1999. Born to a Bengali Brahmin family in India, he started dancing and performing with his brother Uday Shankar's dance group. In 1938, he stopped dancing to study sitar playing under Allauddin Khan. After finishing his studies in 1944, he became a composer and made music for the "Apu Trilogy" films by Satyajit Ray. He also worked as the music director for All India Radio in New Delhi from 1949 to 1956. In 1956, he began touring Europe and the Americas, spreading the popularity of Indian classical music in the 1960s through teaching and performances. His association with violinist Yehudi Menuhin and Beatles guitarist George Harrison helped make Indian instruments popular in Western pop music during the latter half of the 1960s. He wrote compositions for sitar and orchestra and continued performing worldwide in the 1970s and 1980s. From 1986 to 1992, he was a nominated member of the Rajya Sabha, the upper chamber of India's parliament. He kept performing until the end of his life.
Dhillon is a tribe of Jat people found among Sikhs in Punjab, India. Some notable people with the name Dhillon may be part of this tribe.

Joan Mari Torrealdai Nabea was born on November 24, 1942, and died on July 31, 2020. He was a Basque writer, journalist, and sociologist. He lived in the Basque Autonomous Community in Spain. He was also a member of Euskaltzaindia, which is the Royal Academy of the Basque Language.

Cosmology is a part of astronomy that looks at how the universe began and changed over time, from the big bang until now and into the future. It studies the universe's origins, its big structures, and how it moves, as well as the rules that control these things. The term "cosmology" was first used in English in 1656 and later in Latin by a philosopher in 1731. Religious or mythological cosmology deals with stories about how the universe was created and what will happen at the end, based on old writings and beliefs. Physical cosmology is studied by scientists, like astronomers and physicists, and philosophers, such as those who think about the nature of the universe. Because of this, theories in physical cosmology might include both scientific and non-scientific ideas, and can depend on assumptions that can't be tested. Cosmology is different from astronomy, which focuses on individual stars and planets. Today, physical cosmology mainly follows the big bang theory, which tries to connect what we see in space with particle physics. This theory includes dark matter and dark energy, forming what is known as the Lambda-CDM model. A scientist named David N. Spergel described cosmology as a "historical science" because when we look at distant parts of the universe, we are actually seeing how things were in the past due to the speed of light.
L'Ile-Saint-Denis is a town in the northern part of Paris, France. It is near the center of Paris. The town is on an island in the Seine River, which is why it is called Ile-Saint-Denis.

El Paso County is one of Colorado's 64 counties. In 2010, it had 622,263 people. In 2018, it was the second most populous county in Colorado, after Denver. Its main city is Colorado Springs, the second biggest city in the state. El Paso County is part of the Colorado Springs metropolitan area. Since 1871, El Paso County usually votes for the Republican candidate. The last Democrat to win was Lyndon B. Johnson in 1964. Democrats won four times before that, and the Populist Party won in 1892 with James B. Weaver. In 2004, Colorado Springs and El Paso County voters created the Pikes Peak Rural Transportation Authority (PPRTA). They used a 1% sales tax to improve transportation. This was supported by state funding for projects like Cosmix (completed in 2007) and the I-25 interchange with Highway 16 (completed in 2008). Since 2003, progress has been made to meet the area's transportation needs. In 2012, the county voted to legalize marijuana. On March 12, 2019, the county voted unanimously to become a Second Amendment sanctuary.
Hand County is a county in South Dakota, U.S. In 2010, the population was 3,431. The county seat is Miller.
Mary Ann Mobley was born on February 17, 1937, and passed away on December 9, 2014. She was an American actress and television personality. She also won the Miss America contest in 1959.

Mallory Hagan was born on December 23, 1988. She is an American politician who used to be a beauty queen. She won Miss America 2013 while she was Miss New York in 2012. In 2008, she moved to New York after her first year at Auburn University. Before winning Miss America, she was also Miss Brooklyn 2010, Miss Manhattan 2011, Miss New York City 2012, and a two-time Miss New York first runner-up. In Alabama, she was a runner-up in the Miss Alabama's Outstanding Teen program. As Miss Chattahoochee Valley 2007, she was a non-finalist talent winner at Miss Alabama. She won Miss America by talking about stopping child sexual abuse because her family experienced it. She also talked about gun control, saying violence shouldn't be used to fight violence. In 2018, she tried to become a congresswoman as a Democrat in Alabama's 3rd district, which includes her hometown, Opelika.

Irony is a way of saying something that seems different from what you really mean. There are different types, like verbal irony, where someone says the opposite of what they mean, and situational irony, where a situation turns out very differently from what was expected. Dramatic irony happens when the audience knows something the characters don't. These types of irony are used to emphasize a point. Sarcasm and some forms of understatement also use irony to make a stronger point. Other types include dialectic and practical irony.

Warcraft III: The Frozen Throne is an expansion for a real-time strategy video game made by Blizzard Entertainment. It came out on July 1, 2003, for Windows and Mac OS X. The expansion continues the story from "Reign of Chaos" and shows what happens after the main game ends. In the single-player campaign, you can play as new heroes like Maiev Shadowsong and Kael'thas, as well as the returning hero Arthas. The expansion also includes a new orc campaign, which was released in separate parts. It adds new units, buildings, and heroes for each side, introduces two new races, and improves the game with new maps and scenarios. Development began after the main game was released, and the expansion was announced in January 2003. About 20,000 players tested it in public beta tests. Blizzard kept adding new content and updated the game for newer computers. Critics mostly liked the new mission designs, but some thought the graphics and voice-acting were not as good. By August 15, 2003, it had sold over one million copies.

Anthony Frederick Charles Tom Adams was an English actor. He was born on March 9, 1938, and died on December 11, 2014. Tom acted in adventure, horror, and mystery movies and also appeared in several TV shows. He is best known for playing Daniel Fogarty in "The Onedin Line," appearing in multiple series of the show.
Saint-Gervais-en-Belin is a commune in Sarthe, which is in the Pays-de-la-Loire region. This area is in northwestern France.

wood fuel, also called fuelwood, is a type of fuel like firewood, charcoal, chips, pellets, or sawdust. The kind used depends on things like where it comes from, how much there is, how good the quality is, and what it will be used for. In many places, wood is the easiest fuel to find. You can pick up dead wood without any tools, or use a few tools if needed. Special machines like skidders and splitters help make wood fuel production more efficient. Sawmill waste and construction leftovers also include wood scraps. Making fire was a big step for humans, and using wood to heat homes is very old, used even by early humans. Today, wood burning is the most common way to use solid fuel for heating. People use wood for cooking and heating, and sometimes to power engines or generate electricity. You can burn wood inside in a furnace, stove, or fireplace, or outside in a campfire or bonfire.
Daluis is a town in the Alpes-Maritimes area of southeastern France. It is by the River Var and ends the Gorges de Daluis.

Villedieu is a town in Vaucluse, which is in the Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur region of southeastern France. A local story says that people asked Alice Colonieu to make a statue of the Virgin Mary and put it on the back of a house in Villedieu. This statue, in the Renaissance style and decorated with a king scallop shell, is known as the "Virgin of the Smile" and can still be seen in Villedieu today.
Abdulhussain Abdulredha was a Kuwaiti actor. He was born on July 15, 1939, and died on August 11, 2017.
Lenox is a city in Taylor and Adams counties, in the state of Iowa. In 2010, it had 1,407 people living there.

The Ontario New Democratic Party (ONDP or NDP) is a social-democratic political party in Ontario, Canada. Led by Andrea Horwath since March 2009, the ONDP currently forms the official opposition in Ontario after the 2018 general election. It is part of the federal New Democratic Party. The ONDP was formed in October 1961 from the Cooperative Commonwealth Federation (Ontario section) and the Ontario Federation of Labour. For many years, the ONDP was the most successful NDP branch outside the western part of the country. In 1967, under Donald C. MacDonald, the party elected 20 members of provincial parliament (MPPs) to the Ontario Legislative Assembly. Stephen Lewis became the leader in 1970 and helped the party become the official opposition in 1975, the first time since the 1940s when the Cooperative Commonwealth Federation did it twice. In 1977, the party performed poorly and lost second party status. Michael Cassidy became the leader in 1978 but only led one election in 1981, after which the party did poorly again, and Cassidy resigned. Bob Rae became the leader in 1982. In 1985, the party held the balance of power with the Liberals. After the 1987 election, the ONDP became the official opposition again. In 1990, the party unexpectedly formed the first NDP government in Ontario, becoming the first NDP government east of Manitoba. However, the party lost power in 1995 due to unpopular economic policies, and Rae stepped down as leader in 1996. Howard Hampton was elected leader in 1996 and led the party through three elections. Hampton's leadership saw the party lose official party status twice, after the 1999 and 2003 elections. The party regained status after winning by-elections in the mid-2000s. The ONDP maintained its status after the 2007 election and Hampton stepped down in 2009. Andrea Horwath replaced him as leader in 2009 after being elected at the leadership convention. Under Horwath's leadership, the party did well in the 2011 and 2014 elections, with 17 and 21 MPPs elected, respectively. In the 2018 election, the ONDP formed the official opposition with 40 MPPs.

Carlos Rojas Hernández, known as Carlos "Cuco" Rojas, was born on March 28, 1954, in San Martín, Meta. He was a Colombian harpist and songwriter of joropo music. He also directed the Colombian band Cimarron. He passed away on January 10, 2020.

Hans von Borsody was a German film actor born on September 20, 1929, in Vienna. His family had Hungarian roots and was artistic. His father, Eduard, was a film director, and his uncle, Julius, was a set designer. His daughter, Suzanne, is also an actress. When Borsody was three, his family moved to Berlin and he became a German citizen. He was married four times to Karin Dittmann, Rosemarie Fendel, Alwy Becker, and Heide Keller.

Kiel is the capital and biggest city in Schleswig-Holstein, a state in northern Germany. In 2016, it had 249,023 people. Kiel is about north of Hamburg. Because it's near the Baltic Sea and Jutland Peninsula, Kiel is a major shipbuilding and sailing center in Germany. It hosts the Kiel Week, the world's biggest sailing event. Kiel is also known for the Kiel Mutiny, where sailors refused to board ships in 1918, leading to the end of the German monarchy and the start of the Weimar Republic. The city was also the location for sailing competitions during the 1936 and 1972 Summer Olympics. Today, Kiel is a crucial sea transport hub, connected by the Kiel Fjord and the Kiel Canal, one of the busiest waterways in the world. Several ferry services operate from Kiel to other countries. Kiel's history dates back to the 13th century, but was once a Danish village in the 8th century. Until 1864, Kiel was under Danish control. In 1866, Prussia took over, and in 1871, it became part of Germany. Kiel received the European Green Prize in 2006. In 2005, its average income was €35,618, which is higher than Germany's and the EU's average.
