Arctic Monkeys are an English rock band formed in Sheffield in 2002. The band includes Alex Turner (vocals, guitar, keyboards), Jamie Cook (guitar, keyboards), Nick O'Malley (bass guitar, backing vocals), and Matt Healy (drums, backing vocals). Andy Nicholson, a former band member, played bass guitar and backing vocals and left in 2006 after their first album was released. They have made six studio albums: "Whatever People Say I Am, That's What I'm Not" (2006), "Favourite Worst Nightmare" (2007), "Humbug" (2009), "Suck It and See" (2011), "AM" (2013), and "Tranquility Base Hotel & Casino" (2018). They also have one live album, "At the Apollo" (2008). Their first album was the fastest-selling debut album in the UK. In 2013, Rolling Stone ranked it as the 30th-greatest debut album. They have won seven Brit Awards, including Best British Group and Best British Album three times. They have been nominated for five Grammy Awards. The band won the Mercury Prize in 2006 for their first album and was nominated again in 2007, 2013, and 2018. Arctic Monkeys performed at the Glastonbury Festival twice, in 2007 and 2013. They were seen as one of the first bands to gain attention through the internet, which some said could change how new bands are promoted.

Matthew Tyler Oakley, born on March 22, 1989, is an American YouTuber, actor, activist, and author. He focuses much of his activism on LGBTQ+ youth, LGBTQ rights, and issues like health care, education, and preventing suicide among LGBTQ+ youth. Oakley often makes videos about queer politics, pop culture, and humor. He started making videos in 2007. His first video, "Raindrops," had 517,715 views by March 22, 2020. His YouTube channel has over 682 million views and had over 8 million subscribers at its peak. Oakley, who is openly gay, used to be part of a successful collaboration channel called "5awesomegays" and made the Friday video for over three years. He was featured in a 2014 "Frontline" report called "Generation Like." As of November 19, 2017, his YouTube channel was ranked 224th in subscribers and 2,010th in video views. He also had more than 5.9 million followers on Twitter and 5.8 million on Instagram. From March to October 2013, Oakley co-hosted a weekly pop-culture news show called "Top That!" with Becca Frucht for Popsugar. From 2013 to 2014, he voiced Mr. McNeely in five episodes of the comedy web series "The Most Popular Girls in School." He has many followers on Facebook and Tumblr. In 2015, he published his first book of humorous essays titled "Binge" through Simon & Schuster. Oakley hosted the show "The Tyler Oakley Show" on Ellen DeGeneres's Ellentube platform. In 2017, he was named one of Forbes's "30 under 30." In March 2020, he announced he was a landlord, which caused a lot of criticism.

Jacob Tremblay, born on October 5, 2006, is a Canadian actor. He became famous for his role as Jack Newsome in the movie "Room" in 2015. For this performance, he won an award for the best young performer and was also nominated for another award. In 2017, he played August Pullman in the drama "Wonder." August has a special condition called Treacher Collins syndrome. In 2019, Jacob starred in the comedy "Good Boys."

Dr. Hannibal Lecter is a fictional character in books by Thomas Harris. He is a psychiatrist in Baltimore and also a serial killer who eats people. After being caught, he helps the FBI find other killers. He first appeared in the 1981 book "Red Dragon" and was a bad guy in "The Silence of the Lambs" from 1988. In "Hannibal" in 1999, he becomes good. His childhood and becoming a killer are explored in "Hannibal Rising" in 2006. The first movie based on Harris' books is "Manhunter" from 1986, with Brian Cox as Lecter, spelled "Lecktor." Anthony Hopkins won an Oscar for playing Lecter in "The Silence of the Lambs" in 1991 and played him again in "Hannibal" in 2001 and "Red Dragon" in 2002. The most recent movie is "Hannibal Rising" in 2007, with Gaspar Noé playing Lecter. Harris wrote the screenplay for this movie. The TV show "Hannibal" started in 2013 and is about Lecter's friendship with FBI profiler Will Graham. Mads Mikkelsen played Lecter and won a Saturn Award. In 2003, Hopkins' Lecter was named one of the best villains in American cinema. In 2010, "Entertainment Weekly" said he was one of the best characters in movies over 20 years. In 2019, Mikkelsen's Lecter was ranked 18th as a TV villain by "Rolling Stone."

The speaker of the Spanish senate, also called the president of the senate, leads the upper house of Spain's cortes generales. After the monarch (head of state), the prime minister (head of government), and the president of the congress of deputies (speaker of the lower house), this is the fourth most important role in the country. The speaker is chosen by the senators and replaces them if needed. Although the president of the congress shares some duties, the senate's speaker often works in the background. The current role was created in 1978, but the position has a history dating back almost 200 years, starting in 1834 when it was called the president of the house of peers. Pilar Llop, a member of the socialist group, is the current speaker representing Madrid.

Miikka Sakari Kiprusoff, nicknamed Kipper, was born on October 26, 1976. He is a Finnish former professional ice hockey goaltender. Kiprusoff played for the Calgary Flames and San Jose Sharks in the NHL. He was chosen by the San Jose Sharks in the 1995 NHL draft. He also played for TPS in the Finnish SM-liiga and for Aik IF and Timrå IK in the Swedish Elitserien. Kiprusoff represented Finland in international competitions. He won silver medals at the Ice Hockey World Championships in 1999 and 2001. He led Finland to a second-place finish at the 2004 World Cup of Hockey. He also helped the Finnish national team win a bronze medal at the 2010 Winter Olympics in Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada. Kiprusoff started his professional career with TPS in 1994. In 1999, he was named the best goaltender and best player of the playoffs, helping TPS win the SM-liiga championship. Later, he moved to the NHL and played for the San Jose Sharks. He had two all-star seasons in the American Hockey League (AHL) before joining the Sharks. At the Sharks, he was a backup goaltender. He was traded to the Calgary Flames in 2003–04, where he became the starting goaltender. He set a record for the lowest goals against average (1.69) and helped the Flames reach the 2004 Stanley Cup Final. In 2006, he won the Vezina Trophy for being the best goaltender in the NHL and the William M. Jennings Trophy for giving up the fewest goals in the league. He played in his first NHL All-Star Game in 2007 and holds the Flames' franchise records for most wins and shutouts.

In the history of Christianity, docetism is a belief that Jesus only appeared to be human. This means his human form was just an illusion. The word "docetai" first appeared in a letter by Bishop Serapion of Antioch around 197-203. He found this belief in the Gospel of Peter during a visit to a Christian community in Rhosus. Serapion later said it was a fake. This idea came from disagreements about whether "the word was made flesh" in the Gospel of John meant Jesus was truly human or just seemed to be. Docetism was clearly rejected at the First Council of Nicaea in 325. It is considered wrong by many Christian churches, including the Catholic, Eastern Orthodox, Coptic Orthodox, Tewahedo, and some Protestant groups.

The list of Atlantic hurricanes from the 18th century includes all known tropical cyclones from 1700 to 1799. While data for every storm is not available, some coastal areas had enough people to record hurricane occurrences.

Paktika is one of Afghanistan's 34 provinces. It is in the eastern part of the country. Paktika has about 413,800 people, mostly Pashtuns. Sharana is the provincial capital. Uргун is the most populous city.

Stephen Lewis, born on December 17, 1926, and known as Stephen Cato early in his career, was an English actor, comedian, director, screenwriter, and playwright. He is famous for playing Inspector Cyril "Blakey" Blake on "The Buses," Clem "Smiler" Hemmingway in "Last of the Summer Wine," and Harry Lambert in "Oh, Doctor Beeching!" He also appeared in many other stage and film roles. He passed away on August 12, 2015.

In chemistry, a leaving group is a part of a molecule that leaves during a reaction. This happens when a pair of electrons splits. Leaving groups can be negatively charged (anions), positively charged (cations), or neutral. But they must be able to handle extra electrons. Common examples of negatively charged leaving groups are halides like chlorine (Cl), bromine (Br), and iodine (I), and sulfonate esters like tosylate (TsO). Fluoride (F) can also leave in nerve agent Sarin gas. Neutral molecules that can leave include water and ammonia. Positively charged leaving groups, like hydrogen (H) in benzene nitrations, are called electrofuges.

Alfred Lothar Wegener, born on November 1, 1880, and died in 1930, was a German researcher who studied the polar regions, geophysics, and meteorology. He is best known for coming up with the idea of continental drift in 1912. He suggested that the continents slowly move around the Earth. His idea was controversial and not widely accepted by scientists at the time. It gained support in the 1950s when new discoveries, such as paleomagnetism, showed that continental drift was true. Wegener also went on several trips to Greenland to study air movements before jet streams were discovered. During these trips, his team made many weather observations and were the first to spend a winter in the middle of Greenland's ice sheet and the first to take ice cores from a moving glacier in the Arctic.
Paul Konrad Müller, born on March 11, 1923, in Neuchâtel, is a Swiss actor. He mostly appeared in Italian films. He acted in movies in Europe for 51 years.

Northport is a historic maritime village on Long Island's north shore, New York. It was called Great Cow Harbour by English settlers in the 17th century and officially named Northport in 1837. In 1894, Northport became a village to have its own local government. Northport is famous for its Victorian-era village center, which still has old trolley tracks from a former streetcar line. These tracks once carried villagers to the Long Island Rail Road station in East Northport. The village main street goes from the village green, next to the harbor, to the former area of Vernon Valley, now part of East Northport. As of 2010, Northport has about 7,401 people living there. The local schools are part of the Northport-East Northport School District.

Togiola Talalelei A. Tulafono, born on February 28, 1947, is an American Samoan politician and lawyer. He served as the 56th governor of American Samoa and is a member of the Democratic Party. Before becoming governor, he was the lieutenant governor, taking the position on January 3, 1997. Tulafono became acting governor on March 26, 2003, when Governor Tauese Pita Fitia Sunia died. He officially became governor on April 7, 2003. He was elected to a full 4-year term in the 2004 gubernatorial elections and was re-elected in the 2008 elections. In 2012, Tulafono could not run for governor again due to term limits. He tried to become a candidate for American Samoa's at-large congressional district in 2014 but was unsuccessful.

Baked beans is a dish that uses white beans. These beans are first cooked a bit, then baked at a low temperature for a long time in a sauce. In the U.S., this is how baked beans are usually made without using canned beans. In the U.K., the beans are sometimes baked, but more often stewed in a sauce. Canned baked beans are not baked; they are cooked using steam. Baked beans come from Native American cuisine, using local beans. English colonists in New England adopted and changed the recipe in the 17th century. Cookbooks in the 19th century spread the dish to other parts of the U.S. and Canada. In New England today, restaurants and homes use various local beans like Jacob's cattle, soldier beans, yellow-eyed beans, and navy beans (also called native beans). Originally, Native Americans sweetened the beans with maple syrup, a tradition some recipes still follow. English colonists began using brown sugar in the 17th century. In the 18th century, using molasses became popular to avoid taxes on sugar. Molasses and salt pork in the sauce led to Boston being called "Beantown." Today, baked beans are often eaten with barbecue food or at picnics. Beans in various sauces, like brown sugar or corn syrup, are common. Canned baked beans are popular as a quick food. They are made from navy beans in a sauce and can be eaten hot or cold. The H. J. Heinz Company started making canned baked beans in the U.S. in 1895. In the early 20th century, they became very popular in the U.K., where they are often eaten with a full English breakfast.

Caliban is the second-largest retrograde irregular moon of Uranus. It was found on September 6, 1997, by Brett J. Gladman, Philip D. Nicholson, Joseph A. Burns, and John J. Kavelaars using the 200-inch Hale telescope. Caliban was also found with another moon called Sycorax and was temporarily named S/1997 U 1. It was given the official name Uranus Xvi and is named after a character in Shakespeare's play "The Tempest."

Valente Rodriguez was born on February 14, 1964. He is an American actor. He is famous for playing the character Ernie Cárdenas in the TV show "George Lopez." He also acted as César in "Happily Divorced" on TV Land. He appeared in other TV shows like "Yes, Dear," "Mad About You," and "ER." He had a role as Marco in the film "Suckers" in 2001.

Ryan Prosser, born on July 10, 1988, plays professional rugby union. He plays as a hooker. In June 2008, he played for Wales in the under-20 Junior World Cup. He got engaged to Hayley Thomas on January 2, 2018. He is friends with actor Fin Samad. In January 2010, he joined the Cornish Pirates from Bristol.

The flag of Germany is a tricolor consisting of three equal horizontal bands: black, red, and gold. It was first used as the national flag in 1919 during the Weimar Republic and continued until 1933. Since the 1840s, Germany has had two main traditions for national colors: black-red-gold and black-white-red. Black-red-gold represents the 1848 revolutions, the Weimar Republic (1919-1933), and the Federal Republic (since 1949). The German Democratic Republic (1949-1990) also used these colors starting in 1959. Black-white-red first appeared in 1867 for the North German Confederation, a nation for Prussia and other northern and central German states, which later became the German Empire in 1871. These colors were used until 1918-1919. After World War II, black-white-red was still used by some conservative groups or far-right groups, but it is not officially banned. Black-red-gold is the official flag of Germany. It is protected as an official symbol of the constitutional order, and violating this can result in a fine or up to five years in prison.

The conservation movement aims to protect nature, such as animals, plants, and their habitats, for the future. Evidence-based conservation uses science to make conservation efforts more effective. Early conservation efforts focused on managing fisheries and wildlife, protecting water, soil, and forests. Sustainable use of natural resources and preserving wilderness areas were key in the early movement. Today, conservation also aims to protect biodiversity. Some see conservation as part of a larger environmental movement, while others think they differ. In the U.S., conservation is about preserving nature for humans to use sustainably. Elsewhere, conservation includes environmentalism.

A hose is a flexible tube used to move liquids from one place to another. People sometimes call it a "pipe," but a pipe is usually rigid, while a hose is flexible. Hoses are also called "tubing." Hoses are often shaped like a cylinder, which means they have a round cross-section. The design of a hose depends on its use and performance. Common factors include size, how much pressure it can handle, weight, length, whether it is straight or coiled, and what chemicals it needs to be compatible with. Hoses are made from materials like nylon, polyurethane, polyethylene, PVC, or rubber, depending on the environment and how much pressure they need to handle. In recent years, special types of polyethylene (called LDPE and LLDPE) are also used. Other materials include PTFE (teflon), stainless steel, and other metals.
Bell is a town in the Mayen-Koblenz district, which is in Rhineland-Palatinate, a state in western Germany.

Matthew Quincy "Matt" Daddario was born on October 1, 1987. He is an American actor. He is famous for playing Alec Lightwood in the TV show "Shadowhunters" from 2016 to 2019. Matt has a sister named Alexandra Daddario, who is also an actress.

betrayal occurs when someone breaks a trust or confidence, causing conflict in a relationship. It can happen between people, between organizations, or between individuals and organizations. Betrayal might involve supporting a rival group or going against agreed-upon norms. A person who betrays others is usually called a traitor. Betrayal is also used in stories, like in books, movies, and TV shows, often as a surprise twist in the plot.
Francisco Ibáñez Talavera was born on March 15, 1936. He is a Spanish artist and writer who makes comic books.

Blythburgh is a small village in the East Suffolk area of Suffolk, England. It is located west of Southwold and southeast of Halesworth, near the River Blyth. The A12 road goes through the village, splitting it into two parts. In the 2011 census, the village had 297 people. Blythburgh has a church called Holy Trinity, often called the cathedral of the marshes, which is brightly lit at night. This church is a landmark for drivers on the A12. The village also has a history with Blythburgh Priory, which was built by monks from St Osyth's Priory in Essex in the 12th century. The priory was closed in 1537, but its ruins can still be seen today. Blythburgh is part of the Suffolk Coast and Heaths Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty, known as the Suffolk Sandlings. The village is near the Suffolk Heritage Coast, close to marshes and mudflats by the River Blyth. During World War II, part of the area was flooded in 1940 as a defense measure.

Appenzeller cheese is a hard, cow's-milk cheese made in the Appenzell region of northeast Switzerland, in the cantons of Appenzell Innerrhoden and Appenzell Ausserrhoden. During curing, wheels of cheese are sometimes treated with a herbal brine, which may include wine or cider. This brine adds flavor, helps preserve the cheese, and promotes the formation of a rind. The cheese has a history dating back at least 700 years, first mentioned in a document from 1282. The exact manufacturing process from that time was different from today. Currently, about 75 dairies produce Appenzeller cheese, each with its own unique brine recipe, often a trade secret. The cheese is straw-colored, has small holes, and a golden rind. It has a strong smell and a nutty or fruity taste, which can vary from mild to tangy, depending on how long it is aged. There are three types of Appenzeller cheese sold.

Keiunta Denard Span was born on February 27, 1984. He is an American. Span was a professional baseball player who played as a center fielder. He played for the Minnesota Twins, Washington Nationals, San Francisco Giants, Tampa Bay Rays, and Seattle Mariners in the Major League Baseball (MLB). Span batted and threw left-handed. At his best, he was famous for being a top leadoff hitter because he had a very good on-base percentage.

The Toronto Maple Leafs, also known as the Leafs, are a professional ice hockey team in Toronto. They play in the National Hockey League (NHL) and are part of the Atlantic Division in the Eastern Conference. The team is owned by Maple Leaf Sports & Entertainment, Ltd., and is led by chairman Larry Tanenbaum. Their broadcasting rights are shared by BCE Inc. and Rogers Communications. The Leafs first played at Mutual Street Arena for 14 seasons before moving to Maple Leaf Gardens in 1931. They now play at Scotiabank Arena, which was previously called the Air Canada Centre. The team was founded in 1917 as the Toronto Arenas and was renamed the Toronto St. Patrick's in 1919. In 1927, the club was bought by Conn Smythe and renamed the Maple Leafs. The Maple Leafs are one of the "original six" NHL teams and have won 13 Stanley Cup championships, second only to the 24 of the Montreal Canadiens. They had two strong periods, winning from 1947 to 1951 and from 1962 to 1967. Their last championship was in 1967, making their 51-season gap the longest current drought in the NHL. They have rivalries with the Boston Bruins, Detroit Red Wings, Montreal Canadiens, and Ottawa Senators. The Maple Leafs have retired the numbers of 13 players in honor of their achievements, including the first in professional sports. Several individuals connected to the team have also been inducted into the Hockey Hall of Fame. Currently, the team is linked to the Toronto Marlies in the American Hockey League and the Newfoundland Growlers in the ECHL.

Gangwon-do is a province in South Korea. Its capital is Chuncheon. It touches the Sea of Japan on its east side. To the west, it borders Gyeonggi province. To the south, it borders North Gyeongsang and North Chungcheong provinces. Its northern border separates it from North Korea's Kangwŏn province. Before Korea was divided in 1945, Gangwon and Kangwŏn were one province. Pyeongchang county hosted the 2018 Winter Olympics and Paralympics. Gangwon will host the 2024 Winter Youth Olympics.
Unterschächen is a municipality in Switzerland. It is in the canton of Uri and located in the Upper Sacha Valley.

Benjamin Franklin was born on January 17, 1706, and was one of America's founding fathers. He was a writer, printer, politician, scientist, inventor, and civic activist. As a scientist, Franklin was important in the American Enlightenment and the history of physics. He invented the lightning rod, bifocals, and the Franklin stove. He also started several organizations, including the library company, Philadelphia's first fire department, and the University of Pennsylvania. Franklin was known as "the first American" for his work in uniting the colonies. He was the first United States ambassador to France. Franklin helped shape the American ethos with practical values like thrift and hard work, and Enlightenment values like education and opposition to authority. Franklin became a successful newspaper editor and printer in Philadelphia at age 23. He printed the "Pennsylvania Gazette" and the "Poor Richard's Almanack," which he wrote under a fake name. In 1767, he was involved with the "Pennsylvania Chronicle," a newspaper known for criticizing British policies. Franklin was the first president of the Academy and College of Philadelphia, which later became the University of Pennsylvania. He was also the first secretary of the American Philosophical Society and its president in 1769. Franklin was a key figure in getting Britain to repeal the Stamp Act. He was admired in France as America's ambassador to Paris and played a crucial role in getting France to support America during the revolution. He became the first United States postmaster general. Franklin was involved in community and political affairs. He was governor of Pennsylvania from 1785 to 1788. He initially owned slaves but later argued against slavery and promoted education for African Americans. Franklin is remembered for his scientific and political achievements. He is honored on money and other places, like towns, schools, and corporations, and is often referenced in culture.

Salvador Vilar Braamcamp Sobral, born on December 28, 1989, is a Portuguese singer. He won the Eurovision Song Contest in 2017 with the song "Amar pelos Dois," which was written and composed by his sister, Luísa Sobral. By winning, he gave Portugal its first-ever victory in the contest, ending a long winless streak of 53 years. Sobral and his song hold the record for the highest score in Eurovision history, with 758 points, which came from both the jury and televote.
Ile-d'Elle is a commune in the Vendée department, which is in the Pays de la Loire region in western France.

Anna Kavan, born Helen Emily Woods on April 10, 1901, and died on December 5, 1968, was a British writer and painter. She first used the name Helen Ferguson for her writings. In 1939, she changed her name to Anna Kavan, using it not just as a pen name but also as her legal name.

Hamont-Achel is a town in the Belgian province of Limburg. It was formed in 1977 when the city of Hamont joined with the village of Achel. On January 1, 2006, Hamont-Achel had 13,770 people living there. The town covers 43. 66 square kilometers, making the population density about 315 people per square kilometer. Hamont-Achel has a Trappist abbey, and part of it is a brewery called Achelse Kluis. This is one of 11 Trappist breweries. The professional tennis player Elise Mertens lives in Hamont-Achel.

In October 2015, the U.S. House of Representatives elected a new Speaker during the 114th Congress. John Boehner, who was the Speaker, was going to resign on October 30. This was the 124th election for Speaker since 1789. Republican Paul Ryan, who led the Ways and Means Committee, won with 236 votes, which is more than half of the 435 members. Nancy Pelosi, the Democratic leader, got 184 votes. With 432 votes needed, Ryan needed at least 217 to win. Ryan, who is younger than most previous Speakers, was elected on October 29. He was sworn in by John Conyers, the longest-serving member of the House. Boehner had been Speaker since January 2011. He faced disagreements with the Freedom Caucus. On September 25, he said he would resign. Kevin McCarthy, who was the Majority Leader, was expected to win but withdrew. Paul Ryan was then encouraged to run but initially said no. After receiving support from different groups, Ryan agreed. Other candidates like Daniel Webster dropped out. Ryan won the vote on October 28 and was elected the next day.

Mccomb is a city in Pike County, Mississippi, United States. It is south of Jackson. According to the 2010 census, Mccomb had 12,790 people. Mccomb is the main city of the Mccomb, Mississippi micropolitan statistical area.

The Phoenix Dwarf is a dwarf irregular galaxy found in 1976 by Hans-Emil Schuster and Richard Martin West. It was first mistaken for a globular cluster. It is now 1.44 million light-years away from Earth. The galaxy got its name because it is part of the Phoenix constellation.

vauxhall gardens is a public park in kennington, london. It is on the south side of the river thames. From 1785 to 1859, it was a pleasure garden and a top spot for entertainment. Known as new spring gardens first, it opened before 1660, as noted by samuel pepys in 1662. The park had lots of trees and paths. Initially, entrance was free, but food and drinks were sold. People could reach it by boat until the 1810s when vauxhall bridge was built. The area became part of the city in the 19th century. In 1785, it became vauxhall gardens, and an entrance fee was charged. Many people visited; paths were for romantic meetings. There were tightrope walkers, hot-air balloons, concerts, and fireworks. A turkish tent and chinoiserie style buildings were among the attractions. A statue of george frideric handel was later moved to westminster abbey. In 1817, a battle of waterloo reenactment with 1,000 soldiers took place. The gardens closed in 1840 due to financial troubles, reopened in 1841, changed hands in 1842, and closed permanently in 1859. The land was later developed, but part of the original site was turned into a public park in the late 20th century. It is now called vauxhall pleasure gardens and managed by lambeth borough. Vauxhall gardens is also shown in a tile design at vauxhall tube station.
Hansi Müller was born on July 27, 1957, in Stuttgart. He was a German football player who played as a midfielder.

In the 18th and 19th centuries, promenade concerts were musical shows in London's pleasure gardens. People walked around while enjoying the music. The word comes from French, meaning "to walk." Today, "promenade concert" is usually linked to the Proms, a summer series of classical music concerts started in 1895 by Robert Newman and conductor Henry Wood.

Stanley Norman Cohen was born on June 30, 1935, in Perth Amboy, New Jersey, USA. He is an American geneticist and teaches at Stanford University. Cohen and Herbert Boyer were the first scientists to move genes from one living thing to another. This was a big discovery for genetic engineering. Many products have been created using their work, such as human growth hormone and hepatitis B vaccine. According to microbiologist Hugh McDevitt, "Cohen's DNA cloning technology has helped scientists in almost every field." Without this technology, "the world of medicine and biotechnology would look very different."

Knuts Skujenieks, born on September 5, 1936, in Riga, is a Latvian poet, journalist, and translator of fifteen European languages. He grew up near Bauska, Zemgale (southern Latvia). Skujenieks studied at the University of Latvia in Riga and at the Maxim Gorky Literature Institute in Moscow. In 1962, he was convicted of anti-Soviet activities and sentenced to seven years in a prison camp in Mordovia, Russia. Although he wrote a lot of poetry, he could only publish his first collection in 1978. His poems from his time in prison were published in 1990. Skujenieks' poetry has been translated into many European languages. His books have been published in Sweden and Ukraine. In 2008, he received the Baltic Assembly Prize for Literature. Director Ivars Tontegode is making a documentary about Skujenieks' life called "The Deviant/Nepareizais."

Andrew Jackson's second inauguration as the president of the United States took place on Monday, March 4, 1833, in the House Chamber of the U.S. Capitol. This was the start of his second four-year term, and Martin Van Buren's first four-year term as vice president. When Jackson arrived at the Capitol's east front, John Peter Van Ness, the mayor of Washington, and the Council of Corporation members greeted him and Martin Van Buren, then escorted them to the House Chamber. At 12:00, Chief Justice John Marshall swore them in in the House Chamber. This happened inside because of the snow and cold weather, unlike the previous inauguration held in the Capitol's east portico. People present included judges from the Supreme Court, the House Speaker, the Senate President, senators, foreign ministers, and members of the House. Jackson walked to the speaker's seat, and after the crowd cheered, he stood up and was sworn in as president, with his private secretary, Andrew Jackson Donelson, on his right and Martin Van Buren on his left. This was the last time Chief Justice John Marshall swore in a president. After taking the oath, Jackson gave his inaugural speech to the people in the House Chamber. He said he was honored to be re-elected and promised to work for the American people. He also said the United States was at peace with other countries and that a strong, united nation was important. He stressed the need for cooperation between state and federal governments. Two inaugural balls followed Jackson's speech. This was the first time there were more than one ball at an inauguration. One was at Central Masonic Hall, and the other at Carusi's. Boston Republicans celebrated Jackson's re-election by firing 50-gun salutes at 9:00 a.m. and 12:00 p.m. on the day of the inauguration.

Rayon is a man-made fiber created from natural sources like wood and plants turned into cellulose. Rayon can feel and look like natural fibers such as silk, wool, cotton, and linen. It is a type of art silk. Rayon is a fiber made from cellulose with the same molecular structure. Viscose, a type of rayon, can also feel and look like natural fibers. Rayon that looks like silk is often called artificial silk. Rayon is used to make clothes and other items.
Beaulencourt is a commune in the Pas-de-Calais department, which is in the Hauts-de-France region of northern France.

The ARIA Charts, shown as ARIA Charts since November 2018, are Australia's main music sales charts. They are released weekly by the Australian Recording Industry Association. The charts show the top-selling songs and albums in various genres in Australia. ARIA became Australia's official music chart in June 1988, replacing the Kent Music Report, which was used from 1974 to 1988.

Eurovision: Europe Shine a Light was a live TV show. It was organized by the European Broadcasting Union and produced by Dutch broadcasters AVROTROS, NOS, and NPO. This show replaced the Eurovision Song Contest 2020, which was supposed to happen in Rotterdam, Netherlands, but was canceled because of the coronavirus pandemic. The live broadcast took place in Hilversum, Netherlands, on May 16, 2020. It lasted about two hours. The show was hosted by Chantal Janzen, Edsilia Rombley, and Jan Smit. These hosts were originally chosen to present the Eurovision Song Contest 2020 before it was cancelled.
St. Francis is a city in Clay County, Arkansas, United States. It is next to the St. Francis River. The population was 250 in 2010.

The Academy Awards for best dance direction were given from 1935 to 1937. Then, it was stopped.
Monsignor Bernardino Piñera Carvallo lived from September 22, 1915, to June 21, 2020. He was a bishop in the Catholic Church from Chile.

Jean-Martin Charcot, born on November 29, 1825, and died on August 16, 1893, was a French doctor who studied the brain and taught about diseases. He is famous for his studies on sleepwalking and a condition called hysteria, especially his work with a patient named Louise Augustine Gleizes. Known as "the founder of modern neurology," Charcot is connected to at least 15 medical terms named after him, such as Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease and Charcot disease. He is called "the father of French neurology and one of the world's leading neurologists." His work had a big impact on understanding the brain and psychology. Modern doctors in psychiatry owe a lot to his work and that of his followers. He was considered "the top neurologist in France during the late 1800s" and "the Napoleon of the neuroses."
Gigondas is a commune in Vaucluse, which is in the Provence-Alpes-Côte d’Azur region in southeastern France.

Sylvia Robinson, born on May 29, 1935, and died on September 29, 2011, was an American singer, musician, record producer, and record label executive. She had two R&B chart-topping songs: "Love Is Strange" with Mickey & Sylvia in 1957 and "Pillow Talk" as a solo artist in 1973. Later, she founded Sugar Hill Records and became its CEO. Robinson is known for her role in hip-hop music. She helped make two important songs: "Rapper's Delight" by the Sugarhill Gang in 1979, and "The Message" by Grandmaster Flash and the Furious Five in 1982. Because of this, she was called "the mother of hip-hop." In 2000, she received a Pioneer Award for her career and founding Sugarhill Records at the 11th annual R&B awards gala.

jw-jones, born on July 15, 1980, is a Canadian blues guitarist, singer, and songwriter. He has won awards, including being nominated for a Juno Award in 2015 and winning the International Blues Challenge for "Best Self-Produced CD" in 2017 for his album 'High Temperature.' Jones signed his first recording contract with Crosscut Records in Germany in 2000. He released seven CDs in Europe. He later worked with Northernblues Music in Toronto, releasing six recordings with them. He also worked with Ruf Records in the USA and Blind Pig Records. jw-jones has released nine studio albums and one live album. He has performed in 23 countries across four continents and continues to tour frequently. He lives in Ottawa, Ontario, and has played at blues festivals, theaters, and clubs in Canada, the USA, Europe, the United Kingdom, Russia, Australia, and Brazil. On June 19, 2014, jw-jones was given a "Forty Under 40" award by the Ottawa Business Journal and Ottawa Chamber of Commerce. This award honors young business leaders in Ottawa who are successful in their careers and involved in the community.

RADA, or the Royal Academy of Dramatic Art, is a drama school in London. It trains actors for film, TV, and theatre. The school is in the Bloomsbury area, near the University of London's Senate House. RADA is part of a group of drama schools. Founded in 1904 by Herbert Beerbohm Tree, it moved to Gower Street in 1905. In 1920, it got a royal charter. A new theatre was built on Malet Street in 1921 and opened by Edward, Prince of Wales. RADA started getting government money in 1924. Today, it has five theatres and a cinema. RADA teaches basic, college, and advanced acting courses. Its education awards are recognized by King's College London. Edward Kemp is the director, and Sir Kenneth Branagh is the president, succeeding Lord Attenborough. Queen Elizabeth II is the patron of RADA.

Jules Henri Poincaré, born on April 29, 1854, and died on July 17, 1912, was a French mathematician, physicist, engineer, and philosopher of science. He was known as a polymath, excelling in various fields of mathematics. Poincaré made important contributions to pure and applied mathematics, mathematical physics, and celestial mechanics. His research on the three-body problem helped lay the groundwork for modern chaos theory. He is also considered one of the founders of topology. Poincaré highlighted the importance of laws of physics remaining the same under different transformations. He presented the Lorentz transformations in a modern, symmetrical form and discovered the remaining relativistic velocity transformations, which he documented in a letter to Hendrik Lorentz in 1905. This work helped ensure the invariance of Maxwell's equations, an important step in the theory of special relativity. In 1905, Poincaré suggested that gravitational waves, or "ondes gravifiques," would exist and travel at the speed of light, as required by Lorentz transformations. The Poincaré group, used in physics and mathematics, is named after him. In early 20th-century mathematics, Poincaré formulated the Poincaré conjecture, which became a famous unsolved problem in mathematics until it was solved by Grigori Perelman in 2002–2003.

The vertical bar | is a symbol used in math, computing, and writing. It has several names depending on its use: sheffer stroke (in logic), verti-bar, vbar, stick, vertical line, vertical slash, bar, pike, or pipe. Sometimes, it is also called a broken bar.

Wellin is a municipality in Belgium, part of the province of Luxembourg. On January 1, 2007, Wellin had 2,958 people living in an area of 67.52 square kilometers. This means there were about 44 people for every square kilometer. Wellin includes several smaller areas: Wellin, Chanly, Halma, Lomprez, and Sohier. Other smaller communities are Barzin, Froidlieu, Fays-Famenne, and Neupont.

Common wheat, also called bread wheat, is a type of cultivated wheat. Nearly all wheat grown around the world—about 95%—is common wheat. It is the most widely grown crop and brings in the most money as a cereal.

genealogy is the study of families and their histories. Genealogists gather information using interviews, records, and genetic analysis to show family connections and lineages. They often create charts or write about family histories. Family history includes more than just lineages; it also covers family and community backgrounds and stories. When genealogists record their findings, it can be called a "genealogy" or a "family history." A "genealogy" focuses on descendants, while a "family history" focuses on ancestors, but the terms are often used together. A family history might include personal stories and traditions. People study family history for many reasons, such as understanding their place in history, preserving the past for future generations, or feeling satisfied from telling accurate stories. Genealogy research is also done for academic or legal reasons.

Lynwood is a city in Los Angeles County, California. In 2010, the city had 69,772 people, which was a bit less than in 2000 when it had 69,845. Lynwood is close to South Gate and Compton, in the southern part of the Los Angeles area. It became a city in 1921. The city is named after Lynn Wood Sessions, who was the wife of a local dairyman named Charles Sessions. The local railroad station and later the Pacific Electric Railway station were also named after the dairy.

Churchill College is part of the University of Cambridge in England. It mainly teaches science, engineering, and technology but also includes arts and humanities. In 1958, a trust was created with Sir Winston Churchill as the chairman to build and fund the college as a memorial to him. The college received royal approval in August 1960. It is located on the edge of Cambridge, near the university's new development area. It has the largest grounds of all the colleges. Churchill was the first all-male college to accept women students, admitting its first women in 1972. Within 15 years, all other men's colleges followed. The college is known for being more relaxed than other Cambridge colleges and admits more students from state schools. Its motto is "Forward," inspired by Winston Churchill's speech as prime minister.

Trachselwald is a municipality in the Emmental district of the Swiss canton of Bern.

Flensburg (Danish: "Flensborg"; Low Saxon: "Flensborg"; North Frisian: "Flansborj"; South Jutlandic: "Flensborre") is a town in northern Germany, in the state of Schleswig-Holstein. It is the center of the southern Schleswig region. After Kiel and Lübeck, Flensburg is the third-largest town in Schleswig-Holstein. In May 1945, Flensburg was where the last government of Nazi Germany, known as the Flensburg government, led by Karl Dönitz, was based. This government was in power from May 1, when Hitler's death was announced, for one week until German armies surrendered and the town was occupied by Allied troops. The regime officially ended on May 23. The closest larger towns are Kiel to the south and Odense in Denmark to the northeast. Flensburg's city center is near the Danish border.
