In geometry, a line segment is a part of a line that starts and ends at two points. It includes all the points on the line between these two points. A closed line segment includes both starting and ending points. An open line segment does not include either point. A half-open line segment includes just one of the points. Examples of line segments are the sides of a triangle or square. If both endpoints are connected vertices of a polygon or polyhedron, it is called an edge if the vertices are next to each other, or a diagonal if they are not. If the endpoints are on a curve like a circle, the line segment is called a chord.

James Edward Westcott was born on January 20, 1922, and died on March 29, 2019. He was an American photographer. During the Manhattan Project and the Cold War, he worked for the United States government in Oak Ridge, Tennessee. As one of the few people allowed to have a camera in Oak Ridge during the Manhattan Project, he took many photos. These photos became the main visual record of building and operating the Oak Ridge factories. They also showed everyday life in the closed community of Oak Ridge.
Virginia is a city in Cass County, Illinois, United States. In 2010, it had 1,611 people. The city is also the county seat of Cass County.

Madonna Louise Ciccone, born on August 16, 1958, is an American singer, songwriter, actress, author, and record executive. Known as the "queen of pop," she is one of the most influential figures in music and culture. Madonna is known for changing her image and style and for her creative work. She has been at the forefront of music, often challenging norms. Her songs and art cover many topics like society, politics, and religion, earning her both praise and criticism. Born and raised in Michigan, Madonna moved to New York in 1978 to dance. She later joined rock bands Breakfast Club and Emmy, played drums, guitar, and sang. In 1982, she signed with Sire Records and released her first album the following year. Some of her best-known albums include "Like a Virgin" (1984), "True Blue" (1986), "Ray of Light" (1998), and "Confessions on a Dance Floor" (2005). Many of her songs topped the charts. Madonna also starred in movies like "Desperately Seeking Susan" (1985), "Dick Tracy" (1990), "A League of Their Own" (1992), and "Evita" (1996). Although her films were not always well-received, she gained popularity from her acting. She started her own entertainment company, Maverick, which includes a record label. Madonna has also worked in fashion, written children's books, and owned health clubs. She supports charities and founded the Ray of Light Foundation in 1998. She is the best-selling female music artist of all time, with over 300 million record sales. According to Billboard, she has the most number-one hits by a female artist in several countries. Madonna is the highest-grossing solo touring artist, earning over $1.4 billion from concerts. She was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2008 and ranked as one of the greatest artists and songwriters of all time by Rolling Stone and VH1.

Love & Basketball is a 2000 American movie about romance and basketball. It was made by 40 Acres and a Mule Filmworks. Sanaa Lathan and Omar Epps star in the film. The movie is about Quincy McCall, played by Omar Epps, and Monica Wright, played by Sanaa Lathan. They are neighbors in Los Angeles and play basketball. They fall in love. The film was directed by Gina Prince-Bythewood, who also wrote the screenplay. Love & Basketball came out on April 21, 2000, in the United States. Critics liked the movie.
The duped journalist is a 1914 Hungarian silent film. Alexander Korda and Gyula Zilahi directed it.

Like other "Super Smash Bros." games, "Super Smash Bros. for Nintendo 3DS" and "Super Smash Bros. for Wii U" are not traditional fighting games. In these games, players use different attacks to make their opponents weaker and knock them out of the arena. Both games have characters, items, music, and game areas from various Nintendo and some third-party games. They started making these games in 2012 and officially announced them at E3 in 2013. The gameplay is between the faster, more competitive "Super Smash Bros. Melee" and the slower, more casual "Super Smash Bros. Brawl." New features include up to eight players fighting at once in the Wii U version, support for Nintendo's amiibo, playing as custom Mii characters, and downloading new fighters and arenas. Some old features, like the story mode in "Brawl," were removed. Critics liked the improved gameplay but had some complaints about online play. Both versions were popular, with over nine million 3DS copies sold by December 2017, and over five million Wii U copies sold in the same period. After these games, "Super Smash Bros. Ultimate" came out for the Nintendo Switch in 2018.
Beverly Hills is a city in McLennan County, Texas, United States. The 2010 census showed a population of 1,995. It is surrounded by Waco and is part of the Waco metropolitan area.

Pir Sultan Abdul (around 1480-1550) was a Turkish Alevi poet. He used simple and clear language, had a rich imagination, and wrote beautiful verses. People loved him because of this. Pir Sultan Abdul talked about everyday life, religion, and important people in Islam like God, Prophet Muhammad, Imam Ali, and the twelve Imams. He also wrote about love, peace, and fighting against unfair rulers. Because of his rebellion against authority, he had problems with the Ottoman government.
Frances Winfield was an American writer and speaker.

Guttet and Feschel are two villages that merged to form the municipality of Guttet-Feschel. This happened in 2000. Guttet-Feschel is in the district of Leuk, which is in the canton of Valais, Switzerland.
Carol Greitzer, born on January 3, 1925, is an American politician. She served in the New York City Council from 1969 to 1991. She was also the first president of Naral Pro-Choice America.
Midland City is a town in Dale County, Alabama, United States. The 2010 U.S. Census showed a population of 2,344. It became a town in 1890. It is part of the Ozark micropolitan area.

Marian Jurczyk, born on October 16, 1935, and died on December 30, 2014, was a Polish politician and activist for the Solidarity trade union. He was a senator in Poland's senate from 1997 to 2000. From November 18, 1998, to January 24, 2000, he was the mayor of Szczecin. He was elected mayor again on November 21, 2002, and served until December 4, 2006. People criticized his achievements and blamed him for paying over 10 million zlotys because the city canceled a land sale deal. They also criticized him for his lack of formal education and his mistakes, such as forgetting the name of the deputy he just nominated or quoting Jesus in a speech to the council. Because of these criticisms, there were calls to recall him. On March 23, 2004, the necessary 32,000 signatures were collected. A recall referendum took place on May 23, 2004. However, only 19% of voters cast their ballots, not reaching the required 30% turnout. Despite this, 92% of those who voted wanted Jurczyk to be recalled.

Irvinton is a town in Lancaster County, Virginia, United States. It had 432 people in the 2010 census. Irvinton is on a piece of land called the Northern Neck. It is an historic district. From 1889 to 1907, there was a school called the Chesapeake Academy in Irvinton. One of its students, Claybrook Cottingham, later became the assistant principal at the same school. He also became the president of Louisiana College in Pineville and Louisiana Tech University in Ruston during his long teaching career.

Rafael Alkorta Martínez was born on September 16, 1968. He was a Spanish footballer who mainly played as a central defender. He is now the sporting director of Athletic Bilbao. Alkorta played for Athletic Bilbao and Real Madrid for 17 years. He played in 370 La Liga matches and scored 8 goals. He won three trophies with Real Madrid. During the 1990s, Alkorta played in three World Cups with the Spanish national team.
Hideo Tanaka can be about: -

Topfreedom is a movement that wants to change laws. It aims to let women be topless in public places where men can be bare-chested. This is to make things fair for both genders. The movement wants to remove laws that stop women from not wearing a top all the time in public. Also, topfreedom supporters want to allow mothers to feed their babies in public without covering up.
Leandro Damián Marcelo Grimi, born on February 9, 1985, is an Argentine football player. He plays as a left back for Club Atlético Huracán.
Ryland Heights is a city in Kentucky, in the United States. It is in Kenton County. The population was 1,022 in 2010, an increase from 799 in 2000. It is part of the Cincinnati metropolitan area.

The Gibson Les Paul is a solid body electric guitar first sold by Gibson in 1952. It was designed by Gibson’s president, Ted McCarty, and factory manager, John Huis, with help from guitarist Les Paul. It usually has a solid mahogany body with a carved maple top, a mahogany neck, a rosewood fretboard, two pickups with separate volume and tone controls, and a stoptail bridge. Some versions have different designs. When it first came out, it had a gold finish and two P-90 pickups. In 1957, humbucking pickups were added. Sunburst finishes were introduced in 1958. The 1958-1960 sunburst Les Paul became popular but had low sales. In 1961, the Les Paul was redesigned into the Gibson SG. The original single-cutaway Les Paul design was reintroduced in 1968. Since then, many versions of Les Paul guitars have been made. The Les Paul, along with Fender’s Telecaster and Stratocaster, was one of the first mass-produced solid-body electric guitars. These guitars are versatile and have been used in many music genres like rock, country, pop, soul, rhythm and blues, blues, jazz, reggae, punk, and heavy metal.

Ioannis Veryvakis was a Greek army officer. He became a full general. He was the chief of the Hellenic Army General Staff and the Hellenic National Defence General Staff. He was born on November 3, 1930, and died on June 19, 2019.

Anna Jókai (Hungarian: "Jókai Anna") was a Hungarian author, poet, and teacher. She started writing in 1974. In the 1980s, she joined a movement to free Hungary. From 1990 to 1992, she led the Hungarian Writers' Union.

Hans Schneider was born on January 24, 1927, in Vienna, Austria, and died on October 28, 2014. He was a British-American mathematician. Schneider was a professor at the University of Wisconsin–Madison. He was the first president of the International Matrix Group from 1987 to 1990 and its successor, the International Linear Algebra Society, from 1990 to 1996. The society started the Hans Schneider Prize in 1993. Schneider was a founding editor of "Linear Algebra and its Applications" from 1968 to 1972 and then served as editor-in-chief from 1972 to 2012. He also worked as an advisory editor for the "Electronic Journal of Linear Algebra." Schneider earned his Ph.D. from the University of Edinburgh in 1952, with Alexander Craig Aitken as his advisor. He taught at Queen's University of Belfast until 1959, then moved to the University of Wisconsin, where he retired in 1993. Schneider wrote over 160 research papers. His research covered topics like Perron Frobenius theory, inertia theory, and max algebra. He experienced the Kindertransport in 1938-1940. Schneider passed away from cancer at 87 years old. He is the grandfather of YouTube musician/producer Kurt Hugo Schneider.

Lohengrin is a character in German Arthurian stories. He is the son of Parzival (also known as Percival) and a knight of the Holy Grail. Lohengrin arrives in a boat pulled by swans to save a lady who cannot ask his name. This story comes from Wolfram von Eschenbach's "Parzival." Later, two other stories added more details to Wolfram's tale. In 1848, Richard Wagner created an opera called "Lohengrin" based on this legend.

Barbour County is in north-central West Virginia, USA. In 2010, it had 16, 589 people. The county seat is Philippi, which was established in 1844. Both the county and the city are named after Philip Pendleton Barbour (1783-1841), a U.S. congressman from Virginia and an associate justice of the U.S. Supreme Court. Barbour County was created in 1843 when the area was still part of Virginia. In 1871, a small part of Barbour County was given to Tucker County. The Battle of Philippi, also known as the "Philippi Races," took place in Barbour County on June 3, 1861. Although small, it is considered the first land battle of the American Civil War. Alderson Broaddus University is in the county. Its physician assistant program is one of the oldest and best in the world.

Africa is the second-largest and second-most populated continent after Asia. It covers about 30.3 million square kilometers and has around 1 billion people, making up about 16% of the world's population. Africa's population is young, with an average age of 19.7 years in 2012, compared to the world's average of 30.4 years. Despite having many natural resources, Africa is the least wealthy continent per person, possibly because of past European colonization. However, recent economic growth and its large, young population make it an important market globally. Africa is surrounded by the Mediterranean Sea to the north, the Red Sea to the northeast, the Indian Ocean to the southeast, and the Atlantic Ocean to the west. It includes Madagascar and several archipelagos. Africa has 54 fully recognized countries, eight territories, and two self-governing states with limited recognition. Algeria is the largest country by area, and Nigeria has the most people. The African Union, headquartered in Addis Ababa, helps countries work together. Africa spans the equator and includes different climates. The majority of the continent and its countries are in the northern hemisphere, with a significant portion in the southern hemisphere. Africa is known for its biodiversity and megafauna. It faces environmental issues like desertification, deforestation, and water scarcity, which are expected to worsen due to climate change. Africa, especially eastern parts, is considered the origin of humans and great apes. The first human remains, found in Ethiopia, South Africa, and Morocco, date back to around 200,000, 259,000, and 300,000 years ago, respectively. Early human civilizations like ancient Egypt and Phoenicia emerged in North Africa. Over the centuries, Africa developed a diverse mix of ethnicities, cultures, and languages. The last 400 years saw increased European influence, starting in the 16th century, driven by trade and the transatlantic slave trade, which led to large African populations in the Americas. In the late 19th century, most of Africa was colonized by European countries, which ended in the 20th century through decolonization.

Human cloning is creating a copy of a human, exactly like the original. This term usually refers to making copies through artificial means, such as reproducing human cells and tissues. It doesn't mean identical twins, who come from natural conception. Cloning a person has caused many debates. Because of these debates, some countries have made laws about cloning and its legality. There are two main types of human cloning people often talk about: "therapeutic cloning" and "reproductive cloning." Therapeutic cloning means using cloned cells for medical treatments and transplants. Scientists are researching this, but it's not used in medicine yet. Researchers use methods like somatic-cell nuclear transfer and pluripotent stem cell induction. Reproductive cloning aims to create a whole cloned human, not just cells or tissues.
Dorothea Sally Eilers was an actress from the United States. She lived from December 11, 1908, to January 5, 1978.

A satellite state is a country that looks independent but is actually strongly influenced or controlled by another, more powerful country. This term is like describing smaller planets orbiting around a bigger one. It was mainly used for countries in Central and Eastern Europe during the Cold War, like those in the Warsaw Pact, and for Mongolia and Tannu Tuva from 1924 to 1990. For Central and Eastern European countries, it meant they were under the control of the Soviet Union. Sometimes, the term is also used for other countries, such as North Korea during the Korean War and Cuba after joining Comecon in 1972. In general, this term shows strong ideological and military support, while "puppet state" suggests political and military dependence, and "neo-colony" points to economic dependence. Depending on which type of control is focused on, a country might fit into more than one category.

The car-free movement is a broad, informal group of people and organizations, like social activists, urban planners, and transportation experts. They believe that cars and other motorized vehicles are too common in most cities. The movement aims to reduce or eliminate the use of cars by changing roads and parking spaces into areas for other activities. They want cities to become smaller and more compact, making it easy to reach most places by walking, cycling, public transport, or other means of personal transportation.

George Peter Alexander Healy was an American portrait painter. He lived from July 15, 1813, to June 24, 1894. Healy was very productive and popular. Many important people of his time posed for his paintings.

Fort Wayne is a city in Indiana, in the United States. It is in the northeastern part of the state, near the borders with Ohio and Michigan. In 2010, it had about 253, 691 people living there, making it the second-largest city in Indiana after Indianapolis, and the 75th-largest city in the U.S. Fort Wayne is the main city in a larger area that includes Allen, Wells, and Whitley counties, with a population of about 419, 453 in 2011. It is a cultural and economic center for northeastern Indiana. Fort Wayne was built in 1794 by the U.S. Army, named after General Anthony Wayne, who led the American Revolutionary War. The settlement grew where the St. Joseph, St. Marys, and Maumee rivers meet, becoming a trading place for pioneers. It was officially laid out in 1823 and grew a lot after the Wabash and Erie Canal and railroads were completed. In the 21st century, Fort Wayne’s economy focuses on distribution, transportation, logistics, healthcare, business services, leisure, and finance. It has jobs in defense and healthcare, with major providers like Parkview Health and Lutheran Health Network. Fort Wayne has won the All-America City Award in 1982, 1998, and 2009, and got an Outstanding Achievement City Livability Award in 1999.

Matthias Lukas Ginter was born on January 19, 1994. He is a German football player who plays as a centre back. He plays for Borussia Mönchengladbach in the Bundesliga and also for the Germany national team.

Whyatt Mondesire was a reporter at the Philadelphia Inquirer. He later became the owner of the Philadelphia Sun newspaper and served as the president of the Philadelphia branch of the NAACP for more than ten years. He was born on October 14, 1949, and passed away on October 4, 2015.
A consumer is someone who buys or uses items like goods, products, or services for personal, social, family, or household needs. They do not buy these things to use in a business.
wide awake or awake means someone who is fully awake.

Peristeri is a suburb in the northwestern part of Athens, Greece. It has about 139,981 people living there, which makes it the seventh-largest city in Greece by population. The word "peristeri" means "pigeon" or "dove" in Greek.
The national emblem of Algeria is a seal used by the government. It is like the coat of arms used by other countries.

Ana Lila Downs Sánchez, born on September 9, 1968, is a Mexican singer-songwriter and actress. She performs her own songs and those of others in different music genres, including traditional and popular Mexican music. She also uses music from indigenous Mexican cultures, recording in languages like Mixtec, Zapotec, Mayan, Nahuatl, and Purépecha. Born and raised in Oaxaca, she studied at the Oaxaca Institute of Arts and briefly attended the University of Minnesota before focusing on her music career. She started performing in Oaxaca City's traditional music scene. Her first album, "Ofrenda," came out in 1994. In 1999, her album "La Sandunga" gained popularity and was a big success. In 2001, her album "Border" brought her international fame. Her album "Pecados y Milagros" in 2011 topped charts in many countries. "Balas y Chocolate" was released in 2015, and "Salón Lágrimas y Deseo" followed in 2017. Downs started performing in school, showing her ability with traditional, Latin, and American music, and her own style. A native Spanish speaker, she also speaks Mixtec and English. Downs is very active in preserving indigenous Mexican languages, especially Mixtec. She was inspired by artists like Chavela Vargas, Mercedes Sosa, Lucha Villa, and Amparo Ochoa. Downs is known for her colorful, diverse, and unique contributions to the music industry, often wearing traditional indigenous Mexican styles. She has won one Grammy and three Latin Grammy awards. Besides music, she works on helping people and causes, especially those affecting indigenous communities in Latin America.

Stephen Wochy, born Wojciechowski on December 25, 1922, is a Canadian retired ice hockey player. He played 54 games for the Detroit Red Wings in the National Hockey League. Wochy was born in Fort William, Ontario. After Jim Conacher died in April 2020, he became the oldest living former NHL player. Before joining the NHL, Wochy played for the Port Arthur Bearcats in 1942 and was part of the 1942 Allan Cup. After leaving the NHL, he played 10 seasons in the American Hockey League for the Indianapolis Capitals, Philadelphia Rockets, Cleveland Barons, and Buffalo Bisons. In 1952, he was named a first-team AHL all-star.

Diving Machine G5 is a roller coaster at Janfusun Fancyworld in Taiwan. It was built in 2000 by Swiss manufacturers Bolliger & Mabillard. It is the second dive coaster model, with the first being Oblivion at Alton Towers in the UK. Located in the Sky Plaza section, it looks very similar to Oblivion. Diving Machine G5 gets its name from the strong g-forces felt during the drop. Like Insane Speed, it has no theme. Among the roller coasters at the park, it is one of three, along with Ku Ku Roller Coaster. Diving Machine G5 is near the entrance, so it has long lines in the morning and shorter waits in the afternoon and evening.

Patmos is a town in Hempstead County, Arkansas, United States. It had 64 people in the 2010 count. This town shares its name with a Greek island where the Book of Revelation was written. Patmos is part of the Hope micropolitan area.

James W. Hardy III was born on December 24, 1985, and played American football as a wide receiver. He was picked by the Buffalo Bills in the second round of the 2008 NFL draft. He also played for the Baltimore Ravens. Before his professional career, he played college football at Indiana University until June 7, 2017.

Mackenzie Christine Foy, born on November 10, 2000, is an American actress and model. She is famous for playing Renesmee Cullen in the 2012 movie. For this role, she got nominated for a Young Artist Award as Best Supporting Young Actress in a Feature Film. She also played Murphy in the 2014 space movie Interstellar. For her performance, she won a Saturn Award for Best Performance by a Younger Actor. She has been in other movies like The Nutcracker and the Four Realms, where she played Clara.

In the 1935–36 NHL season, it was the 19th year of the National Hockey League. The St. Louis Eagles left the league, reducing the number of teams to eight. The Detroit Red Wings won the Stanley Cup by beating the Toronto Maple Leafs in four games.
Koenigsegg Automotive AB makes high-performance sports cars. They are based in Ängelholm, Skåne County, Sweden.

Jonsered is a small town in Partille municipality, Västra Götaland county, Sweden. It had 930 people living there in 2010. Jonsered is an old industrial town near the Säve River outside of Gothenburg. In 1834, a man named William Gibson, from Scotland, started factories in Jonsered. The first big product was sail canvas. In 1856, the first Swedish state railway between Gothenburg and Jonsered was opened and later extended to Stockholm. The Gibson family controlled the town until the 1920s, but the company continued to be the main force in the area. They owned most of the land until the 1970s. By the 1880s, the company began making wood-processing machines, which are still their main products today. In the 1950s, they started making chainsaws, which became very popular worldwide. This helped the company when the textile industry closed in the late 1960s. Jonsered was then owned by Electrolux, which moved production to Husqvarna in 1984. After the company closed, Jonsered became a suburb for people who work in Gothenburg or Partille. You can reach Jonsered by train, which has a station that opened in 2000.

Alfredo Félix Alcón, born on March 3, 1930, in Buenos Aires, was an Argentine actor who worked in theater and films. He is considered one of the best and most important Argentine actors of the 20th century. He began his film career in 1955 with the movie "Love Never Dies." He acted in over 50 films and received several awards, including the Silver Condor, the Martin Fierro Award, and the 1981 Diamond Konex Award. He passed away on April 11, 2014, at the age of 84.

Uzbekistan joined the Olympic Games as an independent country in 1994. They have sent athletes to every game since then. Before that, Uzbek athletes competed as part of the Soviet Union from 1952 to 1988. After the Soviet Union ended, Uzbekistan joined the unified team in 1992. Uzbek athletes have won 26 medals in summer Olympics, mostly in wrestling and boxing. They also won one medal in winter Olympics. Uzbekistan's national Olympic committee was formed in 1992 and recognized by the International Olympic Committee in 1993.

Richard Andrew Gephardt, born on January 31, 1941, is an American politician. He was a U.S. representative from Missouri from 1977 to 2005. Gephardt was a Democrat and served as House Majority Leader from 1989 to 1995 and Minority Leader from 1995 to 2003. He tried but failed to become the Democratic presidential nominee in 1988 and 2004. Gephardt was considered for the vice presidential nomination in 1988, 1992, 2000, 2004, and 2008. After leaving politics, Gephardt became a lobbyist. He started a firm called Gephardt Government Affairs in Washington and another called The Gephardt Group in Atlanta. He also worked for DLA Piper, FTI Consulting, and Goldman Sachs. Gephardt is part of the Reformers Caucus of Issue One.

Brendan Halligan was born on July 5, 1936, and passed away on August 9, 2020. He was an Irish economist and politician. Halligan started and led the Institute of International and European Affairs, a think tank focusing on European and international matters. He was also the president of the Ireland China Institute, an independent think tank in Dublin that began in October 2019. His career included work in both the Irish public sector and the private sector. At different times, he served as the general secretary of the Labour Party, a Teachta Dála (TD), a senator, and a Member of the European Parliament (MEP).

Robert Costanza was born on September 14, 1950. He is from America and Australia. Costanza is an ecological economist and teaches public policy at the Crawford School of Public Policy in Australia. He is also part of the Academy of the Social Sciences in Australia and the Club of Rome.

Ofter schwang is a town in southern Germany, in Oberallgäu, Bavaria. It hosts professional winter sports events, like World Cup alpine skiing. Ofter schwang is also known for skiing and other sports. The area has traditionally been agricultural. The town has a church with a World War II memorial and small chapels. Tourism is important in the region. People come for skiing in winter and hiking, mountain biking, and parachute flying in summer. Another attraction is the "dorfsabend," a traditional village evening with Bavarian costumes, dancing, food, and beer.

José Sarney de Araújo Costa, born José Ribamar Ferreira de Araújo Costa, was born on April 24, 1930. He is a Brazilian politician, lawyer, and writer. Sarney was the 31st president of Brazil, serving from April 21, 1985, to March 15, 1990. He is the oldest living former president of Brazil, and before João Figueiredo died in 1999, he was one of only two living former presidents who were not elected directly by the people. The other is Michel Temer. Sarney started his political career in the 1950s in his home state of Maranhão. He was part of a group of young politicians known as the "bossa nova generation." They wanted to clean up the government and stop corruption. During the military rule in Brazil, Sarney joined the government party Arena. In 1979, he became the president of the party. When the military regime ended, Arena split. Sarney joined the opposing group and helped form the Liberal Front Party. He ran for vice-president with Tancredo Neves, who was from the PMDB party. Neves won the election, but died before taking office. Sarney became president. He was very popular at first, but his popularity dropped because of the country's economic problems and a failed plan to reduce inflation. His time as president is remembered as difficult. Over time, Sarney and his family gained a lot of power in Maranhão. People see him as the most important of Brazil's political leaders. He owns the biggest newspapers and TV stations in Maranhão and still has a lot of influence there. He has been accused of giving jobs to family members and of corruption. In 2009, The Economist called his election as president of the senate a victory for a "semi-feudal" system. A columnist from Veja magazine said Sarney was the perfect example of a political leader who controls the local area using family and friends. Sarney is also a good writer and a member of the Brazilian Academy of Letters.

The Louisville/Jefferson County Metro Government Balance is a statistical area in Kentucky. It represents part of the city-county that includes unincorporated areas. Before 2003, this area was the city of Louisville. The Balance does not include the 83 separate cities within the larger region. In 2010, the Balance had 597,337 people, while the whole metro area had 741,096 people. This area is part of the Louisville-Jefferson County, KY-IN Metropolitan Statistical Area.
Frank Fakaotimanava Lui, born on November 19, 1935, was a former premier of Niue, a Pacific island country.

Selhurst Park is a football stadium in Selhurst, a part of Croydon in London. Crystal Palace Football Club plays there. The stadium opened in 1924, designed by Archibald Leitch. It hosted an international football match and games for the 1948 Summer Olympics. A part of the stadium has a Sainsbury's store. From 1985 to 1991, Charlton Athletic shared the stadium. Then, from 1991 to 2003, Wimbledon shared it.

The Cheongyang chili pepper, also known as dang jo cheongyang, is a medium-sized chilli from South Korea. It has a heat level of 10,000 on the Scoville scale, making it spicier than regular Korean chili peppers. This pepper is a speciality of Cheongyang County. It was developed by Dr. Yoo Il-woong by mixing local Jejudo chili with Thai chili. When unripe, the peppers can be light purple or green, but they turn deep red as they mature. Even when dried, the peppers stay dark red.
grimbosq is a commune in Calvados, which is in Normandy, a region in northwestern France.

Saliva, also known as spit, is a fluid made by the salivary glands in the mouth. In humans, it is mostly water with small amounts of electrolytes, mucus, white blood cells, epithelial cells, enzymes like amylase and lipase, and agents that fight bacteria. These enzymes help start the digestion of starches and fats in food. They also help clean food particles from between teeth, protecting them from decay. Saliva helps by making food wet, which starts the swallowing process, and keeps the mouth moist. Different animals use saliva in special ways. Some swifts use their sticky saliva to build nests. Certain snakes, like cobras and vipers, use venomous saliva through their fangs to hunt. Some caterpillars produce silk from saliva stored in their glands.
Schortens was an independent municipality and is now a town in the Friesland district of Lower Saxony, Germany.

The British Rail class 52 was a group of 74 diesel-hydraulic trains made for the western region of British railways between 1961 and 1964. Each train had a two-word name, starting with "Western." So, these trains were called Westerns.
Springdale is a city in Hamilton County, Ohio, United States. It is near Cincinnati. According to the 2010 census, the population was 11,223.

Larkana district is in the Sindh province of Pakistan. Its main city is Larkana. Larkana was the home district of two former Pakistani prime ministers, Zulfikar Ali Bhutto and Benazir Bhutto. It is also where Mumtaz Ali Bhutto, a former chief minister of Sindh, was from. Actress Sohai Ali Abro and folk singer Abida Parveen are also from Larkana. There is a cricket team called the Larkana Bulls, which was formed in 2013. Other towns in the district include Ratodero, Dokri, Bakrani, and Naodero. In 2005, under Prime Minister Pervez Musharraf, the district was split into two new districts: Qamber and Shahdadkot.

"The Cat in the Hat" is a storybook for children. It was written and drawn by Theodor Geisel, known as Dr. Seuss, and came out in 1957. The story is about a tall, cat-shaped character in a red and white-striped hat and a red bow tie. One rainy day, when Sally and her brother's mother is not at home, the cat visits them. Despite what their fish says, the cat shows the kids some tricks to keep them entertained. In doing so, he and his friends, Thing One and Thing Two, make a mess of the house. The kids and the fish get worried until the cat uses a cleaning machine to tidy everything up, then leaves just before their mother comes home. Geisel wrote this book to help kids learn to read. A man named William Spaulding, who Geisel met during the war, asked him to make a fun primer. Though Geisel was working with Random House, Houghton Mifflin agreed to publish an educational version for schools, while Random House released a version for stores. Geisel said he created the book by choosing the first two rhyming words from a word list, which were "cat" and "hat." The book was very popular right from the start, and by 1960, it had sold over a million copies. It ranked ninth on "Publishers Weekly's" list of best-selling children's books of all time. The book's success led to the creation of Beginner Books, a company that makes similar books for young readers. Geisel was proud of this book because it helped end the use of traditional primers like "Dick and Jane." It was also turned into a 1971 animated TV show and a 2003 movie.

The Eurocopter (now Airbus Helicopters) EC120 Colibri, nicknamed "Hummingbird," is a small, five-seat helicopter with one engine. It was created by Eurocopter, CATIC, Harbin Aviation Industries, and ST Aerospace at a facility in France. Eurocopter assembled the EC120B in France and Australia. In China, it is made by Harbin Aircraft Manufacturing Corporation as the HC120. In 2004, Harbin started making the HC120 in Harbin, a city in northern China. In China, both the army and local police have bought these helicopters.

Nigel John Taylor, born on June 20, 1960, is an English musician, singer, songwriter, producer, and actor. He was a founding member of Duran Duran, a popular new romantic band. Duran Duran became famous in the 1980s because their music videos were shown a lot on MTV. Taylor played bass guitar for Duran Duran from 1978 to 1997. After leaving the band, he made twelve solo albums and had a role in the movie "Sugar Town." He also appeared in several other films. In 2001, Taylor rejoined Duran Duran with the original members, and he is still with the band. The current members of Duran Duran are Simon Le Bon (singer), John Taylor (bass guitar), Nick Rhodes (synthesizer), and Roger Taylor (drums). Taylor was also part of two supergroups: The Power Station and Neurotic Outsiders.

Last of the Summer Wine is a British TV show created by Roy Clarke. It aired from 1973 to 2010 on BBC. The first episode came out on January 4, 1973. Alan J. W. Bell produced and directed it from 1983 to 2010. The show ended on August 29, 2010. All 295 episodes have been released on DVD. It's shown on TV channels like Gold, Yesterday, and Drama in the UK. The show is also broadcast in over 25 countries, including some PBS stations in the US and VisionTV in Canada. Last of the Summer Wine was set in Holmfirth, West Yorkshire, England. It followed three old men and their funny adventures. Bill Owen played Compo Simmons, Peter Sallis played Norman Clegg, and Michael Bates played Cyril Blamire. Bates left in 1976, so Brian Wilde, Michael Aldridge, and Frank Thornton took turns playing the third man. The men never seemed to grow up and saw their town and its people in a funny way. The show's main trio was joined by other characters over time, making it an ensemble piece. These characters had their own jokes and storylines. After Bill Owen died in 1999, Tom Owen, Keith Clifford, and Brian Murphy took over the roles. A new younger trio formed during the 30th series, with actors Russ Abbot, Luther Hobdyke, and Brian Murphy. Peter Sallis and Frank Thornton continued in supporting roles. Though some thought the show's quality declined, it was still popular. It was praised for its positive image of older people and family-friendly humor. Members of the royal family liked it. The show won awards and had many specials, including 21 Christmas specials, three TV films, and a documentary. It inspired other adaptations, like prequels, novelizations, and stage plays.

The museum about Japanese currency is located in front of the Bank of Japan building in Chūō, Tokyo. It opened in November 1985. In 2010, there was an exhibition of wallets from the Edo period (1603-1867) and the Meiji era (1868-1912).

Charles Henry Pitman Sr. was born on October 20, 1935, and passed away on February 13, 2020. He was a lieutenant general in the United States Marine Corps. In this role, he helped with aviation matters. He retired in 1990. He died from cancer in 2020. He was also part of an important operation called Eagle Claw in 1980.

Gerardus Mercator, a Flemish geographer and cartographer, created the Mercator projection in 1569. This map shows directions and shapes accurately, making it useful for navigation. North is always up and south is always down. The projection stretches areas away from the equator, making them appear larger than they are. This stretching is small near the equator but becomes more significant as you get closer to the poles. For example, Greenland and Antarctica appear much larger on the map than they actually are, while regions near the equator, like Central Africa, appear smaller.

Shakargarh is the capital of Shakargarh tehsil and is a city in the northeast part of Narowal district, Punjab, Pakistan. It is next to Jammu to the north and Sialkot to the west. The city's literacy rate is over 85%, the highest in the tehsil. Shakargarh is at 32°16'N 75°10'E and sits on the western side of the Ravi River. The tehsil is divided into 35 union councils, with three of them forming the capital city, Shakargarh.

Madeleine Vionnet was a French fashion designer born on June 22, 1876, in Loiret, France, and passed away on March 2, 1975. She trained in London before moving back to Paris in 1912 to open her first fashion house. Her house had to close in 1914 during World War I but reopened after the war. Vionnet became a leading designer in Paris between 1919 and 1939. She had to close her fashion house in 1939 and retired in 1940. Known as the "queen of the bias cut" and "the architect among dressmakers," Vionnet is famous for her elegant Grecian-style dresses and for introducing the bias cut to the fashion world. Her work has inspired many recent designers.
Kuthwal is one of 51 union councils in Abbottabad district in Pakistan's Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa province. It is situated to the northwest of Abbottabad city, which is the district capital.

Whidbey Island, also spelled Whidby, Whitbey, or Whitby, is the biggest island in Island County, Washington, in the United States. The other large island is Camano Island, which is to the east. Whidbey Island is about north of Seattle and sits between the Olympic Peninsula and the I-5 corridor. It borders Puget Sound to the south. The island has Naval Air Station Whidbey Island. Whidbey Island has about 67,000 people living there, according to the 2000 census. About 29,000 people live in rural areas. The island is about long if measured along roads from the northernmost to the southernmost point, or about from north to south. Whidbey Island is about wide and covers an area of land, making it the 40th largest island in the United States. It is the fourth longest and fourth largest island in the contiguous United States, after Long Island, New York; Padre Island, Texas; and Isle Royale, Michigan. In Washington state, it is the largest island, followed by Orcas Island.

Blount County is a county in Alabama, U.S. The 2010 census showed it had 57,322 people. Its main town is Oneonta. Blount County allows alcohol sales in some areas since 2013. In 2012, residents voted against allowing alcohol sales county-wide, but smaller towns did allow it. Blount County is known as the "Covered Bridge Capital of Alabama." It has more historic covered bridges than any other county in the state. Every autumn, Oneonta hosts a Covered Bridge Festival to celebrate the remaining three covered bridges.

Hermann Baumann was born on January 23, 1921. He is a retired Swiss wrestler who competed in freestyle wrestling. Hermann won a bronze medal in the lightweight class at the 1948 Summer Olympics in London.

John Norman Haynes was born on October 17, 1934, and passed away on October 18, 2005. He was an English football player. Haynes played 56 times for his national team and led the team as captain in 22 matches. He was chosen for three World Cup squads, playing in the last two. Known as "the maestro," his playing style was praised for his ability to pass with both feet, his vision, and his skillful touch. Haynes is considered Fulham's greatest player, staying with the club for 20 years without winning a major trophy, although he reached the FA Cup semi-finals twice. He became the first player to earn £100 a week after the £20 wage limit was lifted in 1961. Haynes also played for Toronto City on loan in 1961 and finished his career at Durban City, where he won the only trophy of his career.

Yoshihide Kozai, born on April 1, 1928, and died on February 5, 2018, was a Japanese astronomer who studied celestial mechanics. He is famous for discovering the Kozai mechanism, which he found at the same time as Michael Lidov. For this, he received the Imperial Prize from the Japan Academy in 1979. From 1988 to 1991, he was the president of the International Astronomical Union. In 1989, he got the Brouwer Award from the American Astronomical Society. In 2009, he was honored with the Decoration of Cultural Merit by the Japanese government. He passed away because of liver problems. An asteroid was named 3040 Kozai in his honor.
planomicrobium flavidum is a type of bacteria from the planomicrobium group. It was found in a marine salt pond.

Sir Joshua Reynolds lived from July 1723 to February 1792. He was an English painter, mainly known for painting portraits. John Russell thought he was one of the most important painters in Europe during the 18th century. Reynolds promoted the "grand style" in painting, which meant making imperfect things look perfect. He started the Royal Academy of Arts and became its first president. King George III knighted him in 1769.

Chicka Chicka Boom Boom is a popular children's book. Bill Martin Jr. and John Archambault wrote it, and Lois Ehlert illustrated it. It came out in 1989 with Simon & Schuster. The book has letters that can act like people. It appeared on The New York Times best seller list for children's books in 2000.

This list includes names of cities, towns, unincorporated communities, counties, and recognized places in New York. It also shows which counties each place is in, and the lower and upper zip code ranges, if available.

Andrus Ansip, born on October 1, 1956, is an Estonian politician. He is a member of the European Parliament. From 2005 to 2014, he was the prime minister of Estonia. He was also the European Commissioner for Digital Single Market and vice president of the European Commission, starting in 2014. Before his political career, Ansip trained as a chemist and worked in banking and business. He joined the parliament in 2004 and became the minister of economic affairs. In April 2005, he became prime minister. Ansip was appointed to the European Commission on November 1, 2014.

Lynching is when a group kills someone outside of the legal system. It usually involves a mob punishing someone they think has done something wrong, whether the person is officially convicted or not. Sometimes, it's used to scare people. These killings are often public and can include hanging as a way to scare others. Such acts happen in many places. In the U.S., lynchings of African Americans were common in the southern states after the Reconstruction Era, especially when race relations were very bad. Today, lynchings still occur in some countries, especially those with high crime rates like Brazil, Guatemala, and South Africa.

The King and I is the fifth musical by composers Richard Rodgers and lyricist Oscar Hammerstein II. It is based on Margaret Landon's novel "Anna and the King of Siam," which is from Anna Leonowens' memoirs. Anna Leonowens was a British teacher who worked for King Mongkut of Siam in the 1860s. The musical tells Anna's story as she helps modernize Siam. There is conflict and unspoken love between the king and Anna. The musical first appeared on Broadway on March 29, 1951, and was very successful, lasting nearly three years. It has been performed many times since then. In 1950, Fanny Holtzmann, a theater lawyer, wanted to find a role for her client, Gertrude Lawrence. Holtzmann thought Landon's book would be perfect and contacted Rodgers and Hammerstein, who agreed to write the musical. They initially wanted Rex Harrison for the king's role but he was unavailable, so they chose Yul Brynner. The musical was a big hit and won several Tony Awards. Gertrude Lawrence died a year and a half after the opening, and other actresses took over Anna's role. The musical was also successful in London and on a U.S. tour. In 1956, a film version starring Yul Brynner was released, and the film won an Academy Award. Yul Brynner dominated the role in later tours and a 1985 Broadway run. Christopher Renshaw directed successful revivals on Broadway in 1996 and in the West End in 2000. Another Broadway revival in 2015 also won a Tony Award. Many professional and amateur performances of "The King and I" continue around the world.

Illapel is a city in Chile. It is the capital of the Choapa province, in the Coquimbo region. The city is next to the Illapel River and is the narrowest part of the country along a line 94 km long. It is located to the east of Los Vilos.

Michael Jagmin is an American singer. He is famous for being the main singer of a band called A Skylit Drive. He used to sing for a metal band named Odd Project. Jagmin is well-known for his high-pitched voice. He has a very high singing voice and can sing over three octaves.

Gillingham Football Club is a professional soccer team in Gillingham, a town in Kent, England. They play in League One, which is the third level of English soccer leagues. The club was started in 1893 and joined the Football League in 1920. In 1938, they left the league but returned 12 years later when the league had more teams. In the late 1980s, they nearly won a promotion to a higher league, but their performance declined. In 1993, they narrowly avoided going to a lower league. Between 2000 and 2005, they were in the second-tier league for the first time in their history, finishing eleventh in 2002–03.

Universal Studios Japan, located in Osaka, is one of six Universal Studios theme parks. It was opened on March 31, 2001, and is owned by a company called NBCUniversal. The park is similar to Universal Orlando Resort, with many of the same attractions. Over 11 million people visited the park in its first year, making it the fastest amusement park to reach 10 million visitors. Every year since, around 8 million people visit. Most visitors are from Japan, South Korea, and China, but it is also popular with Western tourists. In 2005, Goldman Sachs became the largest shareholder. To celebrate its tenth anniversary in 2011, the park had special events. By then, 88 million people had visited. In June 2012, there were 700,000 annual passport holders. In 2012, 9.75 million people visited, and in 2013, 10.5 million people visited. This increase was due to new rides and attractions, such as the Harry Potter-themed area that opened in July 2014. The park has added attractions like "Biohazard - The Real," "Monster Hunter - The Real," and "One Piece Premier Show." The Harry Potter-themed area, "Wizarding World of Harry Potter," opened in 2014 and welcomed its 100 millionth visitor in 2012. In 2014, it was ranked fifth among the top 25 amusement/theme parks worldwide. Due to the COVID-19 pandemic, the park was closed from February 27, 2020, until June 19, 2020.
Antony Passage is a small village in southeastern Cornwall, England, UK. It is next to the river Lynher. The Lynher is a part of the River Tamar. On the other side of the Lynher is Antony Village.

Daniel Hudson Burnham, born on September 4, 1846, and died on June 1, 1912, was an American architect and urban planner. He was part of the "Beaux-Arts" movement and is known as one of the most successful leaders in American architecture. As a successful architect in Chicago, he became the director of works for the 1892-93 World's Columbian Exposition, often called "the White City." He played key roles in planning for several cities, including Chicago, Manila, Baguio, and Washington, D.C. Additionally, he designed famous buildings such as skyscrapers in Chicago, the triangular Flatiron Building in New York City, Union Station in Washington D.C., Selfridges department store in London, and San Francisco's Merchants Exchange. While he is best known for his skyscrapers, city planning, and "the White City," almost one-third of his total work involved shopping buildings, covering 14.7 million square feet (1.37 million square meters).

Lexington is the second-largest city in Kentucky and the 60th-largest city in the United States. It is called the "horse capital of the world" and is in the heart of the state's bluegrass region. Some notable places in Lexington are the Kentucky Horse Park, the Red Mile and Keeneland race courses, Rupp Arena, Transylvania University, the University of Kentucky, and Bluegrass Community and Technical College. Many people in Lexington have gone to college: 39.5% have at least a bachelor's degree. In 2019, the city had 323,152 people, and the metro area had 517,056. By land area, Lexington is the 28th largest city in the United States. The city is part of Fayette County, and Fayette County is part of Lexington. Lexington has a mayor-council government, with 12 districts and three elected members. The person who gets the most votes becomes the vice mayor.

Ramón Gómez Castillo, known as Ramón Valdés, was a Mexican actor born on September 2, 1923, in Mexico City. He was part of a big family and moved to Ciudad Juárez when he was two years old. Ramón started acting in films in 1949, working alongside his brother Germán, who was famous as Tin-Tan. Ramón acted in many movies during the golden age of Mexican cinema. He had two other brothers who were also actors: Manuel, known as Manuel "El Loco" Valdés, and Antonio, known as El Ratón Valdés. In 1968, Ramón met Roberto Gómez Bolaños, known as Chespirito. They worked together on programs like "Los Supergenios de la Mesa Cuadrada," "Chespirito," and "El Chapulín Colorado." Ramón gained international fame for his role as Don Ramón in the sitcom "El Chavo del Ocho." He left the show in 1979 but returned for one last year in 1981. In 1982, Ramón starred in a Venezuelan sitcom called "Federrico" with Carlos Villagrán. He also appeared in "Ah Que Kiko" in 1987, but these programs were not as successful as expected. Ramón Valdés passed away on August 9, 1988.
Vezot is a commune in the Sarthe department, which is in the Pays de la Loire region of western France.

The secretary of defense (SecDef) is the leader of the United States Department of Defense, an executive department for the armed forces. The SecDef is second only to the president in command and authority over the U.S. military. This role is similar to a defense minister in other countries. The SecDef is chosen by the president, with the Senate's agreement. They are part of the cabinet and on the national security council. The SecDef has authority over the Department of Defense, as directed by the president. They are also the main helper to the president for Department of Defense matters. No one can be SecDef if they recently served as a regular military officer. Only the SecDef, president, or Congress can order military force transfers. The SecDef is in charge of all military branches: army, marine corps, navy, air force, and space force. The SecDef, along with the secretary of state, attorney general, and secretary of the treasury, is considered one of the four most important department heads. Since July 23, 2019, the SecDef has been Mark Esper, the 27th person to hold this position.

The Richmond football club, known as the tigers, is a professional Australian rules football team that plays in the Australian Football League (AFL), the top league for the sport. Formed in 1885 in the Richmond suburb of Melbourne, they competed in the Victorian Football Association (VFA) until 1907, winning two premierships. In 1908, Richmond joined the Victorian Football League (now called the AFL) and has since won twelve premierships, with their most recent win in 2019. The club's main training and headquarters are at the Punt Road Oval, next to the Melbourne Cricket Ground (MCG), where they play from 1965. Richmond wears black uniforms with a yellow strip. Their famous song, "We're from Tigerland," has a "yellow and black" chorus. The team is led by coach Damien Hardwick and captain Trent Cotchin. Five Richmond players, Kevin Bartlett, Jack Dyer, Royce Hart, Kevin Sheedy, and Ian Stewart, are in the Australian Football Hall of Fame as "legends" of the sport.

"Right Behind You (Mafia)" is a song by the Canadian alternative rock band Our Lady Peace. It came out in July 2001. This song was the third and last single from their fourth album, "Spiritual Machines." The song did not do well, leading to the end of its release and music video. It was also their last single with founding guitarist Mike Turner. During Mike Turner's absence, Matt Cameron from Pearl Jam played the drums. Our Lady Peace's drummer, Jeremy Taggart, was recovering from an injury at the time.

Rascal Flatts is an American country music group formed in Columbus, Ohio, in 1999. The group members are Gary Levox (lead vocals), Jay DeMarinis (bass guitar, background vocals), and Joe Don Rooney (lead guitar, background vocals). Jay DeMarinis is Gary Levox's second cousin and used to be in a Christian music duo called East to West. They made music for Disney's Lyric Street Records from 2000 to 2010. During this time, they released six albums, all certified platinum or higher by the Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA). Their albums were: "Rascal Flatts" (2000), "Melt" (2002), "Feels Like Today" (2004), "Me and My Gang" (2006), "Still Feels Good" (2007), and "Unstoppable" (2009). In 2010, they moved to Big Machine Records and made five more albums and a Christmas album: "Nothing Like This" (2010), "Changed" (2012), "Rewind" (2014), "The Greatest Gift of All" (2016), and "Back to Us" (2017). The group had 40 hit songs, 16 of which were number one on Billboard's Hot Country Songs, Country Airplay, or Canada Country charts. Their longest-lasting number one song was "Bless the Broken Road," which stayed there for five weeks in 2005. In 2006-2007, "What Hurts the Most" topped both the Hot Country Songs and Adult Contemporary charts, reaching number 6 on the Billboard Hot 100. On January 7, 2020, the band said they would stop making music after a farewell tour lasting 21 years. However, on May 19, 2020, the tour was cancelled due to the pandemic.
Bizen's original center was in the city of Okayama today. From a very early time, Bizen became one of Japan's main places for making swords.
Phillipsburg is a city in Phillips County, Kansas, United States. It is also the county seat. In 2010, the city had 2,581 people living there.

The Coral Sea is a part of the South Pacific Ocean, located off the northeast coast of Australia. It is considered an interim Australian bioregion. The Coral Sea stretches along Australia's northeast coast. During World War II, there was a major naval battle called the Battle of the Coral Sea between Japan and the United States and Australia. The Coral Sea has many islands and reefs, including the Great Barrier Reef (GBR), which is the world's largest reef system. In 1981, UNESCO declared the Great Barrier Reef a World Heritage Site. No oil exploration was allowed in the Great Barrier Reef since 1975, and fishing is limited in many areas. The Coral Sea's reefs and islands are very rich in bird and aquatic life, making it a popular tourist destination both within and outside of Australia.

A drumstick is a type of percussion mallet used to play the snare drum, drum kit, and some other percussion instruments. It is specifically used for unpitched percussion. Other specialized beaters, like the metal beater or "wand" used with a triangle, or mallets used with tuned percussion such as a xylophone and timpani, are not called drumsticks. Michael Lawrence Marrow, known as Phase 2 and Lonny Wood, was an American aerosol artist who worked in New York City. He was active in the 1970s and is known for creating the "bubble letter" style of aerosol writing, also called "softies." He also played an important role in the early hip hop scene.

Yandobinskoye is a rural settlement in Alikovsky District, Chuvash Republic, Russia. It is in the central part of the district. The administrative center is the village of Yandoba. In 2006, the rural settlement had about 1,081 people. Yandobinskoye includes twelve smaller rural areas. There is a road that goes through the settlement.

A rectifier is a device that changes alternating current (AC), which switches direction, into direct current (DC), which flows in one direction. This process is called "rectification." Rectifiers come in various forms, such as vacuum tubes, chemical cells, mercury valves, copper and selenium plates, semiconductor diodes, and silicon switches. Historically, even mechanical switches and motors have been used. Early crystal radios used a tiny wire on a crystal to act as a rectifier. Rectifiers are used in many ways, especially in power supplies and high-voltage direct current systems. They can also be used to detect radio signals and flames. Depending on the AC supply and circuit arrangement, additional smoothing is needed to produce a steady DC voltage. For devices like radios and computers, filters smooth the output to create a stable DC voltage. Reversing this process, changing DC back to AC, is called an inverter.

Virginia City is a town in Montana, United States. It is also the main town in Madison County. In 1961, Virginia City and the nearby area became a National Historic Landmark District called the Virginia City Historic District. In 2010, the town had 190 people living there.

Emily Bishop is a fictional character from the British TV show "Coronation Street." She is a long-time character, the oldest female one in the show. The character first appeared on December 21, 1960. At first, an unnamed actress played her in a small role. Eileen Derbyshire took over the role in January 1961. Derbyshire stopped acting as Emily on January 1, 2016, after 55 years. However, in August 2019, Derbyshire agreed to return briefly. She appeared for a short time on October 9, 2019, for a special event celebrating another character's birthday.

A nuclear submarine is a submarine that uses a nuclear reactor for power. It has many advantages over conventional submarines, which are typically powered by diesel engines. Nuclear submarines don't need to surface often because they don't rely on air. They can travel at high speeds for long periods due to the large amount of power from the reactor. They can stay underwater almost indefinitely between refuelings, with the only limits being the need to restock food or other supplies. Modern nuclear submarines can last 25 years without refueling. Conventional submarines can only stay submerged for a few days at slow speeds and a few hours at high speeds using batteries. Recent advancements have improved this, but they still have limited underwater time. Because of their high cost, not many countries have nuclear submarines. Serious nuclear and radiation accidents have occurred due to mishaps in Soviet submarines.

Septimia Zenobia, also called Bat-Zabbai, was a queen in Syria around 240 to 274 AD. Many stories exist about her family, but she likely came from a noble background. She married Odaenathus, who became king in 260. Under Odaenathus, Palmyra became very powerful in the eastern part of the Roman Empire. After Odaenathus died, Zenobia ruled for her son Vaballathus. In 270, she led an army that conquered much of the Roman East, including Egypt. At her height, her empire stretched from central Anatolia to southern Egypt, but she stayed connected to Rome. In 272, Zenobia declared her son emperor and herself empress, breaking away from Rome. Aurelian, a Roman emperor, defeated her forces. Zenobia was captured and taken to Rome, where she lived until she died after 274. She was a learned queen who welcomed scholars and protected minorities. Her rule inspired people and she is a symbol of Syrian pride.
This is a list of rivers in Saint Lucia. The rivers are listed going around the island in a circle, beginning from the top of the island.

Jabalpur, formerly known as Jubbulpore, is a city in Madhya Pradesh, India. It is a significant city in the state. As of 2011, it is the third-largest urban area in Madhya Pradesh and the country's 38th-largest urban area. Known for Dhuandhar Falls and white marble rocks at Bhedaghat, Jabalpur is famous for the game of snooker, which some believe originated there. Jabalpur is an important place for government, industry, and business in Madhya Pradesh. It is a major education center. The city has a high court and many state government offices. It is also a major military and industrial base, with factories producing weapons and ammunition. Several smaller industries are also present. Jabalpur is a big trading center and forest products producer, growing rapidly. The city is the main administrative center for Jabalpur district, which is the second-most-populous in Madhya Pradesh. Historically, it was part of the Kalachuri and Rajgond kingdoms. In the early 1800s, the British renamed it Jubbulpore and made it a military town. After India's independence, there have been calls for a new state called Mahakoshal, with Jabalpur as its capital. Jabalpur has the headquarters of the West Central Railway, Madhya Pradesh Electricity Board, Tropical Forest Research Institute, and army headquarters for five states: Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Odisha, Bihar, and Jharkhand. It also serves as the headquarters for two army regiments and a signal training center.

In chemistry, an ester is a compound made from an acid, where one hydroxyl group is replaced by an alkoxy group. Usually, esters come from a reaction between a carboxylic acid and an alcohol. Glycerides, which are esters of glycerol and fatty acids, are important in biology. They make up much of animal fats and vegetable oils. Esters with small molecular weights are often used as fragrances found in essential oils and pheromones. Phosphoesters form the backbone of DNA. Nitrate esters, like nitroglycerin, are known for being explosive. Polyester, made from esters, is an important plastic. Esters often smell sweet and are good solvents for plastics, plasticizers, resins, and lacquers. They are also a major class of synthetic lubricants.

The division of northern Melbourne was an Australian electoral district in Victoria. It covered parts of the inner northern suburbs, including Carlton, North Melbourne, and Fitzroy. In 1906, it was changed to the Batman division. This district had one member. H. B. Higgins was the member from 1904 to 1905. He did not run in the 1906 election because he became a justice in the High Court of Australia in 1906.

Cultured meat is made by growing animal cells in a lab, not by slaughtering animals. It is a type of cellular agriculture. The idea was first popularized by Jason Matheny in the early 2000s. He wrote an important paper about it and helped start New Harvest, the first non-profit focused on in vitro meat research. In 2013, Mark Post, a professor, made the first lab-grown burger. Since then, other companies have created prototypes but haven't yet sold the meat commercially. Memphis Meats and SuperMeat hope to sell lab-grown meat in 2020. People have not tried cultured meat yet, so it's unknown if they will accept it. The production process is still improving. Cultured meat could have big impacts on morals, health, the environment, culture, and money compared to regular meat.

John Guillermin, born on November 11, 1925, and died on September 27, 2015, was a British film director, writer, and producer. He worked mainly on big, exciting movies with adventure and action throughout his long career. Some of his famous films are "I Was Monty's Double" (1958), "Tarzan's Greatest Adventure" (1959), "Never Let Go" (1960), "Tarzan Goes to India" (1962), "Waltz of the Toreadors" (1962), "The Blue Max" (1966), "The Bridge at Remagen" (1969), "The Towering Inferno" (1974), "King Kong" (1976), "Death on the Nile" (1978), "Sheena" (1984), and "King Kong Lives" (1986). From the 1980s, he worked on less important projects. His last films were smaller and made for television. People said he was very strict and often yelled at people on set. This made him unpopular with producers and actors. But his skill in filming both small and big scenes was still respected.

Wake up! The music album with Pope Francis's words and prayers is a progressive rock album. It was released on November 27, 2015, on Believe Digital. The album includes speeches by Pope Francis recorded between 2013 and 2015. There are also music tracks of prayers and hymns by Italian artists and producers.
