anzonic was a town in the leventina area of ticino in switzerland. On April 1, 2012, it joined the town of faido along with other former towns: calpiogna, campello, cavagnago, chironico, mairengo, and osco.

Second German Television, or ZDF, is a public TV channel based in Mainz, a city in Rhineland-Palatinate. It is run as a nonprofit and was created by all German states. ZDF gets money from TV fees and ads. They are famous for two shows: "Heute," a news program started in 1963, and "Wetten, dass..?," an entertainment show that began in 1981 and ended in 2014. The head of ZDF, Thomas Bellut, was chosen in 2011.

Sugar is a generic term for sweet, dissolvable carbohydrates used in food. Table sugar, granulated sugar, or regular sugar, is sucrose, which is made of glucose and fructose. Simple sugars, or monosaccharides, include glucose, fructose, and galactose. Compound sugars, or disaccharides, are made of two monosaccharides joined together, like sucrose (table sugar), lactose (milk sugar), and maltose (two glucose molecules). In the body, compound sugars break down into simple sugars. Longer chains of monosaccharides are called oligosaccharides or polysaccharides and are not considered sugars. Some substances like glycerol and sugar alcohols may taste sweet but are not classified as sugars. Sugar is found in most plants, with honey and fruit being natural sources of simple sugars. Sugarcane and sugar beets have high concentrations of sucrose, making them good for commercial sugar production. In 2016, these crops produced about two billion tonnes of sugar. Maltose is made from malting grain, and lactose is found only in milk, including breast milk and some dairy products. Corn syrup, made from corn starch, is another cheap source of sugar. Sugar is used in many prepared foods, added to processed foods and drinks, and used as a sweetener in foods and beverages. The average person consumes about 150 grams of sugar a year, or over 260 food calories per day, in developed countries. As sugar consumption increased in the latter part of the 20th century, researchers studied whether a diet high in sugar, especially refined sugar, was harmful to health. Excessive sugar intake has been linked to obesity, diabetes, heart disease, dementia, and tooth decay. In 2015, the World Health Organization advised reducing sugar intake to less than 10% of total energy intake and encouraged reducing it to below 5%.

Jessica Mauboy, born on August 4, 1989, is an Australian singer, songwriter, and actress. She grew up in Darwin, Northern Territory. Mauboy became famous in 2006 by coming second on Australian Idol. She then signed a music contract with Sony Music Australia. In 2007, she released a live album from her Idol performances and was part of the girl group Young Divas. Her first album, "Been Waiting," came out in 2008. It had the hit song "Burn," and became the second best-selling Australian album of 2009. Her album "Get 'em Girls" in 2010 had four platinum singles. "Beautiful," released in 2013, had three top-ten hits. Mauboy also acted in movies like "Bran Nue Dae" and "The Sapphires," winning an AACTA award. She starred in "The Secret Daughter" in 2016. Her 2019 album "Hilda" topped the charts. Mauboy has won six top-ten albums and 16 top-twenty singles. She has worked with many international artists and performed at important events. She competed in the Eurovision Song Contest in 2018 and placed 20th.

Red Bank is a borough in Monmouth County, New Jersey. It was incorporated in 1908 and is situated near the Navesink River. As of the 2010 census, the population was 12,206, an increase of 362 from 2000, which had a population of 11,844, an increase of 1,208 from 1990 when it was 10,636. Red Bank was originally a town formed on March 17, 1870, from part of Shrewsbury Township. On February 14, 1879, it became Shrewsbury City but only for a short time, regaining its independence on May 15, 1879. In 1908, it became a borough and separated from Shrewsbury Township by a state law. Red Bank got its name from the red soil near the Navesink River.

George of the Jungle is an American animated TV series. It was created by Jay Ward and Bill Scott, who also made "The Rocky and Bullwinkle Show." The character George was inspired by Tarzan and a cartoon of George Eiferman, known as Mr. America, drawn by a cook during World War II. The show aired 17 episodes on Saturdays from September 9 to December 30, 1967, on ABC.

Michael Andrew Gove, born Graeme Andrew Logan on August 26, 1967, is a British politician. He has been the Chancellor of the Duchy of Lancaster since 2019 and the Minister for the Cabinet Office since 2020. He has been representing Surrey Heath as a Member of Parliament (MP) since 2005. A member of the Conservative Party, Gove was the Education Secretary from 2010 to 2014, Chief Whip from 2014 to 2015, Justice Secretary from 2015 to 2016, and Environment Secretary from 2017 to 2019. He tried to become the leader of the Conservative Party twice in 2016 and 2019, finishing third both times. Gove studied at Robert Gordon's College and Lady Margaret Hall, Oxford. Before entering politics, he was an author and journalist for The Times. He joined the House of Commons in 2005. In 2007, under David Cameron, he was appointed to the Shadow Cabinet as the Shadow Secretary of State for Children, Schools, and Families. He became the Education Secretary in the Cameron-Clegg coalition government. As Education Secretary, he ended the Building Schools for the Future program, changed A-Level and GCSE exams, and dealt with the Trojan Horse scandal. Teachers' unions passed motions of no confidence in his policies. In 2014, Gove became Chief Whip. After the 2015 election and the Cameron majority government, he became Justice Secretary and Lord Chancellor. In 2016, he was a key figure in the UK's Brexit referendum as co-convenor of Vote Leave, alongside Boris Johnson. After the 2016 referendum, Gove withdrew his support for Boris Johnson and ran for the Conservative leadership, finishing third. Following Theresa May's appointment as Prime Minister, he left the cabinet. However, after the 2017 election, he returned to the cabinet as Environment Secretary. He tried to become the Conservative leader again in 2019, but came in third. Upon Boris Johnson's appointment as Prime Minister, Gove was appointed Chancellor of the Duchy of Lancaster, handling Brexit preparations. After Brexit, he also became the Minister for the Cabinet Office.

Dodge is an American car brand made by FCA US LLC, based in Auburn Hills, Michigan. Dodge makes fast cars, but for most of its history, it was Chrysler's mid-priced brand above Plymouth. Dodge was started in the early 1900s by brothers Horace and John Dodge. They first made parts for other car companies. In 1914, they began making whole cars under the "Dodge Brothers" name. This was before Chrysler was founded. The factory was in Hamtramck, Michigan, and was called the Dodge Main Factory until it closed in January 1980. Both Dodge brothers died from the Spanish flu in 1920, and the company was sold to Dillon, Read & Co. in 1925. In 1928, it was sold to Chrysler. For many years, Dodge mainly made trucks and large cars. They also made smaller cars like the Dart from 1963 to 1976 and midsize cars like the Coronet and Charger from 1965 to 1978. In 1973, during the oil crisis, Chrysler created the K platform for compact to midsize cars, which helped the company's business in the 1980s. One of these cars was the Dodge Caravan. Through various changes, Dodge stayed strong. It survived ownership changes at Chrysler from 1998 to 2009, including a merger with Daimler-Benz AG from 1998 to 2007, a sale to Cerberus Capital Management, a government bailout in 2009, and a Chapter 11 bankruptcy before being acquired by Fiat. In 2011, Dodge, Dodge Ram, and Dodge Viper were separated. Dodge said Viper would be an SRT product, and Ram would be a standalone brand. In 2014, SRT was merged back into Dodge. Later that year, Chrysler Group was renamed FCA US LLC to match the merger with Fiat S.p.A. into Fiat Chrysler Automobiles.

The governor of Tasmania represents Queen Elizabeth II in the Australian state of Tasmania. They do the same constitutional and ceremonial jobs as the Governor-General of Australia does at the national level. The governor usually acts on the advice of the Premier, who leads the elected government. However, the governor can still use special powers if needed and has the right to remove the Premier. For more details on the office of governor, see "Governors of Australian States." The governor lives in Government House, which is at the Queen's Domain. The first Tasmanian-born governor was Sir Guy Green, appointed in 1995. Before that, Sir Stanley Burbury, the first Australian-born governor, was appointed in 1973. Since Burbury, all Tasmanian governors were born in Australia, except Peter Underwood, who was born in Britain but moved to Australia when he was young. In 2014, Peter Underwood died unexpectedly, and the governor's position was empty for over five months. During this time, Chief Justice and Lieutenant-Governor Alan Blow acted as the governor. On November 10, 2014, Premier Will Hodgman chose Kate Warner, a University of Tasmania legal expert, as the new governor. Kate Warner was officially sworn in on December 10, 2014. Since Kate Warner became governor, the queen, based on the Premier's recommendation, gave her and all future governors the title "The Honourable" for life.

Frode Johnsen, born on March 17, 1974, is a former Norwegian footballer. He played for Odd and Rosenborg in the Tippeligaen and for Nagoya Grampus and Shimizu S-Pulse in Japan. Johnsen could play in different positions but was often used as a striker or midfielder. He is 188 cm tall and was a good header. In his last season for Odd BK in 2015, he won the Kniksen's Honour Award for his long career. Johnsen retired at 41 years old. In 2013, he became the top scorer in the Tippeligaen and was the oldest top scorer in a European league ever.

Leslie David Reed, born on July 24, 1935, and passed away on April 15, 2019, was an English songwriter, arranger, musician, and leader of a small orchestra. He often wrote songs with Gordon Mills, Barry Mason, and Geoff Stephens. He also wrote songs with other musicians like Roger Greenaway, Roger Cook, Peter Callander, and Johnny Worth. Reed co-wrote about sixty songs that appeared on charts. He is famous for writing "It's Not Unusual," "Delilah," "The Last Waltz," and "Marching on Together." His songs received gold discs and Ivor Novello awards. A source said his songs were so popular that in the mid-1960s, it was rare for a British singles chart to not include one of his songs. He was given a special award, the British Academy Gold Badge of Merit, in 1982.

Duttaphrynus stomaticus, known as the Indian marbled toad, Punjab toad, or indus valley toad, is a toad species found in Asia. It lives in areas from eastern Iran, Pakistan, and Afghanistan to Nepal, and extends into parts of India and Bangladesh. This toad does not have bony bumps on its head. The space between its eyes is wider than its upper eyelid. Its ear has a disc that is about two-thirds the size of its eye. The first and second fingers are almost the same length, and it has a single small bump under the second finger. There is a spiny ridge on its ankle. It has a gland on its ankle and its poison gland is longer than it is wide. Three dark bands run across its forearm. The underside of the toad is white with dark spots on its throat.

Mahavira, also known as Vardhamana, was the 24th leader (tirthankara) in Jainism. He followed Parshvanatha, the 23rd leader. Mahavira was born in the early 6th century BC into a royal family in present-day Bihar, India. His parents were Trishala and Siddhartha, who were followers of Parshvanatha. At about 30 years old, Mahavira gave up all his possessions and became an ascetic, seeking spiritual enlightenment through meditation and severe self-discipline for 12 and a half years. He achieved complete knowledge (kevala jnana) after this period. For 30 years, he taught and eventually reached salvation in the 6th century BC, though the exact year is debated. Mahavira preached following the vows of non-violence, truth, non-stealing, chastity, and non-attachment. He also taught about many-sided reality (anekantavada), including syadvada and nayavada. His teachings were recorded by his main disciple, Indrabhuti Gautama, as the Jain Agamas. These texts were passed down orally and are now some of the core texts of Svetambara Jainism, though their authenticity is questioned by Digambara Jains. Mahavira is often shown sitting or standing, with a lion symbol beneath him. His earliest images come from archaeological sites in Mathura, India, dating back to the 1st century BC to the 2nd century AD. Jains celebrate his birth as Mahavir Janma Kalyanak and his salvation on Diwali.

The Central Australian Aboriginal Media Association (CAAMA) was founded in 1980. Its goal is to share Aboriginal music and culture with all of Australia. Based in Alice Springs, CAAMA works closely with the local Indigenous community. They produce radio, television, and music recordings.

Harvey Phillip Spector, born on December 26, 1939, is an American record producer, musician, and songwriter. He developed the Wall of Sound, a music production style he compared to a Wagnerian approach to rock and roll. Spector is seen as one of the most influential figures in pop music and the first auteur in music for his control over every part of the recording process. After retiring for about 30 years, he was found guilty of killing actress Lana Clarkson in 2003. He is serving a 19-year-to-life sentence and can be released in 2025. Born in the Bronx, Spector started his career in 1958 as a co-founder, guitarist, and vocalist of the Teddy Bears. He wrote their US number-one hit "To Know Him Is to Love Him." In 1960, he co-founded Philles Records and became the youngest US label owner at 21. During the 1960s, he wrote, co-wrote, or produced records for artists like the Ronettes, The Crystals, and Ike & Tina Turner. He often worked with arranger Jack Nitzsche, engineer Larry Levine, and a house band known as "The Wrecking Crew." Spector retired from the music industry in 1966. In 1969, he returned and produced The Beatles' album "Let It Be" (1970), as well as solo records by John Lennon and George Harrison. By the mid-1970s, Spector had produced 18 US top 10 singles for various artists. His chart-topping songs include "You've Lost That Lovin' Feelin'" (1964), "The Long and Winding Road" (1970), and "My Sweet Lord" (1970). According to BMI, "You've Lost That Lovin' Feelin'" received the most US airplay in the 20th century. Through his work, Spector helped create the idea of the studio as an instrument, integrated pop art aesthetics into music, and developed the art rock genre. His 1963 compilation album "A Christmas Gift for You from Philles Records" is considered the best Christmas record of all time. In 1965, he was called the "First Tycoon of Teen" by Tom Wolfe. Spector was honored with a Grammy Award for album of the year in 1973, induction into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 1989, and the Songwriters Hall of Fame in 1997. In 2004, Rolling Stone magazine ranked him 63rd on their list of the "100 Greatest Artists of All Time."

Azerbaijan Airlines, also called Azal, is the main and biggest airline in Azerbaijan. It is based in Baku, next to Heydar Aliyev International Airport. The airline flies to places in Asia, the CIS, Europe, and the USA. Azerbaijan Airlines is part of the International Air Transport Association. It was created on April 7, 1992, as the first national airline after Azerbaijan gained independence.

The adrenal glands, also called suprarenal glands, are endocrine glands located above the kidneys. They produce hormones such as adrenaline and steroids like aldosterone and cortisol. Each gland has two main parts: the outer cortex and the inner medulla. The adrenal cortex is divided into three zones: the zona glomerulosa, zona fasciculata, and zona reticularis. The cortex makes three main types of steroid hormones: mineralocorticoids, glucocorticoids, and androgens. Mineralocorticoids, like aldosterone, produced in the zona glomerulosa, help control blood pressure and electrolytes. Glucocorticoids, including cortisol and cortisone, made in the zona fasciculata, manage metabolism and suppress the immune system. Androgens, produced in the zona reticularis, turn into sex hormones in other parts of the body. Steroid hormones are made through a process called steroidogenesis, which happens in cortical cells. The medulla makes catecholamines, which quickly affect the body in stressful situations. Adrenal gland problems can lead to diseases like Cushing's syndrome from too much cortisol and Addison's disease from too little. Congenital adrenal hyperplasia is a genetic condition due to hormonal control issues. Adrenal tumors can also occur and are often found when looking for other health issues.
The town of Del Norte is a statutory town and the county seat of Rio Grande County in Colorado, United States. People usually say its name as "del nor-tuh." In 2010, the town had 1,686 people.

Cryptosporidium, sometimes called crypto, is a type of parasite that can cause illnesses. These illnesses can affect the lungs or the intestines. In the intestines, it mainly causes watery diarrhea. In the lungs, it can cause a cough that may last. This parasite can affect both healthy and sick people. To treat the illness in the intestines, doctors focus on giving fluids and electrolytes, and managing any pain. Nitazoxanide is the only medicine approved for treating healthy people with crypto. Zinc supplements might help if the infection keeps coming back or if someone is at risk of not having enough zinc. Kuala Terengganu, often abbreviated as KT, is a city and the main administrative, royal, and economic center of Terengganu, Malaysia. It is also the capital of Kuala Terengganu district. Kuala Terengganu is 440 kilometers northeast of Kuala Lumpur on the east coast of Peninsular Malaysia. The city is at the mouth of the Terengganu River, facing the South China Sea. As a district, it has the smallest area but the largest population in Terengganu, with 406,317 people in 2010. Kuala Terengganu became a "Waterfront Heritage City" on January 1, 2008. It is a major political and economic center, and the main entrance to many tourist places in the state. Attractions include Chinese village Kampung Cina, the large Payang market, Terengganu State Museum, and Batu Buruk Beach. Despite modern changes, the city still has strong Malay influences mixed with other cultures due to its long history as a port.
angels in the outfield can mean: a phrase used to describe perfect fielding.

Publius (or Gaius) Cornelius Tacitus lived from the first century AD and was a Roman historian and politician. Modern scholars consider him one of the best Roman historians. He wrote during a time known as the Silver Age of Latin literature. His writing is known for being brief and clear. Tacitus wrote about the reigns of several Roman emperors, including Tiberius, Claudius, Nero, and the Year of the Four Emperors in 69 AD. His works cover Roman history from 14 AD to 70 AD, when the first Jewish–Roman war began. Some parts of his writings are missing, especially in his "Annals." Tacitus also wrote about oratory, Germany, and his father-in-law, Agricola, who was an important Roman general in Britain.

Pratval used to be a municipality in Hinterrhein district, which is in the Swiss canton of Graubünden. On January 1, 2015, Pratval joined with four other former municipalities—Almens, Paspels, Rodels, and Tomils—to create a new municipality called Domleschg.

Kaoru Moto (born April 25, 1917, died August 26, 1992) was a soldier in the United States Army. He was given the Medal of Honor, the highest award in the U.S. military, after he died. This was for his actions during World War II.
The 1957–58 Dutch Eerste Divisie had 32 teams. They were divided into two groups. Willem II and SHS won the championship.

Cameron Barker, born on April 4, 1986, is a Canadian ice hockey player. He plays as a defenseman and is currently not signed to any team. Recently, he played for the Ilves Tampere in a league called SM-liiga. Barker was chosen third overall in the 2004 NHL draft by the Chicago Blackhawks. He played for the Blackhawks for four years before being traded to the Minnesota Wild in 2010. Barker also played for Canada's national team. He won gold medals in the 2005 and 2006 World Junior Championships. Many people think he was not chosen well in the draft.

Karnali zone was one of the fourteen zones in Nepal's mid-western development region. The main office of Karnali zone was in Jumla. It was one of the poorest and most remote areas in Nepal, with limited road access. Except for Kalikot, each district had an airfield. Kalikot was only connected by road to Jumla airport seasonally. Karnali zone was the largest zone in Nepal and had two national parks. Shey Phoksundo National Park, known for snow leopards, was the biggest park in Nepal, covering 3,555 km² and featuring Phoksundo Lake, the deepest lake in the country. Rara National Park was around Rara Lake, the largest lake in Nepal at 10.2 km² and known as the "Pearl of Nepal." Karnali zone was divided into five districts. Since 2015, these districts became part of Karnali Pradesh.

Grandval is a town in the Jura Bernois area of the canton of Bern, Switzerland. It is in the French-speaking part of the Bernese Jura. Grandval was also known as Granfel or Granfelden in German, but these names are not used much now.

Mario Altmann was born on November 4, 1986. He is an ice hockey player from Austria. Altmann plays for EHC Black Wings Linz in the Austrian Hockey League. He played for EC VSV for five seasons before joining EHC Black Wings Linz on April 16, 2015. Altmann is part of the Austria men's national ice hockey team. He played in the 2009, 2011, and 2011 IIHF World Championships and in the 2014 Winter Olympics.

Cee Lo Green's "Magic Moment" is his first Christmas album and his fourth studio album. It came out on October 29, 2012, in the UK. The album was released in the US on October 30, 2012, by Elektra Records. His versions of "Mary, Did You Know?" and "What Christmas Means to Me" reached number 22 and 23 on the US R&B charts on December 22, 2012. The album sold 181,000 copies in the US in 2012. This is Cee Lo Green's first solo album without a parental advisory label.
Jimmy Morales, born James Ernesto Morales Cabrera on March 18, 1969, is a politician from Guatemala. He is also an actor and comedian. Morales was the 50th president of Guatemala from 2016 to 2020.

The Yukon River is a big river in northwestern North America. It starts in British Columbia, Canada, and flows through the Yukon Territory, also named after the river. Most of the river is in Alaska. It ends in the Bering Sea at a delta. The river is very long and flows about 3,200 miles. It has a large area of 832,700 square kilometers, with 323,800 square kilometers in Canada. This area is bigger than Texas or Alberta. The Yukon River is the longest in Alaska and Yukon. It was an important way to travel during the gold rush from 1896 to 1903. A part of the river, called "Thirty Mile," is a national heritage river. The river used to have boats until the 1950s. After Alaska was bought by the United States in 1867, a company built posts along the river. The Yukon River has some pollution, but its water quality is generally good. The Yukon River Inter-Tribal Watershed Council, made up of 70 tribes, works to make the river safe to drink from again.

Rancho Palos Verdes, known as RPV or Palos Verdes, is a coastal city in Los Angeles County, California. It is located on the bluffs of the Palos Verdes Peninsula and neighbors other cities such as Palos Verdes Estates, Rolling Hills, and Rolling Hills Estates. This city is famous for its impressive views of the Pacific Ocean, Santa Catalina Island, and Los Angeles. It also has highly ranked schools, many horse and hiking trails, and very expensive homes.

Ratnasambhava means "jewel-born." He is one of the five meditation buddhas in Vajrayana or tantric Buddhism. Ratnasambhava's mandalas and mantras help develop fairness and equality. In Vajrayana, he helps fight greed and pride. His partner is Mamaki, and he rides a horse or a pair of lions.

Swatch introduced a new time concept in 1998 called "internet time" or ".beat time." Instead of hours and minutes, a day is divided into 1,000 parts called ".beats." Each.beat lasts 1 minute and 26.4 seconds. Time is written as a 3-digit number out of 1,000 after midnight. For example, 248.beats is about 5 hours and 57 minutes after midnight. There are no time zones in Swatch internet time. Instead, a new time scale called Biel Meantime (BMT) is used, based on Swatch's headquarters in Biel, Switzerland, which is equivalent to Central European Time, West Africa Time, and UTC+01. Unlike regular time in many countries, including Switzerland, Swatch internet time does not change for daylight saving time.

The covalent radius, "r," is a measure of an atom's size in a covalent bond. It's usually measured in picometres (pm) or angstroms (Å), where 1 Å equals 100 pm. In theory, the covalent bond length between two atoms, "r" (ab), is the sum of their covalent radii: "r" (ab) = "r" (a) + "r" (b). Different radii can be used for single, double, and triple bonds. The size of an atom isn't constant; it depends on its chemical environment. For bonds between different types of atoms (heteroatomic bonds), ionic effects might be involved. Often, polar covalent bonds are shorter than expected based on the sum of covalent radii. Covalent radii values are typically averages, showing some transferability, making them useful. Bond lengths "r" (ab) are measured using X-ray diffraction or neutron diffraction. For similar atoms (homonuclear bonds), Linus Pauling suggested the covalent radius is half the single bond length in the element, like 74.14 pm for hydrogen, giving a covalent radius of 37.07 pm. Usually, an average value from various covalent compounds is used. Sanderson published recent non-polar covalent radii for main-group elements, but bond lengths from the Cambridge Crystallographic Database are more transferable and have made covalent radii less necessary in many cases.

Osvaldo Bayer was an Argentine writer and journalist. He lived in Buenos Aires. In 1974, during Isabel Perón's presidency, he went to live in Linz am Rhein, Germany. This was during a time of dictatorship in Argentina from 1976 to 1983.

The December 2010 North American blizzard was a big snowstorm that lasted from December 5 to December 29, 2010, affecting parts of the United States and Canada. From January 4 to January 15, it was called "Windstorm Benjamin" in Europe. This was the first big winter storm of the 2010-2011 season and the fifth blizzard in the United States in 2010. The storm hit the Northeast megalopolis, including cities like Norfolk, Philadelphia, Newark, New York City, Hartford, Providence, and Boston. It brought lots of snow to these areas.
Carol Cleveland, born on January 13, 1942, is an actress and comedian from Britain and the United States. She is famous for her work with Monty Python.
Sandslån is a small place in Kramfors municipality, Västernorrland county, Sweden. In 2010, it had 272 people living there.

Muscular dystrophy (MD) is a group of muscle diseases that make skeletal muscles weaker and break down over time. The conditions vary in which muscles are affected, how weak they become, how quickly they get worse, and when symptoms start. Many people can no longer walk later on. Some types also cause problems in other organs. MD includes about 30 different genetic disorders, usually grouped into nine main types. The most common type is Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD), which usually affects boys starting around age four. Other types include Becker muscular dystrophy, facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy, limb-girdle muscular dystrophy, and myotonic dystrophy. These conditions result from gene mutations that affect muscle proteins. The mutations can come from parents or develop during early growth. Disorders can be inherited in different ways: X-linked recessive, autosomal recessive, or autosomal dominant. Diagnosis often involves blood tests and genetic testing. There is no cure for MD, but physical therapy, braces, and corrective surgery can help some symptoms. People with weak breathing muscles may need assisted ventilation. Medications include steroids to slow muscle breakdown, anticonvulsants to control seizures and some muscle activity, and immunosuppressants to delay damage to dying muscle cells. Duchenne muscular dystrophy, which is about half of all cases, affects around one in 5,000 boys at birth. MD was first described in the 1830s by Charles Bell. The term "dystrophy" comes from Greek words meaning "difficult" and "nourish." Gene therapy as a treatment is still being studied.

In Norse mythology, Sigyn is a goddess and Loki's wife. She is mentioned in two important texts: the "Poetic Edda" and the "Prose Edda." In the "Poetic Edda," not much is said about Sigyn, except that she helps Loki during his imprisonment. In the "Prose Edda," Sigyn again helps her husband while he is in captivity. She is also mentioned as a goddess in this text. Some people believe Sigyn might be depicted on the Gosforth Cross. Sigyn has inspired many theories and cultural references.
bluebell, bluebells, or bluebelle can all refer to the same flower.

Rain is a town in Bavaria, Germany, located near the confluence of the Lech and Danube rivers, about 11 km east of Donauwörth. Rain is on the B16 road and has a railway station on the Ingolstadt–Neuoffingen line, part of the Danube Valley Railway. Rain was mentioned in a document from 1257, likely founded between 1248 and 1294. It was built to protect Bavaria and collect customs from a bridge over the Lech. In 1632, during the Thirty Years' War, the Battle of Rain took place. The Swedish army won, and Johann Tserclaes von Tilly died in Ingolstadt. A monument to Tilly was erected in front of Rain's Rococo town hall in 1914. Rain has a Roman Catholic church, St John the Baptist, with late Gothic frescoes from around 1480. Other historic sites include the Schwabian Gate, the historic hospital with its chapel, and the former castle. Rain has three museums: the Lachner Brothers Museum, the Homeland Museum, and the Jean-Duprai Museum. Rain was home to composers Theodor, Franz, Ignaz, and Vincent Lachner, as well as Johann Bayer, a lawyer and astronomer, and Georg Tannstetter, a humanist. Michael Raucheisen, a pianist, was also from Rain. The town is the headquarters of the Dehner chain of garden centers, employing 1,100 people, and has a sugar refinery with 240 to 280 workers. Rain is twin-towns with Tougan, the capital of Sourou province in Burkina Faso.
Heinrich Ludwig Futterer was a German athlete born on October 14, 1931, and died on February 10, 2019. He mostly ran in sprint events.

Viktor Yanukovych, born on July 9, 1950, was a Ukrainian politician who became the fourth president of Ukraine in 2010. He lost his job in 2014 during the Ukrainian Revolution and now lives in Russia. Yanukovych was governor of Donetsk, an area in eastern Ukraine, from 1997 to 2002. He was also prime minister twice under President Leonid Kuchma: from November 21, 2002, to December 7, 2004, and from December 28, 2004, to January 5, 2005. In 2004, Yanukovych first tried to become president but lost to Viktor Yushchenko in a runoff election. The election was controversial, with many complaints about unfair practices. This led to protests and the Orange Revolution. Yanukovych later served as prime minister again, from August 4, 2006, to December 18, 2007, under President Yushchenko. Yanukovych won the 2010 presidential election, defeating Prime Minister Yulia Tymoshenko. The election was considered fair by international observers. In 2013, he faced protests because he refused to sign an agreement with the European Union and chose to get closer to Russia instead. This led to the Euromaidan protests, where people occupied Independence Square in Kyiv. In January 2014, deadly clashes broke out. Yanukovych fled to Kharkiv, then to Crimea, and finally to Russia. On February 22, the Ukrainian parliament removed him from his position. They set May 25, 2014, as the date for a special election to replace him. Two days later, they also issued a warrant for his arrest, accusing him of killing civilians. Yanukovych denied these accusations and said he was the legitimate president. On June 18, 2015, the Verkhovna Rada of Ukraine officially removed his title. In January 2019, he was sentenced to 13 years in prison in absentia for high treason.
To catch a killer is a 1992 TV movie. Eric Till directed it. Brian Dennehy and Michael Riley are in the film. The story is real and about catching a bad guy named John Wayne Gacy.

The Schwarzschild radius, sometimes called the gravitational radius, is a special measurement related to a black hole. It shows the radius of the event horizon of a Schwarzschild black hole. This radius is connected to any mass. The Schwarzschild radius was named after Karl Schwarzschild, a German astronomer who figured out this solution in 1916. The Schwarzschild radius is calculated using this formula: \[ \text{Sch. r} = \frac{2GM}{c^2} \] Here, "G" is the gravitational constant, "M" is the mass of the object, and "c" is the speed of light.
This is a list of important people who were born, raised, or live in Florida, the American state.

João Teixeira de Faria, also known as João de Deus, was born on June 24, 1942. He is a Brazilian man who claims to be a medium and a "psychic surgeon." He was also convicted of sexual offenses. He was based in Abadiânia, Brazil, where he ran a place called Casa de Dom Inácio de Loyola. This place was said to be a center for spiritual healing. He has been on TV shows like CNN, ABC News, and The Oprah Winfrey Show. James Randi and Joe Nickell showed that his healing methods are just like carnival tricks. There is no proof that the benefits people say they got from him were real, just their imagination. In 2018, after more than 600 people accused him of sexual abuse, he went to the police. In December 2019, he was given a 19-year and four-month prison sentence for raping four women. On January 20, 2020, he was sentenced to an extra 40 years in prison for raping five women. This is the third time he has been found guilty. In total, he faces 63 years and four months in prison.
Oxford is a town in Maine, United States. It had 4,110 people in 2010. Oxford has a speedway, a fair, and a casino. The town also includes Welchville.

In the year 235 BC, the Roman calendar was used before Julius Caesar's changes. At that time, it was called the year of the consuls Torquatus and Bulbus (or sometimes, the 519th year since the founding of Rome). People started using 235 BC to mark this year around the early medieval times, when counting years from the birth of Jesus became common in Europe.

Princess Amelia of the United Kingdom was born on August 7, 1783, and died on November 2, 1810. She was the fifteenth and last child, and the sixth daughter, of King George III and Charlotte of Mecklenburg-Strelitz. Princess Amelia was their first daughter to die, and their third child to pass away before them.
Gianni Morandi, born on December 11, 1944, is an Italian singer, actor, and entertainer.
San Carlos is a community in Hidalgo County, Texas. The population was 3,130 in 2010. It is part of the McAllen–Edinburg–Mission metropolitan area. San Carlos is located northeast of McAllen.

The pedal steel guitar is a type of steel guitar with pedals and knee levers that change certain strings' pitch. This allows players to make more varied and complex music than before. Like other steel guitars, it can play smooth sliding notes and deep vibrato—sounds similar to the human voice. Pedal steel guitars are mainly used in American country music. In the 1950s, pedals and knee levers were added to steel guitars. This lets the player play a major scale without moving the bar and bend notes while strumming chords. This creates a unique sound popular in country and western music, something not possible on earlier steel guitars. The steel guitar first appeared in Hawaii in the 1800s. Its sound became popular in the United States from the early to mid-20th century. This led to the creation of various instruments designed to be played horizontally, known as "Hawaiian-style." The first was the Hawaiian guitar, or lap steel. Later, a lap steel with a resonator for louder sound was made by National and Dobro. In 1934, the electric guitar pickup was invented, letting steel guitars be heard as well as other instruments. Amplification allowed the development of electrified lap steels, then console steels, and eventually pedal steel guitars. Playing the pedal steel guitar requires coordinating both hands, feet, and knees. Only the American reed organ has similar requirements. Important developers include Buddy Emmons, Bud Isaacs, Zane Beck, and Paul Bigsby. Besides country music, pedal steel guitars are used in sacred music in the eastern and southern United States, jazz, and Nigerian music.

Twiztid is an American horrorcore rap duo from Detroit, Michigan. They were formed in 1997. The members are Jamie Spaniolo and Paul Methric, who perform as Jamie Madrox and Monoxide. Before forming Twiztid, Spaniolo and Methric were in a group called House of Krazees. That group stopped in 1997. Twiztid released their first album in 1997 and stayed with Psychopathic Records until 2012, when they left. They didn't have a record label until 2014, when they created their own called Majik Ninja Entertainment. Twiztid makes horrorcore rap and has made 12 studio albums, 12 EPs, 10 compilation albums, and 1 mixtape.
Gabriel Pereira de Castro (1571-1632) was a Portuguese priest, lawyer, and poet.

Crystal Palace Football Club is based in Selhurst, South London, England. They play in the Premier League, the top level of English football. The club says it started in 1861 but officially formed in 1905. Both the original and the current club were owned by the same company. Crystal Palace claims to be the oldest professional football club in the world. Both clubs played at the Crystal Palace Exhibition Building. The professional club moved to their current home, Selhurst Park, in 1924. The amateur club joined the Football Association in 1863 and played in the first FA Cup in 1871-72. They stopped appearing in records in 1875-76. Crystal Palace became a professional club in 1905. They joined the Football League in 1920 and the Premier League in 1992. Crystal Palace has mostly played in the top two divisions of English football since 1964. They finished third in the old First Division in the 1990-91 season. Crystal Palace lost the FA Cup finals to Manchester United in 1990 and 2016. They wear red and blue stripes now, after changing from claret and blue in 1973. Crystal Palace has a rivalry with Brighton & Hove Albion and other south London clubs like Millwall and Charlton Athletic.
A gag is a tool made to stop speaking. It can also mean GAG, which stands for:

The great seal of Connecticut has been its coat of arms since May 1784. It shows three grapevines. There is also a ribbon below with the Latin motto: "He who transplanted sustains." In English, this means: "He who moves a plant still supports it." The border around it says "Seal of the State of Connecticut."

In the case Gomillion v. Lightfoot, decided by the U.S. Supreme Court in 1960, the court ruled that an electoral district with boundaries drawn to prevent black people from voting violated the Fifteenth Amendment.

Richard Falk, born on November 13, 1930, is an American professor. He teaches international law at Princeton University. He has written 20 books and worked with others to write another 20 books. In 2008, he got a job as a United Nations special reporter. His job was to look at how human rights were in the Palestinian territories since 1967.

Horace Silver Martin Tavares Silver was an American jazz pianist, composer, and arranger who was born on September 2, 1928, and died on June 18, 2014. He played tenor saxophone and piano in Connecticut before joining Stan Getz's trio in 1950. In 1950, he moved to New York City and gained a reputation for his bluesy piano playing and compositions. His work with the Jazz Messengers, led by Art Blakey, brought him more attention. Their album "Horace Silver and the Jazz Messengers" included his hit song "The Preacher." After leaving Blakey in 1956, Silver formed his own quintet, with a typical small group including a tenor saxophone, trumpet, piano, bass, and drums. Their performances and recordings for Blue Note Records made him popular. His best-selling album was "Song for My Father," recorded in 1963 and 1964. In the early 1970s, Silver disbanded his group to focus on composing and spending time with his wife. He added lyrics to his recordings and became interested in spiritualism, which sometimes resulted in commercially unsuccessful albums like the "United States of Mind" series. After 28 years with Blue Note, he started his own record label and reduced touring in the 1980s, relying on composition royalties for income. In 1993, he returned to major record labels and released five albums before retiring because of health issues. Silver moved from bebop to hard bop by focusing on melodies rather than complex harmonies. He played with clean, often humorous right-hand lines and darker left-hand chords. His compositions featured catchy melodies and sometimes dissonant harmonies. Many of his songs, like "Doodlin'," "Peace," and "Sister Sadie," became jazz standards still played today. His legacy includes influencing other pianists and composers, as well as nurturing young jazz talent over four decades.

Leo Keith Thorsness was born on February 14, 1932, and passed away on May 2, 2017. He was a colonel in the United States Air Force. Thorsness received the Medal of Honor for his actions during the Vietnam War. Specifically, he was awarded the Medal of Honor for an air engagement on April 19, 1967. Two weeks later, he was shot down and became a prisoner of war in North Vietnam for six years. After his military service, Thorsness served one term in the Washington State Senate.
Saint-Vigor-des-Mézerets used to be a separate town in Calvados, which is in Normandy, a region in northwestern France. On January 1, 2017, it became part of a new town called Terres de Druance.

Rex Taylor Reed was born on October 2, 1938. He is an American film critic and has acted occasionally. Rex was also a co-host on a TV show called "At the Movies." He writes a column named "On the Town with Rex Reed" for "The New York Observer."

Consumer confidence measures how optimistic people feel about the economy and their finances. When they feel good, they spend more. When they feel bad, they save more. Consumer confidence changes month by month, showing how people think about jobs and the economy. It usually goes up when the economy grows and down when it slows. In the U.S., consumer confidence follows stock market performance, but it happens after the market changes.

Lawrenceville is a city in Illinois. It is the county seat of Lawrence County. Located near the Embarras River, it had 4,348 people in 2010. Lawrenceville is in southeast Illinois, close to Vincennes, Indiana. The city is known for its high school basketball team. The "Indians" won state championships in 1972, 1974, and back-to-back in 1982 and 1983. They won 68 games in two seasons. The coach, Ron Felling, later became an assistant coach at Indiana University.

Sheikh Ahmed Ismail Hassan Yassin was a Palestinian imam and politician who lived from 1937 to March 22, 2004. He was one of the founders of Hamas, an Islamist Palestinian organization that acts as a military group and a political party. Yassin led the spiritual side of Hamas. Hamas was accepted by Palestinians because it provided charity, setting up hospitals, schools, libraries, and other services. However, Hamas also claimed responsibility for attacks on Israeli civilians. Many countries, including the European Union, Israel, Japan, Canada, and the United States, considered Hamas a terrorist group. Yassin, who was paralyzed and nearly blind, used a wheelchair after a sports accident at age 12. He was killed when an Israeli helicopter missile hit him as he was leaving morning prayers. The attack also killed his bodyguards and nine bystanders. His death was widely criticized. Over 200,000 Palestinians attended his funeral.

Alfred Gomolka was a German politician who lived from July 21, 1942, to March 24, 2020. He was a member of the European Parliament for Mecklenburg-Vorpommern. He also worked as the minister president of Mecklenburg-Vorpommern.

In Norse mythology, the megingjörð, meaning "power-belt" in Old Norse, is a belt worn by the god Thor. According to the "Prose Edda," the belt is one of Thor's three main possessions, along with his hammer Mjölnir and iron gloves Járngreipr. When worn, it doubles Thor's already great strength. In a 10th-century poem called "Þórsdrápa" (Thor's Lay), written by the poet Eilífr Goðrúnarson, there is a line that refers to Thor's power-belt. The line "njótr njarðgjarðar" means "he who benefits from the mighty belt," referring to Thor's magical belt of strength. In "Gylfaginning," the first part of Snorri Sturluson's "Prose Edda," verse 45 mentions Thor's power-belt. In this verse, it says, "When the day came, Thor went out and put on a man who lay not far from him in the woods. He was not a little one. He slept and had a strong dream. Then Thor realized what happened during the night. He girded himself with his belt of strength, and his divine strength grew. And in this way, the man woke up and stood up quickly."

John Francis Welch Jr. was born on November 19, 1935, and died on March 1, 2020. He was an American business leader, chemical engineer, and writer. Welch was the chairman and CEO of General Electric (GE) from 1981 to 2001. When he stopped working at GE, he got a severance payment of $417 million, which was the biggest such payment in business history. In 2006, his net worth was estimated at $720 million.

Soy milk, also called soya milk or soymilk, is a plant-based drink made from soybeans. First, soybeans are soaked and ground. Then, the mixture is boiled and the remaining solids are removed. It has a mixture of oil, water, and protein. Soy milk is originally a by-product of making tofu. It came to be a common drink in Europe and North America later in the 20th century, as it was developed to taste more like dairy milk. Soy milk and other plant-based "milks," like almond and rice milk, can be used instead of dairy milk by vegans or those who cannot tolerate lactose. Some people also drink soy milk for environmental or health reasons.
Ternouwen is a city and municipality in southwestern Netherlands, in Zeeland province, in the middle of Zeelandic Flanders. It has more than 55,000 people and is the most populous in Zeeland.

"March on, Bahamaland" is the national anthem of the Bahamas. Timothy Gibson wrote the words and the music. In 1973, when the Bahamas became independent from the United Kingdom, this anthem was chosen. Before, the country used "God Save the Queen" as its royal anthem.

The Queanbeyan River is a steady stream in New South Wales and the Australian Capital Territory, Australia. It is part of the Molonglo catchment area in the Murray–Darling Basin. The river is in length and has a catchment area. It helps supply water to Canberra and Queanbeyan. Its water quality is protected by federal laws. It is thought that the local Aboriginal Ngarigo people called the river "queanbeyan," which means "clearwater."

Hannah Dominique E. John-Kamen was born on September 7, 1989. She is an English actress. She is famous for playing Yalena "Dutch" Yardeen in the TV show "Killjoys," Orlena in "Game of Thrones," F'nale Zandor in "Ready Player One," Ava Starr/Ghost in "Ant-Man and the Wasp," and the main character in "The Stranger" on Netflix.

William Shakespeare belonged to the King's Men, a acting company, for most of his career. This company was previously called the Lord Chamberlain's Men during Queen Elizabeth I's reign. In 1603, when King James I became the new monarch, the company changed its name to the King's Men. King James I became their patron. On May 19, 1603, a royal patent authorized the King's Men company. The players named in the patent, in order, were: Lawrence Fletcher, William Shakespeare, Richard Burbage, Augustine Phillips, John Heminges, Henry Condell, William Sly, Robert Armin, Richard Cowley, and others. The nine men named in the patent became grooms of the chamber. On March 15, 1604, each of these nine men received four and a half yards of red cloth for the coronation procession.

The coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic in the Philippines is part of a global pandemic caused by severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2). The first case was identified on January 30, 2020, involving a 38-year-old Chinese woman in Metro Manila. On February 1, a 44-year-old Chinese man died, confirming the Philippines as the first country outside China to report a death from the disease. After no new cases for over a month, the Philippines confirmed its first local transmission on March 7. Since then, the virus spread to all 17 regions of the country. Socio-economic factors influence the number of cases across the country. As of August 21, there were 182,365 confirmed cases in the Philippines. Out of these, 114,519 people recovered, and 2,940 people died. The Philippines has the highest number of cases in Southeast Asia, more than Indonesia and Singapore. It ranks 9th in Asia and 22nd in the world. The biggest increase in cases was on August 10, with 6,958 new cases reported. The Philippines had fewer testing capabilities than its neighbors at the start of the pandemic. Tests had to be done outside the country due to a lack of testing kits. This led to controversies involving some government officials who got tested without qualifying. By January 2020, the Research Institute for Tropical Medicine in Metro Manila began testing operations and became the first subnational laboratory. Since then, several laboratories have been accredited by the Department of Health (DOH). As of August 19, the country had 109 subnational laboratories that could detect the virus and had conducted 2,193,448 tests on more than 2,051,983 people.
Cheshire is a county in England. Cheshire can also mean:

cardboard refers to strong paper-based products used for making boxes and containers. It is thicker than regular paper and can be more foldable, stiff, and resistant to impacts. Cardboard can be a thick sheet called paperboard or a special type with layers of corrugated and flat sheets, known as corrugated fiberboard. While people use the term cardboard in everyday language, experts in business and industry prefer more precise terms.

Kalmar BTK is a table tennis club in Kalmar, Sweden. It was founded on June 14, 1960. The club won the Swedish national men's team championship in 1996, 1999, 2000, and 2002. Jan-Ove Waldner played for the club from 1996 to 2006.

Westville is a village in Georgetown Township, Vermilion County, Illinois, United States. It is in the Danville, Illinois, metropolitan area. In 2010, the population was 3,202. By 2018, it had 2,990 people.

Borno, also called Borno State, is a state in northeastern Nigeria. Its capital and biggest city is Maiduguri. It became a separate state in 1976 from a split of the northeastern state. Until 1991, it included what is now Yobe State. The state's slogan is "Home of Peace." Borno is where the Kanuri people and other groups live in Nigeria. Since 2009, it has been where Boko Haram, an Islamist group, started its attacks. In 2009, there were fights between Boko Haram and government soldiers, and Boko Haram's founder, Mohammed Yusuf, was reportedly captured. He was announced dead later. After many years of fighting that hurt the economy and daily life, Borno's governor, Babagana Umara Zulum, in 2019 started a plan. He hired 10,000 people who he thought had magic powers to help defeat the attackers.

In the U.S., a "Terry" stop lets police briefly detain someone if they think the person might be involved in a crime. This is less strict than needing probable cause for an arrest. Stopping and searching a pedestrian is often called a "stop and frisk." When a car is stopped, it's known as a "traffic stop." If police stop a car for small reasons to check for other crimes, it's called a "pretextual stop." Additional rules apply when stops happen on a bus. A single officer stopping one person is different from a police department or city promoting this practice. This can damage trust between police and the community and lead to accusations of racial profiling. The Supreme Court has given many rulings defining how police can search and arrest people based on the Fourth Amendment. However, Congress hasn't set a basic standard for police behavior. Some states have made laws and passed judgments on these issues, and a few cities have created rules too. This article will mainly discuss these issues nationally, unless noted otherwise. Local and state laws might differ, but that's rare.
Hartberg-Fürstenfeld is a district in Styria, Austria. It started on January 1, 2013, after combining the areas of Hartberg and Fürstenfeld.

Frenzy is a 1972 British thriller film directed by Alfred Hitchcock. It is his last major film before moving to Hollywood. The screenplay was written by Anthony Shaffer and based on a 1966 novel by Arthur La Bern. The main actors are Jon Finch, Alec McCowen, and Barry Foster. The film also stars Billie Whitelaw, Anna Massey, Barbara Leigh-Hunt, Bernard Cribbins, and Vivien Merchant. Ron Goodwin composed the music. The story focuses on a serial killer in London and an ex-RAF serviceman who is accused. Early in the film, there is dialogue mentioning two real London serial murders: the Christie murders from the early 1950s and the Jack the Ripper murders in 1888. For his role, Barry Foster studied books about Neville Heath, an English serial killer who often pretended to be an RAF officer. This was Hitchcock's third and final film made in Britain after moving to Hollywood in 1939. The other films were Under Capricorn in 1949 and Stage Fright in 1950 (with some scenes filmed in London for the 1956 remake of The Man Who Knew Too Much). Hitchcock's last film made in Britain before moving to America was Jamaica Inn in 1939. The film was shown at the 1972 Cannes Film Festival but not in the main competition.

Saline, or saline solution, is water with sodium chloride mixed in. It is used in medicine for several purposes. To clean wounds, it is applied directly to the affected area. It also helps remove contact lenses and treats dry eyes. When given through a vein, saline can treat dehydration from conditions like gastroenteritis or diabetic ketoacidosis. It is used to dilute other medications for injection as well. However, using too much can cause fluid overload, swelling, acidosis, and high blood sodium levels. For people with low blood sodium for a long time, excessive use might lead to osmotic demyelination syndrome. Saline belongs to a group called crystalloid medications. The most common form is a sterile 0.9% salt solution, known as normal saline. Other concentrations can also be used occasionally. Saline has a slightly acidic pH, mainly due to dissolved carbon dioxide. The use of saline began around 1831. It is an essential medicine on the World Health Organization's list. In developing countries, a liter of normal saline typically costs between $0.60 and $4.20. In 2017, sodium was the 225th most commonly prescribed medication in the United States, with over two million prescriptions.

Inversnaid, in Scottish Gaelic "inbhir snàthaid," is a small rural community on the east side of Loch Lomond in Scotland. It's near the northern end of the loch. Inversnaid has a pier and a hotel. The West Highland Way also goes through this area. There's a small ferry that runs from Inversnaid to Inveruglas on the opposite side of the loch. There's also a seasonal ferry between Ardlui and Ardleish, which is close to Inversnaid. To get to Inversnaid by road, you need to come from Aberfoyle. Nearby, there's a cave called Rob Roy's Cave, where Rob Roy MacGregor, a historical figure, is said to have hidden. The cave is hard to reach, but you can see its location marked by white paint on Loch Lomond.

Oona Castilla Chaplin, born on June 4, 1986, is a Spanish-British actress. She has played Talisa Maegyr in the TV show "Game of Thrones," Kitty Trevelyan in "The Crimson Field," and Zilpha Geary in "Taboo." She is part of the Chaplin family. Her mother is actress Geraldine Chaplin. Her father is the grandson of filmmaker and actor Charlie Chaplin, and the great-grandson of American playwright Eugene O'Neill. Oona was named after her maternal grandmother, Oona O'Neill, who was Charlie Chaplin's wife.

Andry Nirina Rajoelina, born on May 30, 1974, is a Malagasy politician and businessman. He is currently the president of Madagascar. Rajoelina began his career in the private sector. He organized events like live concerts. Later, he worked in advertising businesses, including Injet, billboards, and print media. He also managed media channels like Viva, as well as TV and radio. He was the mayor of Antananarivo from December 2007 to February 2009. From March 21, 2009, to January 25, 2014, he was the president of the High Transitional Authority of Madagascar. After the 2013 general elections, he continued as the head of the majority party, MAPAR. He won the 2018 presidential election and was inaugurated as president on January 19, 2019.
Rény Angélil was a Canadian music producer, talent manager, and singer. He worked as Céline Dion's manager from 1981 to 2014. They were also husband and wife from 1994 until his death in 2016.

alfred pleasonton was born on july 7, 1824, and died on february 17, 1897. He was a soldier in the united states army and became a major general in the union cavalry during the american civil war. During the gettysburg campaign, he led the cavalry corps of the army of the potomac. This included the largest battle mainly involving cavalry, known as brandy station. In 1864, he moved to the trans-mississippi theater. There, he defeated confederate general sterling price in two important battles, including the battle of mine creek, which was the second largest cavalry battle of the war. This helped end the war in missouri. He was the son of stephen pleasonton and the younger brother of augustus pleasonton.

The Metre Convention, also known as the Treaty of the Metre, is an international agreement signed on May 20, 1875, in Paris. Seventeen countries signed it: Argentina, Austria-Hungary, Belgium, Brazil, Denmark, France, Germany, Italy, Peru, Portugal, Russia, Spain, Sweden and Norway, Switzerland, the Ottoman Empire, the United States, and Venezuela. This treaty created the International Bureau of Weights and Measures (BIPM), an organization under the General Conference on Weights and Measures (CGPM) and the International Committee for Weights and Measures (ICWM). The BIPM helps with measuring and developing the metric system. The convention set up a permanent structure for countries to work together on measurement matters. Only countries can be official members, but in 1999, the CGPM allowed states and economic entities to join as associates through their national metrology institutes. Being a member means paying fees, and failing to pay for years can lead to a country being removed. Initially, the convention dealt with mass and length units. In 1921, at the 6th CGPM meeting, it was updated to cover more areas in physics. In 1960, at the 11th CGPM meeting, the system of units it created was named the International System of Units (SI).

The king's gambit is a chess move where white gives up a pawn to make black's e-pawn less secure. If black accepts, white has two main strategies. One is to play d4 and bxf4, regaining the pawn and controlling the center. The other is to play nf3 and bc4, followed by 0-0. This creates an open f-file, allowing white to attack black's f7 pawn. Black might need to weaken their position with moves like g5 or placing pieces oddly. A downside is that white's king becomes weaker, making it vulnerable to checks like qh4+. With a black pawn on f4, white can't respond with g3. Moving the king also means losing the right to castle. The king's gambit is one of the oldest documented chess openings. It was studied by 17th-century Italian chess player Giulio Cesare Polerio and appears in Luis Ramírez de Lucena's "Repetición de amores y arte de ajedrez" (1497). It was very popular until the late 19th century but is now rarely seen in high-level games because black has good defenses. However, it remains popular among amateur players.

A strongpoint is a crucial part of a defensive position. It helps hold the overall defense. Strongpoints can be redoubts, bunkers, pillboxes, trenches, or fortresses, used alone or together. The main rule is that they must be hard to take over or bypass. In good defense, blocking positions on high ground are preferred, as they control the paths that enemies might use. History shows examples like Thermopylae, where ancient Greeks kept back a much larger Persian army, and Monte Cassino, which supported the winter line in Italy during World War II.

A hedgehog is a spiny mammal belonging to the subfamily Erinaceinae in the Erinaceidae family. There are 17 species of hedgehogs in five groups, found in parts of Europe, Asia, and Africa, as well as in New Zealand by introduction. There are no native hedgehogs in Australia, and none native to the Americas, except for an extinct type in North America. Hedgehogs are distant relatives of shrews and possibly related to gymnures. They have not changed much over the last 15 million years and are mostly active at night. Their spines look similar to those of porcupines and echidnas.

Kembangan MRT station is an above-ground Mass Rapid Transit (MRT) station on the East-West Line in Bedok, Singapore. It is near the junction of Sims Avenue East and Jalan Kembangan. Part of the station is directly above the Siglap Canal. The name "Kembangan" means "expansion" in Malay.

The Industrial and Mining Water Research Unit (IMWARU) is part of the School of Chemical and Metallurgical Engineering at the University of the Witwatersrand in Johannesburg. IMWARU does research and supervises master's and doctoral students. It also helps businesses with their water-related issues.

Madison County is in Arkansas, a state in the U.S. In 2010, it had 15, 717 people. The county seat is Huntsville. Madison County was created on September 30, 1836, and was named after James Madison, the fourth president of the United States. It is part of Northwest Arkansas.

Mary Fallin (born December 9, 1954) was an American politician who was Oklahoma's governor from 2011 to 2019. She was a Republican and was elected in 2010, then re-elected in 2014. Before becoming governor, Fallin was in politics. She was first elected to the Oklahoma House of Representatives in 1990 and served two terms from 1990 to 1995. In 1994, she became the 14th Lieutenant Governor of Oklahoma, serving for three terms until 2007. In 2007, Fallin was elected to the U.S. House of Representatives, representing Oklahoma's 5th district, where she served until 2011. In 2010, Fallin ran for governor. She won the Republican primary with 54% of the votes and the general election with 60% of the votes. She was re-elected in 2014. However, her time as governor was controversial, with many people disagreeing with her. A 2018 poll showed she was the most unpopular governor in the country. Fallin could not run for governor again due to term limits. Kevin Stitt became the new governor after her.

In algebra, a nested radical is a radical expression that contains another radical expression. For example, a nested radical like appears in studying a regular pentagon. More complex ones exist as well.

"Baby, Don't Forget My Number" is a song by the German dance-pop group Milli Vanilli. It came out in December 1988 as the second single from their album "Girl You Know It's True." In 1989, it became their first number one hit on the Billboard Hot 100 chart. In 1992, Weird Al Yankovic made fun of this song and another one called "Blame It on the Rain" by singing "The Plumbing Song" for his album "Off the Deep End." The single was also certified gold in the USA by the RIAA.

Echinoderms are marine animals, including starfish, sea urchins, sand dollars, and sea cucumbers. They are known for their five-point radial symmetry. Echinoderms are found in all ocean depths, from shallow to deep water. There are about 7,000 species of echinoderms, making them the second-largest group of deuterostomes, after chordates, which include vertebrates like mammals, birds, and fish. Unlike many other animals, echinoderms do not live in freshwater or on land. The first echinoderms appeared early in the Cambrian period. Some Cambrian echinoderms had external gills for filter feeding. Echinoderms are important in both ecology and geology. They are abundant in deep seas and shallow waters, and can reproduce asexually and regrow body parts. Their hard skeletons contribute to limestone formations and helped with regenerative research in the 19th and 20th centuries. Some scientists believe the rise of echinoderms contributed to the Mesozoic Marine Revolution.

Ataç Ankara was a former prime minister of the Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus. He was prime minister from 1994 to 1996. Born in 1935 in Famagusta, he became an engineer-architect in 1959 after studying in Istanbul. He also studied urban planning at Manchester and Nottingham universities. From 1961 to 1975, he held several public jobs. In 1963, he was the regional director of planning for Limassol-Paphos. In 1967, he became the head of the planning and construction department. In 1975, he was the undersecretary of housing. In 1976, 1981, 1985, and 1990, he was elected as a member of parliament from the National Unity Party. He served as minister of settlement and rehabilitation, minister of economy and finance, and minister of national education, culture, youth, and sports. He was also the secretary general of the National Unity Party. In 1983, he was a member of the constituent assembly and served as minister of settlement in the first republican government. From 1985 to 1993, he was the speaker of the assembly of the republic. In 1992, he became the president of the Democratic Party, formed from a movement within the National Unity Party. In 1993, he was elected to parliament from the Democratic Party and served as prime minister in 1994-1996. He was re-elected as the speaker of the assembly in 1996. He did not participate in parliament afterward. He is the honorary president of the Democratic Party and speaks English and some Greek. He is married with two children. His aunt is the third president of the Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus, Derviş Eroğlu.

Drake's "Scorpion" is the fifth album he made. It came out on June 29, 2018. The album has two parts and 25 songs. The first part is mostly hip hop, while the second has r & b and pop songs. Drake made it with help from 40 and Oliver El-Khatib. Jay-Z and Ty Dolla Sign are on the album. Michael Jackson and Static Major are there too, but they're not alive. The songs talk about Drake's fame, his relationships, and how he became successful. The music uses different styles like soul, pop, and trap. Seven songs from the album were popular. They were on the top 20 of the Billboard Hot 100. "God's Plan," "Nice for What," and "In My Feelings" even reached number one. On its first day, the album streamed over 132 million times on Spotify and 170 million times on Apple Music. It sold 732,000 album-equivalent units on its first day. By January 2019, it had sold five times more than a million copies. Critics didn't like the album much, but it was a big hit. "Scorpion" got five nominations at the 2019 Grammys, including Album of the Year. "God's Plan" won Best Rap Song. Drake also won the Top Billboard 200 Album award at the 2019 Billboard Music Awards.

Exology Chapter 1: The Lost Planet is the first live album by EXO, a South Korean-Chinese boy band. It came out on December 22, 2014, through SM Entertainment. The album has two CDs with a total of 36 songs. Each member of EXO has individual tracks, and some songs have remix versions in Korean and Mandarin. There were two versions of the album: a regular one and a special edition.

An ofrenda is a collection of objects for a special display during the Day of the Dead celebration in Mexico. An ofrenda, which can be large and fancy, is usually made for someone who has died. It is meant to welcome that person to the altar.
Chidester is a city in Ouachita County, Arkansas, United States. In the year 2000, it had 335 people living there. Chidester is part of the Camden micropolitan area.

Guatemala is a department in Guatemala. The capital is Guatemala City, which is also the national capital. The department includes Guatemala City and some nearby suburbs. It covers an area of and had 3,015,081 people living there according to the 2018 census.
Hardancourt is a commune in the Vosges department, which is in the Grand Est region of northeastern France.

Bill Moggridge, born on June 25, 1943, and passed away on September 8, 2012, was a British designer, writer, and teacher. He helped start the design company ideo and led the Cooper-Hewitt, National Design Museum in New York. Moggridge was known for focusing on people in his designs. He is credited with creating the term "interaction design." He also designed the first laptop computer, the Grid Compass. He received awards for his lifetime achievements and the Prince Philip Designers Prize. Moggridge once said, "The main idea tying everything I've done together is my interest in people and how they use things."

Lady Susan is a short novel by Jane Austen. It was likely written in 1794 but not published until 1871. This early complete work, which the author never tried to publish, tells about the schemes of the main character.

The Vickers Viscount is a British medium-range turboprop airliner. It first flew in 1948. Made by Vickers-Armstrongs, it entered service in 1953. It was the first turboprop-powered airliner. People liked it because it had a comfortable cabin with pressurization, less vibration and noise, and big windows. It was very successful and profitable after World War II. In total, 445 Viscounts were built for customers around the world, including in North America.

The Blossoms were an American girl group from California. In the 1960s, they were most known for Darlene Love, Fanita James, and Jean King. Although they had their own recordings, they were famous for singing backup on big hit songs. They recorded the number one hit "He's a Rebel," which Phil Spector credited to the Crystals. The Blossoms were like the Sweet Inspirations on the West Coast and the Andantes for Motown.

TesOL International Association, formerly known as Teachers of English to Speakers of Other Languages, is the biggest organization for English as a second or foreign language teachers. It was created in 1966 and is based in Alexandria, Virginia, United States. In 2018, it had 10,113 members worldwide, and was linked to 109 language education organizations, with most of them located outside the United States. The organization had around 44,000 members in total, including those from affiliated groups. TesOL publishes two academic journals: "TESOL Quarterly" and "TESOL Journal". During summer, it holds professional development seminars called "TESOL Academies" in the United States. It also organizes an annual convention.

Neptune Beach is a beach city in Duval County, Florida, east of Jacksonville. In 1968, most of Duval County's communities joined Jacksonville. However, Neptune Beach, along with Jacksonville Beach, Atlantic Beach, and Baldwin, stayed mostly separate. These towns keep their own local government. Neptune Beach residents vote for the Jacksonville mayor and have representatives on the Jacksonville city council. The 2010 census showed the population was 7,037. Neptune Beach is part of the Jacksonville Beaches area.

The Plymouth Fury was a car made by Plymouth from 1955 to 1989. It was first sold in 1956 as part of the Plymouth Belvedere series. In 1959, it became a separate series, one level above the Belvedere. The Fury was a full-size car from 1959 to 1961. Then, it became a mid-size car from 1962 to 1964. It was again a full-size car from 1965 to 1974, and from 1975 to 1978, it was a mid-size car. From 1975 to 1977, the Fury was sold together with the full-size Plymouth Gran Fury. In 1978, the Fury was the largest Plymouth. In 1979, there were no large Plymouths. To fix this, in 1980, the Gran Fury with the R-body was introduced. The M-body Fury was produced in 1982. The last V8, rear-wheel-drive Plymouth Fury was made in Kenosha, Wisconsin, on December 23, 1988. Unlike its sister brand Dodge, Plymouth did not survive the revival of large, V8 rear-wheel-drive sedans. The last Plymouth car rolled off the Belvedere assembly line in 2001.

Franzobel is the pen name of the Austrian writer Franz Stefan Griebl. He was born on March 1, 1967, in Vöcklabruck. In 1997, he won the Wolfgang Weyrauch Prize, and in 1998, the Kassel Literary Prize. He has also received many other literary awards. In 2017, he won the Nicolas Born Prize and was nominated for the German Book Prize for his novel "Das Floß der Medusa." He now lives in Vienna.

Westmeath is a county in Ireland. It is in the province of Leinster and is part of the Midlands region. The county originally belonged to a historic kingdom called Meath, which means "middle." Westmeath got its name because it was in the middle of Ireland. The county council manages the area, and the county town is Mullingar. In 2016, the county had 88,770 people.

Graves' disease, also called toxic diffuse goiter, is an autoimmune disorder affecting the thyroid. It usually leads to hyperthyroidism, an overactive thyroid, and often causes an enlarged thyroid. Symptoms of hyperthyroidism include irritability, weak muscles, trouble sleeping, fast heartbeat, sensitivity to heat, diarrhea, and unexpected weight loss. Other symptoms may be thick, puffy skin on the shins and eye bulging, caused by Graves' ophthalmopathy. About 25 to 80% of people with the disease may develop eye problems. The exact cause is unknown but involves genes and environment. Having a family member with the disease increases the risk. The disease can start after physical or emotional stress, an infection, or giving birth. People with other autoimmune diseases like type 1 diabetes or rheumatoid arthritis are more likely to get it. Smoking raises the risk and can make eye problems worse. Graves' disease results from antibodies called thyroid-stimulating immunoglobulin (TSI) that act like thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH), causing the thyroid to produce too much hormone. Diagnosis involves symptoms, blood tests, and radioactive iodine uptake. Three treatment options are radioiodine therapy, medication, and surgery. Radioiodine therapy uses iodine-131 to destroy the thyroid, leading to hypothyroidism treated with thyroid hormone pills. Medications like beta blockers can control symptoms, and antithyroid drugs like methimazole can help. Eye problems need special treatment. About 0.5% of men and 3% of women get Graves' disease, happening 7.5 times more often in women. It often starts between 40 and 60 years old but can occur at any age. It is the leading cause of hyperthyroidism in the US, making up 50 to 80% of cases. The disease was named after Irish surgeon Robert Graves, who first described it in 1835. Earlier descriptions also exist.
