Bradford Interchange is a transport hub in Bradford, West Yorkshire, England. It includes a railway station and a bus and coach station next to each other. The interchange was designed in 1962 and opened on January 14, 1973. Most bus services in the city center stop there, along with National Express coaches. The railway station, one of two in the city center, is served by Northern trains and is also the final stop for Grand Central services from London King's Cross.
"When the tigers broke free" is a Pink Floyd song by Roger Waters. The song talks about the death of his father, Eric Fletcher Waters. Eric Waters died in the Battle of Anzio during World War II.

Neon Trees is an American rock band from Provo, Utah. In late 2008, they opened for the band The Killers on several North American tour dates. This helped them become well-known across the country. Not long after, Mercury Records signed them. In 2010, they released their first album, "Habits." Their first single, "Animal," was very popular. It reached number 13 on the Billboard Hot 100 and number 1 on the Alternative Songs chart.

Elbert D. Glover is a researcher and writer about tobacco addiction and helping people stop smoking. He teaches at the University of Maryland in College Park. He is a professor of public health and heads the department of behavioral and community health.

Margaret Jobeth Williams, born on December 6, 1948, is an American actress and television director. In 1994, she directed a short film called "On Hope," which got her nominated for an Academy Award. Since 2009, she has been the president of the Screen Actors Guild Foundation. Williams became famous for her roles in movies like "Stir Crazy" (1980), "Poltergeist" (1982), "The Big Chill" (1983), "The Day After" (1983), "Teachers" (1984), and "Working Girl" (1986). She has been nominated for three Emmy Awards. Her nominations were for acting in TV movies and shows. She was nominated for her role in "Adam" (1983) and "Baby M" (1988). She also got nominated for her role in the sitcom "Frasier" (1993-94). Williams also appeared in TV series like "The Client" (1995-96), and had regular roles in "Dexter" (2007) and "Private Practice" (2009-11).

Versigny is a town in Aisne, which is in Hauts-de-France, a region in northern France. It belongs to a group called Communauté de communes des villes d'Oise. Versigny is located between Saint-Quentin, Laon, and Chauny.

Forgetting Sarah Marshall is a 2008 American romantic comedy. Nicholas Stoller directed it, with Jason Segel, Kristen Bell, Mila Kunis, and Russell Brand in the main roles. Segel also wrote the screenplay, and Judd Apatow co-produced. Universal Pictures released the film. Filming started in April 2007 at the Turtle Bay Resort in Hawaii. The movie came out in North American theaters on April 18, 2008, and in the UK a week later, on April 25, 2008. The story is about Peter Brett, a music composer for a TV show. His girlfriend, Sarah Marshall, plays the lead role in the show. After five years together, Sarah suddenly breaks up with Peter. Feeling sad, Peter goes to Hawaii for a vacation to move on. However, he meets Sarah there, who is there with her new boyfriend.

Justin Marie Bomboko Lokumba was born on September 22, 1928, and died on April 10, 2014. He was a Congolese politician and statesman. Bomboko served as the foreign minister of Congo. He also led the Congolese government as the chairman of the college of commissioners. People often call him "the father of independence" for Congo. He held the position of foreign minister three times: from 1960 to 1963, from 1965 to 1969, and again in 1981. Bomboko passed away in Brussels, Belgium, due to a long illness, at the age of 85.
Anthony Lane is a British journalist. He works as a film critic for The New Yorker magazine.

Meccano is a model construction system created in 1898 by Frank Hornby in Liverpool, United Kingdom. It includes metal strips, plates, angle girders, wheels, axles, and gears, which are connected using nuts and bolts. You can build working models and mechanical devices with it. Meccano has a manufacturing facility in Calais, France. In 2013, the Meccano brand was bought by a Canadian toy company called Spin Master. In 1913, a similar construction set was introduced in the United States under the name Erector. In 2000, Meccano acquired the Erector brand and became present on all continents.

Red is a color at the end of the light spectrum, next to orange and opposite violet. It has a wavelength of about 625 to 740 nanometers. Red is a primary color in both the RGB and CMYK color models. It is also the complementary color of cyan. Red comes in many shades, from bright yellow-tinged scarlet and vermillion to bluish-red crimson. It ranges from pale pink to dark burgundy. People used red ochre pigment in prehistoric art. Ancient Egyptians and Mayans wore red during ceremonies, and Roman generals had their faces painted red to celebrate victories. In China, red was used to color early pottery and later to paint palace gates and walls. During the Renaissance, nobles and the wealthy wore brilliant red clothing made from kermes and cochineal dyes. The 19th century brought synthetic red dyes, which replaced the traditional ones. Red became the color of revolution; after the Bolshevik revolution in 1917, Soviet Russia adopted a red flag. Later, China, Vietnam, and other communist countries followed suit. Red relates to blood, historically associated with sacrifice, danger, and courage. In modern surveys in Europe and the US, red is often linked to heat, activity, passion, sexuality, anger, love, and joy. In China, India, and many other Asian countries, red symbolizes happiness and good fortune.

Timothy J. Davlin was the mayor of Springfield, Illinois, from April 2003 until his suicide in December 2010. He was 53 years old when he died. The mayor's job is supposed to be non-partisan, but in Springfield, there is a strong tradition of political parties. Both main parties in Sangamon County support candidates. Davlin was supported by the Democratic Party.
José Francisco "El Nene" Sanfilippo was born on May 4, 1935. He is a former Argentine football player who played as a striker.

leishmania causes leishmaniasis. It is spread by sandflies. In the Old World, these sandflies are from the "Phlebotomus" genus. In the New World, they are from the "Lutzomyia" genus. At least 93 sandfly species can spread the disease. Sandflies primarily feed on vertebrates. Leishmania commonly infects hyraxes, dogs, rodents, and humans.

Mycoplasma genitalium (Mgen) is a small, sexually transmitted bacterium found in the skin cells of the urinary and genital areas. Reports from 2007 and 2015 show it is becoming more common. It now has resistance to some antibiotics, including azithromycin, which was previously the main treatment. Mgen was first identified in 1981 and became a new species in 1983. It can affect both men and women, causing health issues like urethritis and cervicitis. It also increases the risk of HIV spread, especially in men who have sex with men and those treated with azithromycin. Mgen causes symptoms similar to chlamydia and is found more often than chlamydia and gonorrhea in some groups. Its complete genetic code was published in 1995, with 475 genes and a size of 0.58 megabases. It once had the smallest known genome until 2003, when a new species was found. However, it still has the smallest genome of any self-replicating organism, making it a key subject in minimal genome research. In 2008, the first organism with a synthetic genome, named "Mycoplasma genitalium" JCVI-1.0, was created at the J. Craig Venter Institute. In 2014, a protein called protein M from M. genitalium was discovered.
accept can mean: agree receive consent
Code name: Kids Next Door – Operation: S.O.D.A. is a platformer video game based on the animated TV show. It came out in 2004, only for the Game Boy Advance.

"Mr. Know It All" is a song by American pop singer Kelly Clarkson. It was written and produced by Brian Kennedy, Ester Dean, Brett James, and Dante Jones. Clarkson said the song sounds like her live performances and has minimal auto-tune. The song came out on September 5, 2011, as the first single from her album "Stronger." "Mr. Know It All" is a mid-tempo song with R&B influences, about heartbreak and relationships with snobs. Critics mostly liked the song, saying it was different from Clarkson's earlier work. Some compared it to Alicia Keys' "Doesn't Mean Anything" and Bruno Mars' "Just the Way You Are." The song was a hit, reaching the top 10 on the Billboard Hot 100 and the Adult Pop Songs chart. It topped charts in Australia and South Korea, and made top-10 in New Zealand, Poland, and the UK. It was also a country hit, Clarkson's first solo single on the Billboard Hot Country Songs chart since 2002. RCA later made a country version with Dann Huff producing. Clarkson performed "Mr. Know It All" at the 2011 NRL Grand Final, on The X Factor in Australia, Britain, and Germany, and during her Stronger Tour. The music video, directed by Justin Francis, shows mean headlines about Clarkson.

Huáscar Inca (Quechua: "Waskar Inca," 1503–1532) was the sapa Inca, or ruler, of the Inca Empire from 1527 to 1532. He took over from his father, Huayna Capac, and his brother, Ninan Cuyochi. Both his father and brother died from smallpox while fighting near Quito.
cléden-poher is a commune in Finistère, which is in Brittany, a region in western France.

Jacques Dupont was born on June 19, 1928, and passed away on November 4, 2019. He was a French racing cyclist and won a gold medal in the 1000m time trial at the 1948 Summer Olympics in London. He also won a bronze medal in the team road race with José Beyaert and Alain Moineau. Dupont won the Paris–Tours race in 1951 and again in 1955. In 1955, he set a record speed for a 253 km professional race, cycling at an average of 43.666 km per hour and was awarded the yellow ribbon.

UFCHandle 152: Jones vs. Belfort was a fight event. It was a mixed martial arts pay-per-view. The Ultimate Fighting Championship organized it. It happened on September 22, 2012. The location was Air Canada Centre in Toronto, Ontario, Canada.

A combat sport is a competitive contact sport that usually involves one-on-one fighting. In many combat sports, a contestant wins by scoring more points or by making the opponent unable to fight back. Common combat sports include mixed martial arts, boxing, wrestling, judo, kickboxing, muay thai, and sumo.

The Zitter Forest is in the Eifel region, in the Euskirchen district of North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany, and in the Liège province of Wallonia, Belgium. It is between Hellenthal (north), Dahlem (east), Kronenburg (south), and the Belgian village of Büllingen (west). The Zitter Forest is part of the Hohes Venn-Eifel nature park. To the north, it borders the Eifel National Park. To the south, the River Kyll forms its border with the Schnee Eifel. In the Zitter Forest, between 500 and 692 meters, are the sources of the Olef, Urft, and Kyll rivers. The highest point is at the White Stone (692 meters), southwest of Udenbreth, with ski slopes. Other hills include Bärbelkreuz (662.8 meters), Hühnerhöhe (659.9 meters), and Kamberg (637.8 meters). Villages like Giescheid, Miescheid, Neuhaus, Ramscheid, and Udenbreth in the northern part of the Zitter Forest are in the highest parishes of the Rhineland. The Zitter Forest is one of the last homes of wildcats in Germany. There is a transmission tower called Eifel-Bärbelkreuz within the forest.

Islamgarh, formerly known as Akalgarh, is a municipal committee in Mirpur district, near the Mangla Dam in Azad Jammu and Kashmir. It is located in the southern part of the Pir Panjal range, about 28 kilometers northeast of Mirpur. In 2017, it had a population of 16,651.
Survivor can mean someone who lived through something.

Mallika Sherawat, born on October 24, 1976, is an Indian actress who mostly works in Hindi films. She is known for her bold roles in movies like "Khwahish" (2003) and "Murder" (2004), making her a sex symbol and one of the most popular stars in Bollywood. She gained critical acclaim for her performance in the romantic comedy "Pyaar Ke Side Effects" (2006). Since then, she has appeared in successful films like "Aap Ka Suroor" and "Welcome" (both in 2007), and "Double Dhamaal" (2011). She is one of the few Bollywood actors trying to work in Hollywood, with movies like "Hissss" (2010) and "Politics of Love" (2011).
Midway is a town in eastern Bullock County, Alabama, United States. In 2010, the population was 499 people.

Grenay is a commune in the Pas-de-Calais department, which is in the Hauts-de-France region of France. It is part of the Lens arrondissement and the Wingles canton. Grenay is also in the Lens-Liévin communaupole. In 2013, the population was 6,899. The mayor resigned on March 31, 2019. He was replaced by his first deputy, Mathieu Feutry, until an election.

The 2011 Daytona 500, the 53rd race, happened on February 20, 2011, at Daytona International Speedway in Daytona Beach, Florida. It was the first race of the 2011 NASCAR Sprint Cup season. Trevor Bayne, driving for Wood Brothers Racing, won. He was the youngest to win the Daytona 500. Carl Edwards came in second, and David Gilliland, Bobby Labonte, and Kurt Busch finished third to fifth. Bayne took the lead before the last restart and kept it to win his first cup series race and Wood Brothers' fifth Daytona 500 win. The race had 16 cautions and 74 lead changes by 22 different drivers. After the race, Carl Edwards led in the drivers' championship with 42 points, one more than David Gilliland and Bobby Labonte. Ford led the manufacturers' championship with nine points, three ahead of Toyota and five ahead of Dodge. About 182,000 people attended the race, and 15.6 million watched it on TV.

A flat lens is a lens with a flat shape that can create clear images without distortion. It can have very large openings. Sometimes, the term flat lens is also used for lenses with a negative index of refraction. Flat lenses need a refractive index near -1 over a wide angle. Recently, researchers have shown flat lenses made from metasurfaces.

An LC circuit is a type of electric circuit with an inductor (L) and a capacitor (C) connected together. This circuit can store and release energy as it oscillates at a specific frequency, much like a tuning fork. LC circuits are used to either create signals at a certain frequency or to filter out signals of a specific frequency from complex signals. They are important parts in many electronic devices, especially in radios, where they are used in oscillators, filters, tuners, and mixers. LC circuits are idealized because they assume no energy is lost due to resistance. In real circuits, some energy is lost because of the small but non-zero resistance in the components and wires. The goal is usually to make the circuit oscillate with minimal damping, so the resistance is kept as low as possible. Studying the ideal LC circuit helps us understand how it works, even though real circuits always have some losses. For circuits that include resistance, see RLC circuits.

Ottawa, the capital city of Canada, is located on the south bank of the Ottawa River in eastern southern Ontario. It borders Gatineau, Quebec, and forms the core of the Ottawa-Gatineau area and the National Capital Region. In 2016, Ottawa had 934,243 people in the city and 1,323,783 in the metropolitan area, making it the fourth-largest city and the fifth-largest metropolitan area in Canada. By June 2019, the city had more than a million people. Ottawa was founded as Bytown in 1826 and became Ottawa in 1855. The city grew through many additions and became the political center of Canada. In 2001, Ottawa's area was greatly increased through a new city combination. The name "Ottawa" comes from the Algonquin word "Odawa," meaning "to trade." The city has the most educated people of any Canadian city and is home to many important institutions like the National Arts Centre, the National Gallery, and various national museums.
"Der er et yndigt land," (meaning "There is a beautiful country") is one of Denmark's national anthems.

Young Frankenstein is a 1974 American comedy horror movie. It was directed by Mel Brooks and stars Gene Wilder as the title character, a descendant of Dr. Victor Frankenstein. Peter Boyle plays the monster. Other actors include Teri Garr, Cloris Leachman, Marty Feldman, Madeline Kahn, Kenneth Mars, Richard Haydn, and Gene Hackman. The screenplay was written by Gene Wilder and Mel Brooks. The film mocks classic horror films, especially the 1930s Universal Pictures versions of Mary Shelley's "Frankenstein." Many props, like lab equipment, were created by Kenneth Strickfaden for the 1931 film. To match the older movies, Brooks filmed it in black and white and used 1930s style opening credits and scene transitions. The movie has a period score by John Morris, Brooks' longtime composer. It was both a critical success and a box-office hit. "Young Frankenstein" is ranked #28 on "Total Film" magazine's list of the 50 greatest comedy films. It's also listed as one of the 100 funniest movies by Bravo and as one of the 100 funniest American movies by the American Film Institute. In 2003, it was chosen for preservation by the United States National Film Preservation Board and included in the Library of Congress National Film Registry. Brooks later adapted the film into a stage musical. At its 40th anniversary, Brooks thought it was his best film as a writer-director, though not the funniest.

Vaz/Obervaz is a municipality in the Albula region of Graubünden in Switzerland. It includes these villages: Lain, Muldain, Zorten, Lenzerheide, and Valbella. It also has these hamlets: Nivaigl, Fuso, Trantermoira, Sporz, Tgantieni, Sartons, Creusen, and Obersolis.
Olaf Marschall was born on March 19, 1966. He is a retired German footballer and now works as a sports manager. He played as a forward.

Lafayette County is a county in Wisconsin. It was part of the Wisconsin Territory when it was created. In 2010, there were 16, 836 people living there. The county seat is Darlington. Lafayette County was named after the Marquis de Lafayette, a French general who helped the American army in the Revolutionary War. Scenes from the 2009 movie Public Enemies were filmed at the Lafayette County Courthouse in Darlington.
On October 1, 2016, the city had about 65,075 people. There were around 7,300 people for every square kilometer. The city covers an area of 8.89 square kilometers.
Coimbatore (South) taluk is a part of the Coimbatore city in the state of Tamil Nadu, India.

The Pharaoh hound is a hunting dog from Malta. In Maltese, it's called "imx-xucxr," which means "rabbit dog." It's used to hunt rabbits in Malta's rocky areas. This dog is part of the "spitz and primitive" group according to the Fédération Cynologique Internationale. It looks similar to other Mediterranean hunting dogs like the Cirneco dell'Etna, Podenco Andaluz, Podenco Canario, Podenco Ibizan, and Portuguese Podengo. It's the only Maltese dog breed recognized internationally.

Salem is a city in Livingston County, Kentucky, in the United States. It is part of the Paducah micropolitan area. In 2010, the population was 752, down from 769 in 2000. Salem is the biggest city in Livingston County, but an area called Ledbetter, which is not officially a city, has more people.

Gianni Infantino, born on March 23, 1970, is Swiss and Italian. He works in football administration. He became the president of FIFA in 2016. He was chosen again as FIFA president in 2019. In 2020, he joined the International Olympic Committee.

Rabbi Baruch Mordechai Ezrahi is a well-known rabbi among Haredi Jews. He leads the non-Hassidic Lithuanian Jews. Rabbi Ezrahi is the head teacher at Ateres Yisrael yeshiva in Bayit Vegan, Jerusalem. He is also a member of Degel Hatorah's council of great rabbis. His brother, Rabbi Yitzchok Ezrahi, is the head teacher at the Mir Yeshiva in Jerusalem. Rabbi Ezrahi is married to the daughter of Rabbi Meir Chodosh, who was the spiritual supervisor at the Hebron Yeshiva.

The RSA, based in London, is a British organization that aims to find practical solutions to social challenges. Founded in 1754 by William Shipley, it got a royal charter in 1847 and was allowed to use "Royal" in its name by King Edward VII in 1908. People often use its shorter name, the Royal Society of Arts, and the RSA acronym more than the full name. Notable past members include Charles Dickens, Benjamin Franklin, Stephen Hawking, Karl Marx, Adam Smith, Nelson Mandela, David Attenborough, William Hogarth, John Diefenbaker, and Tim Berners-Lee. Today, the RSA has members from 80 countries around the world. The RSA gives out three medals: the Albert Medal, the Benjamin Franklin Medal, and the Bicentenary Medal. Medal winners include Nelson Mandela, Sir Frank Whittle, and Professor Stephen Hawking. RSA members are creative thinkers who contribute to knowledge, as seen in the first use of "sustainability" in the environmental sense, recorded in the RSA Journal in 1980.

Tokyo, called "Tōkyō" in Japanese, is the capital and most populated prefecture in Japan. Located at the head of Tokyo Bay, it's in the Kantō region on Japan's main island, Honshu. Tokyo is a key political and economic center in the country, home to the Emperor and the national government. In 2019, it had about 13.9 million people. The greater Tokyo area has more than 37.3 million people, making it the world's most populous metropolitan area. Tokyo started as a fishing village named Edo. In 1603, it became an important political center when the Tokugawa Shogunate chose it as their seat. By the mid-1700s, Edo had over a million people, making it one of the world's largest cities. In 1868, the city became the imperial capital, renamed Tokyo, meaning "Eastern Capital." Tokyo faced destruction in the 1923 Great Kantō earthquake and Allied bombing during World War II. Starting in the 1950s, the city was rebuilt and grew quickly, leading Japan's post-war economic recovery. Since 1943, the Tokyo Metropolitan Government has managed 23 special wards, some bed towns, and two island chains. Tokyo has the world's largest urban economy by GDP and is an alpha+ city according to the Globalization and World Cities Research Network. It hosts major businesses, including 36 Fortune Global 500 companies. Tokyo hosted the 1964 Summer Olympics and three G7 summits. It was also set to host the 2020 Summer Olympics, which were delayed due to the COVID-19 pandemic. The city is a research and development hub with notable universities like the University of Tokyo. Tokyo Station serves as a central hub for Japan's high-speed train network, and the city has a large rail and subway system. Distinct areas include Chiyoda, home to the Imperial Palace; Shinjuku, the city's administrative center; and Shibuya, a business and commercial hub.

Frankfort is a city in Clinton County, Indiana, United States. In 2010, it had 16,422 people. The city is also the county seat of Clinton County.

John Paul Gimble was an American country musician. He lived from May 30, 1926, to May 9, 2015. Gimble was known as one of the best fiddlers in western swing music. In 1999, he was recognized for his influence by being inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame as part of Bob Wills and his Texas Playboys. He was also honored after his death in 2018 when he was inducted into the Country Music Hall of Fame.
Clarence M. Kelley was born on October 24, 1911, and died on August 5, 1997. He was an American police officer. Kelley became the second director of the Federal Bureau of Investigation.

The Chaldean Catholic Church is a Catholic church that follows the Eastern rite and uses the Syriac language. It is part of Syriac Christianity and is led by the Chaldean Catholic Patriarch of Babylon. Since 1950, it has had its headquarters in the Cathedral of Mary Mother of Sorrows in Baghdad, Iraq. The current leader is Catholicos-Patriarch Louis Raphaël I Sako. In 2010, the church had 490,371 members, with 310,235 (63.27%) living in the Middle East, mainly in Iraq. Reports show that about 80% of Iraqi Christians belong to this church. According to the U.S. Department of State, Chaldean Catholics make up about 67% of Christians in Iraq. The European Asylum Support Office confirms the same information.

Jesse Lingard, born on December 15, 1992, is an English footballer. He plays as an attacking midfielder or a winger for Manchester United and the England national team. Lingard has won the UEFA Europa League, FA Cup, FA Community Shield, and EFL Cup. He scored in the finals of the FA Cup, FA Community Shield, and EFL Cup. Lingard first played for a senior team while on loan at Leicester City in 2012. He was also on loan at Birmingham City and Brighton & Hove Albion in 2013-2014 and at Derby County in 2015. Before playing for the senior national team, Lingard represented England at the under-17 and under-21 levels. He made his senior international debut in October 2016 and played in the 2018 FIFA World Cup. In the World Cup, England reached the semi-finals and finished fourth.
This is a list of Australia's rivers. Rivers are listed alphabetically by state. Some rivers appear in more than one state because they cross state borders.

racewalking is a long-distance event in track and field. Unlike running, in racewalking, one foot must always touch the ground. Race judges check if this rule is followed. Racewalking events happen on roads or tracks, and common distances range up to 100 kilometers. At the Summer Olympics, there are two racewalking events: 20 kilometers for both men and women, and 50 kilometers for men only. These are road races. The World Athletics Championships also includes these events, plus a 50-kilometer race for women. The IAAF World Race Walking Cup, started in 1961, is a special competition for this sport. It has 10-kilometer races for young athletes, as well as the usual Olympic events. Racewalking developed from an old British activity called pedestrianism, which began setting rules in the mid-1800s. Since the 1950s, athletes from Russia and China have often won. Other top walkers come from Europe and parts of Latin America. To run fast, racewalkers take shorter steps and move as quickly as the best 800-meter runners.

Carl Gustaf Ekman was a Swedish politician born on October 6, 1872, and died on June 15, 1945. He was in the parliament from 1911 to 1932, working in both lower and upper houses. From 1924 to 1932, he led the Freeminded People's Party. Ekman was prime minister twice: from 1926 to 1928, and again from 1930 to 1932.

Rip Taylor Jr. was an American actor and comedian. He was born on January 13, 1931, and passed away on October 6, 2019. Rip was known for his lively personality and colorful appearance, with his wild mustache, toupee, and the habit of showering himself and others with confetti. He performed in nightclubs and on television for over six decades. The Hollywood Reporter described him as a regular at nightclubs and on TV for more than six decades.
Ghost in the machine can mean: A person's mind or soul in their body.

Timpani, or kettledrums, are drums in the percussion family. These drums have a stretched membrane, called a head, over a large bowl usually made of copper. Modern timpani can be tuned quickly using a foot-pedal. They are played with a special stick called a timpani stick. Timpani were once used in military bands but became common in classical orchestras by the late 1700s. Today, they are found in various groups, like concert bands, marching bands, orchestras, and even some rock bands. In Italian, "timpani" means "drums," but in English, "timpano" is used as a singular. Many people call these drums "kettledrums," "timps," or "timp-toms." Sometimes, they are incorrectly called "timpanis." A person who plays timpani is called a timpanist.

Ricardo Montaner is an Argentine-Venezuelan singer and songwriter. His first album, which has the same name as him, was released in 1986. It was called "Ricardo Montaner." This album became number one on the Billboard Latin Pop Albums chart.

Orangeburg County is in South Carolina, a state in the U.S. As of 2010, it had 92, 501 people. The main city is Orangeburg. Orangeburg County was created in 1769. It includes the Orangeburg, SC micropolitan area, part of the Columbia-Orangeburg-Newberry, SC combined statistical area. The county is in South Carolina's Midlands region. Orangeburg County has South Carolina State University, the only public four-year HBCU in the state. It also has Claflin University, the oldest HBCU in the state.

Jasonville is a city in Greene County, Indiana, United States. In 2010, it had 2,222 people. It is the westernmost part of the Bloomington, Indiana, metropolitan area. It is about 15 miles closer to Terre Haute than to Bloomington.

Ganderbal is a town and municipality committee located in the Ganderbal district of Jammu and Kashmir, an Indian union territory. It sits at an average elevation of 1,619 meters (5,312 feet). Ganderbal is surrounded by Srinagar to the south, Bandipore to the north, Kargil to the northeast, Anantnag to the southeast, and Baramulla to the southwest.
Lupsingen is a municipality in the district of Liestal, in the canton of Basel-Country, in Switzerland.
Västerfärnebo is a place in Sala municipality, Västmanland county, Sweden. It had 477 people living there in 2010.

Alejo Carpentier y Valmont was a Cuban writer who lived from 1904 to 1980. He wrote novels, essays, and studied music. Carpentier was born in Switzerland but grew up in Cuba and considered himself Cuban. He traveled a lot, especially in France, South America, and Mexico, where he met important people in the Latin American cultural world. Carpentier cared about politics and supported revolutionary movements, like Fidel Castro’s in Cuba. He was once jailed and had to leave his country because of his political beliefs. Carpentier knew a lot about music and wrote about Cuban music. He used musical ideas in his writing and explored African influences in Cuban culture. He wrote in many genres, but is best known for his novels. Carpentier was one of the first writers to use magical realism, called “lo real maravilloso,” to show the strange and amazing aspects of Latin American history and culture. His famous novel “The Kingdom of This World” is about the Haitian revolution. Carpentier’s writing style mixed Baroque elements with new ideas from European and Latin American art. He was also influenced by French Surrealism. Carpentier explored more than just Cuban culture through his travels in Europe and Latin America. His works included stories about Latin American history, music, social problems, and art. Writers like Lisandro Otero, Leonardo Padura, and Fernando Velázquez Medina were influenced by Carpentier’s work. Carpentier died in Paris in 1980 and was buried in Havana's Colon Cemetery with other important Cuban political and artistic figures.

The United Nations General Assembly adopted Resolution 68/262 on March 27, 2014, during its sixty-eighth session. This resolution responded to Russia's annexation of Crimea. It was called "Territorial Integrity of Ukraine." The resolution, which is not binding, was supported by 100 UN member states. It stated that the United Nations General Assembly is committed to Ukraine's territorial integrity within its internationally recognized borders. It also said that the 2014 Crimean referendum was invalid. Eleven countries voted against the resolution, 58 abstained, and 24 countries were not present when the vote was held. The resolution was introduced by Canada, Costa Rica, Germany, Lithuania, Poland, and Ukraine. Before this resolution, the United Nations Security Council tried to address the Crimean crisis by holding seven meetings. However, Russia vetoed a draft resolution that was proposed by 42 countries, including S/2014/189.
Lavau is a commune in the Yonne department, which is in Bourgogne-Franche-Comté in central France.
Forbing is a community in Caddo Parish, Louisiana, United States. It is in the Shreveport–Bossier City metropolitan area.
Commodore Laurie Brokenshire (1952–2017) was a naval officer, magician, and expert puzzle solver.

Saydabad district is in Maidan, Wardak province, Afghanistan. The district has a nice climate with hills, streams, and orchards. It used to be a popular place for people from Kabul to visit until the late 2000s because of increased violence. The city of Saydabad is the capital of the district and has the most people, with 114,793. Saydabad is in the area where Wardak tribe Pashtuns live.

Nigel David Short, born on June 1, 1965, is an English chess grandmaster. He is also a columnist, coach, and commentator. Since October 2018, he has been the vice-president of FIDE. Short became a grandmaster at 19. He was ranked third in the world by FIDE from January 1988 to July 1989. In 1993, he was the first English player to play in a world chess championship match. He played against Garry Kasparov in the 1993 world chess championship in London. Kasparov won that match with a score of 12½ to 7½.

Nicole Sinclair, born on July 26, 1968, is a British politician. She used to lead a party called "We Demand a Referendum." She was an MEP (Member of the European Parliament) for the West Midlands from 2009 to 2014. Sinclair first became an MEP in June 2009 as a candidate from the UK Independence Party (UKIP). Later, she left UKIP and the European Freedom and Democracy group because some members had extreme right-wing views. She thought these views were not good, especially those that criticized homosexuals and immigrants. From January 2010 to September 2012, she was an independent MEP. During this time, she started "We Demand a Referendum." She lost in the 2014 elections and said, "My workmates have told me I didn't do well enough to be elected as an MEP again for the West Midlands area." Sinclair was the first transgender person to serve in the British parliament.

In physics, a shock wave is a sudden disturbance that travels faster than the speed of sound. It moves through a medium like any other wave but has a sharp change in pressure, temperature, and density. In supersonic flows, an expansion fan, also known as a Prandtl-Meyer expansion fan, can create additional expansion. The expansion wave can interact with the shock wave, causing interference. A sonic boom from a supersonic aircraft is a type of sound wave due to this interference. Unlike solitons, a shock wave's energy and speed decrease quickly over distance. When a shock wave passes through matter, energy is kept but the matter becomes more disordered, increasing entropy. This means less energy can be used as work, and creates resistance for supersonic objects, making shock waves difficult to reverse.

Lewis Collins was an actor born on May 27, 1946, and died on November 27, 2013. He was in films and theater. His most famous role was playing Bodie in a British TV show called "The Professionals" from the late 1970s to the early 1980s.

Summerland, a town with about 11, 615 people, is located on the west side of Okanagan Lake in British Columbia, Canada. It is between Peachland to the north and Penticton to the south. The biggest nearby city is Kelowna, which is north, about 70 kilometers away, reachable via Highway 97. Vancouver is about 320 kilometers west. Summerland is known for "Bottleneck Drive," a route that connects several wineries.

Northeastern University (NU or NEU) is a private research university in Boston, Massachusetts, founded in 1898. It offers undergraduate and graduate programs on its main campus in Boston. The university also has smaller campuses in Charlotte, North Carolina; Seattle, Washington; San Jose, California; San Francisco, California; and in Toronto, Vancouver, and Portland, Maine. In 2019, NEU bought a college of humanities in London, England. It has about 18, 000 undergraduate students and 8, 000 graduate students. NEU is known for a special program called "co-op" that lets students work while studying. Over 3, 100 companies across the world are part of this program. Nearly all undergraduate students do co-op because it makes their university experience different from others. NEU also has a big program for studying abroad. More than 76% of students get financial help. In the 2019-2020 school year, the university gave over $296 million in grants and scholarships. NEU's sports teams, the Huskies, play in Division I of the NCAA. They are part of the Colonial Athletic Association and compete in 18 sports. In recent years, the men's track and field team won two straight championships, and other teams also won titles. The men's hockey team won the Beanpot championship three times in a row.

Esther Salas was born on December 29, 1968. She is a United States district judge who sits in Newark, New Jersey. Before becoming a district judge, she served as a United States magistrate judge for the same court from 2006 until 2011. In 2011, she was confirmed as a district judge. Salas is the first Hispanic woman to hold both positions in New Jersey.

Trapani (,;;; ) is a city and "comune" on the west coast of Sicily, Italy. It is the capital of the Trapani province. Trapani was founded by the Elymians and is still an important fishing port. It is also the main gateway to the nearby Egadi Islands.

Christian Karembeu, born on December 3, 1970, is a French former professional footballer. Currently, he works as a strategic advisor for Olympiacos. During his playing career, he played for several teams, including Nantes, Sampdoria, Real Madrid, Middlesbrough, Olympiacos, Servette, and Bastia. Karembeu had great success with the French national team. Born in New Caledonia, an overseas territory, he was an important player in the 1998 FIFA World Cup held in France and participated in one match in the 2000 UEFA Euro. He is also part of a group in Paris planning to add a Pacific island team to the A-League.

Abdullah bin Abdulaziz Al Saud was the king of Saudi Arabia and custodian of the two holy mosques from August 2005 until his death in 2015. He was one of many sons of Ibn Saud, who started modern Saudi Arabia. Abdullah had important jobs in politics. In 1961, he became the mayor of Mecca. The next year, he became commander of the Saudi Arabian National Guard. He was also deputy defense minister and became crown prince when King Fahd took the throne in 1982. After King Fahd had a serious illness in 1995, Abdullah became the main ruler of Saudi Arabia until he became king. During his rule, Abdullah kept good relations with the United States and the United Kingdom. He also let women vote and compete in the Olympics. He did not change things during the Arab Spring protests. In 2013, a BBC report said Saudi Arabia could get nuclear weapons from Pakistan because of their close relationship. Abdullah also helped Pakistan's ex-leaders by asking General Musharraf to live in Saudi Arabia for 10 years. Before Abdullah became king, he named his half-brother Salman as his successor after the deaths of two other crown princes. Abdullah was married many times and had many children. He was very rich, with a personal fortune of $18 billion. Abdullah died on January 23, 2015, at 90 years old, and was replaced by his half-brother Salman.

A community is a group of people who share common things like rules, beliefs, values, and traditions. They might live in the same place, like a village or neighborhood, or they might connect through communication. Long-lasting relationships beyond family ties also make up a community, which is important for family, work, government, and society. Communities can be small, like a neighborhood, or large, like a country or online group. The word "community" comes from old French and Latin, meaning "shared" or "public spirit." People in a community often have similar goals, beliefs, and needs, which helps them stick together.
Laigné used to be a small village in the Mayenne department of northwestern France. On January 1, 2018, it joined with another village to form a new village called Prée-d'Anjou.

Shaw is a city in Bolivar and Sunflower counties, Mississippi, United States. It is in the Mississippi Delta region. The city's name came from an old Indian tribe located northeast of this area. In 2010, Shaw had a population of 1,952 people.

Cantabria is an autonomous community in northern Spain, with its capital city being Santander. It is known as a historic region and is bordered on the east by the Basque Autonomous Community, on the south by Castile and León, on the west by Asturias, and on the north by the Cantabrian Sea. Cantabria is part of "Green Spain," a region between the Bay of Biscay and the Cantabrian Mountains, famous for its lush vegetation due to its wet and mild climate. The climate is affected by Atlantic winds that are blocked by the mountains, and the yearly average rainfall is around 1,000 millimeters. Cantabria has archaeological sites from the Upper Paleolithic period, with the Cave of Altamira being a significant site for cave paintings, dating back to about 37,000 BC. This cave, along with nine others, was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Cantabria became an official province on July 28, 1778, in Puente San Miguel, Reocín. This date is celebrated as the Province's Institutional Day. The Organic Law of the Autonomy Statute of Cantabria was approved on December 30, 1981, giving the region its own self-governing institutions.

James John Benzelock was born on June 21, 1947. He used to play professional ice hockey as a right winger. In 1968, he was chosen fifth overall in the NHL amateur draft by the Minnesota North Stars. He never played in the National Hockey League. However, he played in 166 World Hockey Association games for the Alberta Oilers, Chicago Cougars, and Quebec Nordiques. Most of his career was with minor professional league teams like the CHL, IHL, and Nahl.

Imperia Tower is a complex on Plot 4 of the Moscow International Business Center in Moscow, Russia. It includes a 60-story skyscraper and a 14-story building under construction. The skyscraper was started in 2001 to 2002, stopped in 2003, then restarted in 2006 and finished in 2011. The 14-story building began construction in 2013 and is expected to be completed by 2018.

Chess Records was an American record company that started in 1950 in Chicago. They focused on blues and rhythm and blues. Over time, they added soul music, gospel, early rock and roll, and some jazz and comedy. Their main label was Chess, and they had other labels like Checker, Argo/Cadet, and Cadet Concept. The entire Chess collection is now owned by Universal Music Group and managed by Geffen Records. The company was run by two brothers, Leonard and Phil Chess, who were Jewish immigrants from Poland. They produced and released many important singles and albums that are considered key in rock music. Musician and critic Cub Koda called Chess "America's greatest blues label." The company had several offices on Chicago's South Side. Their most famous location was at 2120 S. Michigan Avenue from May 1957 to 1965. The Rolling Stones recorded there during their first U.S. tour in 1964 and also recorded there twice more. The building was officially called Ter-Mar Studios but was known as Chess Studios. It is now home to Willie Dixon's Blues Heaven Foundation. In the mid-1960s, Chess moved to a bigger building at 320 E. 21st Street, which was previously the home of Revere Camera Company. Leonard Chess died in 1969, and the brothers sold the company before he passed away.
Raspberry is a color like the color of raspberries. The word "raspberry" as a color name was first used in English in 1892. A book about the "raspberry" color was published by Coloratura in 2018.

chondrostei is a group of fish that have some bones but mostly cartilage. Their ancestors were bony fish with full skeletons. These fish share some features with elasmobranchs, like having spiracles and heterocercal tails. They also lack scales. However, fossils show they are more similar to teleosts. Chondrostei is likely not a perfect group, as it includes about 52 living species in two orders: acipenseriformes (sturgeons and paddlefishes) and polypteriformes (reedfishes and bichirs).

Retalhuleu is a department in southwest Guatemala, stretching from the mountains to the Pacific Ocean. Its area is 1,856 square kilometers. In 2018, Retalhuleu had 326,828 people. The capital is the city of Retalhuleu. The largest group of indigenous people are the K'iche' Maya. The department has several ancient ruins, like Takalik Abaj.

typesetting involves arranging physical letters or digital ones. In mechanical systems, these are called sorts; in digital ones, they are called glyphs. They are arranged based on a language's writing system for display. Typesetting needs one or more fonts, which are sometimes confused with typefaces. An important result of typesetting is that authors can be easily identified, making it harder for those who copy without permission.

Color of Night is a 1994 American erotic mystery film. It was produced by Cinergi Pictures and released in the United States by Hollywood Pictures. Richard Rush directed the movie, starring Bruce Willis and Jane March. Other actors include Ruben Blades, Lesley Ann Warren, Brad Dourif, Lance Henriksen, Kevin J. O'Connor, and Scott Bakula. This is one of two well-known films directed by Rush, the other being "The Stunt Man" 14 years earlier. The film didn't do well at the box office and won a Golden Raspberry Award as the worst film of 1994. However, it became one of the 20 most-rented films in the U.S. home video market in 1995. The "Maxim" magazine named it as having the best sex scene in film history. In 2018, Kino Lorber released a special edition Blu-ray of the film with an audio commentary by director Richard Rush.
Stora Vika is a small place in Nynäshamn municipality, Stockholm County, Sweden. In 2010, it had 651 people living there.

Marie Eugène François Thomas Dubois was born on January 28, 1858, and died on December 16, 1940. He was a Dutch paleoanthropologist and geologist. Dubois gained worldwide fame for finding "Pithecanthropus erectus," later known as "Homo erectus," or "Java Man." Before Dubois, hominid fossils had been discovered and studied, but he was the first to look for them on purpose.

Karch Kiraly, born on November 3, 1960, is from the United States. He played volleyball, coached, and did broadcast work. In the 1980s, he was a key player for the U.S. national team, winning gold medals in the 1984 and 1988 Olympics. He also won gold in the 1996 Olympics, which included beach volleyball for the first time. Kiraly is the only person, male or female, to win Olympic gold in both indoor and beach volleyball. He played college volleyball for UCLA, where his team won three national championships under Coach Al Scates. Currently, Kiraly is the coach of the U.S. women's national volleyball team.

Snap! is a German eurodance group. They were formed in 1989 by producers Michael Münzing and Luca Anzilotti. Over the years, the group has had different members, including American singers, songwriters, and rappers like Thea Austin, Turbo B, and Penny Ford. Their most famous songs are "The Power" and "Rhythm Is a Dancer." Both songs reached number one in many countries.

The glass frogs are part of the centrolenidae family, which is a group of frogs. Most glass frogs are green. However, their belly skin is see-through. You can see their organs, like the heart and liver, through their skin, which is why they are called glass frogs. Glass frogs live in trees and come down for mating only.

benthos is the community of organisms that live on, in, or near the seabed. These organisms are also called benthic zone creatures. They live in or near underwater environments, from the foreshore to the continental shelf, and even to very deep parts of the ocean. Many deep-sea creatures can't survive in the upper parts of the water because of the pressure. The pressure increases by about one atmosphere for every 10 meters of water depth. In the deep ocean, light can't reach, so organisms rely on organic matter that sinks from higher in the water. This matter, when dead and decaying, supports the benthic food chain, with most organisms being scavengers or detritivores. The term "benthos" comes from the Greek word for "depth of the sea" and is used in freshwater biology to describe organisms at the bottom of lakes, rivers, and streams. There is also a similar term, "benthon," though it is rarely used.

Monday is the day between Sunday and Tuesday. In many countries, it is considered the first day of the week. According to ISO 8601, it is officially the first day. In some countries, it is the second day. The name comes from Old English "mōnandæg" and Middle English "monenday," which originally meant "day of the moon."

Development started in 1994, first for the Super Nintendo Entertainment System. Due to delays and technical issues from experimenting with real-time rendering, Square switched to pre-rendered videos. This required more storage space, so they left Nintendo for the PlayStation. Veteran "Final Fantasy" staff, including series creator Hironobu Sakaguchi, director Yoshinori Kitase, and composer Nobuo Uematsu, returned. "Final Fantasy VII" was the first in the series to use full motion video and 3D graphics, with 3D character models over 2D backgrounds. It included more science fiction elements and a more realistic look, but kept similar gameplay to previous games, adding new features like Materia, Limit Breaks, and new mini-games. The development team, about 100 people, had a big budget for both development and marketing. With a large promotional campaign, "Final Fantasy VII" was a big hit, getting good reviews and selling lots of copies. It's seen as an important game and one of the best ever. It won many "Game of the Year" awards and helped sell more PlayStation consoles worldwide. The game's success led to better versions on other platforms, a multimedia sub-series, and a high-definition remake released in 2020.

Melide is a town in the Lugano district of Ticino, Switzerland. It is close to Monte San Salvatore mountain and sits right by Lake Lugano. To the east, there is a causeway called Melide. This was built to connect Melide with Bissone and to allow a north-south highway. Melide is famous for the Swissminiatur museum, which displays miniature versions of famous Swiss buildings.

Ullared is a small town in Falkenberg municipality, Halland county, Sweden. It had 791 people living there in 2010. The village has a big department store called Gekås. It is the biggest store in Sweden and Scandinavia. Because the store sells things at low prices, people often think of Ullared and low prices together. Many stores with lower prices have opened in the village since the early 1990s.

The Durrells, known as The Durrells in Corfu in North America, is a 26-episode British comedy-drama series. It is based on Gerald Durrell's three autobiographical books about his family's four years on the Greek island of Corfu from 1935 to 1939. The series started on April 3, 2016, and ended on May 12, 2019. Simon Nye wrote the series, Steve Barron and Roger Goldby directed it, and Christopher Hall produced it. Lee Morris and Sally Woodward Gentle are the executive producers. Lee Durrell, widow of Gerald Durrell and director of the Durrell Wildlife Conservation Trust, served as a consultant. The series was partly filmed at Ealing Studios and Twickenham Studios in London.

Reading Rainbow was a 30-minute children's educational TV show on PBS Kids. It first aired on July 11, 1983, and ended on August 28, 2009. The show had 155 episodes over 21 seasons. It aimed to encourage kids to read. In 2012, an iPad and Kindle Fire app was launched, also called Reading Rainbow. The TV show won many awards, including a Peabody Award and 26 Emmy Awards. It was created by Twila Liggett, with help from Cecily Truett Lancit, Larry Lancit, Lynne Brenner Ganek, and Ellen Schecter. Levar Burton hosted the show. Each episode focused on a children's book, featuring segments and stories. It also suggested books for kids to find in the library. Reading Rainbow was the third-longest-running children's series on PBS, after Sesame Street and Mister Rogers' Neighborhood. After the show ended in 2006, reruns continued until 2009. In 2012, the Reading Rainbow app was launched, becoming the top educational app in just 36 hours. By 2013, it celebrated its 30th anniversary. In 2014, a Kickstarter campaign raised $5.4 million to make the app available on more devices and provide free access to 13,000 disadvantaged classrooms.

Paul Anthony Samuelson was an American economist, born on May 15, 1915, and died on December 13, 2009. He was the first American to win the Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences. When awarded the prize in 1970, the Swedish Royal Academy said he "had raised the level of scientific analysis in economic theory more than any other contemporary economist." The New York Times considered him the "foremost academic economist of the 20th century." Samuelson was one of the most influential economists of the latter part of the 20th century. In 1996, he received the National Medal of Science, a top honor in America, for his contributions to economic science over 60 years. He saw math as the "language" for economists and wrote a book on the subject, "Foundations of Economic Analysis." He also wrote the best-selling economics textbook of all time, "Economics: An Introductory Analysis," first published in 1948. This book, now in its 19th edition, has sold nearly 4 million copies in 40 languages. Samuelson joined the University of Chicago at age 16 during the Great Depression and earned his PhD from Harvard. He became an assistant professor at MIT at 25 and a full professor at 32. In 1966, he was named Institute Professor, MIT's highest faculty honor. He worked at MIT, helping to make its economics department world-renowned by attracting other famous economists, such as Robert M. Solow, Franco Modigliani, Robert C. Merton, Joseph E. Stiglitz, and Paul Krugman, all of whom won Nobel Prizes. Samuelson advised Presidents John F. Kennedy and Lyndon B. Johnson and worked as a consultant for the U.S. Treasury, the Bureau of the Budget, and the President's Council of Economic Advisers. He wrote a weekly column for Newsweek with Milton Friedman, representing opposing views: Samuelson was a "cafeteria Keynesian," while Friedman held monetarist views. Their columns earned Newsweek a special award in 1968.

richard benaud (born 6 October 1930, died 10 April 2015) was an Australian cricketer. After stopping playing for Australia in 1964, he became a well-known cricket commentator. Benaud was good at both bowling and batting. He used leg spin and was brave in his lower-order batting. He and another bowler, alan davidson, helped Australia become top in world cricket in the late 1950s and early 1960s after a bad period in the early 1950s. In 1958, he became the captain of Australia's test team until he stopped playing in 1964. He was the first player to get 200 wickets and 2,000 runs in test cricket, reaching that in 1963. gideon haigh said benaud was "one of the most important cricket figures since after the second world war." in his review of benaud's book "anything but," sri lankan cricket writer harold de andrado wrote: "richie benaud is one of the greatest cricket personalities as a player, researcher, writer, critic, author, organizer, adviser, and student of the game, next to sir don bradman."

"THE LOUD HOUSE" is an American animated comedy TV show. It first came out on Nickelodeon on May 2, 2016. The show is about Lincoln Loud. He is the only boy and the middle child in a family of girls. Lincoln often talks directly to viewers. He explains the messy home life and sibling relationships in their house.

In Japan, most old provinces had one or more "ichinomiya," which led to place names, like the city of Ichinomiya in Aichi. Shrines of lower rank are called "ninomiya" (second), "sannomiya" (third), "shinomiya" (fourth), and so on.

Jed Allan Brown, born on March 1, 1935, and known as Jed Allan, was an American actor and TV host. He was famous for his roles as C.C. Capwell in "Santa Barbara," Don Craig in "Days of Our Lives," Rush Sanders in "Beverly Hills, 90210," Scott Turner in "Lassie," and Harold Johnson in "The Bay." He also hosted "Celebrity Bowling." He passed away on March 9, 2019.

Gliese 667 cc is an exoplanet in the habitable zone of a red dwarf star called Gliese 667 C. Gliese 667 C is part of a triple star system. This exoplanet is about 23. 62 light-years away, in the constellation of Scorpius. Scientists found it by looking at how the star moves due to the planet's gravitational pull. They noticed changes in the star's light spectrum.

Neumarkt is a "landkreis" (district) in Bavaria, Germany. It is surrounded by the districts of Nürnberger Land, Amberg-Sulzbach, Schwandorf, Regensburg, Kelheim, Eichstätt, and Roth, in a clockwise direction starting from the north.

Caryophyllaceae, often called the pink family or carnation family, is a group of flowering plants. This family, part of the dicotyledon order Caryophyllales, includes 33 other plant families such as amaranthaceae, cactaceae, and polygonaceae. Caryophyllaceae is large, with 81 genera and about 2,625 species. These plants are mostly found in temperate climates but some grow on tropical mountains. Well-known plants in this family include pinks and carnations, and firepink and campions. Many of these plants are grown as ornamental flowers, and some are weeds. Most species can be found in the Mediterranean and surrounding areas of Europe and Asia. In the southern hemisphere, the family has fewer genera and species, but it includes the Antarctic pearlwort, which is the world's southernmost dicot and one of only two flowering plants in Antarctica. The name comes from "caryophyllus," an old name for "dianthus."

Terrel Howard Bell was the secretary of education in President Ronald Reagan's cabinet. He served as the second secretary of education after Shirley Hufstedler. He was born on November 11, 1921, and died on June 22, 1996.

Oberstrass is a quarter in district 6 of Zürich. It used to be its own municipality but became part of Zürich in 1893. The quarter has 9,494 people and covers an area. One of the two funiculars in Zürich is in Oberstrass. Built in 1901 as a restaurant called "Rigiblick," the place was turned into a theater called "Theater Rigiblick" in 1984.

Hemphill is a city in Sabine County, Texas, United States. In 2010, the city had 1,198 people. It is the county seat of Sabine County. Hemphill is on State Highway 87, where State Highway 184 meets it. The city is surrounded by the Sabine National Forest and Toledo Bend Reservoir.

Carla Ragin Bozulich, born on December 24, 1965, is an American musician in Los Angeles. She is the lead singer, writes lyrics, and founded the bands Geraldine Fibbers and Evangelista. Bozulich was also one of the founding members of Ethyl Meatplow and Scarnella. The Geraldine Fibbers made two albums for Virgin Records. Their first album, "Lost Somewhere Between the Earth and My Home," was called "a country feedback masterpiece" by Vice. Bozulich started her Evangelista project in 2006. The first Evangelista album was titled "Evangelista" and came out in 2006. It was released by Constellation Records in Montreal, Quebec, which was the first release by a non-Canadian artist for that label. In 2007, The Sunday Times praised the album, calling it "a vivid inner darkness that outshines rock's wealthy singers." On albums "Hello, Voyager" (2008), "Prince of Truth" (2009), and "In Animal Tongue" (2011), Bozulich used the name Evangelista. Some regular members include bassist Tara Barnes, keyboardist Dominic Cramp, guitarist Nels Cline, violinist Jessica Moss, organist Nadia Moss, drummer Ches Smith, and multi-instrumentalist and co-producer. Various members of Godspeed! You Black Emperor helped with arranging, recording, and writing songs. The Evangelista lineup changes each time they play or record. The "Hello, Voyager" album features music by 14 different musicians. In 2014, Constellation released "Boy," Bozulich's solo work. Her most recent album, "Quieter," came out in May 2018 and includes unreleased recordings. Bozulich has also worked with Francesco Guerri, Novariant/Sarah Lipstate, and Devin Sarno on other projects.
Arkelstorp is a small place in Kristianstad municipality, Skåne county, Sweden. As of the end of 2010, it had 768 people living there.
