A leaf blower, often called a blower, is a tool used in gardening to push air out of a nozzle. This moves things like leaves and grass clippings. Leaf blowers can be powered by electricity or gasoline. Some older gasoline models had two-stroke engines, but newer ones use four-stroke engines to help reduce air pollution. Most leaf blowers are small, handheld devices. Some are worn on a backpack with a handheld wand. This type is better for long use. Larger leaf blowers can have wheels and even use a motor for movement. They are sometimes called "walk behind leaf blowers" because you push them to operate. Some leaf blowers can also suck up leaves and small twigs with a vacuum, then shred them into a bag. In this case, they are known as blower vacs.

Sheyi Emmanuel Adebayor, born on February 26, 1984, is a professional football player from Togo. He plays as a striker. He has played for several clubs, including Arsenal, Manchester City, Tottenham Hotspur, Crystal Palace, Metz, Monaco, Real Madrid, Istanbul Başakşehir, and Kayserispor. He also played for Olimpia in Paraguay. In 2008, while at Arsenal, he was voted African Footballer of the Year. In 2020, he joined Olimpia in Paraguay, becoming their most famous player and the highest-paid player in the country’s history. Adebayor played for the Togo national team in the 2006 FIFA World Cup in Germany. It was the first and only time Togo participated in the World Cup. In January 2010, his Togo team bus was attacked by gunfire on the way to the 2010 Africa Cup of Nations in Angola. After this, he stopped playing for the national team. In 2013, he returned to the national team for the 2013 African Cup of Nations in South Africa, helping Togo reach the quarter-finals. He is Togo’s all-time top goalscorer with 32 goals.

Andrzej Wojciech Suski, born on December 24, 1941, is a retired Polish Roman Catholic prelate. He was born in Płock. Suski became a priest in 1965. He was an auxiliary bishop of Płock from 1986 to 1992. In 1992, he became the bishop of Toruń. He retired in November 2017.

rmjm, also known as Robert Matthew Johnson Marshall, is a large architecture and design company. They offer services like architecture, development management, engineering, interior design, landscape design, and urban design. They also provide master planning, product design, specialist advisory services, and consultancy. The company works with various types of clients, including those in mixed-use, education, healthcare, energy, residential, government, and hospitality sectors. They have specific teams for sport, healthcare, development, and product design. Founded in 1956 by architects Robert Matthew and Stirrat Johnson-Marshall, the company first had offices in London and Edinburgh. Since its beginning, rmjm has focused on modern and contemporary architecture inspired by cultures from around the world.

Herbert Eser "Herb" Gray (May 25, 1931 – April 21, 2014) was a well-known Canadian politician. He was a member of parliament for Windsor West for 40 years, from 1962 to 2002. He was Canada's longest-serving member of parliament. He worked as a cabinet minister under three prime ministers and was deputy prime minister from 1997 to 2002. Gray was Canada's first Jewish federal cabinet minister. He was one of few Canadians given the honorific "The Right Honourable" without holding such a position.
Bodcaw is a town in Arkansas. It is in Nevada County. The population was 154 in the year 2000. Bodcaw is part of the Hope micropolitan statistical area.
Serres-Morlaàs is a village in the Pyrénées-Atlantiques area, which is in southwestern France.

One Nation, a political party in Australia, was founded in 1997 by Pauline Hanson and her advisors, David Ettridge, and David Oldfield. This happened after Hanson was no longer supported by the Liberal Party of Australia in 1996. The disendorsement was due to comments she made about Indigenous Australians. Hanson sat as an independent for one year before forming One Nation. No One Nation candidate has ever been elected to the House of Representatives. However, a candidate from the party was elected to the Senate in 1998, and four were elected in 2016. In state politics, One Nation performed better. In the 1998 Queensland state election, the party won 22% of the vote and 11 seats. In 2016, the party got 4.3% of the nationwide primary vote in the Senate, with the highest percentage in Queensland at 9.2%. Hanson and three other One Nation candidates were elected to the Senate. Hanson serves a six-year term, while the other three serve three years. Culleton lost his seat in January 2017 after going bankrupt. In March 2017, the High Court ruled Culleton's election was invalid due to a criminal conviction. Georgiou took his place. Former Labor Party leader Mark Latham joined One Nation in 2018 as leader for New South Wales and won a seat in the legislative council in 2019. One Nation has a strong nationalist platform. Hanson and other members say they are not racist. Hanson stated, "criticism is not racism; there is real racism in this country: black racism, where you get help because of your skin color." However, a 2001 study showed the party has no formal ties with racist groups but has informal ties with them. These groups include the League of Rights, Australians Against Further Immigration, the Confederate Action Party, National Action, and several militia groups. In 2019, members of the True Blue Crew, a militant white supremacist group, were linked to One Nation candidate Nikhil Reddy.

Interstate 69 (I-69) is a highway in the United States made up of ten separate parts. Originally, it ran from Indianapolis, Indiana, to Port Huron, Michigan, at the Canada–US border. Now, there are other parts that go southwest to the Mexican border in Texas. Some of these parts are fully built and have signs, while others are not yet complete. One part of the extension, nicknamed the NAFTA Superhighway, connects with Canada and Mexico because of the North American Free Trade Agreement. Five sections of this extension, near Corpus Christi, Houston, northwest Mississippi, Memphis, and Evansville, have been completed and have signs. Another part, through Kentucky, was added in 2008 but only a small section has signs. The proposed extension was based on two routes, 18 and 20, from a 1991 law. It includes parts like I-94 between Chicago and Port Huron and some connecting roads. It also suggests extending I-530, upgrading US 59, and adding more roads in southern Texas. In 2007, I-69 was chosen as one of six future corridors, making it get extra federal money and easier planning. But the funding has stopped, causing some states to stop building it.

An observation deck or platform is a raised area where you can see the view, often on tall buildings like skyscrapers or towers. Sometimes, these decks are protected from the weather. Some may even have telescopes you can use with coins to see far-off sights.

Khufu was an ancient Egyptian king and the second ruler of the fourth dynasty. He lived in the Old Kingdom period, around 2600 BC. Khufu took over from his father, Sneferu. He is believed to have built the Great Pyramid of Giza, one of the ancient wonders. The only complete picture we have of him is a small ivory figurine found later in a temple in Abydos. Other pictures and statues of him were damaged. Few of his buildings still exist. Most of what we know about him comes from writings in his burial area and later documents. The Westcar Papyrus, from the 13th dynasty, mentions him. Ancient Egyptian and Greek writers, like Manetho, Diodorus, and Herodotus, wrote about him around 300 BC. They had mixed views, saying he had a good cultural impact but also describing him negatively. These writings give us a unclear, but critical, view of Khufu.

Sela's Closet was a boutique, salon, and clothing store in South Texas. It was opened by the famous Latin singer Selena. Sela's Closet opened in Corpus Christi, Texas on January 27, 1994. A similar store opened in San Antonio, Texas around the same time, and both had in-house salons. Selena also started making clothing with the help of designer Martin Gomez, creating unique Latin American styles. These boutiques earned her over $5 million according to Hispanic Business Magazine. Plans for another store in Monterrey, Mexico, were made but never came to fruition due to Selena's death. The San Antonio store closed around 1999. After Selena's passing, her husband Chris Pérez took over the business. The Corpus Christi store closed in 2009. Chris Pérez sold the store for $165,000. The store sold clothing, jewelry, and Selena memorabilia. Afterward, the merchandise was moved to the Selena Museum.

Cardi B, born Belcalis Marlenis Almánzar on October 11, 1992, is an American rapper, songwriter, TV personality, and actress. She grew up in the Bronx, New York City. Cardi B became famous on the internet after her posts and videos gained popularity on Vine and Instagram. From 2015 to 2017, she was a regular on the TV show "Love & Hip Hop," where she showed her journey in music. She released two mixtapes before signing with Atlantic Records in 2017. Her first big album, "Invasion of Privacy," came out in 2018 and did very well. It was number one on the Billboard charts and won a Grammy for Best Rap Album. This made Cardi B the first female rapper to win this award and the first female rapper to be nominated for Album of the Year in 15 years. Her songs "Bodak Yellow" and "I Like It" were number one hits on the Billboard Hot 100. Her collaboration with Maroon 5, "Girls Like You," was also a number one hit. Cardi B's song "Wap" was another number one hit. Cardi B has received many awards, including a Grammy, Billboard Music Awards, Guinness World Records, and more. She is known for her strong style and honest lyrics. In 2018, Time magazine named her one of the most influential people in the world.
Göteborg Cathedral is a cathedral in Göteborg, Sweden's second-largest city. It serves as the bishop's seat for the Göteborg diocese in the Church of Sweden.
William Thomas Hart, born on February 4, 1929, is a senior judge in the United States District Court for the Northern District of Illinois.

Kahuta tehsil is one of eight subdivisions in the Rawalpindi district, located in the Punjab province of Pakistan. The nearby tehsil, Kallar Sayedan, used to be part of Kahuta but is now separate. Kahuta's name comes from "koh," a local tree with leaves like olives, and "boota." Over time, "koh boota" may have been shortened to Kahuta.

Richard John Hadlee, born on July 3, 1951, is a former New Zealand cricketer. He is considered one of the best fast bowlers and all-rounders in cricket history. Hadlee was made an MBE in 1980 and knighted in 1990 for his contributions to cricket. He used to be the chairman of New Zealand's board of selectors. In December 2002, Wisden chose him as the second greatest Test bowler of all time. In March 2009, Hadlee was honored as one of the twelve local heroes, and a bronze statue of him was unveiled outside the Christchurch Arts Centre. On April 3, 2009, Hadlee was inducted into the ICC Cricket Hall of Fame. He is the most famous player from the Hadlee cricket family.

On August 15, 1945, Emperor Hirohito of Japan announced the country's surrender. This was made official on September 2, 1945. By July 1945, the Japanese navy could not fight anymore, and an attack by Allied forces was expected. In July 1945, the United States, Britain, and China asked Japan to surrender without conditions or face destruction. Even though Japan's leaders wanted to keep fighting, they secretly asked the Soviet Union to help negotiate better terms. The Soviet Union, while pretending to be neutral, secretly planned to attack Japanese forces in Manchuria and Korea. On August 6, 1945, the United States dropped an atomic bomb on Hiroshima. The next day, President Harry Truman warned Japan to surrender. On August 8, 1945, the Soviet Union declared war on Japan and invaded Manchuria. On August 9, 1945, the United States dropped another atomic bomb on Nagasaki. Emperor Hirohito then ordered Japan's leaders to accept the Allied terms, and on August 15, he announced Japan's surrender on the radio. The Allied forces began to occupy Japan on August 28. The surrender ceremony happened on September 2, 1945, on the USS Missouri. Japan signed the surrender document, ending the war. V-J Day was celebrated by Allied forces. However, some Japanese soldiers continued to resist for months and even years. The war officially ended on April 28, 1952, when the Treaty of San Francisco took effect. Japan and the Soviet Union signed a peace agreement in 1956.

Kathleen Rachel Makinson, born White, was born on February 15, 1917, and died on October 18, 2014. She was an Australian physicist. Makinson became the first woman to lead a research team as a chief research scientist at CSIRO, Australia's research organization.

Heian-kyō was one of the names for the city now called Kyoto. It was the official capital of Japan for over one thousand years, from 794 to 1868, with a break in 1180. Emperor Kanmu made Heian-kyō the capital in 794, after his advisor Wake no Kiyomaro suggested moving the imperial court from Nagaoka-kyō. This move started the Heian period in Japanese history. Heian-kyō was the main political center until 1185, when the samurai Minamoto clan defeated the Taira clan in the Genpei War. They moved the administration to Kamakura and set up the Kamakura Shogunate. Although the samurai class controlled politics, Heian-kyō remained the place of the imperial court and the center of imperial power, so it stayed the official capital. Even after the imperial court moved to Tokyo in 1868, some people think Kyoto is still the official capital legally. In 1994, Kyoto celebrated its 1200th anniversary with different events.

The globe artichoke, also called French artichoke or green artichoke in the U.S., is a type of thistle grown for food. The part we eat are the flower buds before they bloom. These buds are clusters of small flowers surrounded by bracts and an edible base. Once they bloom, the structure becomes coarse and not very tasty. Another variety of the same plant is the cardoon, a perennial found in the Mediterranean region. Both wild and cultivated forms exist.

Sportverein Grödig is an Austrian soccer team from Grödig. They play in the Austrian Regional League West, which is the third level of Austrian football. Grödig were moved down from the Austrian Bundesliga at the end of the 2015–16 season because of financial troubles.

Singapore began sending athletes to most summer Olympics after 1948. In 1948, Singapore became a separate British crown colony just before the 1948 summer Olympics. Singapore kept sending teams until 1964, when Singapore was part of Malaysia. Malaysia then sent a combined team. After Singapore fully became independent in 1965, the country continued to join all summer Olympics except the 1980 Olympics. In 2018, Singapore first competed in the winter Olympics with Cheyenne Goh in speed skating. Singapore has won five Olympic medals in total: one in 1960, two in 2008, two more in 2012, and a gold in 2016.

Donnan Alan Pennebaker, known as D.A. Pennebaker, was an American documentary filmmaker. He was born on July 15, 1925, and passed away on August 1, 2019. Pennebaker was one of the early creators of direct cinema. He mainly focused on performing arts and politics in his films. In 2013, the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences honored his work with an honorary award. He is often called "possibly the top chronicler of 1960s counterculture."

Pullman is the biggest city in Whitman County, in southeastern Washington State, part of the Palouse region in the Pacific Northwest. In 2010, it had 29,799 people, and by 2019, the population was estimated to be 34,506. Originally called Three Forks, the city was renamed after industrialist George Pullman in 1884. Pullman is known for its fertile land, with many rolling hills, and is famous for growing wheat and legumes. It has Washington State University, a public research university, and the headquarters of Schweitzer Engineering Laboratories. Pullman is near Moscow, Idaho, which has the University of Idaho. The city has its own airport, the Pullman-Moscow Regional Airport.

International Left Handers Day is celebrated every August 13 to honor left-handed people. The day was first observed in 1976 by Dean R. Campbell, who started Lefthanders International, Inc. This day is about celebrating left-handers and raising awareness about their advantages and challenges. It highlights that about 7 to 10 percent of people are left-handed. The day also brings attention to issues left-handers face, such as the special needs of left-handed children and the increased chance of developing schizophrenia. There are roughly 708 million left-handed people worldwide. Men are more likely to be left-handed than women. In the past, left-handers were forced to use their right hand. For example, former U.S. President Harry S. Truman was made to write right-handed as a child. On International Left Handers Day, we can help raise awareness about the challenges left-handers face.

bayzo was a Maltese singer born on April 3, 1947, in St. Paul's Bay. He was known for his special voice and a song called "Qalu Li Raw," which he performed at the Malta Song Festival in 1986. He passed away on February 1, 2018.

Jiang Yi-huah, born on November 18, 1960, is a Taiwanese politician. He used to be the premier of the Republic of China (ROC). On November 29, 2014, he quit his job and Mao Chi-kuo became the new premier on December 8, 2014. Before becoming premier, Jiang was the vice premier from 2012 to 2013. He was also the minister of the interior from 2009 to 2012 and the minister of the Research, Development, and Evaluation Commission of the Executive Yuan from 2008 to 2009.

iran is divided into thirty-one provinces, each with a capital city. The capital city is usually the largest city in the province. Each province has a governor-general called an "ostāndār." This governor-general is chosen by the minister of the interior and must be approved by the cabinet.

Voltage, also called electric potential difference or electric tension, is the difference in electric potential between two points. It is the amount of work needed to move a test charge between these points in a static electric field. In the International System of Units (SI), voltage is measured in volts. This unit represents the work done per unit of charge, where 1 volt equals 1 joule of work per 1 coulomb of charge. Since 1990, voltage has been defined using the quantum Hall and Josephson effects. In 2019, fundamental physical constants were used to define all SI units, including voltage. Voltage is often denoted by the symbol "V" or "U" and is measured using a voltmeter. Voltage can be due to electric charge, electric current through a magnetic field, time-varying magnetic fields, or a combination of these. Voltage can represent energy from a source (electromotive force) or energy that is lost, used, or stored.

Wisconsin's 8th congressional district is in the northeastern part of the state. It is now represented by Mike Gallagher, a Republican. Gallagher won the seat in 2016 when Reid Ribble left. This district is special because it once had a Catholic priest, Robert John Cornell, as its representative. The district used to strongly support Republicans for a long time. Only four Democrats represented it in the 20th century. However, it became more competitive in the 1990s. In 2004, Republican George W. Bush got 55% of the votes, while in 2008, Democrat Barack Obama got 53.6%. The last Democrat to represent the district was Steve Kagen from 2007 to 2011. Since then, Republicans have won the seat, often by a lot of votes, in every election since 2012. Since the 1970s, the 8th district has included parts of northeastern Wisconsin, like Green Bay and Appleton, and most of the counties along Michigan's border.

Merced County is in the northern San Joaquin Valley of California. The 2010 census showed the population was 255,793. The county seat is Merced. The county is named after the Merced River. Merced County is part of the Merced metropolitan area, which is part of the Modesto-Merced combined statistical area. It is north of Fresno County and Fresno, and southeast of Santa Clara County and San Jose.

fish processing involves dealing with fish and fish products from when they are caught until they reach the customer. While the term mainly applies to fish, it is also used for other sea creatures like shrimp or crab that are caught for selling. Big fish processing companies might have their own fishing boats or fish farms. Their products are usually sold to big stores or middlemen. Fish are very easy to go bad, so fish processing focuses on keeping them fresh. This is important even during other processing steps. Fish processing can be divided into two parts: first, handling raw fish, and second, making fish products. Primary processing means cutting fish into fillets and freezing them for shops that sell fresh fish or food services. Secondary processing includes making chilled, frozen, or canned fish products for regular stores or food services. People have been processing fish since ancient times. Today, fish processing happens on boats or at special fish processing places.

Lars Mortimer was born on March 22, 1946, and passed away on August 25, 2014, in Alfta, Helsingland. He was 68 years old. Lars Mortimer was a Swedish comic artist who created comics like "Bubo" and "Hälge."

Cagliari was a province in Sardinia, an autonomous region in Italy. Its capital city was also called Cagliari. The province had an area and a population of 543,310 in 2001. There were 71 "comuni" (a type of municipality) in the province. In 2016, the province was replaced by the metropolitan city of Cagliari.
A blast injury happens when someone is hurt by an explosion. This can be from big or small explosions. The injuries are worse when the explosion happens in a small space.

Rachel Emily Nichols was born on January 8, 1980. She is an American actress and model. She started modeling while studying at Columbia University in New York City during the late 1990s. By the early 2000s, she began acting. She appeared in the movie "Autumn in New York" (2000) and had a single episode in the fourth season of "Sex and the City" (2002). Her first big role was in the comedy "The Break-Up" (2003). She became more famous for playing Rachel Gibson in the final season of the TV show "Alias" (2005–2006) and for her part in the horror movie "The Amityville Horror" (2005). Nichols got her first main role in a thriller called "P2" (2007). She then became popular with the science-fiction action movies "Star Trek" (2009) and "Star Trek Into Darkness" (2013). Other notable films include "The Sisterhood of the Traveling Pants 2" (2008), "Conan the Barbarian" (2011), "Alex Cross" (2012), "Raze" (2013), and "Inside" (2016). She starred in the TV series "Continuum" (2012–2015). She also played in the sixth season of "Criminal Minds" (2010–2011), and in the fourth seasons of "Chicago Fire" (2015–2016) and "The Librarians" (2017–2018). She also appeared in "The Man in the High Castle" as a character named Martha.

Mullsjö AIS is a floorball club in Mullsjö, Sweden. It was started on November 1, 1989, by people from the Mullsjö Mission Covenant Church. In March 2008, the men's team got into the Swedish top division.

Atlantis is a made-up island mentioned by Plato in his works "Timaeus" and "Critias." It's a place that Plato uses to tell a story about a powerful navy that attacks Athens, which represents his ideal state from "The Republic." Athens successfully defends itself, supposedly showing that Plato’s idea of a perfect state is better. The story ends with Atlantis sinking into the Atlantic Ocean because the gods were unhappy with it. Although it’s not a major part of Plato’s work, the story of Atlantis has influenced many other stories. Renaissance writers like Francis Bacon and Thomas More used it in their own works. In the 19th century, some people thought Plato was telling a true story about a real place, like Ignatius L. Donnelly in his book. Because Plato didn't say exactly when or where the events happened, many people have speculated about Atlantis. It has become a symbol for lost, advanced ancient civilizations and inspires many stories, like comic books and movies. Today, scholars agree that Atlantis is a fictional place. Some think Plato might have based it on real events like the eruption of Thera or the Sea Peoples invasion. Others believe he made it up entirely, maybe inspired by events like the failed Athenian invasion of Sicily in 415-413 BC or the destruction of Helike in 373 BC.

Jose C. Vitug, born on July 15, 1934, is a Filipino lawyer and judge. He became an associate justice of the Supreme Court of the Philippines in 1993, appointed by President Fidel Ramos. Vitug left the court in 2004. He also started the Angeles University Foundation School of Law. He works as an independent director at Abbotie Equity Ventures.

Monster Buster Club is a French-Canadian children's science fiction TV show. It was made by Marathon Media, an French company, Image Entertainment Corporation, a Canadian animation studio, and Jetix Europe. The show first aired on June 2, 2008, on Jetix in Europe. In the United States and Asia, it started on June 9, 2008. In Canada, it premiered on YTV. A total of 52 episodes were created.

The Caledonian Railway (CR) was a big Scottish train company. It was created in the early 1800s to connect English railways with Glasgow. Over time, it built more tracks and reached Edinburgh and Aberdeen. It had many smaller railway lines around Glasgow. In 1923, it became part of the London, Midland and Scottish Railway. Many of its main routes are still in use today. The original line from Carlisle to Glasgow is now part of the West Coast Main Line.

The British Rail class 304 electric trains were made for use in suburbs on the West Coast Main Line between Crewe and Manchester/Liverpool/Rugby. At first, they were called AM4 units, but later became class 304 in the TOPS system. These trains ran on most of the West Coast Main Line. They followed the 1959 design for trains that use alternating current (AC). They looked similar to class 305, class 308, and 1,200 V direct current (DC) class 504 trains. None of these trains were saved for museums, and all were eventually taken apart.

Sir Herbert Benjamin Edwardes was a British leader who lived from November 12, 1819, to December 23, 1868. He worked as an administrator, soldier, and important official in the Punjab area of India ruled by Britain. He is famous as the "Hero of Multan" for his key role in winning the Second Anglo-Sikh War for Britain.

sts-122 was a NASA space shuttle mission to the International Space Station (ISS). This was the 24th shuttle mission to the ISS and the 121st space shuttle flight overall. The mission was also known as ISS-1E. The main goal was to bring the European "Columbus" science lab to the station. It also brought back an astronaut named Daniel M. Tani. A new astronaut, Léopold Eyharts from France, joined the station to replace Tani. The shuttle was supposed to launch on December 6, 2007, but because of problems with the sensors, it was delayed to December 9, 2007. During the second try, the sensors failed again, so the launch was stopped. Engineers found the problem was likely with a connector between the external fuel tank and the shuttle. After fixing the connector, the shuttle finally launched on February 7, 2008.
The Cathedral of Solsona is in Solsona, Catalonia. The apse, in Roman style, likely dates back to the 12th century.

In mathematics, a continuous function is one without sudden changes. Small changes in the input lead to small changes in the output. Functions without these changes are called continuous. If there are sudden changes, they are called "discontinuous." Before the 19th century, mathematicians used ideas about continuity, and later, precise definitions like the epsilon–delta definition were created. In topology, continuity is a fundamental concept. When functions have real numbers as inputs and outputs, continuity is important. A stronger type of continuity is uniform continuity. This article also covers continuity for functions between metric spaces. In order theory, especially domain theory, a type of continuity known as Scott continuity is considered. Other forms of continuity exist but are not covered here. As an example, a function showing a growing flower's height over time would be continuous. In contrast, a function showing a bank account balance over time would be discontinuous, as it changes only at specific moments when money is added or taken out.
