Harads is a small village in Boden Municipality, Norrbotten County, Sweden. It is about 50 kilometers (31 miles) south of the Arctic Circle and had 501 people living there in 2010. The main village in the Edefors parish is Harads. Edefors Church, built in 1928, is a key site in the municipality. Designed by architect John Åkerlund from Stockholm, it combines Nordic classicism with national romantic elements. This church replaced an older one from 1888, which was destroyed by fire in 1918. Harads also has the Treehotel, created by entrepreneur Kent Lindvall in 2010. The hotel's "rooms" are built high in the pine forest, connected by walkways. Each room, designed by a different architect, has a unique name, such as "Mirrorcube," "UFO," "Blue Cone," and "Bird's Nest." Lindvall says the hotel's design aims to be environmentally friendly.

Angelo Peruzzi, born on February 16, 1970, is an Italian football coach and former goalkeeper. He won the Serie A Goalkeeper of the Year award three times. Currently, he is the team manager for Lazio. Peruzzi is considered one of the best goalkeepers in Italian football history and one of the best from his generation. He played for several Italian clubs: Roma, Hellas Verona, Juventus, Inter Milan, and Lazio. Peruzzi had a very successful time at Juventus, winning three Serie A titles, the Coppa Italia, the UEFA Cup, and the UEFA Champions League. He also won another Coppa Italia with Lazio before retiring in 2007. Internationally, Peruzzi played 31 times for the Italy national team from 1995. He was part of the team that won the 2006 FIFA World Cup. He also represented Italy at the 1992 Olympics, the 1996 UEFA Euro, and the 2004 UEFA Euro.

Alfred A. Bianchi was born on March 26, 1932, and passed away on October 28, 2019. He was an American who worked in basketball. He played basketball as a professional. Later, he became a coach, general manager, consultant, and scout.
Ambrières-les-Vallées is a town in the Mayenne department of Northwestern France. It is near the Normandy region.

Fernando James Ferrer was born on April 30, 1950. He is an American politician. From 1987 to 2001, he was the Borough President of the Bronx. In 2001, he ran as a candidate for mayor of New York City. In 2005, he was the Democratic Party's nominee for mayor.

Montluçon is a town in central France, located on the Cher River. It is the biggest town in the Allier department, but the department's main town, Moulins, is smaller. People who live there are called "montluçonnais". Montluçon is in a traditional region called Bourbonnais and was part of an old duchy named Bourbon.

Hurricane Erin was the first hurricane to hit the United States since Hurricane Andrew in 1992. It was the fifth tropical storm and the second hurricane of the 1995 Atlantic hurricane season, which was unusually active. Erin formed near the southeastern Bahamas on July 31. It moved northwest and became a Category 1 hurricane on August 1 near Rum Cay. The hurricane moved over the northwestern Bahamas, including the Abaco Islands and Grand Bahama. On August 2, it hit Vero Beach, Florida, with winds of 85 mph. As it moved across Florida, it weakened to a tropical storm before entering the Gulf of Mexico. Erin re-intensified to a Category 1 hurricane on August 3. It strengthened briefly to a Category 2, with winds of 100 mph, hitting Fort Walton Beach, Florida. The hurricane weakened slightly before making landfall at Pensacola Beach, Florida, with 85 mph winds. It continued inland, weakening to a tropical storm over Mississippi and then to a tropical depression a few hours later. Erin's outer bands caused seven deaths in Jamaica, mostly due to a plane crash and lightning strikes. The Bahamas experienced some damage, but it was minor, costing about $400,000. In Florida, sustained winds reached 86 mph at Sebastian Inlet and 101 mph at Pensacola Naval Air Station. Over one million people lost power during the storm. More than 5,000 homes and buildings were damaged, mostly in Brevard County and the western Florida panhandle. Nine deaths occurred in Florida, with six from drowning and three from indirect causes. In Alabama, the storm damaged over 100 homes and 50 to 75 percent of pecan crops in Baldwin County. Other states reported minor flooding and wind damage. Overall, Erin caused about $700 million in damage, with most in Florida.

The Sea of Marmara, also known as the Marmora Sea, connects the Black Sea to the Aegean Sea and is inside Turkey. It separates Turkey's Asian and European parts. The Bosphorus strait links the Sea of Marmara to the Black Sea, while the Dardanelles strait connects it to the Aegean Sea. The Bosphorus also divides Istanbul into its Asian and European sides. The Sea of Marmara is a small sea with an area of and certain dimensions. Its deepest part is.

Warcraft II: Beyond the Dark Portal is an expansion for a real-time strategy video game. It was created by Blizzard Entertainment and Cyberlore Studios and released in 1996. To play this game, you need to have the original game first.

Jean-Michel Larrasket, born on May 22, 1950, and died on March 19, 2018, was a French professor and engineer. He was also the vice president for the French Basque country in the Basque Studies Society. Larrasket promoted projects to help the social and economic growth of the French Basque country. He was one of the founders of Eticoop, a cooperative that supports starting businesses in this region.

Ingram Olkin was born on July 23, 1924, and passed away on April 28, 2016. He was a professor at Stanford University and the Stanford Graduate School of Education. Olkin helped develop methods to study policies, especially in education. He also made important contributions to understanding how to combine results from different studies, teaching statistics, analyzing multiple variables, and a theory about ordering numbers.

The People's Party was a political party in the United States. It was formed in 1971 by several groups, including the Peace and Freedom Party and the Common Good People's Party. The party wanted to present a united anti-war platform for the elections. They ran for the presidency twice. In 1972, Dr. Benjamin Spock, a pediatrician, was their presidential candidate. Margaret Wright was their candidate in 1976. Dr. Spock was also their vice-presidential candidate in 1972. After the elections, the party became a loose group and soon stopped existing. Most of the founding parties also dissolved. The party's papers are now kept at the Western Historical Manuscript Collection in the University of Missouri–St. Louis.

Ramo Peter Ceresino (Ray), born on April 24, 1929, and passed away on May 1, 2015, was a Canadian ice hockey player. He played as a left winger for the Toronto Maple Leafs in the NHL. On June 2, 1953, he married Lorraine Giardetti, and they stayed married for 62 years. In 1962, he moved his family to California and settled in Los Angeles, where he worked as a mortgage broker. Later, he retired to San Diego. He had three children, one of them being Gordon Ceresino.

Tagetes is a group of plants that can grow for one year or more. They are usually soft and leafy. These plants belong to the sunflower family. Carl Linnaeus named this group in 1753. Originally, these plants were found in southern Mexico. Now, some species can be found naturally growing in many places. One type, called Tagetes minuta, can be considered a problem plant in some areas.

China uses one standard time, which is eight hours ahead of UTC. Even though China has five time zones, it follows the same time. This time is called "Beijing Time" in China and "China Standard Time" internationally. They do not use daylight saving time since 1991.

Allosaurus is a type of meat-eating dinosaur that lived about 155 to 145 million years ago, during the Late Jurassic period. The name "allosaurus" means "different lizard," referring to its unique spine. Allosaurus was discovered by Othniel Charles Marsh in 1877. It was a large, two-legged predator with a big head and sharp, pointed teeth. Its front limbs were small compared to its strong back legs, and it had a long, muscular tail to help balance. Allosaurus belongs to a group called allosaurids, which are a type of carnivorous theropod dinosaur. The best-known species is "A. fragilis." Most of the allosaurus fossils found come from the Morrison Formation in North America, with some also found in Portugal. For many years, it was known as "antrodemus," but studies showed that "allosaurus" was the correct name. Allosaurus was one of the most common large predators in the Morrison Formation, probably eating other dinosaurs like ornithopods, stegosaurids, and sauropods. Some scientists think allosaurus might have hunted in groups, while others believe they were often aggressive towards each other and gathered around the same dead animals to feed.

Joseph Thomas Elliott, Jr., was born on August 1, 1959. He is from England and sings songs he writes. He also plays music, makes records, and presents on the radio. He is famous as the main singer in the rock band Def Leppard. He was one of the first members and has sung on every Def Leppard album. Elliott also sings songs that sound like David Bowie and other bands. His voice is special and deep.

White Colne is a village and parish in Essex, England. It is located on the north side of the River Colne, across from Earls Colne, and on the Colchester road. It is 4 miles east-southeast of Halstead. The village's history dates back to the Domesday Book and earlier. There is evidence of ancient settlements in the area from the Paleolithic and Mesolithic periods. White Colne had a railway station on the Colne Valley and Halstead railway. The village church is dedicated to St. Andrew. The German film actor Anton Diffring is buried in the churchyard.
Stapleford Tawney is a village and civil parish in Epping Forest, Essex, England. It is roughly southwest of Chipping Ongar and south of Chelmsford, the county town.
Lignerolles is a commune in Central France, in the Allier department.

Nadine Vanessa Dorries, born on May 21, 1957, is a British politician who has been a minister for mental health, suicide prevention, and patient safety since 2019. She is a member of the Conservative Party and has served as the Member of Parliament (MP) for Mid Bedfordshire since 2005. Dorries is considered to be on the right side of the Conservative Party. Born in Liverpool to a working-class family, Dorries started as a nurse trainee and later became a medical representative. In her early career, she worked as the head of a community school in Zambia for a year. After returning to the UK, she founded Kids Ltd., a company that provided child care for working parents. She sold the company in 1998. In the 2005 general election, Dorries was elected as the MP for Mid Bedfordshire, winning by 11,355 votes. As a backbencher, she proposed several unsuccessful bills, such as trying to shorten the time limit for abortions in the UK and changing rules for counselling women. She also pushed for abstinence in sex education for girls. Dorries opposed John Bercow, the Speaker of the House of Commons, and tried to get him removed. She also had conflicts with David Cameron and George Osborne, calling them "two arrogant posh boys." In November 2012, she was suspended from the Conservative Party whip for participating in the reality TV show "I'm a Celebrity... Get Me Out of Here!" without permission. She was allowed back in May 2013. In July 2019, Boris Johnson appointed Dorries as the Parliamentary Under-Secretary of State at the Department of Health and Social Care, focusing on mental health, suicide prevention, and patient safety. In February 2020, she became the first MP to be diagnosed with COVID-19 during the pandemic. In May of that year, she was promoted to the rank of Minister of State.

Abel Ferrara, born on July 19, 1951, is an American filmmaker. He is known for making movies with provocative and often controversial content. He uses neo-noir imagery and gritty urban settings in his films. Ferrara has been an independent filmmaker for a long time. Some of his well-known movies are "Ms. 45" (1981), "King of New York" (1990), "Bad Lieutenant" (1992), and "The Funeral" (1996).

Minnie Mouse is a cartoon character created by Ub Iwerks and Walt Disney. She and Mickey Mouse were first drawn in 1928. In a comic strip story from 1942, her full name was given as Minerva Mouse, but this is not used often. In a 1930 story, Minnie's father Marcus Mouse and her unnamed mother, farmers, were introduced. The same story showed Minnie's uncle Milton Mouse with his family, and her grandparents Marvel Mouse and Matilda Mouse. Her most well-known relatives are her uncle Mortimer Mouse and her twin nieces, Millie and Melody Mouse. Melody is often the only niece shown. Minnie is often depicted as Mickey Mouse's girlfriend, a close friend of Daisy Duck, and a friend to Clarabelle Cow. On January 22, 2018, Minnie received her own star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame.
Louis Réard, a French engineer who made cars and designed clothes, introduced the modern two-piece bikini in July 1946. He opened a shop selling bikinis and ran it for 40 years until 1984.

Manchukuo was a puppet state under Japanese control in northeast China and Inner Mongolia from 1932 to 1945. It was called the State of Manchuria before 1934 and the Empire of Manchuria from 1934 onwards. The Japanese invaded Manchuria in 1931 following the Mukden Incident. The last Qing emperor, Puyi, became the nominal leader in 1932. In 1934, Manchukuo became a constitutional monarchy. It lost international recognition and was dissolved in 1945 after Japan surrendered at the end of World War II. Soviet forces took control of Manchukuo in August 1945, and China took over in the following year. The Han Chinese were the largest ethnic group, while Manchus were a minority. There were also Koreans, Japanese, Mongols, and other minorities. The Mongol regions in the west had their own system. The southern part of the Liaodong Peninsula remained directly controlled by Japan.

Jane Child, born on February 15, 1967, is a singer, songwriter, and record producer from Canada. She is famous for the song "Don't Wanna Fall in Love." Jane is also known for her unusual fashion, like a spiked hairstyle and long braids reaching her ankles, along with a nose chain.

Bartolomeo Alberto Cappellari, born on September 18, 1765, and who later became Pope Gregory XVI, was the leader of the Catholic Church and ruler of the Papal States from February 2, 1831, until his death on June 1, 1846. He used the name Mauro when he joined the Camaldolese religious order. Pope Gregory XVI was very traditional and conservative. He did not like democratic and modern changes in the Papal States and in Europe, seeing them as dangerous. He wanted to make the power of the Pope stronger (ultramontanism). In a letter called "Mirari vos," he said that allowing people to choose their own beliefs was wrong. He also supported spreading Christianity and stopping the slave trade. However, his strict rules, spending too much money, and not caring enough about people at home made him very unpopular. He was the last Pope to use the name "Gregory" and the last non-bishop to become Pope. Before becoming Pope Francis in 2013, he was the last Pope who was part of a religious order and only a priest.
In economics and political economy, returns are the payments given to those who provide a good or service.

Patrik Jonas Andersson, born on August 18, 1971, is a Swedish former football player who played as a defender. His father, Roy Andersson, and his younger brother, Daniel Andersson, also played professional football.
The year was 1227.

Colonization is a historical event that happened worldwide and over time. Ancient and medieval colonizers included the Phoenicians, Greeks, and Crusaders. Modern colonization started with the "Age of Discovery," led by the Portuguese and later the Spanish, who explored America, Africa, the Middle East, India, and East Asia. The Portuguese and Spanish empires were the first global ones because they controlled territories on different continents. From 1580 to 1640, both empires were ruled by Spanish monarchs. During the late 16th and 17th centuries, England, France, and the Dutch also created their own overseas empires, competing with each other. By the late 18th and early 19th centuries, there was the first wave of decolonization. Most European colonies in America, especially those of Spain, New France, and the 13 colonies, gained independence. Britain, France, Portugal, and the Dutch focused on Africa, South Africa, India, and Southeast Asia, where they already had coastal settlements. The Second Industrial Revolution in the 19th century led to the "New Imperialism" era. Colonization increased rapidly, with the "Scramble for Africa" involving Belgium, Germany, and Italy. Conflicts between colonizers and revolutions in colonized areas shaped control and led to the establishment of independent nations. In the 20th century, the colonies of defeated World War I powers were given to victors as mandates. It wasn't until the end of World War II that the second wave of decolonization began.

World music, also called global or international music, is a category in Western music that includes various types of music from different parts of the world. It covers ethnic, indigenous, and folk music, as well as music that mixes non-Western and Western popular styles. World music doesn't have a clear definition, but it focuses on interesting foreign music. A magazine called "Froots" describes it as "local music from far away." The term became popular in the 1980s for marketing non-Western traditional music. Over time, it has included subgenres like ethnic fusion, which combines different cultural styles, with examples like Clannad, Ry Cooder, and Enya.

Ophthalmosauridae is an extinct family of ichthyosaurs from the middle Jurassic to the early Cretaceous period, found in Asia, Australia, Europe, North America, and South America. The oldest known ophthalmosaurid is "Mollesaurus" from Argentina, discovered in the early Bajocian period. It was named by George H. Baur in 1887. "Ophthalmosaurus" is one of the basal taxa. In 1956, Appleby named the taxon "Ophthalmosauria," but "Ophthalmosauridae" has priority over "Ophthalmosauria."

Everett Lee, born on August 31, 1916, is an American conductor and violinist. He achieved several firsts for African Americans in music. He was the first to conduct a Broadway musical. He also was the first to lead a symphony orchestra below the Mason–Dixon Line. Additionally, he conducted a performance by a major American opera company for the first time.

Rodney Adolphus Wilkes, born on March 11, 1925, and died on March 24, 2014, was a weightlifter from Trinidad and Tobago. Known as "the mighty midget," he was not very famous outside his local area until he won a gold medal in the 1946 Central American and Caribbean games in Barranquilla, Colombia. His performance included lifting record weights: 100 kg in the press, 55 kg in the snatch, and 65 kg in the clean and jerk. He was chosen to represent his country at the 1948 Olympics in London, competing in the lightweight division. There, he became the first athlete from Trinidad and Tobago to win an Olympic medal, taking the silver behind Egypt's Mahmoud Fayad, who set a new Olympic and world record with a lift of 160 kg. In 1951, Wilkes won the lightweight gold medal at the first Pan American Games in Buenos Aires. The following year, he was selected for the Olympics in Helsinki, where he won the bronze medal, behind Russia's Rafael Chimishkyan and Nikolai Saksonov. After a short break, Wilkes returned to competition in 1954 and won gold at the British Empire and Commonwealth Games in Vancouver. Four years later, he won bronze at the games in Cardiff. Wilkes's final Olympic appearance was at the 1956 Olympics in Melbourne, where he finished fourth with a combined lift of 165 kg, missing a medal by one place and 5 kg. He continued competing until 1960 but retired permanently when he failed to make the West Indies team for the 1960 Rome Olympics. After retiring, Wilkes worked as an electrician in his hometown of San Fernando, Trinidad and Tobago. He passed away from prostate cancer in a San Fernando hospital in 2014, at the age of 89.

Gorillaz are a British virtual band created in 1998 by Damon Albarn and Jamie Hewlett. The band has four animated members: 2-D, Murdoc Niccals, Noodle, and Russell Hobbs. Their universe is shown in music videos, interviews, and cartoons. Albarn is the only permanent musical contributor, and Gorillaz often work with other artists. Remi Kabaka Jr. became the band's producer in 2016 and was listed as an official member in 2019. Albarn created Gorillaz after Blur, exploring different music styles like hip hop, electronic, and world music. Their first album, "Gorillaz," came out in 2001 and became very popular in the UK and Europe. The second album, "Demon Days," in 2005, was also successful, especially in the UK and the US. The third album, "Plastic Beach," in 2010, talked about the environment and had a pop sound. "The Fall," recorded during their tour, was released in 2010. The fifth album, "Humanz," came out in 2017 after a break. "The Now Now" in 2018 had simpler music. Gorillaz now release new songs every month in a project called "Song Machine." Gorillaz have shown themselves in different ways, like hiding the live band or using holograms. They have won several awards and sold over 20 million records worldwide, making them the most successful virtual band.

Mortality rate measures how many deaths occur in a group of people over time, per 1,000 individuals yearly. For example, a mortality rate of 9.5 per 1,000 means 9.5 deaths per year out of 1,000 people, or 0.95%. It's different from morbidity, which is about how many people have a disease, and from the incidence rate, which is about new cases of a disease. A specific type of mortality rate is the crude death rate, which counts all deaths in a given time for a population. The CIA estimates the global crude death rate is 7.7 deaths per 1,000 people yearly. Mortality rates can be calculated using this formula: deaths divided by the population size, then multiplied by a factor to get the rate per 1,000.

The Kama is a long river in Russia. It is the longest left tributary of the Volga and the largest in terms of water flow. At their meeting point, the Kama is even bigger than the Volga. It starts in the Udmurt Republic, near Kuliga, flowing northwest for a while, then turns northeast near Loyno and continues for more distance, then heads south and west in Perm Krai. It goes through the Udmurt Republic again and the Republic of Tatarstan before joining the Volga. Before trains, important paths allowed travel between the Kama and the Northern Dvina and Pechora river basins. In the early 1800s, the Northern Ekaterininsky Canal connected the upper part of the Kama with the Vychegda River (a tributary of the Northern Dvina). However, it was mostly abandoned shortly after due to low usage. The Kama appeared in a 2013 Russian movie called "The Geographer Drank His Globe Away," featuring a rapids scene.

William Edgar Buchanan II was born on March 20, 1903, and died on April 4, 1979. He was an American actor with a long career in film and television. Today, he is best known for his role as Uncle Joe Carson in the TV shows "Petticoat Junction," "Green Acres," and "The Beverly Hillbillies" in the 1960s.

Steven Ralph Schirripa, born on September 3, 1957, is an American actor, producer, author, and voice artist. He is famous for playing Bobby Baccalieri in "The Sopranos" and Detective Anthony Abetemarco in "Blue Bloods." Schirripa also produced and hosted two shows on Investigation Discovery: "Karma's a B*tch!" and "Nothing Personal." He was a regular on "The Secret Life of the American Teenager" and voiced Roberto in the "Open Season" movies. Schirripa appeared in commercials for Lamisil, Dick's Sporting Goods, and McDonald's.

Mamasani County is in Fars province in Iran. Its capital is Nurabad, located 180 kilometers from Shiraz. People in Mamasani speak Luri, a southern Luri dialect. In 2006, the population, including parts later split into Rostam County, was 162,694 families. Excluding those parts, it was 166,317 people in 26,011 families. Mamasani County has three districts: Central, Mahvarmilani, and Doshman Zari. It includes three cities: Nurabad, Khumeh Zar, and Baba Monir. Mamasani, also known as Muhammad Hasni, is an ancient tribe with many sub-tribes. The main tribe lives in Mamasani County, Fars province, Iran, and speaks Luri. The Sistani Mamasanis are in Sistan and Baluchistan. In Iran and Pakistan, the Brahui and Baluchi Mamasanis, also known as Muhammad Hassani, live in Baluchistan. In Afghanistan, they live in Nimruz and Helmand provinces.

The Arrondissement of Perpignan is in France, in the Pyrénées-Orientales department, which is in Northern Catalonia and the Occitanie region. It includes 39 towns. In 2016, it had about 285,077 people.

Rameswaram is a town and municipality in Tamil Nadu, India. It is on an island called Pamban, which is separated from the mainland by the Pamban Channel. Pamban Island is connected to the mainland by the Pamban Bridge. Rameswaram is at the end of a railway line from Chennai and Madurai. It is considered one of the most holy places in India for Hindus, along with Varanasi. According to the Ramayana, Rama and Hanuman built a bridge to rescue Sita from Ravana. The Ramanathaswamy temple, dedicated to Shiva, is the main temple in Rameswaram. The town is close to Sri Lanka and has been involved in news about the Setusamudram shipping canal project and fishing activities. Rameswaram has a population of about 44,856 and is mainly known for tourism and fishing.
Wolfgang Feiersinger was born on January 30, 1965. He is from Austria. He played football as a defender and is now retired.

Lil' Kim's "La Bella Mafia" is her third album. It came out on March 4, 2003, through Atlantic Records. The album did well, starting at number five on the Billboard 200. It sold more than one million copies in the U.S., and over two million worldwide. Critics said the album showed Lil' Kim's strong skills and presence. Two songs from the album were hits. "The Jump Off" reached number 17 on the Billboard Hot 100 and number 16 in the UK. "Magic Stick," featuring 50 Cent, went to number two on the Billboard Hot 100. Songs "Magic Stick" and "Come Back for You" got Lil' Kim Grammy nominations.

Priscilla Moran was an American silent film actress. She was born on November 23, 1917, in Sedalia, Missouri. She started acting in films in 1922. She stopped acting in 1937, when she was 20 years old. She appeared in 14 films during her career.
This NHL list includes players with last names starting with "M" who have played at least one game from 1917 to now. The list was updated for the 2018-19 NHL season.

Arianism is a belief that Jesus Christ, the son of God, was begotten by God the Father and is different from the Father (subordinate to him), but is still considered God. This belief was first associated with Arius, a Christian leader from Alexandria, Egypt. People called him "Arian" because his opponents gave him that name, and he never accepted it. Arianism and the belief in the Trinity had different views about Jesus's divinity. Arianism taught that the son of God was created within time, not eternal. There was a debate between these two views, each claiming to be orthodox. The first two ecumenical councils formally affirmed the trinitarian view, which was considered heretical. Athanasius of Alexandria strongly supported the trinitarian view. Arianism was declared a heresy at the First Council of Nicaea in 325. Emperor Constantine later exiled Athanasius and effectively cleared Arius. However, Athanasius returned and was eventually re-exiled. The First Council of Constantinople in 381 officially condemned Arius again. Some rulers, like Constantius II, Valens, and Odoacer, were Arians or semi-Arians. Arianism spread among Goths and Vandals. It is also used to describe other nontrinitarian beliefs from the 4th century that saw Jesus as a created being or not created in the usual sense.

Marc Angéle Vanderlinden, born on February 4, 1964, in Merksem, is a Belgian former footballer. He started his career with SC Merksem, his local team. In 1982, he joined Royal Antwerp FC. After seven seasons, he moved to R.S.C. Anderlecht in 1989. Two years later, he played for K.A.A. Gent. In 1995, he went to Israel to play for Hapoel Ironi Rishon Lezion F.C. and then for Hapoel Herzliya F.C. He returned to SC Merksem in 1997 and retired in 2002. He played 19 times for the Belgium national team, scoring nine goals, and was part of the 1990 FIFA World Cup.

In physics, escape velocity is the minimum speed needed for an object to escape a planet's gravity. This speed depends on the planet's mass and the distance from its center. A rocket can escape without reaching this speed because it keeps getting energy from its fuel. Earth's escape velocity from the surface is about. Once an object reaches escape velocity, it will keep moving away, slowing down but never stopping. To escape, a rocket must have enough fuel to keep pushing. Escape velocity is the speed where an object's kinetic energy equals its gravitational potential energy. After reaching escape velocity, an object will keep moving away, slowing down as it gets farther, but it will never return. For a spherical object like a planet or star, the escape velocity formula is: where "g" is a constant, "m" is the planet's mass, and "r" is the distance from the center. This formula doesn't depend on the escaping object's mass. An object falling from space towards a planet, starting with zero speed, will hit the planet with the same speed as the planet's escape velocity. If an object is given a speed higher than the escape velocity, it will keep moving away, getting slower but never stopping.

Lichtervelde is a town in Belgium, in the province of West Flanders. It covers an area of 25.93 square kilometers. On January 1, 2006, the town had 8,400 people living there. The population density is 324 people per square kilometer. There is a church that is 64 meters tall. Charles Joseph van Depoele, an inventor, was born in this town.
Plains is a town and the county seat of Yoakum County in Western Texas, USA. It's in the south part of the Panhandle region. According to the 2010 census, Plains had 1,481 people living there.
Gillespie is a city in Macoupin County, Illinois, United States. It is part of the Metro East area near St. Louis. According to the 2010 census, the population was 3,319.

Bernard Verlhac, known as Tignous, was a French cartoonist. He worked as a long-time staff cartoonist for the French satirical magazine "Charlie Hebdo." Tignous was killed on January 7, 2015, during the "Charlie Hebdo" shooting.

The list includes domestic cat breeds and their hybrid forms. It covers recognized breeds, new ones, and those in development. There are also distinct domestic groups not actively bred and breeds that are no longer recognized. As of 2019, TICA recognizes 71 breeds, CFA 44, and FIFE 43. Different cat organizations sometimes classify the same cat as different breeds. For instance, TICA's Himalayan is seen as a color version of the Persian by CFA, while CFA and TICA consider the Javanese a color variation of the Balinese. WCF combines these breeds into a single "mega-breed" called Colorpoint, using the name "Javanese" for the Oriental Longhair. Colorpoint Longhair can mean different breeds in various organizations. Many cat breeds have names that sound exotic but don’t reflect their true origins. Examples include Balinese, Javanese, and Himalayan. Domestic short-haired and long-haired cats are terms used to describe mixed-breed cats by their fur length. Some registries allow them to be registered, and they have been used to create new breeds. They shouldn’t be confused with recognized breeds with similar names, like the British Shorthair and Oriental Longhair.

The Rubik's Revenge, also called the Master Cube, is a 4×4×4 version of the Rubik's cube. It came out in 1981. Peter Sebesteny invented it. At first, it might have been called the Sebesteny Cube, but they decided to name it after the original Rubik's cube. Unlike the 3×3×3 cube and other odd-numbered cubes like the 5×5×5, the center pieces on the Rubik's Revenge can move. You can solve the edges and corners of the 4×4×4 cube using methods for the 3×3×3 cube, but you need to correctly identify the colors because the center pieces don't stay in one place.
The middle angles were an important group in Mercia, a larger kingdom in England during the Anglo-Saxon period.

Robert Michael Schneider was born on October 31, 1963. He is an American actor, comedian, writer, and director. Schneider was a stand-up comic and appeared on the NBC show "Saturday Night Live." He has acted in several movies, such as "The Animal," "The Hot Chick," "The Benchwarmers," and "Grown Ups." Schneider is the father of singer Elle King.

Alexander Smart was a Canadian ice hockey player born on May 29, 1918, and died on April 18, 2005. He played as a forward. He played one season for the Montreal Canadiens in the National Hockey League. Most of his career was in the Quebec Senior Hockey League.

Charles Anthony Ryan Silvera, nicknamed Swede, was an American baseball player and coach. He played for the New York Yankees and won six World Series championships with them. He was born on October 13, 1924, and passed away on September 7, 2019.

Hamilton County is in the southwestern part of Ohio. In 2010, it had 802, 374 people, which made it the third-largest county in Ohio. The main city and biggest in the county is Cincinnati. It was named after Alexander Hamilton, the first U.S. Secretary of the Treasury. Hamilton County is part of the Cincinnati-Middletown metropolitan area.
Palmer is a city in Washington County, Kansas, United States. In 2010, the city had 111 people.

Norman Steven Maciver, born on September 1, 1964, is from Canada. He used to play ice hockey professionally and is now an assistant general manager for the Chicago Blackhawks in the NHL. As a player, he defended the net for six different NHL teams during his thirteen-year career.

Hiragana and katakana are both kana systems. Each syllable in Japanese, or most moras, is represented by one or two characters in these systems. These characters can be vowels like "あ" (a), consonants followed by vowels like "か" (ka) or "ん" (n), or nasal sounds like "ん" (n) which can sound like English "m", "n", or "ng", or like French, Portuguese, or Galician nasal vowels. Kana characters are called syllabic symbols, not letters, because they don't represent single consonants except for "ん" (n). Hiragana is used for "okurigana" (suffixes after kanji, like verb endings), certain words, particles, and other native words without kanji. Authors might use hiragana for informal writing. Hiragana also helps with "furigana," showing how to read kanji. Hiragana has two main ordering systems: old-fashioned "iroha" and more common "gojūon."
San Diego is a city in Texas, United States. It is mainly in Duval County and is the county seat. The population was 4,488 in 2010.

Michel Suleiman was born on November 21, 1948. He served as Lebanon's president from 2008 to 2014. Before becoming president, he was the commander of the Lebanese Armed Forces from 1998 to 2008. When Emile Lahoud, the previous commander of the Lebanese Armed Forces, became president in November 1998, Suleiman took his place as the new commander in December 1998. Suleiman was then elected president and took office on May 25, 2008.

Ivan's Childhood, sometimes called My Name Is Ivan in the US, is a 1962 Soviet war movie directed by Andrei Tarkovsky. It stars Nikolai Burlyayev as Ivan, an orphan whose parents died during World War II. Other actors include Valentin Zubkov, Evgeny Zharikov, Stepan Krylov, Nikolai Grinko, and Tarkovsky's wife, Irma Raush. The film tells Ivan's story during the war. It was one of several Soviet films in that time, like The Cranes Are Flying and Ballad of a Soldier, that showed the human cost of war without glorifying it. Tarkovsky wanted to express his hatred of war and chose childhood as a contrast to the war. This was Tarkovsky's first feature film. It gained him critical praise and made him famous internationally. It won the Golden Lion at the Venice Film Festival and the Golden Gate Award at the San Francisco International Film Festival in 1962. The film was also considered for the best foreign language film at the Academy Awards but was not nominated. It influenced many famous filmmakers like Ingmar Bergman, Sergei Parajanov, and Krzysztof Kieślowski.
Sannes is a commune in the Vaucluse department, which is in the Provence-Alpes-Côte d’Azur region of southeastern France.

Linux Mint is a community-driven Linux version based on Ubuntu or Debian. It includes many free and open-source applications. Users can add multimedia support by checking a box during installation. This support includes some proprietary software like multimedia codecs. The project started with Clement Lefevre and is developed by the Linux Mint team and community.

Crooked Island is an island and district. It is part of a group of Bahamian islands that form a large, shallow lagoon called the Bight of Acklins. The largest islands in this group are Crooked Island in the north and Acklins in the southeast. There are also smaller islands, such as Long Cay, once known as Fortune Island, in the northwest, and Castle Island in the south.

Vientiane is the capital and largest city of Laos. It is located on the Mekong River, near the border with Thailand. Vientiane became the capital in 1573 because people were worried about a Burmese invasion. It was later destroyed in 1827 by the Siamese (Thais). During French rule, Vientiane was the administrative capital. Now, it is also the economic center of Laos. The city's population was 820,000 in the 2015 census. Vientiane is famous for That Luang, a big monument that is a symbol of Laos and a sign of Buddhism. Other important Buddhist temples can also be found there, like Haw Phra Kaew, which used to house the Emerald Buddha. Vientiane hosted the 25th Southeast Asian Games in December 2009, to celebrate 50 years of the games.
A crescent is a shape that represents the moon. It may also refer to:

Our Band Could Be Your Life: Scenes from the American Indie Underground, 1981–1991, is a book by Michael Azerrad. It tells the stories of several underground rock bands. These bands didn't get much attention from the mainstream but were very important in creating American alternative and indie rock. They did this by touring a lot and releasing music on small, local independent record labels. Azerrad talked to many band members and also looked at old fanzines, as well as more widely known newspapers and books.

Everland is South Korea's biggest theme park. It is in Yongin, a city in Gyeonggi-do. Everland gets about 5.85 million visitors each year. In 2018, it was the 19th most visited amusement park in the world. Along with rides and attractions, Everland has a zoo called Caribbean Bay. The park is run by Samsung C&T Corporation, part of the Samsung group. Everland used to be called "Jayeon Nongwon," which means "Natural Farm" in Korean. Its old English name was "Farmland."

Dr. Strangelove, or How I Learned to Stop Worrying and Love the Bomb, known simply as Dr. Strangelove, is a 1964 black comedy film. It makes fun of the fear of a nuclear war between the Soviet Union and the United States during the Cold War. The movie was directed, produced, and co-written by Stanley Kubrick and stars Peter Sellers, George C. Scott, Sterling Hayden, and Slim Pickens. Filming happened in the United Kingdom. The story is about an unstable U.S. Air Force general who orders a nuclear attack on the Soviet Union. The President, his advisors, the Joint Chiefs of Staff, and a Royal Air Force officer try to stop the B-52 plane crew from carrying out the attack. Dr. Strangelove is often seen as one of the best comedies and one of the greatest films ever made. In 1998, the American Film Institute ranked it 26th among the best American movies (it was 39th in the 2007 list). In 2000, it was third on the list of the funniest American films. In 1989, the U.S. Library of Congress included Dr. Strangelove in the national film registry because it is culturally, historically, or aesthetically significant.
Warendorf is a district in the northern part of North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany. It borders the districts of Steinfurt, Osnabrück, Gütersloh, Soest, Hamm, Coesfeld, and Münster.

Frank Cloud Cooksey was born on June 3, 1933. He is an American public servant. In the 1950s, he was the president of the student body at the University of Texas. He worked as a lawyer. He had different jobs, including in the civil rights division of the U.S. District Attorney's office, the Texas Attorney General's office (under John Hill), and in private practice. He was the mayor of Austin, Texas, from 1985 to 1988. He is also an environmental activist and was known for his progressive ideas when he was mayor.

Zonia Baber, born Mary Arizona Baber on August 24, 1862, in Clark County, Illinois, was an American geographer and geologist. She is known for creating methods to teach geography. Her teaching focused on hands-on learning through fieldwork and experiments.

José Hugo Garaycoa Hawkins was born on June 2, 1930, and died on March 27, 2018. He was a Roman Catholic bishop. Garaycoa Hawkins became a priest in 1961. He worked as the auxiliary bishop of the Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Lima, Peru, from 1982 to 1991. After that, he served as the bishop of the Roman Catholic Diocese of Tacna y Moquegua, Peru, from 1991 to 2006.

The London, Brighton and South Coast Railway (LB&SCR) was a train company in the United Kingdom from 1846 to 1922. It covered an area shaped like a triangle, with London at the top and most of the Sussex coastline at the bottom. Parts of Surrey were also included. On the western side, it shared routes with the London and South Western Railway (L&SWR), which went to Portsmouth. On the eastern side, the LB&SCR shared routes with the South Eastern Railway (SER), later part of the South Eastern and Chatham Railway (SE&CR), which led to Bexhill, St. Leonards-on-Sea, and Hastings. The LB&SCR had the most direct routes from London to seaside towns like Brighton, Eastbourne, Worthing, Littlehampton, and Bognor Regis. It also served the ports of Newhaven and Shoreham-by-Sea. It connected to inland towns like Chichester, Horsham, East Grinstead, and Lewes, and shared services with Croydon, Tunbridge Wells, Dorking, and Guildford. Near London, it had many train lines starting from London Bridge and Victoria stations. In 1846, it was created by merging five smaller companies. In 1921, it joined the L&SWR, SE&CR, and some smaller railways to form the Southern Railway on January 1, 1923.

The Colombo crime family is one of the five main groups that control organized crime in New York City. It started in 1928 with Joseph Profaci's bootlegging gang. Profaci led the family until the late 1950s. There were three major fights within the family. The first was in the late 1950s, when Joe Gallo rebelled against Profaci. It stopped when Gallo was arrested, and Profaci died. In the early 1960s, Joseph Colombo took over. A second fight began in 1971 after Gallo was released from prison and shot Colombo. Carmine Persico's supporters won. From 1975 to 1991, the family was peaceful. Then, in 1991, a bloody war broke out when Acting Boss Victor Orena tried to take control from the imprisoned Persico. This war ended in 1993, leaving 12 family members dead and Orena in prison. Persico then ruled the family until 2019. After his death, the family was weaker than before, with many members in trouble with the law. On March 7, 2019, Carmine Persico died in prison.

Prunella Margaret Rumney West Scales, born on June 22, 1932, is an English actress. She is famous for playing Sybil, the wife of Basil Fawlty, in the BBC comedy "Fawlty Towers." She was also nominated for a BAFTA award for her role as Queen Elizabeth II in "A Question of Attribution," a BBC One show from 1991 by Alan Bennett.
Beyrie-en-Béarn is a town in the Pyrénées-Atlantiques department of southwestern France.

Achim Mentzel was born on July 15, 1946, in Berlin. He died on January 4, 2016, in Cottbus, at the age of 69. Mentzel was a musician, TV host, and actor. He is best known for hosting "Achim's Hit Parade" from 1989 to 2006. He also worked with Oliver Kalkofe on "Kalkofe's Vinyl Disk." Mentzel released 23 singles and seven albums between 1978 and 2010. He was part of a cover band called Fritzens Dampferband, with Nina Hagen. He appeared in films like "The Legend of Paul and Paula" (1973) and "The Wixxer" (2004), and in TV shows such as "Das Amt" and "Leipzig Homicide." Mentzel was married four times and had eight children. The cause of his death was believed to be a heart attack or stroke.

Åge Fridtjof Hareide, born on September 23, 1953, is a Norwegian football manager. He recently managed the Denmark national football team. As a player, he played for Hødd and Molde in Norway, and Manchester City and Norwich City in England. Hareide was chosen to play for Norway 50 times. As a coach, he won league titles in all Scandinavian countries. He won with Helsingborgs IF in Sweden in 1999, and with Malmö FF in 2014. He also won with Brøndby in Denmark in 2001–02, and with Rosenborg in Norway in 2003. Hareide led the Norway national team from 2003 to 2008.

Arsène Lupin is a fictional gentleman thief and master of disguise created in 1905 by French writer Maurice Leblanc. He was originally named Arsène Lopin, but changed because a local politician had the same name. The first story, "The Arrest of Arsène Lupin," came out on July 15, 1905. Leblanc wrote 17 novels and 39 novellas about Lupin, making a total of 24 books. In 1923, there was a novel called "The Secret Tomb" that doesn't feature Lupin, but the main character, Dorothée, solves one of his secrets. Other writers and artists have also created stories and adaptations of Lupin for books, movies, TV, theater, and comics. Five more books about Lupin were written in the 1970s by the famous mystery writers Boileau and Narcejac.

Tuili is a "municipality" in the province of South Sardinia, which is in the Italian region of Sardinia. It is located north of Cagliari and northeast of Sanluri. Tuili borders the following municipalities: Barumini, Gesturi, Las Plassas, Pauli Arbarei, Setzu, and Turri.

Bussigny-sur-Oron was a town in the Lavaux-Oron district of Vaud, Switzerland. On January 1, 2012, Bussigny-sur-Oron joined with other towns—Châtillens, Chesalles-sur-Oron, Ecoteaux, Oron-la-Ville, Oron-le-Châtel, Palézieux, Les Tavernes, Les Thioleyres, and Vuibroye—to form a new town called Oron.

Jack Klugman, born on April 27, 1922, and died on December 24, 2012, was an American actor. He started his career in 1950 and appeared in "12 Angry Men" in 1957 and "Cry Terror!" in 1958. In the 1960s, he was in many TV shows. Klugman won his first Emmy in 1964 for a role on "The Defenders." He also appeared four times on "The Twilight Zone" from 1960 to 1963. In 1965, Klugman took over the role of Oscar Madison from Walter Matthau in "The Odd Couple." He later played the same character in a TV show from 1970 to 1975. Klugman also acted as Henry Willows in "You Again?" from 1986 to 1987. Klugman won two more Emmys and a Golden Globe for his work on "The Odd Couple." From 1976 to 1983, he starred as Quincy, M.E., and was nominated for four Emmys.

Alain Émile Louis Marie Poher was a French politician born on April 17, 1909, and died on December 9, 1996. He was a centrist politician. At first, he was part of the Popular Republican Movement, later joining the Democratic Centre. Poher was a senator for Val-de-Marne from 1946 to 1995. He was the president of the Senate from October 3, 1968, to October 1, 1992. In this role, he served as an interim president twice. In the 1969 presidential election, he lost to Georges Pompidou in the second round.

Cipriano de Rore, also known as Cypriano, lived from 1515 or 1516 to sometime between September 11 and 20, 1565. He was a composer from Franco-Flemish background during the Renaissance period. He worked in Italy. De Rore was an important composer after Josquin des Prez. He was one of the best madrigal composers in the mid-16th century. His music was experimental, used many notes, and very expressive. His style had a big impact on madrigals that came after.

Luis Maldonado Venegas, born on November 19, 1956, and died on April 30, 2019, was a Mexican politician and lawyer. He was part of the Party of the Democratic Revolution. Maldonado was a federal deputy for Mexico City and the fourth electoral region in the 63rd legislature of the Mexican Congress. He also became the national president of the Convergencia political party and represented it in both houses of Congress.

Abigail Kathleen Breslin, born on April 14, 1996, is an American actress and singer. She grew up in New York City. Breslin started acting in commercials when she was three. Her first movie role came at age five in the science fiction horror film "Signs" (2002), for which she was nominated for a Young Artist Award. She then appeared in movies like "Raising Helen" and "Lilo & Stitch" (both in 2004). Breslin got a lot of praise for her role as Olive Hoover in "Little Miss Sunshine" (2006). She was nominated for Screen Actors Guild, BAFTA, and Academy Awards for Best Supporting Actress. She won a Screen Actors Guild award for best performance in a movie and a Critics' Choice Award for best young performer. Breslin continued to act in movies such as "No Reservations" (2007), "Nim's Island" (2008), "Definitely, Maybe" (2008), "My Sister's Keeper" (2009), "Zombieland" (2009), "Rango" (2011), "The Call" (2013), "The Place Beyond the Pines" (2013) where she was nominated for a Screen Actors Guild Award, "Ender's Game" (2013), and "Hunters" (2019). From 2015 to 2016, she had a regular role in the horror-comedy TV show "Scream Queens" on Fox.

Boyd County is in Nebraska. In 2010, it had 2,099 people. The main town is Butte. Boyd County was created in 1891 and named after James E. Boyd, who was Nebraska's governor at that time. In 1922, Boyd County was given the number 63 in Nebraska's license plate system. At the 2010 census, three small towns had very few people: Anoka with 6, Gross with 2, and Monowi with just 1 person. Monowi was the only town in the US with only one resident in 2010.
Kurt Paul Schmitt was born on October 7, 1886, in Heidelberg and died on November 2, 1950, in Heidelberg. He was a German economic leader and served as the Reich Economy Minister.

Plymouth County is in Massachusetts. As of 2010, it had 494, 919 people. Its main cities are Plymouth and Brockton. In 1685, Plymouth County was made by the Plymouth General Court, which was the government of Plymouth Colony. This happened before it became part of the Massachusetts Bay Colony. The Spanish treasure fleet, also known as the West Indies fleet, silver fleet, or plate fleet, was a group of ships organized by Spain from 1566 to 1790. These ships traveled between Spain and its American territories across the Atlantic Ocean. The fleets carried many different items, such as food, wood, metals like silver and gold, precious stones, pearls, spices, sugar, tobacco, silk, and other goods from Spain's areas in the Americas. Spain sent goods like oil, wine, fabrics, books, and tools in the opposite direction. The West Indies fleet was the first regular trade route between the Atlantic and the Americas. Similarly, the Manila galleons were the first regular trade route between the Pacific.

McLaren Racing Limited is a British motor racing team based in Woking, Surrey, England. They are famous for competing in Formula One and have also raced in American open wheel racing. McLaren won the Canadian-American Challenge Cup (Can-Am) sports car racing championship. The team is the second oldest and second most successful Formula One team after Ferrari. They have won 12 drivers' championships and eight constructors' championships. McLaren is a part of the McLaren Group and was founded in 1963 by Bruce McLaren. The team won its first grand prix in 1968. They had great success in Can-Am from 1967 to 1971. In American racing, McLaren cars won the Indianapolis 500 in 1972 and 1974-1976. After Bruce McLaren's death in 1970, Teddy Mayer took over. He led the team to their first Formula One constructors' championship in 1974, with Emerson Fittipaldi and James Hunt winning the drivers' championship. 1974 also marked the start of a long-term sponsorship with Marlboro. In 1981, McLaren merged with Ron Dennis's Project Four Racing. Dennis took full control and the team had a very successful period. Niki Lauda, Alain Prost, and Ayrton Senna won seven drivers' championships, and the team won six constructors' championships. Prost and Senna were especially dominant, winning almost all races in 1988. Senna left for Ferrari in 1989, and during the 1990s, Williams posed the strongest challenge. By the mid-1990s, Honda left Formula One, and Senna moved to Williams, causing McLaren to go three seasons without a win. With Mercedes-Benz engines and driver Mika Häkkinen, they won titles in the 2000s. Lewis Hamilton was a key driver during this time. Ron Dennis retired in 2009, handing over to Martin Whitmarsh. However, in 2013, Whitmarsh was removed after a poor season. In 2013, McLaren started using Honda engines, replacing Mercedes-Benz. They raced as McLaren Honda for the first time since 1992 in the 2015 Australian Grand Prix. In 2017, McLaren agreed with Renault to use their engines from 2018 to 2020. They will use Mercedes-Benz engines from 2021 until at least 2024. McLaren returned to the Indianapolis 500 in 2017 and ran full Indycar series in 2020 with Arrow Schmidt Peterson Motorsports, under the name Arrow McLaren SP.

Flushing is in the middle part of the New York City borough of Queens. It's one of the biggest business areas in New York City. Downtown Flushing, where Main Street and Roosevelt Avenue meet, is very busy. It's the third-busiest crossing in the city. Flushing started as a Dutch settlement called Vlissingen in 1645. When the English took over in 1664, it became part of Queens County. In 1683, it was one of the first towns in Queens. In 1898, it joined New York City. In the early 1900s, Flushing grew because of new bridges and transport. Many immigrants, mainly from China and Korea, moved there later. Flushing has many smaller areas for living. The different groups of people who live there show its diversity. There are train stations on the Long Island Rail Road and the New York City subway. The subway line ends at Main Street. Flushing is in Community District 7 of Queens. Its zip codes are 11354, 11355, and 11358. It's watched by the New York City Police Department's 109th precinct.

Return to Neverland, also known as Peter Pan in Disney's Return to Neverland and later called Peter Pan II: Return to Neverland, is a 2002 American animated movie. It was made by Walt Disney Television Animation and released by Walt Disney Pictures, with distribution by Buena Vista Pictures. The film came out on February 15, 2002. It is a sequel to the 1953 movie Peter Pan and is based on J. M. Barrie's 1911 novel Peter and Wendy. The film earned $115 million worldwide. Critics say it has forgettable songs and a weak story. The movie follows Wendy's daughter, who doesn't believe in fairy tales during the Blitz in London. By mistake, she is taken to Neverland by the pirates. To get home, she meets Peter Pan, Tinker Bell, and the Lost Boys. They help her learn to fly and believe in magic.

Elizabeth I, born on September 7, 1533, and died on March 24, 1603, was queen of England and Ireland from November 17, 1558, until her death. Sometimes called the Virgin Queen, she was the last ruler of the Tudor dynasty. Elizabeth was the daughter of Henry VIII and Anne Boleyn. Anne was executed two and a half years after Elizabeth's birth, and Henry declared Elizabeth illegitimate. Her half-brother, Edward VI, ruled until 1553, when he died. Edward left the crown to Lady Jane Grey, but ignored his half-sisters Mary and Elizabeth. Mary became queen, after Lady Jane Grey was deposed. During Mary's rule, Elizabeth was imprisoned for almost a year, suspected of supporting Protestant rebels. In 1558, upon Mary's death, Elizabeth became queen. She was advised by William Cecil, later Lord Burghley. Elizabeth established England's Protestant church, becoming its supreme governor. She did not marry or have children. She was succeeded by her cousin, James I of Scotland, who united England and Scotland. During her rule, Elizabeth tried to stay neutral between France and Spain, but supported some military campaigns. Her reign, known as the Elizabethan era, saw the flourishing of English drama, led by playwrights like William Shakespeare and Christopher Marlowe. Elizabeth was celebrated for her virginity, and her long rule brought stability to England. However, at the end of her reign, she faced economic and military problems.

Silicon is an element with the symbol Si and atomic number 14. It is hard, brittle, and has a metallic sheen. Silicon is a metalloid and semiconductor. It belongs to group 14 in the periodic table, with carbon above and germanium, tin, and lead below. It is not very reactive, but oxygen bonds with it easily. It was first prepared and studied in 1823 by Jöns Jakob Berzelius. Silicon's oxides are called silicates. Its melting and boiling points are 1414°C and 3265°C, respectively, which are the second-highest among metalloids and nonmetals, just after boron. Silicon is the eighth most common element in the universe but is rarely found in its pure form in the Earth's crust. It is widely found in cosmic dust, planetoids, and planets, mainly as silica or silicates. About 28% of the Earth's crust is made of silicate minerals, making silicon the second most abundant element after oxygen. Most silicon is used without processing, often in natural minerals. It's used in construction with materials like clay, sand, and stone. Silicates are used in cement for mortar and stucco, and in concrete for walkways, foundations, and roads. They are also used in ceramics and in glasses. Silicon compounds, like silicon carbide, are used in abrasives and strong ceramics. Silicon is the base for synthetic polymers called silicones. In the late 20th and early 21st centuries, silicon was crucial in the digital or information age. Only a small part of purified silicon is used in electronics, but it's essential for making MOS transistors and integrated circuits, which are used in computers and cell phones. Pure silicon is also used in steel and aluminum production, and in making fine chemicals like fumed silica. Silicon is important in biology, but only needed in small amounts by animals. Some sea sponges, microorganisms like diatoms, and radiolaria use silica to build their structures. Plants also store silica in their tissues.

The band members are Jim Adkins (lead vocals and guitar), Tom Linton (rhythm guitar and backing vocals), Rick Burch (bass), and Zach Lind (drums). They have made 10 studio albums, with the current lineup since the ninth album. Their most successful songs came from the album "Bleed American" (2001). The band's albums "Bleed American" and "Futures" were certified platinum and gold by the RIAA, meaning they sold more than 1.5 million copies. Their sixth album, "Chase This Light" (2007), was their highest-charting album, reaching number five on the Billboard 200. Jimmy Eat World released their tenth album, "Surviving", in October 2019.

"All Quiet on the Western Front" is a novel by Erich Maria Remarque, a German soldier who fought in World War I. The book talks about how German soldiers felt very tired and stressed during the war. After the war, many soldiers felt detached from normal life when they went home. The novel was first published in a German newspaper in November and December 1928, and in book form in late January 1929. It sold 2.5 million copies in 22 languages in its first 18 months. In 1930, the book was made into a film that won an Academy Award. A TV film version was made in 1979, starring Richard Thomas and Ernest Borgnine.

Kari Peter Conrad von Bagh was a Finnish film historian and director who lived from August 29, 1943, to September 17, 2014. He worked as the head of the Finnish Film Archive. von Bagh edited a magazine called "Filmihullu" and helped start the Midnight Sun Film Festival, where he also directed the festival. He also wrote a book about Aki Kaurismäki that was translated into several languages. von Bagh died in 2014 at the age of 71.

Princeton, formerly known as Vermilion Forks, is a town in southern British Columbia, Canada, in the Similkameen region. It is located east of the Cascade Mountains, which extend south into Washington, Oregon, and California. The Tulameen and Similkameen rivers meet here. In 2016, the town had 2,828 people. Princeton's biggest employers are the Copper Mountain Mine, a sawmill owned by Weyerhaeuser, and some smaller timber companies, such as Princeton Wood Preservers and Princeton Post and Rail.

Ingar Axel Harald Ericsson was a Swedish runner who specialized in the 1500 meters. He participated in the 1952 and 1956 Summer Olympics. In 1952, he finished eighth. He placed seventh in the European Championships in 1950 and fourth in 1954. Ericsson won the national 1500 meters title three times—1952, 1954, and 1955—and set a new national record in 1956. He worked as a firefighter.

A medical school is a place that teaches about medicine and gives professional degrees to become doctors or surgeons. Degrees like the bachelor of medicine, bachelor of surgery, doctor of medicine, or doctor of osteopathic medicine are examples. Some medical schools offer other degrees too, like a doctor of philosophy, master's degree, or programs for physician assistants. Medical schools also do research and run teaching hospitals. The rules, structure, teaching methods, and programs can be very different around the world. Getting into a medical school can be tough; they look at test scores, grades, and leadership roles. In most countries, studying medicine is done as part of an undergraduate degree, not needing extra classes before. But more places are opening for students who have already finished an undergraduate degree. In the U.S. and Canada, almost all medical schools take students after they've completed some university studies. Students get their medical degree after finishing their program, which usually takes five or more years for an undergraduate and four years for a graduate. Many schools mix learning basic sciences with clinical training right from the start. Others have separate preclinical and clinical parts. In the preclinical phase, students study subjects like biochemistry, genetics, pharmacology, and more. The clinical phase includes rotations in areas like internal medicine, surgery, pediatrics, psychiatry, and obstetrics and gynecology. After graduating, doctors need to be licensed by the government to practice medicine. This often involves passing tests, background checks, and completing postgraduate training. Each country has its own rules, and schools are listed in the World Directory of Medical Schools.

Freedom riders were people who, in 1961 and later, took buses into the southern United States to challenge segregation. These buses were ruled by the Supreme Court to be not allowed to be segregated. However, the southern states did not follow these rulings, and the federal government did not enforce them. The first group of freedom riders left Washington, D.C., on May 4, 1961, and planned to reach New Orleans on May 17. The Boynton ruling in 1960 said that restaurants and waiting rooms in bus terminals should not be segregated. In 1955, the Interstate Commerce Commission said the "separate but equal" rule from Plessy v. Ferguson was wrong, but they did not enforce this. Freedom riders mixed races on buses to protest segregation. These rides brought attention to the federal law being ignored and the violence used to enforce segregation. Riders were arrested for small things like trespassing, but police often let attackers hurt them. The Congress of Racial Equality (CORE) organized most of the rides, while some were run by the Student Nonviolent Coordinating Committee (SNCC). The rides came after sit-ins and boycotts by students and young people. The Boynton ruling supported travelers ignoring local segregation laws. Southern police saw the riders as criminals and arrested them. In some places, like Birmingham, the police worked with groups opposing the riders and let mobs attack them.

Christian Science is a belief system connected to the Church of Christ, Scientist. People who follow it are often called Christian Scientists or students of Christian Science. The church is sometimes called the Christian Science Church. It started in New England in the 19th century by Mary Baker Eddy. In her 1875 book "Science and Health," she said sickness can be healed through prayer. This book is a key part of Christian Science, along with the Bible. By 2001, it had sold over nine million copies. Eddy and 26 people got a charter in 1879 to start the Church of Christ, Scientist. In 1894, the first Mother Church was built in Boston, Massachusetts. Christian Science grew fast in the United States. In 1936, there were nearly 270,000 members. By 1990, this number had dropped to over 100,000. In 2009, there were reportedly fewer than 50,000 members. The church makes a newspaper called "The Christian Science Monitor" that won seven Pulitzer Prizes between 1950 and 2002. They also have reading rooms around the world. Eddy said Christian Science is a return to "original Christianity and its healing element." Christian Science beliefs differ from traditional Christianity. Adherents believe reality is purely spiritual, and the material world is an illusion. They think disease is a mental mistake, not a physical problem. They believe sick people should be treated with prayer, not medicine. While the church doesn't stop people from using doctors for some needs, they say prayer is most effective without medicine. Some people criticize Christian Science for not using medicine, blaming it for the deaths of several followers and their children between the 1880s and 1990s.
Wayne County is in Georgia, a U.S. state. In 2010, it had 30,099 people. Jesup is the county seat. Wayne County includes the Jesup, Georgia micropolitan area.

Carovado National Park is in southwestern Costa Rica, on the Osa Peninsula. It covers a large area and is part of the Osa Conservation Area. Established on October 24, 1975, it is Costa Rica's biggest park, protecting about a third of the Osa Peninsula. Carcovado is famous for its rich biodiversity and has been called "the most biologically intense place on Earth." Tropical ecologists often study the park. Visitors can see lots of wildlife there. The park has the largest primary forest on the American Pacific coast and one of the few remaining large areas of lowland tropical forest. Historically, logging happened in lowland areas because they are easier to reach. Even though logging reduced biodiversity, the remaining forests are too small for many animals. Larger animals especially need large, undisturbed habitats. Tourism, which is good for the economy, can threaten the park's long-term biodiversity. The park's waters are calm and rich in life. Cano Island Biological Reserve is one of the special areas along the coast. Humpback whales visit the Osa Peninsula in winter, and there are also other whale and dolphin species. Whale watching tours are available. Manatees, which were hunted, are now rare but can be seen occasionally at some beaches.

Syed Mir Jafar Ali Khan Bahadur (– 5 February 1765) was a military general who became the first dependent ruler of Bengal for the British East India Company. His rule marked the beginning of British imperialism in Indian history and was a crucial step towards British control over vast areas of the Indian subcontinent. Mir Jafar served as the commander of Bengal's forces under Siraj ud-Daulah, the ruler of Bengal, but betrayed him during the Battle of Plassey in 1757. After the British victory, Mir Jafar succeeded Siraj ud-Daulah. The British supported Mir Jafar until 1760 but were not satisfied with his actions. In 1758, Robert Clive found out that Jafar had made a treaty with the Dutch through his agent Khoja Wajid. Dutch ships were also seen in the Hooghly River. This led to the Battle of Chinsurah. British official Henry Vansittart suggested that Mir Qasim, Jafar's son-in-law, should act as deputy subahdar if Jafar could not handle the situation. In October 1760, the company forced Jafar to step down in favor of Qasim. However, Qasim's independent spirit and plans to remove the East India Company from his domain led to his overthrow. In 1763, the company restored Jafar as the nawab. Mir Qasim refused to accept this and went to war against the company. Mir Jafar ruled until his death on 5 February 1765 and is buried at the Jafarganj cemetery in Murshidabad, West Bengal. Mir Jafar remains a controversial figure in Indian history, seen as a traitor by many Bengalis.

Aquarius is a constellation in the zodiac. It is between Capricorn and Pisces. Its name means "water-carrier" or "cup-carrier" in Latin, and it has the symbol ♒, which looks like water. Aquarius is one of the oldest known constellations in the zodiac. It was listed by Ptolemy in the 2nd century and is still one of the 88 modern constellations today. This constellation is in an area often called the sea because it has many stars that remind us of water, like Cetus the whale, Pisces the fish, and Eridanus the river. Beta Aquarii is the brightest star in the Aquarius constellation, with an apparent magnitude of 2.9.

Nuclear espionage involves giving state secrets about nuclear weapons to other countries without permission. This has happened in many cases, both known and suspected. Because nuclear weapons are very important secrets, countries that have them have strict rules against sharing information about how they are made, how many they have, how they are delivered, and where they are stored. Countries also limit what they can say about nuclear weapons due to agreements that prevent their spread.

The word seneschal can mean different things, all related to supervising or managing in the past. Most often, it referred to a high-ranking court position in a royal, ducal, or noble household during the Middle Ages. This role was similar to that of a steward or majordomo. In a medieval royal household, the seneschal handled domestic affairs and managed servants. At that time, the seneschal might oversee many laborers and servants, having significant power in the community, especially since much of the local economy depended on such households. In late medieval and early modern France, a seneschal was a royal official responsible for justice and managing certain southern provinces called seneschalties. This position was like a northern French bailiff. In the United Kingdom, seneschal is used for an ecclesiastical role, referring to an official at a cathedral.

The battle took place on September 24, 1877, in Kagoshima, Japan. It was the final battle of the Satsuma Rebellion. Saigō Takamori led samurai with fewer troops against the imperial Japanese army led by Generals Yamagata Aritomo and Kawamura Sumiyoshi. Saigō's army was completely destroyed, and Saigō died. This battle ended the Satsuma Rebellion. The imperial army's win made their power stronger, and there were no more internal rebellions.
