Fakenham is a market town and civil parish in Norfolk, England. It is located near the River Wensum, northwest of Norwich. The town is where several local roads meet, including the A148 from King's Lynn to Cromer, A1067 to Norwich, and A1065 to Swaffham. In the 2001 census, Fakenham had 7,357 people living in 3,292 households. By 2011, the population grew to 7,617. For local government, Fakenham falls under the North Norfolk district. Fakenham has been a market town since 1250, known for trading corn, barley, and wheat. In the 19th century, it also became famous for printing. Fakenham Racecourse, a thoroughbred horse racing venue south of the town, has Charles, Prince of Wales, as its patron. The town has a long name, "Fakenham Lancaster," which comes from John of Gaunt, the Duke of Lancaster, owning the manor in 1377. This name is still used today, appearing on history trail plaques around the town. The two wards that cover the town for local council elections are called Lancaster North and Lancaster South.

Hartselle is the second largest city in Morgan County, Alabama, United States. It is near Decatur, about to the south. Hartselle is part of the Decatur metropolitan area and the Huntsville-Decatur combined statistical area. In 2010, the city had 14,255 people. Hartselle was founded in 1870 when the South and North Alabama Railroad came. It was named after George Hartsell, one of the railroad owners. The post office opened in 1873. Hartselle became a formal city on March 1, 1875. Most of the oldest buildings were destroyed in a big fire in 1916.

Western romance languages include Gallo-Romance and Iberian-Romance, plus northern Italian. They use "s" for plurals, soften some sounds, and pronounce "soft c" as /t͡s/ or /s/. While there's a lot of similarity between Italian and French, and between Spanish and Italian dialects, French and Spanish are less similar. Based on how easily people can understand each other, there are about a dozen Western romance languages, including Portuguese, Spanish, Catalan, Galician, and French. Some groups also include Italian and Dalmatian together. Sardinian is a bit different and may have split off earlier. Today, Spanish, Portuguese, French, and Catalan are the most widely spoken Western romance languages. Many people speak French as a second language in Africa.

A cleaner shrimp is a type of small sea creature that helps other animals by cleaning them. These shrimps belong to different families: Hippolytidae, Palaemonidae, and Stenopodidae. Some common species include the Pacific cleaner shrimp and the banded coral shrimp. Cleaner shrimps get their name because they remove parasites from fish, which benefits the fish and provides nutrition for the shrimp. They also eat mucus and parasites near fish wounds, helping the fish heal and reducing stress. At coral reefs, groups of cleaner shrimps often gather at cleaning stations, similar to cleaner fish. Some cleaner shrimps, like those in the Urocaridella genus, live in caves and are not always seen by other animals. These shrimps perform a rocking dance to attract fish at cleaning stations. At night, one species, Urocaridella antonbruunii, cleans sleeping fish to avoid competition. People often keep cleaner shrimps in saltwater aquariums because they help clean the tank and look colorful.

Mount Vernon is a city in Posey County, Indiana, United States. It is in the southwestern part of the state and is the westernmost city. Rockport, located near the Ohio River, is the southernmost city. Mount Vernon had 6,687 people in 2010. It is in Black Township and is part of the Evansville, Indiana, metropolitan area, which had 358,676 people in 2010.

Runa Laila, born on November 17, 1952, is a famous Bangladeshi singer and composer. She is well-known in South Asia. She began her career in the Pakistan film industry in the late 1960s. Her singing style was inspired by Pakistani singer Ahmed Rushdi. She replaced another singer named Mala and started singing with Rushdi. She sang in films like "The Rain" (1976), "Jadur Banshi" (1977), "Accident" (1989), "Ontore Ontore" (1994), "Devdas" (2013), and "Priya Tumi Shukhi Hou" (2014). For her performances in these films, she won seven Bangladesh National Film Awards for best female playback singer. She also won the best music composer award for the film "Ekti Cinemar Golpo" (2018).

Cebuano, also called Bisaya or Binisaya, is an Austronesian language spoken in southern Philippines, especially in Central Visayas, Western Eastern Visayas, and most of Mindanao. It comes from Cebu Island and is mainly used by the Visayan people, including the Cebuanos. Cebuano had the most native speakers in the Philippines from the 1950s to the 1980s. It is the most widely spoken Visayan language, part of the larger group of Philippine languages. People call it "Visayan," but this term doesn't refer to other Visayan languages. Cebuano is the main language in the Central Visayas, some parts of Eastern Visayas, western Palawan, and most of Mindanao. The language is also spoken in Western Leyte, particularly in Ormoc and nearby towns, but locals use other names like "Ormocanon" or "Albuerahanon." Cebuano has the ISO code CEB but no two-letter code. The Komisyon ng Wikang Filipino regulates the language and spells its name as Sebwano. Cebuano and its dialects, such as Boholano, are sometimes called Cebuan in linguistics, one of the main branches of Visayan languages.

ʿilm al-kalām, or kalām, is the study of Islamic beliefs. It helps defend Islamic faith against doubters. A person who studies kalām is called a mutakallim. Kalām is different from Islamic philosophers, jurists, and scientists. The term kalām comes from the Arabic word meaning "speech." In Islamic theology, it focuses on discussing and defending basic Islamic beliefs. Murtada Mutahhari says it explains, argues about, and defends important Islamic ideas. This discipline might have been called kalām because it debates whether the words of the Quran are part of God's essence or created like normal speech.

Eden Riegel, born on January 1, 1981, is an American actress and dialogue director. She played Bianca Montgomery in the TV show "All My Children." This role made Bianca a popular and iconic character. Eden received a Daytime Emmy Award for her performance in 2005. She has also appeared in other TV shows and films. She starred as Eden in the web series "Imaginary Bitches." Riegel acted as Heather Stevens in "The Young and the Restless" from April 2010 to November 2011. Additionally, she directs the voices for Disney's animated TV series "Amphibia" and "The Owl House."

dhayam is a 2017 Indian Tamil thriller film. It was written and directed by Kannan Rangaswamy and produced by A. R. S. Sunder. The entire movie was filmed inside one room. The main actors are Santhosh Prathap, Jayakumar, Aanchal Singh, Sandhu Samaira, and Iraa Agarwal. The music was composed by Sathish Selvam, the cinematography was done by A. Packiaraj, and R. Sudharsan edited it. The film was first shown in theaters on March 24, 2017.

Mystery Science Theater 3000, or MST3K, is an American TV comedy show. It was created by Joel Hodgson and made by Alternaversal Productions. The show first aired on November 24, 1988, on KTMA-TV in Minneapolis, and later on Comedy Central for seven seasons until 1996. It was then shown on the Sci-Fi Channel for three seasons until 1999. In 1993, a 60-episode package called "The Mystery Science Theater Hour" was made and shown in 1995. In 2015, Hodgson started a new MST3K with 14 episodes, released on Netflix in 2017, followed by another six episodes in 2018. The show has 217 episodes and two live tours. The story of MST3K is about Joel Robinson, a janitor trapped on the "Satellite of Love" by two mad scientists. He watches bad movies and uses his robots, Tom Servo, Crow T. Robot, and Gypsy, to keep him company and make fun of the movies. Each episode has a movie and interstitial sketches. The main cast included Joel, Tom, and Crow, with other writers like Trace Beaulieu, Josh Weinstein, and Kevin Murphy. In 2017, a new cast took over, including Jonah Ray as the new character Jonah Heston, and Patton Oswalt and Felicia Day as the mad scientists. The 2017 revival was well-received and won a Peabody Award in 1993. MST3K became popular among fans, known as "MSTies," who shared the show and it later appeared on home media. The show was considered influential and inspired similar projects like Rifftrax and Cinematic Titanic. Many forgotten movies gained attention and recognition.

Sir David Wing Cheung Tang was a businessman, philanthropist, and socialite from Hong Kong. He was born on August 2, 1954, and passed away on August 29, 2017. He is best known for starting the Shanghai Tang fashion chain in 1994. He sold this company to Richemont in 1998.

Seminole County is in Oklahoma, a U.S. state. In 2010, it had 25, 482 people. The main town is Wewoka. Most of the county is part of the Seminole Nation reservation. A small part in the east belongs to the Muscogee (Creek) Nation. Seminole County is known for the Greater Seminole Field, a very important oil field that is still producing. This field extends into nearby counties. During the early oil boom, many workers and adventurers came to the county, making the population triple quickly. When oil production went down later, people and jobs left.

granzymes are enzymes that help kill cells, especially those that are cancerous or infected by viruses or bacteria. They can also fight bacteria and stop viruses from copying themselves. In immune cells like cytotoxic T cells and natural killer cells, granzymes are stored with another protein called perforin in small bags called cytotoxic granules. When the immune cells attack a target cell, these granules release their contents into a special contact area called an immune synapse. Perforin helps granzymes enter the target cell's interior, where granzymes can do their job. Granzymes belong to a family of enzymes and are similar to other immune enzymes. One type, granzyme B, triggers cell death by activating caspases, which cut proteins and start the cell death process. Granzyme B also cuts a protein called Bid, which changes the mitochondria's membrane and releases important proteins that help with cell death. Granzymes can also target and kill harmful cells inside the body. They do this by cutting proteins in bacteria, causing damage, and by cutting viral proteins, stopping them from copying. Some granzymes can also bind to DNA and RNA, which can help in killing cells. Granzymes are not only found in T cells but also in other immune cells like dendritic cells, B cells, and mast cells. They can even be found in some non-immune cells like keratinocytes, pneumocytes, and chondrocytes. In cells that don't have perforin or don't form immune synapses, granzyme B can be released outside the cell. When granzyme B is outside the cell, it can build up in the spaces between cells in conditions where there is inflammation. This can break down the tissue and affect how it heals. Excess granzyme B has been linked to problems like hardening of the arteries, swelling, poor wound healing, and skin aging.

The East Midlands is one of nine official regions in England. It includes Derbyshire, Leicestershire, Lincolnshire (excluding North and North East Lincolnshire), Northamptonshire, Nottinghamshire, and Rutland. The region covers an area and had more than 4.5 million people in 2011. Six main cities are Derby, Leicester, Lincoln, Mansfield, Northampton, and Nottingham. Other cities include Boston, Chesterfield, Corby, Grantham, Hinckley, Kettering, Loughborough, Newark-on-Trent, Skegness, Wellingborough, and Worksop. The East Midlands is close to London and has good roads, which help the region do well economically. Nottingham and Leicester are important cities known as world cities. The main airport is East Midlands Airport, located between Derby, Loughborough, and Nottingham.

The muskmelon, also known as "cucumis melo," is a type of melon that has many different cultivated varieties. Some smooth-skinned varieties include honeydew, crenshaw, and casaba. There are also netted types like cantaloupe, Persian melon, and Christmas melon. Many different muskmelon varieties exist, similar to wild cabbage. Muskmelons' origins are not clear. Some scientists believe they came from the Levant and Egypt, while others think they originated in India or central Asia. Some researchers suggest an African origin, and today, wild muskmelons can still be found in some African countries.
elitserien is the top division for men's volleyball in Sweden. By late February or early March, it is followed by the Swedish national championship playoff.

John Walton, born in 1952 in St. Ives, Sydney, was an Australian actor. He acted on stage, television, and in films. He is best known for his role in the TV show "The Young Doctors." He passed away on July 17, 2014.

Northern California, or NorCal, is the top part of California. It covers 48 counties. Main cities include San Jose, San Francisco, Oakland in the San Francisco Bay Area; Sacramento, the capital city; and Fresno. The area has redwood forests, the Sierra Nevada with Yosemite Valley and part of Lake Tahoe. Mount Shasta is a big mountain here. The Central Valley, a very productive farming area, is also part of it. The 48-county definition is not used for the Northern California megaregion, one of 11 in the U.S. Instead, it includes Fresno to Sacramento and east to Nevada, covering Lake Tahoe and Reno. People lived in the area for at least 19,000 years. European explorers arrived between the 1500s and 1750s but did not settle in northern California. The first European settlement was in 1770, when Spanish missions began in Monterey. Other missions along the coast followed, eventually reaching Sonoma County.

M'sila, also spelled Msila, is a province in northern Algeria. It has a population of about 1 million and covers an area of 18,718 square kilometers. The capital city, also named M'sila, has about 100,000 people and is home to M'sila University. Some other places in this province are Bou Saada and Maadid. There's a salt lake called Chott el Hodna in M'sila. Most of the region is semi-arid and not well-developed. M'sila is famous for farming. It was also where the first village, called Maader, was built as part of a government program to help nomadic Algerians settle down using local materials. Maader now has houses, public spaces, a trading area, and a mosque.

Dominique Baudis was a French rights defender, also known as an ombudsman. He was born on April 14, 1947, and passed away on April 10, 2014. Before this role, he was a journalist and politician. He also served as the mayor of Toulouse. He belonged to the DL party and later joined the leading center-right party called Union for a Popular Movement.

Hawthorn Football Club, nicknamed the Hawks, is a professional Australian rules football team in the Australian Football League (AFL). Founded in 1902, it's the youngest Victorian-based team in the AFL and has won thirteen premierships. The Hawks have won in every decade since the 1960s. Their uniforms are brown and gold, vertically striped. The club's motto is "let us be judged by our acts." Hawthorn is from the inner-eastern Melbourne suburb of Hawthorn and used to play at Glenferrie Oval, but matches haven't been there since 1973. In 2006, their training and office moved to Waverley Park, 21 km from the city center, in the area where most fans live. Their mascot is a hawk. Since 2007, they've played four games a year at York Park in Launceston, Tasmania, and the rest at the Melbourne Cricket Ground. Hawthorn's local team is the Box Hill Hawks.
